methods.doc: Registers this family's blocks with the renderer.

methods.name: query
methods.doc:
The query wrapper is stored markup; the block sets the loop its
children read, run only once one of them asks (a post template,
pagination, no results, the total), as the reference runs it in
those blocks: a query block with nothing that lists posts queries
nothing (security review 2026-10-22).

methods.name: navigating
methods.doc:
A loop that navigates on the client (enhancedPagination), as the
reference marks it: the wrapper an interactive core/query region keyed
by the query's id, its attributes ahead of the stored ones, and the
block's view module on the page. The router region, once processed,
brings the loading bar.

methods.name: enhanced
methods.doc: Whether the innermost loop being rendered navigates on the client.

methods.name: queried
methods.doc:
A query loop's posts as the reference finds them: the arguments
build_query_vars_from_query_block makes of the block's query (through
query_loop_block_query_vars) for the page its query-{id}-page asks
for, run through WP_Query, so pre_get_posts and the posts_* filters
shape it too.

methods.name: page
methods.doc: A query's posts as a page of records.

methods.name: loop
methods.doc:
A loop as the query block sets it: the main query's page when it
inherits, else its own query for the page its query-{id}-page asks for.
An inheriting loop inside the main query's loop (a singular page's
template, a post's content in a listing) walks a copy of the main query
from its start, as the reference does (no query runs again), so it shows
the main query's posts rather than finding that loop already under way.
shapes: @return array{page: Page, query: ?Query, inherit: bool, paged: int, perPage: int, id: int}

methods.name: current
methods.doc: The innermost loop being rendered; outside one, the loop a block's context provides (a post template called by its render callback).

methods.name: total
methods.doc: How many posts the loop found, or which of them this page shows (displayType range-display).

methods.name: postTemplate
methods.doc:
The loop's posts, walked as the reference walks them: the loop's query
is asked whether it has posts (an empty one fires loop_no_results),
each post is set up with the_post (loop_start before the first,
loop_end after the last), and the main query's post is set up again
once the loop is done. Plugins see the global post and in_the_loop()
move with the loop.

methods.name: pagination
methods.doc:
Pagination renders only when the loop it belongs to has more than one
page: the main query's pages for an inheriting loop, its own query's
(as many as the block's page limit allows) for any other, paged by
query-{id}-page. The links keep the address's other arguments; the
numbers show the first and last page and those around the current one,
dots between (probe query-pagination-custom).

methods.name: paginationBase
methods.doc: The current listing's own URL, without a page number.

methods.name: numbers
methods.doc:
The page numbers: the first and last page, and those within $around of
the current one, with dots where pages are left out. In a navigating
loop each item is keyed by its place (index-N) and each link navigates.

methods.name: archiveTitle
methods.doc: A post type archive's title: the type's label, renamed by the post_type_archive_title filter when a plugin does.

methods.name: templatePart
methods.doc:
A template part, as the reference renders one (probe
template-part-lookup): the part found, the tag its area wraps it in
asked for, its shortcodes run before its blocks are rendered, then
texturized, its smilies converted and its images and iframes fitted
out for the part's area; wrapped in tagName when it names a tag the
engine allows, else the area's.

methods.name: areaTag
methods.doc: The tag an area's parts are wrapped in, from the areas core knows; a div for any other.

methods.name: unbooted
methods.doc: A part with no runtime to ask: the saved part, else the theme's file, in the tag tagName or its area names.

methods.name: lookedUp
methods.doc:
A part's markup and area as the reference finds them, with what it
tells plugins on the way (probe template-part-lookup): only a part of
the active theme is looked for, first as a saved part through
WP_Query (so pre_get_posts can steer the lookup and loop_no_results
hears a miss; the engine answers it from the theme's saved templates
unless a plugin changes it), its template made from the post (the
area its term names), then the theme's file through
get_block_file_template; the file looked for again, and each found or
missing one announced. Null when there is none.

classes.name: Minn\Blocks\Dynamic\Theme\TermBlocks
classes.doc:
term-name, term-count and term-description: the term a block's context
names (termId and taxonomy, as a terms query provides them), else the
term archive being viewed; nothing for neither (probe core-blocks).

classes.name: Minn\Blocks\Elements
classes.doc:
Per-block element styles (style.elements in a block's attributes, the
link colour most often; probe block-supports). A block whose element
styles set a colour gets a numbered wp-elements-N class and a rule per
element and state, recorded with the page's block-support styles in
render order: links (their text colour, plain or on hover), headings,
each heading level and buttons (text, background or gradient). A block
type whose colour support skips serialization, whole or for links,
headings or buttons, writes none for those.

constants.name: SELECTORS
constants.value: array (   'link' => 'a:where(:not(.wp-element-button))',   'heading' => 'h1, h2, h3, h4, h5, h6',   'h1' => 'h1',   'h2' => 'h2',   'h3' => 'h3',   'h4' => 'h4',   'h5' => 'h5',   'h6' => 'h6',   'button' => '.wp-element-button, .wp-block-button__link', )

The block's wp-elements-N class, recording its rules; null when its
element styles earn none.

Whether element styles earn a class: a link's text colour (or its

background or gradient, for a kind not skipped.

classes.name: Minn\Blocks\ImageTags
classes.doc: The attributes the reference adds to an that carries a wp-image-{id} class: loading, decoding, width and height (prepended, in that order), and srcset plus sizes (appended). The srcset lists the displayed size first, then every same-ratio size in stored order, then the original.

params.doc: whether the images are on a front-end page, where the loading budget applies

methods.name: enrich
methods.doc: Rewrites every wp-image-* in a fragment; other images pass through.

methods.name: enrichGallery
methods.doc: The same for a gallery: every image also carries its data-id.

methods.name: enrichPlugin
methods.doc: The same for a plugin block's output, where the reference adds no sizes="auto".

methods.name: content
methods.doc: Every and

methods.name: optimized
methods.doc: An given what it lacks of decoding, loading and fetchpriority, as the context earns them (wp_img_tag_add_loading_optimization_attrs): an image with no source given none of them; decoding through wp_img_tag_add_decoding_attr; for an image that writes a width and a height, lazy loading asked, then a loading through wp_img_tag_add_loading_attr (lazy or eager as given, any other answer keeping the loading the context earned, a false one none); then a high priority. Each is placed straight after "

methods.name: finished
methods.doc:
Content the engine fitted out itself, with what the_content's other
callbacks added on the way (an attachment's own link, a plugin's
image): an image still without its loading attributes is fitted as
the rest were, then each is offered to wp_content_img_tag, as
wp_filter_content_tags would.

methods.name: featured
methods.doc:
A post's featured image at full size, in the reference's attribute
order (dimensions, source, class, alt, style, then the loading
attributes and the srcset). Empty when the attachment has no file.

methods.name: contentImage
methods.doc: One content image fitted out as wp_filter_content_tags fits it, then through wp_content_img_tag.

methods.name: frame
methods.doc: An iframe given the loading its context earns (wp_iframe_tag_add_loading_attr), when it has a width and a height.

methods.name: dimensioned
methods.doc: An attachment's image given the width and height its source names, when it is one of the attachment's files.

methods.name: lazySizes
methods.doc: A lazy image's sizes led by "auto", unless they already are.

methods.name: attributeOf
methods.doc:
An attribute's value as written after a space, or null: its name in
lower case (any case for src), as the reference reads it.

methods.name: sizeOf
methods.doc: An image's width and height, each as a whole number when it is written as one. @return array{width: ?int, height: ?int}

methods.name: sized
methods.doc: A template's image: an attachment's gets its srcset and sizes in place, nothing more; any other is left as it is.

methods.name: fit
methods.doc: One content image fitted out: an attachment's (by its wp-image class) in full, any other with its loading attributes.

methods.name: closeWith
methods.doc: The tag with its attributes added before the close; a callback, so a $0 in an address stays text.

methods.name: plainImage
methods.doc: An image that is not an attachment's: decoding always, loading when its size is known and it has none.

methods.name: autoSized
methods.doc: A lazy image's sizes led by "auto" (wp_img_tag_add_auto_sizes), unless they already are or a plugin says not to (probe rest-attachments-controller).

methods.name: autoSizedWhenLazy
methods.doc: An image a plugin made lazy after it was fitted (Elementor's image loading does) gets "auto" sizes on the next pass, as on the reference.

methods.name: loadingPrefix
methods.doc:
On a page the first big-enough content image is fetched eagerly with
high priority, the next few are eager, and the rest lazy; only lazy
images carry the "auto" sizes hint. In a REST response every image is
lazy. A plugin that turns lazy loading off (wp_lazy_loading_enabled;
Elementor's image loading does) leaves every image without it.

methods.name: givenLoading
methods.doc: An image that names its own loading keeps it: an eager one large enough is fetched first, every one is decoded asynchronously. @return array{0: string, 1: bool}

methods.name: lazyAllowed
methods.doc: Whether content images or iframes may load lazily (wp_lazy_loading_enabled, asked for the_content).

methods.name: minimumPriorityPixels
methods.doc: The area an image must cover before it is worth fetching first.

methods.name: candidates
methods.doc:
The srcset candidates for an attachment's image, keyed by width: the
shown size first, then same-ratio sizes in stored order, then the
original; with the shown width and height, the metadata and the src.
Null when the image is not one of the attachment's files.
shapes: @return array{0: array<int, string>, 1: int, 2: int, 3: array<string, mixed>, 4: string}|null

methods.name: srcsetAttributes
methods.signature: srcsetAttributes(array $candidates, int $width, bool $auto, int $attachmentId = 0, array $meta = array ( ), string $src = '', int $height = 0): string
methods.doc:
A srcset needs a choice: one candidate yields no srcset and no sizes.
With the runtime up, plugin code filters the candidates and the sizes
hint the way the reference lets it (wp_calculate_image_srcset,
wp_calculate_image_sizes).

classes.name: Minn\Blocks\Layout
classes.doc:
The layout support's classes and rules (wp_render_layout_support_flag,
probe block-supports), for core and plugin blocks alike:

- is-layout-{type} and {block}-is-layout-{type} for the layout the block
uses (its own over its type's default), with has-global-padding for a
constrained layout under a theme with root-padding-aware alignments;
- is-vertical or is-horizontal, is-content-justification-* and is-nowrap
from the layout the block itself stores;
- a wp-container-{block}-is-layout-* class when the layout writes CSS
(LayoutStyle), and wp-container-content-* for a child's own size or
place in its parent's layout.

The rules go to the page's block-support styles through the private
minn_block_support_rules action. A container class's suffix is a digest
the engine cannot reproduce (its inputs are not observable), so the engine
derives its own from the layout: same shape, different value, which the
parity suites normalise.

methods.name: classes
methods.doc:
The layout classes a core block's wrapper carries, under its type's
supports (data/blocks.json).

methods.name: forBlock
methods.doc:
The layout classes a block's wrapper carries, its container's rules
recorded, under the theme's layout settings the render state holds
(root-padding-aware alignments, block gaps).
shapes: @param array<string, mixed> $supports the block type's supports (layout and its default, spacing)

params.doc: the block type's supports (layout and its default, spacing)

methods.name: childClass
methods.doc:
The class a child's own layout earns (its size or place in the parent's
layout), its rules recorded; null when it writes none.

methods.name: sanitizeGap
methods.doc:
A block gap as the layout reads it: a value with a character that could
end a declaration or open a function (\ ( & = } or a comment) is
dropped, a side of one too; anything not a string is left as it is.

methods.name: gapCss
methods.doc: A gap with its presets as custom properties, a side at a time.

methods.name: paddingCss
methods.doc: A block's side padding with its presets as custom properties.

methods.name: widths
methods.doc:
A layout with its widths checked: the first declaration of each, through
the style attribute filter, empty when that drops it.

methods.name: used
methods.doc:
The layout a block uses: its own over its type's default; the legacy
inherit flag means constrained.

classes.name: Minn\Blocks\LayoutStyle
classes.doc:
The CSS rules a block's layout writes (wp_get_layout_style, probe
block-supports), as selector => declarations pairs the style engine turns
into a stylesheet:

- flow: only the gap between children (none, then the gap, on each);
- constrained: the content width on the children that are not aligned
left, right or full, the wide width on wide ones, no limit on full ones
(justifyContent pushes the children to a side: both margins with a
width, the one side alone without), negative margins on full ones for a
block with side padding, then the children's gap;
- flex: nowrap, the gap, then the direction and alignments the
orientation reads from justifyContent and verticalAlignment;
- grid: the column template (a count, a minimum width, or both folded
together with the gap, or the fallback gap without one), then the gap.

Widths arrive checked (one dropped as unsafe is empty) and gaps with
presets turned into custom properties.

methods.name: rules
methods.signature: rules(string $selector, array $layout, array|string|null $gap, array $padding = array ( ), string $fallbackGap = '0.5em'): array
methods.doc: The rules for a container.
shapes: @param array<string, mixed> $layout the layout, its widths checked
@param string|array<string, string>|null $gap the block gap (a value, or top and left), null when it is not written
@param array<string, string> $padding the block's own padding (left, right), for full-width children

params.doc: the block gap (a value, or top and left), null when it is not written

params.doc: the block's own padding (left, right), for full-width children

params.doc: the gap a grid with a minimum column width counts when the block writes none

methods.name: childRules
methods.doc:
The rules a child writes from its own layout (wp_get_child_layout_style_rules):
a fixed or filling flex size, a grid span, a grid position, released
again (the full row for a span) in a container narrower than the
columns it needs: the columns at the parent's minimum width (12rem by
default) and the gaps between them (1.5rem, or 24px for a width in px).
shapes: @param array<string, mixed> $child the child's layout (selfStretch, flexSize, columnSpan, rowSpan, columnStart, rowStart)

params.name: child
params.doc: the child's layout (selfStretch, flexSize, columnSpan, rowSpan, columnStart, rowStart)

Parses block markup into a tree. The grammar is the delimiter comment:
an opener with optional JSON attributes, a closer, or a self-closing
void block; a name without a namespace is core/. Anything outside a
block is a freeform block that renders as-is.

The parser class block_parser_class names when a plugin swaps its own
in for WP_Block_Parser; null for the engine's own.

methods.name: named

A document's blocks as do_blocks reads them: by the parser
block_parser_class names, the engine's own unless a plugin swaps
its own in.

The first block delimiter at or after an offset: where it starts, its
length, its name (core/ when it names no namespace), its attributes as
written (null when it has none), and whether it closes a block or is
a void one. Null when no delimiter follows.

reference's build_query_vars_from_query_block builds them (probe
query-loop): a viewable post type; stickies only, left out, or ignored;

@param array{viewableType: callable(string): bool, hierarchicalType: callable(string): bool, viewableTaxonomy: callable(string): bool, formats: list<string>} $site what the site says about types, taxonomies and formats

params.doc: what the site says about types, taxonomies and formats

methods.doc: The old categoryIds and tagIds settings as clauses. @param array<string, mixed> $context @return list<array<string, mixed>>

shapes: @param array<string, mixed> $context @param callable(string): bool $viewable @return list<array<string, mixed>>

The formats asked for (standard, or one the site knows) OR'd; beside

methods.doc: Authors: a list or a comma list as author__in, one id as author. @param array<string, mixed> $query @return array<string, mixed>

classes.name: Minn\Blocks\RenderState
classes.doc:
Per-request rendering state, owned by the renderer. The reference numbers
galleries, style variations, and search inputs from ONE counter that runs
across every block rendered in the request (a list response keeps
counting from post to post), so the counter lives here, not on any block.
Leaf helpers with no renderer in hand reach it through current().

constants.name: MAX_SOURCES
constants.doc:
How many sources (parts, patterns, synced blocks, menus, posts' content)
one outermost render may open: distinct sources nest combinatorially
under the depth cap, and an author's content is rendered for every
view. The reference has no such budget; a page past it renders the
rest as a cycle renders, as nothing.

properties.name: request
properties.doc: Whether this state is one request's: its budget then holds for the whole request (every do_blocks of it), not each outermost render.

properties.name: rootPaddingAware
properties.doc: Whether the theme's layout puts root padding in custom properties; render configuration, so reset() leaves it.

properties.name: blockGap
properties.doc: Whether the theme writes block gaps (settings.spacing.blockGap); render configuration too.

properties.name: directives
properties.doc: What interactivity_process_directives last answered, for the block rendering now.

properties.name: offRequest
properties.doc: The state for code that renders with no request behind it: the command line and the unit suite.

properties.name: pendingElements
properties.doc: the element class claimed for the dynamic block being rendered, until its wrapper takes it

properties.name: pendingVariation
properties.doc: the numbered style variation class claimed for the dynamic block being rendered, until its wrapper takes it

methods.name: forRequest
methods.doc: A request's own state, its source budget held for the whole request.

methods.name: current
methods.doc:
The state of the request being rendered, which its runtime holds, so
a request cannot count on from the one before it. Rendering with no
runtime (the command line, the unit suite) shares one off-request
state instead, since the counters have to survive between calls.

methods.name: adopt
methods.doc: Makes this the state current() answers with, for the renderer that brought its own.

methods.name: rootPaddingAware
methods.doc: Whether the theme puts root padding in custom properties, which decides the constrained layout's classes.

methods.name: useRootPadding
methods.doc: Records what the active theme's layout settings say about root padding.

methods.name: blockGap
methods.doc: Whether the theme writes block gaps, which decides whether a layout's gap makes CSS.

methods.name: useBlockGap
methods.doc: Records whether the active theme's spacing settings write block gaps.

methods.name: nextId
methods.doc: The next per-request counter value.

methods.name: countImages
methods.doc: Adds to the page's count of content images (wp_increase_content_media_count) and returns the new count.

methods.name: nextImage
methods.doc: Content images seen so far in this page, for the loading rules.

methods.name: refundImages
methods.doc:
Images a plugin's block filter removed from the page give their budget
back, so the next image still counts as if the hidden ones never rendered.

methods.name: aside
methods.doc:
Runs rendering whose images do not count toward the page's loading
budget (an excerpt's): the reference fits no image while it makes one,
so whatever was seen meanwhile is given back.

methods.name: filteringContent
methods.doc:
$filter run while the_content filters content the engine rendered: the
images it already holds count as fitted out, so only what the filter's
other callbacks add is fitted (fittedImage()).

methods.name: postContent
methods.doc:
A post's content as a post-content block renders it, or '' while that
post's content is already being rendered further out: the reference
prints nothing there, so a post that shows its own content (directly,
or through an inheriting query loop) renders it once. Also '' once the
render's source budget is spent (MAX_SOURCES).

methods.name: within
methods.doc:
Renders inside the context the content's images are fitted out for (a
template part's template_part_{area}, a post's the_content), the
innermost one standing.

methods.name: contentContext
methods.doc: The context content is rendered in now (within), or null outside any.

methods.name: renderAdded
methods.doc:
Block markup a the_content filter put before or after what the engine
rendered, rendered by $render (do_blocks, in its place on the_content).
The engine's own rendering is never parsed again, so block delimiters
in comment text or an embed's markup stay inert, as the reference parses
only the stored content; where a filter changed the rendering itself,
nothing is parsed.

methods.name: renderedInFilter
methods.doc:
The engine rendered the content being filtered in do_blocks's place
(Runtime::blockContentFilter): its images count as fitted out from
here on, as those of content rendered before the filter began do.

methods.name: fittedImage
methods.doc: Whether an image tag is one the content being filtered held when the filter began.

methods.name: claimPriority
methods.doc: True once, for the image that gets fetchpriority="high".

methods.name: priorityAvailable
methods.doc: Whether no element has taken high fetch priority yet on this page.

methods.name: closePriority
methods.doc: Takes high fetch priority off the table for the rest of the page; a plugin prioritising its own element does this.

methods.name: reopenPriority
methods.doc: Puts high fetch priority back on offer, so the next large enough image takes it.

methods.name: recordBlock
methods.doc: Every block name the page rendered; the stylesheet prints block styles for these only.

methods.name: blocks
methods.doc: The block names rendering met.

methods.name: nextElements
methods.doc: The next wp-elements-N class; the reference numbers these apart from the shared counter.

methods.name: uniqueLabel
methods.doc: A navigation's aria-label: the label itself the first time, then "label N" for repeats.

methods.name: uniqueCaptionId
methods.doc: A caption's id, or its text's: as given the first time on the page, then "id-N" for repeats (probe gallery-captions).

methods.name: enterNavigation
methods.doc:
A page list renders plain on its own and takes the navigation block's
item classes, submenu toggles, and interactivity only while it sits
inside one, so the navigation block marks the span it owns.

methods.name: leaveNavigation
methods.doc: Leaves a navigation block.

methods.name: processesDirectives
methods.doc:
Whether the block rendering now has its Interactivity API directives
processed, as interactivity_process_directives answered for it.

methods.name: inNavigation
methods.doc: Whether rendering is inside a navigation block.

methods.name: enter
methods.doc: Marks a nested source as being rendered; false when it is already open (a cycle) or the render's budget is spent.

methods.name: leave
methods.doc: Leaves a cycle-guarded key.

methods.name: inside
methods.doc: Whether a key is open: a source being rendered, or the page template ("template").

methods.name: descend
methods.doc: True while the block tree is shallower than the cap; deeper blocks render as nothing.

methods.name: ascend
methods.doc: Leaves one nesting level.

methods.name: depth
methods.doc: How deep the block tree is right now; zero outside any block render.

methods.name: setPendingElements
methods.doc: A dynamic block claims its element class before rendering, so a block that renders nothing still counts.

methods.name: takePendingElements
methods.doc: The pending elements class, cleared.

methods.name: setPendingVariation
methods.doc: Holds the numbered style variation class a dynamic block claimed before rendering; returns the one it replaces.

methods.name: takePendingVariation
methods.doc: The numbered style variation class the dynamic block being rendered claimed, once: its wrapper takes it.

methods.name: recordGallery
methods.doc: Notes a gallery instance.

methods.name: galleries
methods.doc: The gallery instances rendering met.

methods.name: reset
methods.doc: Clears every per-request counter.

methods.name: spend
methods.doc: Counts one more source opened (per request, or per outermost render off a request); false past MAX_SOURCES.

classes.name: Minn\Blocks\Renderer
classes.doc:
Renders a block tree the way the reference renders post_content:
delimiters gone, each block's own HTML kept with inner blocks rendered
in place, then the per-block render-time additions (layout classes, the
paragraph class, image attributes, gallery ids, style-variation
counters), and finally texturize over the whole.

constants.name: CLASSNAME_ALWAYS
constants.doc: The dynamic core blocks that ask block_default_classname even when they render nothing (generatedClass()).

constants.name: CLASSNAME_NEVER
constants.doc: The dynamic core blocks that never ask it (the tabs and accordion blocks edit their saved markup instead).

properties.name: unfiltered
properties.doc: Whether the next block renders without the block filters around it (renderNativeUnfiltered()).

properties.name: asCallback
properties.doc: Whether the next block renders as its render callback called alone would (renderNativeAsCallback()).

properties.name: handedInstance
properties.doc: The WP_Block the facade renders the next block as (handContext()).

properties.name: ownInstance
properties.doc: The WP_Block the block that has just started to render began as (ownInstance()).

properties.name: made
properties.doc: Whether the next block is made as its parent's list makes it, without the block filters before it (renderMade()).

methods.name: numberedStyle
methods.doc:
The numbered companion of a block style variation the block's class
names (is-style-{name}--N), consuming the counter: a variation with
styles of its own, the theme's or a registered style's (the facade
answers the private minn_block_style_variation filter), whose CSS the
facade prints once numbered (minn_block_style_variation_used). Null
when none applies.

methods.name: state
methods.doc: The per-request rendering state: counters, containers, variations, the images seen.

methods.name: context
methods.doc: What is being rendered.

methods.name: withContext
methods.doc: Sets what is being rendered.

methods.name: images
methods.doc: The image tag builder.

methods.name: forDb
methods.doc: A renderer with every dynamic block wired over the database door.

methods.name: registerDynamic
methods.doc:
Registers the engine's own renderer for a dynamic block. A plugin's
callback that already took the block over (bridge()) keeps it, as a
replaced render callback does on the reference.

methods.name: bridge
methods.doc:
Hands a block to a plugin's render callback; the engine's own renderer
for it stays for renderNative().

methods.name: renderNative
methods.doc:
One block as HTML through the engine's own renderer for its name (its
static markup when it has none), even where a plugin's callback took
the block over: what a core render callback gives, so a plugin's
callback that calls the one it replaced does not call itself.

methods.name: render
methods.doc: Block markup as HTML, texturized: a document of its own (renderRoots()).

methods.name: renderBlocks
methods.doc: A tree of blocks as HTML.

methods.name: renderNativeUnfiltered
methods.doc:
A core block as renderNative() renders it, without the block filters
around this one block (its inner blocks keep theirs): its caller, the
facade's WP_Block::render, applies them once.

methods.name: renderNativeAsCallback
methods.doc:
A core block as its render callback called directly renders it: not a
block being rendered, so enqueue_empty_block_content_assets is not
asked for it (its inner blocks are), as the reference asks it only in
a block's render (probe plugin-surface2).

methods.name: finishImagesWith
methods.doc:
What the runtime does to an image block's markup once the engine has
rendered it: the lightbox, when the image's settings or the theme's ask
for one.

methods.name: handContext
methods.doc:
The context render_block_context already gave the next block, when
render_block() or a WP_Block renders it: a block that provides its
own context (a tabs block's id) reads it with ownContext() rather
than asking again. The WP_Block is the parent its inner blocks are
begun with.

methods.name: ownInstance
methods.doc: The WP_Block the block that has just begun to render was made as; null when the block filters did not begin it.

methods.name: renderRoots
methods.doc:
Blocks that begin a document of their own (a pattern's, a part's, a
post's content), as do_blocks renders them: no parent block.

methods.name: under
methods.doc: Renders with a WP_Block of the renderer's making as the parent of the blocks inside (a synced pattern's, a post template's item).

methods.name: renderItem
methods.doc:
One item of a loop rendered as the reference renders it (a post
template's post, a comment template's comment): inside a WP_Block of
its own, made from the parsed block given with the context given as
all it has, which goes through render_block itself (probe
block-instances).

methods.name: renderMade
methods.doc:
A block as the reference renders an item of a block list its parent
walks itself (a navigation's own items): made from what the parent
gives its inner blocks, without pre_render_block, render_block_data
or render_block_context before it.

methods.name: ownContext
methods.doc:
The context render_block_context gave the block that has just begun
to render; null when nothing did. A block's renderer reads it first,
before its inner blocks begin.

methods.name: renderBlock
methods.doc: One block as HTML, with the filters around it (unless renderNativeUnfiltered() asked for this one without).

methods.name: blockContext
methods.doc:
The context a block's bindings read: the post being rendered (postId,
postType) and what enclosing blocks provide (a synced pattern's
overrides).

methods.name: providing
methods.doc: Renders with context provided to the blocks inside (render_block_context's job on the reference). @param array<string, mixed> $context

methods.name: rendersNatively
methods.doc:
Whether the engine's own renderer answers for a block: a core block no
plugin's callback took over. It applies the block supports it knows
itself (layout, element styles); the facade's render_block filters do
the rest, and all of them for any other block.

methods.name: freeform
methods.doc: Text between blocks, through the block filters as do_blocks hands it them (probe block-instances).

methods.name: parent
methods.doc: The WP_Block of the block the next one renders inside; null at a document's top.

methods.name: generatedClass
methods.doc:
A dynamic core block's own class through block_default_classname, as
the reference asks it while the block takes its wrapper attributes:
for a block that renders something (the query pagination links even
when they do not; the RSS and widget-group blocks never), and a class
a plugin changes replaces the block's on its wrapper.

methods.name: supportClasses
methods.doc: A core block's wp-elements-N class (rules recorded) and numbered style variation, with no block filters about to add them (probe block-class-stages). @return array{0: ?string, 1: ?string}

methods.name: renderNamed
shapes: @param array<string, mixed> $bound the bound attributes' values, put into a static block's HTML

params.name: bound
params.doc: the bound attributes' values, put into a static block's HTML

classes.name: Minn\Blocks\Selector
classes.doc: The CSS selector a block type declares for its root or for one feature, from its `selectors` map or the older per-support keys.

methods.name: resolve
methods.doc: The CSS selector a block's style targets, or null.
shapes: @param array<string, mixed> $selectors the block type's selectors map
@param array<string, mixed> $supports the block type's supports
@param string|list<string>|null $target 'root', a dotted feature path, or a path list

params.name: target
params.doc: 'root', a dotted feature path, or a path list

classes.name: Minn\Blocks\Serializer
classes.doc:
Parsed blocks back to markup. A core block is written by its short name;
attributes are JSON with every character that could end the comment or
open a tag spelled as an escape ("<" "<", "--" "--", a
backslash "\"), so a value can never break out of its delimiter.

methods.name: blocks
methods.doc: A list of parsed blocks back to markup, freeform runs as written.

methods.name: block
methods.doc: One block with its inner blocks, as the delimiter comments the parser reads.

methods.name: delimited
methods.doc: Content wrapped in a block's delimiters; a block with no content is written self-closing.

methods.name: attributes
methods.doc: Block attributes as the delimiter carries them.

methods.name: spreadInnerContent
methods.doc:
A parsed block's inner content with each inner block's place (a null)
taken as many times as that block became blocks, as a pattern that
expands does; one that became none keeps its place.
shapes: @param list<int> $counts how many blocks each inner block became, in order

params.name: counts
params.doc: how many blocks each inner block became, in order

classes.name: Minn\Blocks\States
classes.doc:
Block state styles (a block's style[":hover"] and the like, probe
block-supports): the selector arithmetic and the fallbacks the reference
applies when it writes a state's rules. Pure: styles and selectors in,
styles, groups and declarations out.

methods.name: split
methods.doc:
A selector list split at its top-level commas (none inside parentheses
counts), each part as written.

methods.name: selector
methods.doc:
A state on each selector of a block's list, its leading compound
selector swapped for the base; the base alone for an empty list.

methods.name: presetVars
methods.doc: Presets (var:preset|{kind}|{slug}) as their custom properties, through arrays; anything else as it is.

methods.name: backgroundResets
methods.doc:
Declarations with a background image unset under a background colour
that sets neither a background nor an image of its own.

methods.name: borderFallbacks
methods.doc:
Declarations with a solid border style for a border (or a side of one)
given a width or a colour and no style.

methods.name: dimensionFallbacks
methods.doc:
A state's style with an explicit aspect ratio unsetting the height and
minimum height, or a height or minimum height unsetting the aspect ratio.

methods.name: groups
methods.doc:
A state's style split by the selectors a block gives its features: a
feature (or one of its properties) with a selector of its own goes
there, a feature's other properties to its root selector, the rest to
the block's root. Groups keep the order they are first met in.
shapes: @param array<string, mixed> $selectors the block's selectors, root among them

params.name: selectors
params.doc: the block's selectors, root among them

methods.name: addGroup
methods.doc: Adds a style to the group of a selector, merged into what it holds.

classes.name: Minn\Blocks\StyleEngine
classes.doc:
What a block's style object comes to, as the reference's style engine
reads it (probe style-engine): the declarations each style property
makes and the class names a preset or a set colour earns.

- Groups in the order background, colour, border, shadow, dimensions,
spacing, typography, and properties in their order within a group.
- A value goes into the declarations as given. Whether it makes CSS is
for the declarations holder to judge.
- A preset ("var:preset|color|base") becomes a custom property only
where the definition names one for its kind (a colour, a gradient,
spacing, a font size or family, a shadow, a dimension, a border radius,
a border side's colour). Elsewhere it makes nothing, and with presets
turned into class names it makes none anywhere.
- Sides and corners ("padding" => ["top" => ...]) name their own
properties in the order given. Border sides come after the whole
border.

methods.name: kebab
methods.doc:
A name in kebab case, as the reference cuts a style property, a preset
slug and the class made from it ("lineHeight" line-height, "h1" h-1,
"XMLHttpRequest" xml-http-request, "1st Place" 1st-place, "ÜberCool"
Über-cool: probe media, kebab cases). Words follow lodash's kebabCase:
a capital starts one, a run of capitals is one, digits are one apart
from letters unless they make an ordinal. Unlike lodash, a straight
apostrophe is dropped and a curly one separates, a symbol outside
Latin-1's punctuation (×, an emoji, a CJK letter) joins the word it
touches, and only ASCII letters are lower-cased.

property the definition names for its kind, and is dropped when there
is none; with no custom properties to use (presets as class names, or

classes.name: Minn\Cli\Bundled
classes.doc:
WP-CLI's own bundled command for a verb the engine answers. Its docs give
an engine verb the same synopsis (the arguments, defaults and allowed
values the running WP-CLI accepts, which change between releases), and a
call the engine does not answer itself is handed back to it, run against
the engine's WordPress runtime as any bundled command is.

methods.name: docs
methods.doc:
The bundled method's description and synopsis, as WP-CLI reads them
from its doc comment, for add_command's arguments; empty when this
WP-CLI has no such command.

methods.name: loadable
methods.doc:
Whether WP-CLI can load this site, as it checks before loading one: the
core version file readable under ABSPATH and a wp-config.php found. A
Minn site carries both (its placeholder files); a bare webroot does not.

methods.name: run
methods.doc:
Runs the bundled command for a call: WP-CLI loads the site (the engine
stands in for WordPress, plugins loaded), then the bundled method
answers with the arguments the shared synopsis already validated.

classes.name: Minn\Cli\CacheCommand
classes.doc: `wp cache flush`: the engine has no object cache, so this is a no-op success.

methods.name: flush
methods.doc:
Flushes the object cache.

The engine does not run an object cache. The verb still succeeds so
fleet scripts that call it after a write do not abort.

classes.name: Minn\Cli\Commands
classes.doc:
The verbs the engine answers to. Every one is registered for the
before_wp_load phase, which WP-CLI runs before it looks for WordPress,
and each replaces the bundled subcommand of the same name (a deferred
addition lands after the bundle and overrides its leaf).

methods.name: register
methods.doc: Registers every engine verb with WP-CLI in the phase it runs in.

methods.name: leaf
methods.signature: leaf(string $name, callable|array $callable, array $args, array $bundled = array ( )): void
methods.doc:
Registers a leaf and re-adds it after the parent lands. WP-CLI
registers `plugin` as a namespace first; its later class command
would otherwise overwrite our list. With a bundled class and method,
the re-added leaf takes that method's docs: WP-CLI loads its bundled
commands' classes only after the engine registers, by the time the
parent lands.

methods.name: runner
methods.doc:
What a leaf runs: the engine's method, or, for a verb named with
WP-CLI's own command, that command whenever WP-CLI can load the site.

methods.name: replace
methods.doc:
A root command the bundle also registers. Re-add after the bundle
without recursing into our own after_add_command hook.

classes.name: Minn\Cli\CoreCommand
classes.doc:
WP-CLI's core verbs where a host's automation meets a Minn site. A Minn
site has none of WordPress's core files, so a WordPress core update
neither applies nor may pretend to: `core update` says the site is up to
date (Minn reports the latest release it speaks) and refuses outright
when asked for a version or a package, and `core download` is held back
over a Minn install, since it would put WordPress's files over the
engine. `core verify-checksums` checks the engine's own files against
its signed release. Minn's own updater is `wp minn update`.

constants.name: REFUSAL
constants.value: 'This site runs Minn Engine, which keeps WordPress\'s API but none of its core files, so a WordPress core update does not apply. Update Minn instead: wp minn update.'

Says whether WordPress core is up to date; on Minn it always is, and an asked-for version or package is refused.

classes.name: Minn\Cli\Installer
classes.doc:
The swap, both ways. Install parks WordPress's own files beside the
webroot, lays the engine and its shape files down, and leaves
wp-config.php and wp-content untouched; eject puts every parked file
back and removes what install wrote. The install record at the webroot
(.minn-install.php) is what eject works from. Preflight says what the site will and
will not get before anything moves.

constants.name: RECORD
constants.doc:
The install record sits at the webroot, so every site keeps its own
(a symlinked minn/ is shared between sites) and an engine update
cannot take it. It is PHP that returns first, so a web request for it
prints nothing, and it names the webroot it belongs to.

constants.name: PARK_MARK
constants.doc: The mark install leaves in the park, naming the webroot parked there; eject takes no park without it.

constants.name: PARK_GUARD
constants.doc: Apache's refusal for the whole park, for a host whose park still sits under a served folder (nginx ignores it).

constants.name: PARK_GUARD_TEXT
constants.value: '# Minn: WordPress\'s own files, parked by the engine. Nothing here is served. <IfModule mod_authz_core.c> 	Require all denied </IfModule> <IfModule !mod_authz_core.c> 	Deny from all </IfModule> '

constants.name: SERVED_FILES
constants.doc: What marks a folder as a site's own webroot, and the names hosts give one.

constants.name: SERVED_NAMES
constants.doc: Names only a served folder carries, on the webroot's parent or any folder above it.

constants.name: INDEXED_NAMES
constants.doc:
Names that are a served folder only when it holds an index of its own (nginx's /var/www/html and its default
page); without one they are a project's or a panel's folder (HestiaCP's ~/web, DevKinsta's ~/DevKinsta/public).

constants.name: RECORD_HEAD
constants.value: '<?php return; // Minn Engine\'s install record: what `wp minn eject` puts back. ?> '

constants.name: LEGACY_RECORD
constants.doc: Where installs kept it before: read from a site's own minn/ copy, never through a shared symlink.

constants.name: CORE_ENTRIES
constants.doc: The files WordPress keeps at the webroot, moved aside as a set.

constants.name: WRITTEN_TREES
constants.doc: Webroot trees install writes (shape files + require placeholders) and eject deletes before restoring the park.

constants.name: LEGACY_PUBLISHED
constants.doc:
Leftover webroot copies from an earlier installer that published
assets outside minn/. Eject still deletes them.

constants.name: SKIP
constants.doc: Development-only trees inside the engine or the admin bundle that never ship.

constants.name: OPTIONS
constants.value: array (   'preflight' =>    array (   ),   'install' =>    array (     0 => 'park',     1 => 'force',   ),   'eject' =>    array (     0 => 'park',   ),   'status' =>    array (   ),   'update' =>    array (     0 => 'check',   ),   'login' =>    array (     0 => 'to',     1 => 'format',   ), )
constants.doc: The options each command reads; any other option refuses the command before it does anything.

methods.name: main
methods.doc:
The bin entry: runs one command against a webroot, prints its report
and returns the exit code.

methods.name: run
methods.doc:
Runs one command against a webroot and hands back its exit code and
report, printing nothing: how Minn Admin switches a WordPress site
from a web request, where there is no STDOUT.

methods.name: preflight
methods.doc: What the site will and will not get; the worst light decides install. The report lands in the output.

methods.name: login
methods.doc:
A one-time sign-in link (LoginLink), for the user named after the
webroot or the first administrator.

methods.name: update
methods.doc: Replaces this engine with the latest release from the Minn update service; --check only says whether there is one.

methods.name: status
methods.doc: Prints what the webroot is running.

methods.name: install
methods.doc: Installs the engine into a webroot when the preflight allows it.

methods.name: guardPark
methods.doc:
Guards a park an earlier engine left without it: the Apache refusal
written when the install record names a park carrying this webroot's
mark and holding none. Run once per engine version (AdminPlugin::settle),
so a site installed by 0.1.0 is guarded by its first request after an
update (fix-delta review of the 2026-11-12 sweep).

methods.name: parkStatus
methods.doc:
What the System view says of this webroot's park: none on record; not
checked (beyond open_basedir, or its mark not this webroot's as PHP
sees it here); in a folder that looks served; without its refusal; or
fine. A pass only when the park was read.

methods.name: eject
methods.doc:
Puts WordPress back and removes the engine's files. The park is the
one the install record names only when it carries the mark install
left there for this webroot: the record is a file in the webroot, so
anything able to write there could otherwise point an eject at any
folder the operator can read. --park=<dir> names it outright.

methods.name: state
methods.doc: What a webroot is running: minn, wordpress, or unknown.

methods.name: record
methods.doc:
The install record for a webroot: its owner, when, the engine
version, the park, what moved, what was laid down. Empty when there
is none, or when the one found names another webroot (a site that
was moved or copied keeps a record its own eject must not act on).

methods.name: served
methods.doc:
Why a folder looks served, or null: it holds a file only a webroot
holds, or it or a folder above it carries a host's webroot name
(public_html/sites/ is served under public_html's address).

methods.name: recordedPark
methods.doc: The park the install record names, when PHP may reach it and it is there carrying this webroot's mark.

methods.name: inside
methods.doc:
Whether a path from the install record stays inside the webroot (or
the park): relative, with no climbing segment and no NUL. The record
is a file in the webroot, so anything able to write there could
otherwise point an eject's removals anywhere the operator can write.

methods.name: move
methods.doc: rename() first; copy+remove when the park is on another filesystem, a link copied as the link it is.

classes.name: Minn\Cli\LoginLink
classes.doc:
`minn login <webroot> [<user>]`: the one-time sign-in link, minted by the
engine alone. wp-config.php is read as text, never run, so neither
WP-CLI, the WordPress runtime nor the site's plugins take part, and the
link works whatever MINN_WP_API says. With no user named it signs in the
first administrator by login. The link opens the engine's own sign-in
page (`wp user login` keeps wp-login.php, the address hosting tools
expect); --to lands somewhere other than the admin.

methods.name: run
methods.doc:
Mints a link for a webroot and hands back the exit code and what to
print: the address alone, or with --format=json the address, the user,
their roles and when the link expires.

methods.name: address
methods.doc: A path's address on the site, on WP_HOME when wp-config.php names it.

methods.name: firstAdministrator
methods.doc: The first user by login holding the administrator role, as `wp user list --role=administrator` lists them.

classes.name: Minn\Content\Autop
classes.doc:
Classic-content paragraphing (wpautop): blank lines become paragraphs, single newlines become line breaks when asked, and block-level tags are never wrapped. Rebuilt against the reference's output on a corpus of fuzzed and real content plus targeted experiments (probe autop); every rule below is one that corpus demanded, written as the behaviour seen, in the order it applies: - 
 elements are cut out first and put back untouched at the end.
- A pair of 
 tags is a paragraph break; block tags get blank lines
around them, so they always sit outside paragraphs.
- Newlines inside a tag, comment or CDATA section (an unclosed one runs
to the end) are held aside, so they never split a paragraph and come
back as plain newlines. While held, such a newline ends the tag as far
as the block rules can tell.
- Whitespace around object, param, embed, audio, video, source, track,
figcaption and option tags is squeezed out when those tags are used.
- Blank-line separated runs become 
 paragraphs, then paragraphs that
only hold a block tag lose their 
 and 
.
- With line breaks on, remaining newlines become 
, except inside
script, style, svg and math elements, and breaks next to block tags go.

classes.name: Minn\Content\PostSlugs
classes.doc:
Which slug a live post may take beside the others, as the reference
settles it (probe insert-defaults). A flat type's slugs are its own: a
post, a page and a plugin's type may share one. A hierarchical type's
are its own and its attachments' under the same parent. An attachment's
are every post's. Never free: the feed names and embed; for a
hierarchical type, a number or a page number (2, page2); for posts, a
number a date archive would answer to: any number when the permalink
structure begins with the post name, a month (below 13) when the post
name follows the year, a day (below 32) when it follows the month. A post
keeps a number it already has. A taken slug gets the first free -2, -3
form, cut (and stripped of a trailing hyphen) to fit the column's 200
characters. The slug is taken as given, not sanitized.

link whatever the post's status (a draft or trashed post goes to
its `?p=` form).

Walks a page hierarchy: ["sample-page", "docs"] finds the page named

The post at a slug path among the given types (each segment's parent
the one before it), in any status but trash; at the last segment the
first type wins over the others, as the reference prefers the type it
was asked for over the attachment it also looks at.

The published post whose name starts with the given text, among the
given types, as the reference guesses a destination for a missing
URL: one prefix query and no order of its own, so the database's
plan for it decides which match comes first (on a small table its

Published posts of a type for a post-by-post archive, by date or by

classes.name: Minn\Content\Reader

Who is reading this request: their user id, whether they may read
private content, whether they may edit a given post, and the
post-password cookie they carry. Built once per surface by the engine,
carried by the request's context, and consulted by the resolver, the
queries, and the renderers.

constructor.signature: __construct(int $userId, bool $readsPrivatePosts, bool $readsPrivatePages, Closure $canEditPost, string $postPassword, string $sessionToken = '', array $roles = array ( ))

methods.name: anonymous
methods.doc: The reader who is nobody: no session, no private posts, only the post password they typed.

methods.doc:
The reader a signed-in user is, asked of the capability engine: what
they may read privately, what they may edit, and the roles they hold.
User 0 is nobody, whatever the capabilities say.

methods.name: current
methods.doc:
The reader of the request being answered. The runtime holds it (the
context it was built with carries it), so there is one holder and a
request cannot see the reader of the one before it. Without a
runtime, on the command line and in unit tests, nobody is reading.

methods.doc: Whether the reader has a session.

methods.name: canEdit
methods.doc: Whether this reader may edit a given post.

methods.doc: The revisions, or the autosaves, of a post, newest first, as rows.

methods.doc: Every revision of a post, its autosaves among them, newest first by date then id, as rows: what the revisions route lists (probe rest-latest-revision).

methods.name: autosavesOf
methods.doc: The autosaves of a post, newest first, as rows.

classes.name: Minn\Content\RowCache
classes.doc:
Rows read once a request: posts, their terms, users, and every object's
meta, as the reference keeps them in its object cache, so a loop or a
REST list does not read the same row once per use. A write to a table
drops everything kept from it (Db::wrote, through the engine's own door
or the facade's wpdb), as does a rolled-back transaction, so a read after
a write finds the row as it now is. Nothing outlives the request.

constants.name: SOURCES
constants.value: array (   'posts' =>    array (     0 => 'posts',   ),   'post_terms' =>    array (     0 => 'term_relationships',     1 => 'term_taxonomy',     2 => 'terms',   ),   'revisions' =>    array (     0 => 'posts',   ),   'theme_templates' =>    array (     0 => 'posts',     1 => 'term_relationships',     2 => 'term_taxonomy',     3 => 'terms',   ),   'users' =>    array (     0 => 'users',   ),   'comments' =>    array (     0 => 'comments',   ),   'comment_queries' =>    array (     0 => 'comments',     1 => 'commentmeta',   ),   'term_rows' =>    array (     0 => 'terms',     1 => 'term_taxonomy',   ),   'term_queries' =>    array (     0 => 'terms',     1 => 'term_taxonomy',     2 => 'term_relationships',     3 => 'termmeta',   ),   'term_lookups' =>    array (     0 => 'terms',     1 => 'term_taxonomy',   ),   'post_meta' =>    array (     0 => 'postmeta',   ),   'user_meta' =>    array (     0 => 'usermeta',   ),   'term_meta' =>    array (     0 => 'termmeta',   ),   'comment_meta' =>    array (     0 => 'commentmeta',   ), )

methods.name: remember

methods.name: put

Has a kind named at run time (a plugin's meta type, whose table only
the registration knows) dropped whenever that table is written, as
the kinds above are by theirs.

methods.name: forget

methods.name: flush
methods.doc: Drops everything kept.

classes.name: Minn\Content\Site
classes.doc: Site-wide options and the site's clock.

methods.name: option
methods.doc: One option's raw value, or null when it is unset.

methods.name: setOption
methods.doc:
Writes an option, inserting it as autoloaded when it does not exist;
the option store hears of it. An $autoload given is written too, so a
cache the engine reads on demand (autoload "off") stays out of the
list every request loads.

methods.name: deleteOption
methods.doc: Removes an option row; the option store hears of it.

methods.name: defaultDiscussion
methods.doc:
A new post's comment or ping status, as the reference picks it: a post
follows the site's two defaults, an attachment follows the comment
default and never takes pings, a page and every other type start
closed; with plugins loaded, get_default_comment_status() decides
(support a plugin removed, the filter). $kind is "comment" or
"pingback".

methods.name: timezone
methods.doc:
The site's timezone (wp_timezone): the zone timezone_string names, else
gmt_offset as a fixed offset. With a zone set, the stored gmt_offset is
not read at all, as the reference does not read it.

methods.name: gmtOffset
methods.doc: The site's offset from UTC in seconds now: the zone's, daylight saving included, or gmt_offset's.

methods.name: localNow
methods.doc: Now in the site's local time, MySQL format.

methods.doc:
A site-local datetime from a write body ("2031-01-01T00:00:00") to
the pair of columns it fills, plus its timestamp.
shapes: @return array{0: string, 1: string, 2: int} local, gmt, timestamp

methods.doc:
A GMT datetime from a write body (date_gmt) to the same pair of
columns, its local half in the site's zone at that date.
shapes: @return array{0: string, 1: string, 2: int} local, gmt, timestamp

classes.name: Minn\Content\SiteIcon
classes.doc:
The site icon: the attachment the site_icon option names, as the file
under uploads it points at. Read by the favicon route, the head links,
and the admin app's sidebar.

methods.name: file
methods.doc: The icon's path under uploads, or null when the site has none.

methods.name: urlAt
methods.doc:
The URL of the icon's smallest generated size that covers a square of
$size pixels, or of the original when no size does; empty without an icon.

methods.name: url
methods.doc: The icon's URL, empty when the site has none.

methods.name: links
methods.doc: The head links a site with an icon prints (wp_site_icon): the 32 and 192 pixel icons, the Apple touch icon, and the tile image; empty without one.

methods.name: sanitize
methods.doc:
A title as the reference's sanitize_title makes a slug of it when
saving, without the filters (the runtime's sanitize_title adds those):
accents spelled plainly, then the dash form, non-ASCII percent-encoded
up to 200 bytes.

methods.name: uriEncode
methods.doc:
Non-ASCII characters as lower-case percent escapes, a whole character
at a time, stopping before one would take the text past $length bytes
(0 for no limit); each ASCII character goes through $ascii (as it is,
or rawurlencode).

methods.name: truncate
methods.doc:
A slug cut to a byte length without splitting a multibyte character or
leaving a dash hanging off the end.

methods.name: dashes
methods.doc: The reference's dash form of a title: tags and marks stripped, spaces to dashes, and the save-time rules when saving.

classes.name: Minn\Content\TagBalancer
classes.doc:
Closes what markup leaves open and drops what it closes without opening, as the reference's force_balance_tags does, from its observed rules (contracts/runtime.md "The content filters"): tag names are lowercased; a void element is written self-closed (bare as
, with attributes as , one already self-closed as given); reopening the innermost open element closes it first unless it is one of the ten that may contain themselves; a closer shuts every element opened inside its own; a closer with nothing to close goes; what is still open at the end closes in reverse. Script and style text is left as it is, and a "<" not followed by a name is text.

methods.name: balance
methods.doc: The markup with every element closed in order and every stray closer gone.

methods.name: close
methods.doc: A closer: every element opened inside the named one closes with it; with nothing to close it is dropped. @param list<string> $stack

methods.name: voidAttributes
methods.doc: A void element's attributes, written self-closed.

methods.name: rawText
methods.doc: Script or style text up to the element's own closer, which stays for the main loop. @return array{0: string, 1: int}

classes.name: Minn\Content\TermLinks
classes.doc:
A post's terms rendered as links, in the two shapes the reference
emits: a plain joined run for a taxonomy, and the category list, which
becomes a `post-categories` unordered list when the caller names no
separator and a joined run when it does.

Names arrive already filtered; the caller applies the reference's own
filters around the result.

methods.name: joined
methods.doc: Anchor tags for these terms joined by a separator, the way the reference prints a term list.

methods.name: categories
methods.doc:
The category list: an unordered list when the separator is empty,
a joined run otherwise. Both carry the rel given ("category tag" under
pretty permalinks, "category" under plain ones). A row may bring
markup to go before its link (its parents) and the space before rel.
shapes: @param list<array{name: string, url: string, before?: string, space?: string}> $categories

params.name: categories
params.shape: list<array{name: string, url: string, before?: string, space?: string}>

The reference keeps "{taxonomy}_children" (each parent's child term
ids, by id) for a hierarchical taxonomy and rewrites it on every term
change; one left stale hides new children from WordPress after a

classes.name: Minn\Content\TextFilters
classes.doc:
The small text filters the reference runs over content, titles and
comments, each from its observed rules (contracts/runtime.md "The content
filters", "The comment form"): smilies, the capital P, insecure home
addresses, the feed's embed clean-up, and a comment's links and spans.

methods.name: smiliesSearch
methods.doc:
The search pattern smilies_init leaves in $wp_smiliessearch, from the
codes in their stored order (reverse-sorted): one alternative per first
character, its code's rest quoted and joined, each bounded by
whitespace, a no-break space or the line's ends (probe functions-utils).

methods.name: smilies
methods.doc:
Text with $run applied to each stretch outside a tag and outside a
code, pre, script, style or textarea element, as convert_smilies
runs the smilies search over it.

methods.name: capitalP
methods.doc: "Wordpress" spelled right after a space, a parenthesis, a tag, or an opening curly quote; elsewhere it stays.

methods.name: capitalPEverywhere
methods.doc: "Wordpress" spelled right everywhere, as a title is.

methods.name: secureHome
methods.doc: The site's own http address made https, escaped forms included.

methods.name: feedEmbeds
methods.doc: A feed carries an embedded post's iframe without the style that hides it until its script runs.

methods.name: rel
methods.doc:
Every link given a rel (wp_rel_nofollow, wp_rel_ugc), on slashed text
as the content filters carry it, slashed again after (probes
comment-fields, plugin-queue5). A link to the site itself does not
take "nofollow".
shapes: @param Closure(string $href): bool $internal whether an href points at the site itself

methods.doc:
One link's opening tag with the rel added (wp_rel_callback): a tag
that has a rel keeps its words first, gains the new ones, and is
written again with every attribute double-quoted and rel last; one
without keeps its attributes as written and takes rel at the end.

methods.name: noteMentionClasses
methods.doc: A span keeps no class in a comment (where a note's mention would be faked); slashed text in, slashed out.

methods.name: ignoring
methods.doc: The element whose text is left alone after a tag: one of the ignored elements opening, or the one still open.

methods.doc: A tag's attributes in order, name => value (quotes removed; a bare name has null). @return array<string, ?string>

classes.name: Minn\Content\Texturize
classes.doc:
The texturize subset the reference applies to rendered text: straight
quotes, apostrophes, ellipses, dashes, and primes become numeric
entities, outside the skip elements only. Coverage is pinned by the
texturize battery post; anything beyond it is a documented gap.

properties.name: run
properties.doc: Whether text is texturized at all (run_wptexturize), once asked; null until then.

methods.name: enabled
methods.doc:
Whether text is texturized at all (run_wptexturize): asked on the first
text of a request and again after askAgain(); once the answer is no, it
holds for the rest of the request (probe filter-inputs-3).

methods.name: askAgain
methods.doc: Has the next text ask run_wptexturize again (wptexturize's reset), unless the answer was already no.

methods.name: characters
methods.doc:
The characters texturizing writes, as the site's language writes them
(each asked by its translation context, as the reference asks them):
the dashes, the curly quotes, the apostrophe and the primes.
shapes: @return array{en: string, em: string, open1: string, close1: string, apostrophe: string, open2: string, close2: string, prime: string, prime2: string}

methods.name: skipPattern
methods.doc:
The elements whose text stays as written (no_texturize_tags: pre, code,
kbd, style, script and tt), read on every text, as a pattern alternation.

methods.name: html
methods.doc:
Curly quotes, dashes, and ellipses in the text of HTML, leaving tags
and the skipped elements alone; registered shortcodes stay as written
(probe shortcode-run), and so does the text inside the ones
no_texturize_shortcodes names ([code] by default). Nothing changes once
texturizing is off. A caller that already read the skip pattern hands
it over, so each text asks the filters once.

methods.name: entities
methods.doc: Bare ampersands made entities outside the skipped elements, as wptexturize leaves them after the rest.

methods.name: apply
methods.doc:
Text with its quotes, dashes and ellipses made typographic
(wptexturize), its tags and the elements and shortcodes that keep
their text skipped; empty text, or any while texturizing is off, as
given. Asked to reset, the switches are asked again.

methods.name: text
methods.doc: The same substitutions on a plain string with no tags.

methods.name: splitPattern
methods.doc:
The pattern that cuts markup for texturizing (wp_html_split's pieces
with comments whole and, given, shortcodes): comments run to "-->" or
the end, a tag to its first ">", and each piece is captured.

methods.name: shortcodeTags
methods.doc:
The pattern fragment for shortcodes with these names: an opening or
closing tag, or an escaped [[one]], its name ended by a space, "/" or
"]", its attributes up to the first "]".

methods.name: pushPop
methods.doc:
Keeps the stack of open elements texturize leaves alone: an opening
tag or shortcode of a listed name is pushed (a self-closing one is
not), its closing one pops it when it is the last opened.

methods.name: primes
methods.doc:
Each $needle in the text made a prime after a digit; otherwise a
double quote becomes the closing quote, and a single one does only
where a word ends (before the end, whitespace, a no-break space or
. , ; : ! ? ) ] } -), staying an apostrophe or opening quote elsewhere.

methods.name: shortcodePattern
methods.doc: The pattern for the registered shortcodes the text opens a bracket with, or "" for none.

methods.name: quiet
methods.doc:
Keeps count of the quiet shortcodes open around the text: an opening
one is pushed, its closing one pops it, others pass.

methods.name: endsWord
methods.doc: Whether what follows a single quote ends a word: nothing, whitespace, a no-break space, or . , ; : ! ? ) ] } -.
