nicename?: string,
nickname?: string,
first_name?: string,
last_name?: string,
description?: string,
locale?: string,
} $fields

methods.name: defaultDisplayName
methods.doc:
The display name an account gets when none is given, as the reference
picks it: first and last name, whichever of the two there is, or the
login. The nickname plays no part.

methods.name: insertAccount
methods.doc: A new account's row alone: the caller adds its meta and role, and keeps the count. @param array<string, mixed> $fields

methods.name: profileMeta
methods.doc:
The twelve profile meta rows the reference gives a new account, in its
order (the role's two follow).

methods.name: recount
methods.doc: Recounts the accounts into user_count, quietly.

methods.name: deleteRow
methods.doc: Removes the account's row alone: the caller removes its meta and keeps the count.

methods.name: insert
methods.doc: Inserts a users row from column => value pairs and returns the new id.

methods.name: update
methods.doc:
Sets the given columns on one user, in one write as the reference
makes it (tests/tools/side-effects.php).

methods.name: delete
methods.doc: Removes the user and their meta; their posts are reassigned or removed first by the caller.

methods.name: ids
methods.doc: User ids in login order, optionally the first N. @return list<int>

methods.name: setPassword
methods.doc: Stores a new password hash and clears any pending reset key.

methods.name: clearResetKey
methods.doc:
A pending password reset dropped: a good sign-in (wp_signon, the
sign-in page) ends it, so a link mailed earlier no longer opens the
reset form (probe sweep-1020b, login suite).

methods.name: count
methods.doc: How many users the site has.

methods.name: registeredAfter
methods.doc: The newest users registered since a site-local time, up to the limit.
shapes: @return list<array> the newest registrations after a site-local timestamp

methods.name: idsWithMeta
methods.doc:
The users holding a usermeta key, in id order: the owner of a key named
for something only one user has (a passkey's credential).

methods.name: metaWithPrefix
methods.doc:
A user's usermeta values whose keys start with a prefix, raw, by key in
row order (one row per key; a later row for the same key wins).

methods.name: deleteMeta
methods.doc: Removes one meta key from a user: through the meta API once the runtime is up (delete_user_meta's hooks), else directly.

methods.name: withCapabilities
methods.doc:
Every user with a capabilities row under the key given, as the old
get_users_of_blog listed them: id twice, login, display name, email
and the stored capabilities, in id order.

methods.name: withoutRole
methods.doc: The ids of users whose capabilities row names none of the roles (a pattern of their names). @return list<string>

methods.name: meta
methods.doc:
One usermeta value, raw: serialized blobs come back serialized. Once the
runtime is up it is read as get_user_meta reads it, through its filter
and the cache (probe user-meta-writes); before it, from the table.

methods.name: setMeta
methods.doc:
Replaces one usermeta row. The (user_id, meta_key) pair carries no
unique index on the stock schema, so this is a delete plus insert
rather than an upsert. The value is the stored form: a string that
reads as serialized is revived on the way through the meta API, so a
caller with text from outside passes it through Options::toStorage.

methods.name: refreshCount
methods.doc:
The user_count option, which the reference keeps current as accounts
come and go. A site without the row is left without it.

methods.name: writeAccount
methods.doc:
The account's row and the fourteen meta rows the reference gives a new
user, written as one unit by createAccount().

classes.name: Minn\Context
classes.doc:
One request, as a value: the database door, who is asking, what they
may do, and where the site's files are. It is built once at the front
door and handed down, so nothing below has to reach for a global to
learn what request it is answering.

The reader is the one part that differs by surface (REST resolves it
from the nonce-bound caller, the front from the session cookie), so a
context is made with the reader its surface resolved.

constructor.signature: __construct(Minn\Db $db, Minn\Content\Site $site, ?Minn\Http\Request $request, Minn\Content\Reader $reader, Minn\Auth\Capabilities $capabilities, string $engineDir, string $absPath, string $version)

properties.name: engineDir
properties.doc: the minn/ folder: the engine's own files

properties.name: absPath
properties.doc: the site root with a trailing slash, as ABSPATH holds it

properties.name: version
properties.doc: the WordPress release whose contracts the runtime speaks

methods.name: withReader
methods.doc: The same context with another reader, for a surface that resolves one later.

methods.name: contentDir
methods.doc: wp-content under the site root.

methods.name: themesDir
methods.doc: The themes folder under wp-content.

methods.name: isSecure
methods.doc: Whether the request is over HTTPS.

classes.name: Minn\Cron\Cron
classes.doc:
The engine's scheduled work: scheduled posts go live when their time
comes, the cron option's due events fire, expired throttle rows and
transients are swept, and once every 24 hours the update service is
asked about Minn, plugins and themes before automatic updates run. Triggered
by wp-cron.php, `wp minn cron`, `minn cron`, or a front request that
finds something due (after its response is sent). One run at a time,
through a short-lived lock option.

Firing the cron option's due hooks needs the booted runtime and the
facade, so it arrives as a closure the caller supplies (from the front
pipeline, or the CLI once it has booted the runtime); with none, only
the engine's own scheduled posts and sweeps run.

shapes: @param ?Closure(): int $fireDueEvents fires the cron option's due hooks and returns how many ran

params.name: fireDueEvents
params.doc: fires the cron option's due hooks and returns how many ran

constants.name: DAILY
constants.doc: When the next daily update pass is due (a timestamp); the slots stay 24 hours apart however late a run is.

methods.name: create
methods.doc:
The one recipe every trigger builds from: the post writer, the
updater over the site's wp-content, and the runtime's firing closure.

methods.name: run
methods.doc: Runs every due job; the report lists what happened. @return list<string>

methods.name: idle
methods.doc:
True when a hit has nothing to do: no job is due and the housekeeping
(expired transients and throttle rows) ran within the last minute, so
a request repeated as fast as a visitor can send it costs two reads.

methods.name: due
methods.doc: True when a scheduled post's time has come, the cron option holds a due event, or the daily update pass is due.

methods.name: nextSlot
methods.doc:
The slot after a daily pass that ran at `$now` for `$slot`: 24 hours on
from the first run, then whole days on from the slot, the first one
still ahead (a site that slept a week checks once, not seven times).

methods.name: fireEvents
methods.doc:
Fires the due events through the runtime. A callback that throws
ends the events step, as a fatal ends the reference's cron request;
the event was already rescheduled or removed, so it does not repeat
on the next trigger, and the sweeps still run.

methods.name: dailySlot
methods.doc: When the daily update pass is next due; 0 on a site that has never run one.

methods.name: daily
methods.doc:
The daily update pass, once every 24 hours: the update service asked
about Minn's releases and about the site's plugins and themes, each
marked as the day's scheduled check (the service counts those, one a
site, and keeps nothing else), then the automatic updates. The next
slot is written first, 24 hours after this one and never in the past,
so a failure waits for tomorrow instead of repeating on every trigger,
and a late run does not push the next one later. What was refused is
reported by name.

methods.name: publishDue
methods.doc:
A scheduled post goes live as the reference publishes it: status only,
dates and modified untouched, term counts refreshed. With plugins
loaded it goes through check_and_publish_future_post, the reference's
own publish_future_post work, so they hear publish_post and the
transition; a plugin that throws on one post holds back no other.

classes.name: Minn\Db
classes.doc:
The one door to the database. Every query is a prepared statement; the
placeholder types are derived from the PHP values, so callers pass plain
arrays and never spell out "issd". A parameter that is a list stands for
a list of values: its "?" becomes as many placeholders as the list is
long, so "post_type IN (?)" takes the types themselves.

constants.name: INCOMPATIBLE_MODES
constants.doc: The SQL modes WordPress turns off for its session (wpdb's incompatible modes): strictness and the modes that change what queries mean.

properties.name: inTransaction
properties.doc: Whether a transaction this door opened is still open, so a nested call joins it instead of starting another.

properties.name: refused
properties.doc: Whether the last write was refused for its text (execute).

methods.name: columnLength
methods.doc:
The most a column of a MySQL type holds, as wpdb::get_col_length
answers: characters for char and varchar, bytes for the binary, blob
and text types; false for any other type.

methods.name: current
methods.doc:
The connection the request being answered speaks through: its
runtime's own, so nothing deep in a render can reach a connection
belonging to another request. With no runtime (the command line, the
unit suite) it is the process's own connection.

This is the one place in the core that asks the runtime anything; the
alternative is a database door threaded through every renderer, and
the seam is here until that threading is done.

methods.name: shared
methods.doc:
The one connection for this process, opened from wp-config's constants
on first use, its session without the incompatible modes, as
WordPress's own connection is (a plugin's insert that leaves out a text
column then succeeds, as it does there).

methods.name: sessionModes
methods.doc:
The session's modes: the server's, less the reference's incompatible
ones and NO_BACKSLASH_ESCAPES, which the engine's own literal escaping
(Query\Sql) relies on being off. Plugins see only the reference's list
(incompatible_sql_modes).

methods.name: compatibleModes
methods.doc: A comma-separated SQL mode list without the incompatible ones (any case).

methods.name: setModes
methods.doc:
Sets this session's SQL modes, never NO_BACKSLASH_ESCAPES: the
engine's literals escape quotes with a backslash (Query\Sql), which
that mode would turn into a plain character, so a set_sql_mode()
asking for it gets every other mode it named.

methods.name: connection
methods.doc: The underlying mysqli handle, for the facade's wpdb.

methods.name: escape
methods.doc: A value escaped for direct interpolation into SQL, for callers that build their own statements.

methods.name: prefix
methods.doc: The table prefix from wp-config.

methods.name: table
methods.doc: `posts` becomes `wp_posts`; the prefix comes from wp-config.php.

methods.name: rows
methods.doc: Every row of a prepared query, as associative arrays.

methods.name: row
methods.doc: The first row of a prepared query, or null.

methods.name: value
methods.doc: The first column of the first row, or null when there is no row.

methods.name: execute
methods.doc: Runs a write and returns the affected row count.

methods.name: invalidText
methods.doc:
Whether a statement carries text the site's utf8mb4 tables cannot
hold (bytes that are not UTF-8): the reference's database door runs
no such query, a write among them (probe sanitize-option; the
side-effect diff, rest-embed-details).

methods.name: fieldRefusal
methods.doc: The database error the reference's door gives for a field whose value it would not write.

methods.name: invalidColumn
methods.doc:
The first of the given columns whose text the database door refuses
(invalidText), or null.

methods.name: onWrite
methods.doc: Asks to be told whenever a write statement names a table (Content\RowCache drops what it kept from it).

methods.name: wrote
methods.doc:
Tells the listeners of every table a write statement names, whichever
door ran it (this one, or the facade's wpdb for plugin code). A name
that merely contains another (wp_postmeta for posts) is not it.

methods.name: expand
methods.doc:
Rewrites every "?" whose parameter is a list into that many
placeholders, and flattens the values to match, so "IN (?)" becomes
"IN (?, ?, ?)". An empty list becomes NULL, which nothing is IN, so a
caller that means "everything" when the list is empty says so itself.

methods.name: transaction
methods.doc:
Runs a unit of work as one transaction: everything the closure writes
lands, or none of it does. The closure's return value is passed back.

A transaction already open is joined rather than nested, since the
storage engine has no nested transactions; the outermost call is the
one that commits. A table that cannot do transactions (MyISAM, which
no WordPress core table uses) silently keeps each write, which is the
behaviour there was before this existed.

methods.name: insertId
methods.doc: The id the last INSERT produced.

methods.name: refused
methods.doc: Whether the last write was refused for its text (invalidText): nothing was sent.

methods.name: option
methods.doc:
One option's stored value, or null when it is unset; home and siteurl
answer to WP_HOME and WP_SITEURL. Once the runtime boots, the read is
its option store's (the autoloaded list, wp_cache's options group),
so the engine's own reads cost no query each, as get_option()'s don't.

methods.name: readOptionsThrough
methods.doc: Where option reads come from from now on: the runtime's option store, or null for the row itself.

methods.name: configured
methods.doc:
What wp-config.php sets for an option, or null: WP_HOME and WP_SITEURL,
when defined, stand for home and siteurl on every read, as on the
reference (_config_wp_home), without a trailing slash.

methods.name: storedOption
methods.doc: One option's row as stored, whatever wp-config.php says, or null when it is unset.

methods.name: placeholders
methods.doc:
The statement split into placeholders and everything between them. A
"?" inside a quoted string is text, not a placeholder.

classes.name: Minn\Engine
classes.doc:
The engine's front door. An unmodified wp-config.php ends by requiring
wp-settings.php, which is the engine's own boot file; it hands off here.
REST is dispatched first (from the path or from ?rest_route=), then the
admin, the login endpoint, and finally the public site.

constants.name: WP_VERSION
constants.doc: The WordPress release whose contracts the runtime speaks; wp-includes/version.php says the same.

constants.name: SCRIPTS_WITHOUT_REST
constants.doc: The reference's entry scripts that never run the main query, so never answer ?rest_route=.

constants.name: FRONT_ROUTES
constants.doc: The engine's routes a public page meets ahead of the extensions' own, in the front pipeline's order.

properties.name: engineDir
properties.doc: the minn/ folder: the engine's own files (assets, data, the admin bundle)

methods.name: serve
methods.doc:
The front door: answer the request that arrived and send it. This is
the only place the engine touches the world, so everything under it
is a function of a request, callable more than once in a process.

methods.name: answer
methods.doc:
The response for one request, whatever happens: a database that
cannot be reached, salts that are not set, or a failure anywhere
underneath, each answered in the language the request asked in.

methods.name: bootRuntimeForRest
methods.doc:
The WordPress runtime for a REST request: the caller the REST layer
resolved is the reader, plugins load, and rest_api_init fires so
their routes answer after the engine's own.

methods.name: recheckNonce
methods.doc:
A plugin's nonce lifetime (nonce_life) is heard only once plugins
load: a cookie caller's nonce is checked again under it, as the
reference checks it. A caller the default lifetime refused was nobody
while plugins loaded; when the plugin's lifetime proves the nonce, that
user reads the request from here (unless plugin code named someone).

methods.name: adoptSettledUser
methods.doc:
The user plugin code settled (determine_current_user) as the REST
caller, as the reference's cookie check leaves it: a request a
plugin signs in by its own token is that user; a sign-in cookie
vouches only for its own user (another one fails its nonce, and
without a nonce the request is nobody, plugin code included).

methods.name: armRecoveryPause
methods.doc:
With the database in hand, a fatal during boot can be blamed on the
extension it came from. The window in which this applies is opened by
Plugins::load. A visitor's request only notes the failure, and only
when it carries no query, body, upload or cookie: its path and headers
are still the visitor's, and an extension that fails on some input
fails for that input alone (security review 2026-10-22; Austin,
2026-10-24). On the first note inside the window the engine asks the
site itself, once (Recovery::check); that request carries its token,
and when it fails at boot on the same extension, the extension is
paused and the next request comes back without it.

methods.name: plain
methods.doc: Whether a request carries nothing a visitor chose but its path: a GET or HEAD with no query, body, upload or cookie.

methods.name: frontPipeline
methods.signature: frontPipeline(Minn\Context $context, Minn\Http\Request $request, Minn\Runtime\Runtime $runtime, Minn\Content\Users $users, Minn\Auth\Cookie $cookie, Minn\Auth\Authenticator $authenticator, Minn\Admin\App $app, mixed $session, Minn\Front\Resolver $resolver, Minn\Front\Permalinks $permalinks, ?Minn\Theme\Theme $theme, ?Minn\Theme\ClassicTheme $classicTheme, Minn\Runtime\WpApiMode $mode, ?Minn\Front\FrontParts $parts): Minn\Http\Response
methods.doc: The themed front, admin app, and probe pipeline; split out so a mid-request ServeLogin signal can unwind it cleanly.

methods.name: maintenance
methods.doc: Whether Minn Admin's maintenance mode is on: the option set and Minn Admin active (its holds decide who it keeps out).

methods.name: withoutRuntime
methods.doc:
A public page an extension route answers, with no runtime: no facade,
no plugins, no boot hooks (MINN_WP_API 'auto' or 'off'). Null when an
engine route claims the path or no extension route answers it; the
request then boots as any other, on the same registered extensions.

methods.name: frontGate
methods.doc:
The front's gate: its routes are public or judge their own session; a
policy that asks for more is refused outright rather than judged half-way.

classes.name: Minn\Extension\Accounts
classes.doc:
Accounts for a sign-in surface of an extension's own (a game's players, a
members' area), from its REST routes: the sign-in, sign-out, registration
and password reset the engine's sign-in page runs, with the same
throttle, hooks, sessions and mail, handed back as values the extension
words itself. A refusal is a Refusal: its code, its message as plain
text, and every code and message in data.notices. A refused sign-in
never says which half was wrong (code incorrect_credentials) unless a
plugin refused it in its own words. They run the sign-in hooks plugins
listen on, so they belong on an extension's REST routes.

constants.name: REFUSALS
constants.doc: The authenticate chain's own refusals, which read as one.

methods.name: signIn
methods.doc:
Signs in with a login (or email) and password, as the sign-in page
does, for two days ending with the browser: the response with the new
session's cookies and the user, or the refusal (too_many_attempts with
data.retryAfter in seconds, incorrect_credentials, or a plugin's own).

methods.name: signInRemembered
methods.doc: Signs in as signIn does, remembered: fourteen days, the cookies kept past the browser session.

methods.name: signOut
methods.doc:
Ends the session the sign-in cookie names, and clears the cookies,
when the request carries that session's REST nonce (the X-WP-Nonce
header or a form's _wpnonce, as the sign-in page's sign-out asks for
its own); with no live session it only clears the cookies. A request
naming a live session without its nonce, or with a lapsed one, is
refused (rest_cookie_invalid_nonce, 403) and changes nothing, so a page
on another site, or a navigation to an extension page that signs out,
signs nobody out, cookies included, while a client whose nonce lapsed
can fetch a fresh one and ask again (security sweep 2026-11-12,
finding 1.4, closed by the fix-delta review).

methods.name: registrationOpen
methods.doc: Whether the site takes new accounts (users_can_register).

methods.name: register
methods.doc:
A new account with the password its holder chose, the role asked for
(one the site has, else the site's default role) and, when given, the
name shown for it (display name and nickname; an email-only sign-up
passes a login of its own making), when the site takes new accounts:
the user, or every refusal (registration_closed, unknown_role, role_not_allowed for a role holding more than
the default role does; the name empty, illegal, taken or barred; the
email empty, malformed or taken; no password; whatever plugins add).
The site's address is told; nobody is signed in.

methods.name: registerQuietly
methods.doc: A new account as register makes it, with the site's address told nothing (a game's players, say).

methods.name: passwordHash
methods.doc:
A password hashed as an account stores it (slashed, as a sign-in form
sends it, through wp_hash_password), for a sign-up that holds it until
the email is proven: registerQuietlyWithHash makes the account from it.

methods.name: registerQuietlyWithHash
methods.doc:
A new account as registerQuietly makes it, its password one that
passwordHash hashed earlier (a sign-up held until its email was
proven), so the password itself never had to be kept: the same checks
and refusals, and a hash that is empty or not a hash refused as no
password (empty_password).

methods.name: signInVerified
methods.doc:
Signs in a user the extension vouches for without a password (an
emailed link proved the address), remembered as signInRemembered
signs in: a new session and the three cookies on the response,
wp_login fired. The extension's own proof is the only check, so it
belongs after a single-use secret of the extension's own.

methods.name: passkeyOptions
methods.doc:
Options for navigator.credentials.create() to add a passkey to a
signed-in user (the JSON parseCreationOptionsFromJSON reads); the
extension adds its own client extensions, such as prf, in the browser.

methods.name: addPasskey
methods.doc:
Keeps the passkey a browser made from passkeyOptions (its toJSON()
answer) under a label of the user's, or the refusal: passkey_refused,
data.reason naming the check that failed.

methods.name: passkeySignInOptions
methods.doc:
Options for navigator.credentials.get() to sign in with any of the
site's passkeys (the JSON parseRequestOptionsFromJSON reads).

methods.name: signInWithPasskey
methods.doc:
Signs in with a browser's answer to passkeySignInOptions, remembered
as signInVerified signs in, and throttled per address as passwords
are: the response with the session's cookies, or the refusal
(too_many_attempts with data.retryAfter, or passkey_refused with
data.reason). Plugins' authenticate filters are not asked: the
passkey is the proof.

methods.name: passkeys
methods.doc: A user's passkeys, newest first.

methods.name: removePasskey
methods.doc: Removes one of a user's passkeys by its id: whether the user had it.

methods.name: mail
methods.doc:
Sends an email of the extension's own through the site's mailer
(wp_mail: its filters, an SMTP plugin), headers as wp_mail takes them
(an HTML mail's Content-Type, a From): whether it was accepted.

methods.name: lostPassword
methods.doc:
A password reset link mailed to the account a login or email names,
as the lost-password page sends it: true, or the refusal. $link makes
the link from the account's login and the key, for a reset page of the
extension's own (which hands both to resetPassword); without it the
link opens the sign-in page's reset form. $words writes the mail
(subject, body, and optionally headers: an HTML mail's Content-Type, a
From) from the link and the account's display name, for a site whose
people never see a login; without it the mail is the sign-in page's,
which names the login.

methods.name: resetPassword
methods.doc:
A new password for the account a reset link named, as the reset form
saves one: the key must still be good (a day, or what
password_reset_expiration says), plugins may refuse the password
(validate_password_reset), and every session of the account ends. The
user, or the refusal (too_many_attempts, invalid_key, expired_key,
empty_password, a plugin's). Nobody is signed in.

methods.name: changePassword
methods.doc:
A new password for a signed-in user, once the current one checks out:
saved as a profile save saves it (wp_update_user, its hooks and its
notice to the account's address, in the extension's words when $words
gives them), every session of the account ended, and a new one on the
response: a sign-in cookie is bound to the password it was made under,
so the old ones stop working anyway. Refusals: too_many_attempts,
incorrect_password (counts against the throttle), empty_password, a
plugin's.
shapes: @param (Closure(string): array{0: string, 1: string, 2?: string|list<string>})|null $words the notice from the display name

params.name: words
params.doc: the notice from the display name

methods.name: changeEmail
methods.doc:
A new email for a signed-in user, once the current password checks
out: saved as a profile save saves it, the old address told (in the
extension's words when $words gives them). Refusals:
too_many_attempts, incorrect_password, invalid_email, email_exists, a
plugin's.
shapes: @param (Closure(string): array{0: string, 1: string, 2?: string|list<string>})|null $words the notice from the display name

params.name: words
params.doc: the notice from the display name

methods.name: storedHash
methods.doc: Whether a value reads as a stored password hash: "$"-led, of a hash's length.

methods.name: refuseRegistration
methods.doc: Why the site takes no new account in that role, or null when it does.

methods.name: checkCurrent
methods.doc: The current password, judged under the sign-in throttle: null when it checks out, else the refusal.

methods.name: worded
methods.doc:
Runs a save whose notice goes through $filter (password_change_email,
email_change_email) with the extension's words in place of the
reference's, early, so plugins' filters still have the last word.

methods.name: refusal
methods.doc: A refusal from the WordPress layer's errors: the first as the answer, all of them in data.notices; the chain's own as one sentence.

methods.name: plain
methods.doc: A notice's words without its markup or its "Error:" label.

classes.name: Minn\Extension\Extension
classes.doc:
What a Minn extension is: a class the engine constructs once per request
and asks to register what it provides. Everything it can touch is on the
Seams object; there is no global state to reach for.

methods.name: register
methods.doc: Registers the extension's seams.

classes.name: Minn\Extension\Extensions
classes.doc:
Where the engine looks for the seams an extension registered. The
request's runtime holds them, so nothing here keeps state of its own
and a request cannot inherit the extensions of the one before it.
Before the front or a REST request has loaded any (the command line
never does) there are none.

methods.name: set
methods.doc: Installs the seams for this request.

methods.name: setBlocks
methods.doc:
Installs the extensions' blocks and content rules, for a REST request:
its answers (content.rendered, the editor's previews) draw the blocks
and hide what the page hides, while the page's own parts stay with
the themed front.

methods.name: runner
methods.doc: The engine side of the seams, if any.

methods.name: install
methods.doc:
The runner, and each extension block registered as a dynamic block
type, so the block-type registry (wp/v2/block-types, Minn Admin's
inspector and inserter) lists it and the renderer draws it. The
callback asks the runner of the request it renders in, so a type
registered once never holds an earlier request's extension.

methods.name: typeArgs
methods.doc:
A block.json's keys as a block type's properties: the camelCase keys
become the snake_case properties they fill, and the keys that only
name files for a build step (scripts, styles, render) are left out.

classes.name: Minn\Extension\Loader
classes.doc:
Finds extensions under wp-content/plugins and wp-content/mu-plugins, and
in the active theme (a theme folder with a minn.json is an extension too,
active because it is the theme: the child, then its parent), decides
which are active, autoloads them, and asks each to register.
An extension that throws is logged and skipped; the page still renders.

methods.name: found
methods.doc: Every extension manifest on disk.

methods.name: refresh
methods.doc: Forgets the cached activation list after an option write.

methods.name: active
methods.doc: The manifests that are active.
shapes: @return list<Manifest> the extensions this site has switched on

methods.name: declaredTypes
methods.doc: Extra post types declared by active extensions, keyed by slug.

methods.name: declaredTaxonomies
methods.doc: Extra taxonomies declared by active extensions, keyed by slug.

methods.name: replacements
methods.doc: Which active WordPress plugin files an extension stands in for. @return array<string, string> plugin file => extension slug
shapes: @return array<string, string> plugin file => extension slug

methods.name: register
methods.doc:
Registers every active extension, each on seams of its own; one that
throws adds nothing. An extension's declared tables are settled first
(Tables), so its routes find them on the request that creates them.

methods.name: themeDirs
methods.doc: The active theme's folders, child first, that carry a minn.json.

classes.name: Minn\Extension\Manifest
classes.doc:
minn.json, read as data. A folder under wp-content/plugins (or
mu-plugins) with this file is an extension; the same folder may also be
a WordPress plugin, in which case the two share a name and a version.

{
"name": "Block Visibility for Minn",
"version": "1.0.0",
"license": "MIT",
"replaces": ["block-visibility/block-visibility.php"],
"autoload": {"Minn\\Ext\\BlockVisibility\\": "src/"},
"extension": "Minn\\Ext\\BlockVisibility\\Extension",
"shortcodes": ["example_tag"],
"blocks": ["vendor/block"],
"types": [{"slug": "zz_note", "name": "Notes", "rest_base": "zz-note"}],
"taxonomies": [{"slug": "zz_topic", "name": "Topics", "types": ["zz_note"]}],
"tables": {"minn_block_visibility_log": ["id bigint(20) unsigned NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT", "PRIMARY KEY  (id)"]},
"needs": {"http": ["https://api.example.com/"]}
}

"replaces" names the WordPress plugin files whose behaviour this
extension stands in for; the extension is active whenever one of them is
in active_plugins, or when its own folder is listed there, or when it is
named in the minn_active_extensions option. "shortcodes" and "blocks"
are the content tokens preflight treats as provided instead of missing.
"types" are extra post types and "taxonomies" extra taxonomies, each
registered on init as a plugin registers its own (DeclaredTypes).
"tables" are the extension's own tables, each a name (the extension's
slug, dashes as underscores, then "_" and more) and its column and key
lines; the engine creates them under the site's table prefix and adds
what a later version declares, never dropping or changing (Tables).
"needs" says what the extension reaches outside the process: "http" is
the URL prefixes its $minn->http may request (true for any public host).

constructor.signature: __construct(string $slug, string $dir, string $name, string $version, string $license, array $replaces, array $autoload, string $extension, string $covers = '', array $shortcodes = array ( ), array $blocks = array ( ), array $types = array ( ), array $taxonomies = array ( ), ?array $http = NULL, array $tables = array ( ))
shapes: @param array<string, list<string>> $tables table name without the prefix => its column and key lines

params.name: tables
params.doc: table name without the prefix => its column and key lines

properties.name: covers
properties.doc: what of the replaced plugin this provides, when not all of it

methods.name: read
methods.doc: A folder's minn.json, or null when there is none.

methods.name: tables
methods.doc:
"tables" as name => lines: a name with a list of strings is kept as
written, anything else is left out (Tables judges the names).

methods.name: http
methods.doc:
needs.http as a grant: true for any public host, or a URL prefix (or a
list of them) every request must start with; null when the manifest
does not ask. A prefix naming only a host is closed with "/", so
https://api.example.com does not also admit api.example.com.evil.net.

classes.name: Minn\Extension\Registrations
classes.doc: Everything the extensions registered for this request, handed from Seams to the runner once.

constructor.signature: __construct(array $blockGates, array $blockFilters, array $shortcodes, array $contentFilters, array $head, array $footer, array $bodyClasses, array $documentFilters, ?Closure $title, array $routes = array ( ), array $blocks = array ( ), array $editorStyles = array ( ), array $rest = array ( ))
shapes: @param array<string, array{metadata: array<string, mixed>, render: Closure}> $blocks
@param list<object> $rest controllers with #[Route] methods for the REST API

params.name: blocks
params.shape: array<string, array{metadata: array<string, mixed>, render: Closure}>

params.name: rest
params.doc: controllers with #[Route] methods for the REST API

methods.name: onlyBlocks
methods.doc:
What a request that draws content but is no themed page (REST) keeps:
the blocks and what previews them, and everything that decides what
content shows (block gates and filters, shortcodes, content filters),
so content.rendered hides what the page hides. The page's own parts
(head, footer, classes, routes) stay with the themed front.

classes.name: Minn\Extension\SeamRunner
classes.doc:
The engine's side of the seams: what the loader collected, called at the
right moment and in registration order. An extension never sees this
class; it sees Seams, which is only the registrations.

methods.name: allowsBlock
methods.doc: Whether every block gate lets a block render.

methods.name: filterBlock
methods.doc: A block's HTML through every block filter.

methods.name: shortcodeNames
methods.doc: The extensions' shortcode names, which strip_shortcodes takes out too.

methods.name: filterContent
methods.doc:
Shortcodes, then the content filters, over rendered post content. An
extension's filter is promised the post as a row (contracts/extensions.md),
so a record is handed over as one.

methods.name: title
methods.doc: The document title through the title filter.

methods.name: head
methods.doc: What the extensions add to the head.

methods.name: footer
methods.doc: What the extensions add to the footer.

methods.name: bodyClasses
methods.doc: The body classes the extensions add.

methods.name: filterDocument
methods.doc: The whole document through every document filter.

methods.name: renderBlock
methods.doc: An extension's block drawn from its attributes and rendered inner blocks; null for a name no extension registered.

methods.name: editorStyles
methods.doc: The stylesheets the editor's previews load for the extensions, each once.

methods.name: blockTypes
methods.doc: Every extension block's block.json, by name.

classes.name: Minn\Extension\Seams
classes.doc:
Where an extension can take part in a request: thirteen typed registrations,
the request they run in (and who it speaks for), the accounts a sign-in
surface of its own may sign in and make, and the outgoing HTTP its
minn.json asks for.
This is the whole surface an extension sees. Each extension registers on
its own (forExtension), and what it registered joins the request's once
its register() returns (adopt). The engine calls what was registered
through SeamRunner, at the right moment and in registration order.

properties.name: bar
properties.doc: The Minn bar for a signed-in editor on this request, or null.

properties.name: dir
properties.doc: The registering extension's folder, which its block.json paths are read from.

properties.name: http
properties.doc: Outgoing HTTP, bound to the hosts the extension's needs.http lists; a client that throws when it asked for none.

methods.name: forExtension
methods.doc:
The seams one extension registers on: this request, and the outgoing
HTTP its manifest grants. A manifest without needs.http gets a client
that throws at its first request, naming the key to add.

methods.name: adopt
methods.doc:
Takes on what one extension registered, after its register() returned,
so an extension that throws half-way adds nothing. A closure the
engine hands seams to is handed that extension's own.

methods.name: gateBlocks
methods.doc: Decides whether a block renders at all; the first gate to answer false wins.

methods.name: filterBlocks
methods.doc: Rewrites a block's rendered markup.

methods.name: shortcode
methods.doc: Renders [tag attr="…"]content[/tag] wherever it appears in post content.

methods.name: filterContent
methods.doc: Rewrites rendered post content (after blocks and shortcodes).

methods.name: head
methods.doc: Markup for the document head (a style, a meta tag, a script).

methods.name: footer
methods.doc: Markup before </body>.

methods.name: bodyClass
methods.doc: Adds a body class.

methods.name: title
methods.doc: Replaces the document title; receives the engine's own.

methods.name: filterDocument
methods.doc: Rewrites the whole themed document before it is sent (what an output buffer did on the reference).

methods.name: routes
methods.doc:
Answers paths with controllers whose public methods carry #[Route]
attributes, as the engine's own do: each method takes the Request and
the captures it names and returns a Response. They are asked after the
engine's own routes and before the themed front, so an extension can
add pages but never take over one the engine answers.

methods.name: rest
methods.doc:
Answers REST routes (under /wp-json/, and as ?rest_route=) with
controllers whose public methods carry #[Route] attributes, as the
engine's own REST controllers do: the pattern leaves out /wp-json
("/acme/v1/notes/{id:\d+}"), and the route's Policy is judged by the
engine's REST gate, so the sign-in cookie counts only with its
wp_rest nonce (X-WP-Nonce or _wpnonce) or an application password,
and a refusal is the engine's own (401 rest_not_logged_in, 403
rest_cookie_invalid_nonce, 403 for a missing capability). They are
asked after the engine's routes and before plugins' routes; user()
is the caller the gate judged. Each pattern names a namespace of the
extension's own: one under wp, wp-*, oembed or minn-admin (where
WordPress's and the engine's routes live) throws, which skips the
extension.

methods.name: user
methods.doc:
The signed-in user this request speaks for, or null for nobody. On a
REST route that is the caller the REST gate accepted (the cookie with
its nonce, or an application password); on a page it is the sign-in
cookie alone, so a page reads with it and never writes on it.

methods.name: accounts
methods.doc:
Accounts for a sign-in surface of the extension's own, from its REST
routes: sign in and out, register with a chosen password, mail a
reset link, each as the engine's sign-in page does it (Accounts).

methods.name: block
methods.doc:
A block of the extension's own. Its block.json (a folder holding one,
or the file, relative to the extension's folder) is the schema editors
read: name, title, attributes with their types and defaults, parent.
$render draws the block from its attributes (defaults filled in) and
its rendered inner blocks. The engine registers it as a dynamic block,
so it renders on the front, in REST answers and in the editor's
previews, and Minn Admin edits its attributes with a form. A file
that is missing or names no block throws, which skips the extension.

methods.name: editorStyles
methods.doc:
Stylesheets the editor's block previews load, after the theme's own:
what an extension's blocks are drawn against when the theme's
style.css is not all of it. URLs, absolute or from the site root.

methods.name: frontBar
methods.doc:
A whole HTML document an extension built, with the Minn bar a signed-in
editor sees on themed pages: its stylesheet before </head> and the bar
before </body>. Name the post the page shows and the bar's Edit opens
it. Anyone else gets the document unchanged.

methods.name: useFrontBar
methods.doc: The engine hands over this request's Minn bar before extensions register. Extensions have no reason to call this.

methods.name: registrations
methods.doc: What was registered, for the engine's runner. Extensions have no reason to call this.

classes.name: Minn\Extension\Shortcodes
classes.doc:
The shortcode syntax in rendered content: [tag], [tag attr="v" flag],
[tag]inner[/tag], and [[tag]] as the escaped literal. Unregistered tags
stay as written, which is what the reference shows for a plugin that is
not installed.

methods.name: apply
methods.doc: Content with the registered shortcodes run.

methods.name: attributes
methods.doc: A shortcode's attributes parsed, curly quotes included.
shapes: @return array<string, string> named attributes; bare words keyed by position

classes.name: Minn\Extension\SignedIn
classes.doc: A sign-in that worked (Accounts::signIn): who, and the response carrying the session's cookies.

classes.name: Minn\Extension\Tables
classes.doc:
An extension's own tables, from the "tables" its minn.json declares:
created under the site's table prefix the first time the extension
registers, and brought up to date (missing columns and keys added, as
dbDelta adds them) when its version or its declaration changes. What
was applied is recorded per extension in one option, so a request
after that costs one autoloaded read. Nothing is ever dropped, renamed
or changed: a column a later version leaves out stays, and so does
every table when the extension goes away.

constants.name: OPTION
constants.doc: The option recording, per extension slug, the version and declaration last applied.

constants.name: CORE_TABLES
constants.doc: WordPress's own tables, unprefixed: no extension declares one, whatever its slug ("term" would own term_relationships).

methods.name: settle
methods.doc:
Applies an extension's tables when they changed since the last time,
and records them. Returns what was done (empty when nothing was due),
by table or table.column, in DbDelta's words. A declaration that
names a table outside the extension's own throws, which skips it.

methods.name: statements
methods.signature: statements(Minn\Extension\Manifest $manifest, string $prefix, string $collation = self::FALLBACK_COLLATION, array $others = array ( )): array
methods.doc:
The CREATE TABLE statements an extension declares, keyed by the
prefixed table name: each name must be the extension's slug (dashes
as underscores) followed by "_" and lowercase letters, digits or
underscores, and each line one column or key definition. No name is
one of WordPress's own tables, or inside the names of another
extension (from $others, the slugs with tables recorded) whose slug
is longer: acme may not declare acme_x_orders while acme-x has tables
(security sweep 2026-11-12, finding 1.5).

methods.name: marker
methods.doc: What is recorded for an extension once its tables are applied: its version and a digest of the declaration.

methods.name: collation
methods.doc: The collation the site's own options table was made with, so extension tables sort text as the site does.

classes.name: Minn\Feed\Charset
classes.doc:
A feed document as UTF-8. The encoding comes from a byte-order mark,
then the XML declaration, then the Content-Type charset, then UTF-8; a
document in another encoding is converted and its declaration rewritten,
so the parser only ever reads UTF-8.

methods.name: toUtf8
methods.doc: The document converted to UTF-8, with no byte-order mark.

methods.name: declared
methods.doc: The encoding the XML declaration names, if it names one.

classes.name: Minn\Feed\Dates
classes.doc: Feed dates (RFC 822, W3C, and the looser forms feeds carry) as Unix timestamps; a date without a zone is UTC.

methods.name: parse
methods.doc: The timestamp, or null when the text names no date.

classes.name: Minn\Feed\Document
classes.doc:
A parsed feed: the tree and the format it was recognized as (the
reference's type bits: RSS 0.90 1, the 0.9x versions 2 to 32, RSS 1.0 64,
RSS 2.0 128, Atom 0.3 256, Atom 1.0 512), with the lookups the feed
object is built on: the root's children, the channel's, the image's, and
the items of every format the document carries.

methods.name: parse
methods.doc: A document read from bytes; the type is NONE when it parsed but is no feed.

methods.name: fromTree
methods.doc: A document over a tree already parsed (a cached feed), its type read from the root.

methods.name: root
methods.doc: The root element (rss, rdf:RDF or feed), or null.

methods.name: channel
methods.doc: The channel element: an RSS channel, or the Atom feed itself.

methods.name: image
methods.doc: The image element: inside an RSS 2.0 channel, beside an RSS 1.0 one.

methods.name: feedTags
methods.doc: Children of the root element by namespace and name, or null.

methods.name: channelTags
methods.doc: Children of the channel by namespace and name, or null.

methods.name: imageTags
methods.doc: Children of the image by namespace and name, or null.

methods.name: items
methods.doc:
Every item node, in document order: Atom 1.0 and 0.3 entries, RSS 1.0
and 0.90 items beside the channel, RSS 2.0 items inside it.

classes.name: Minn\Feed\FeedError
classes.doc: A feed that could not be read: the message is the one the reference reports.

classes.name: Minn\Feed\Iri
classes.doc:
URLs in feeds: a reference resolved against its base (RFC 3986), then
normalized the way the reference prints them: scheme and host in lower
case, the default port dropped, dot segments removed, and every byte a
URL may not carry (spaces, angle brackets, non-ASCII) percent-encoded.

methods.name: resolve
methods.doc: The reference resolved against the base and normalized; null when neither is absolute.

methods.name: clean
methods.doc: An absolute URL normalized; anything else returned as given.

methods.name: split
shapes: @return array{scheme: ?string, authority: ?string, path: string, query: ?string, fragment: ?string}

methods.name: encode
methods.doc:
Percent-encodes every byte outside the unreserved and sub-delimiter sets
and the extra characters a component allows, then writes each escape
the reference's way (unescape()).

methods.name: unescape
methods.doc: Escapes of letters, digits, "-", "." and "~" decoded, the rest in upper case ("_" stays escaped, as on the reference; probe feed-urls).

classes.name: Minn\Feed\Locator
classes.doc:
Feed autodiscovery: the feeds an HTML page names in its
<link rel="alternate"> elements with a feed type, in page order, each
resolved against the page (or its <base href>).

methods.name: looksLikeFeed
methods.doc: Whether a response looks like a feed document rather than a page or text.

methods.name: alternates
methods.doc: The feed URLs a page names, resolved, in page order, each once.

classes.name: Minn\Feed\Parts
classes.doc:
The repeating parts of a feed element read out of the tree as raw
values: links by relation, categories, and enclosures (Media RSS
contents, Atom enclosure links, RSS enclosures). The feed object
sanitizes and wraps them; each raw value travels with the node it came
from, so a relative URL resolves against that node's base.

methods.name: links
methods.doc:
Links by relation: Atom links (rel defaults to alternate, IANA names
answer to both spellings), then the RSS-style link elements and the
given extra alternates.
shapes: @param array<string, array<string, list<array<string, mixed>>>> $child the element's children
@param list<array{0: string, 1: string}> $plain RSS-style link tags, by namespace and name
@param list<string> $more alternates already in their final form
@param Closure(string, array<string, mixed>): string $iri a URL as the feed hands it out, given its node

params.name: plain
params.doc: RSS-style link tags, by namespace and name

params.name: more
params.doc: alternates already in their final form

params.name: iri
params.doc: a URL as the feed hands it out, given its node

methods.name: categories
methods.doc:
Categories as raw text: Atom (term, scheme, label), RSS 2.0 (the text,
the domain as scheme), Dublin Core subjects.

methods.name: enclosures
methods.doc:
An item's enclosures as raw fields, Media RSS contents first (with the
item's thumbnails when a content has none of its own), then Atom
enclosure links, then RSS enclosures. "node" is where the URL came from.

methods.name: thumbnails
methods.doc: The media:thumbnail URLs directly under an element, each with its node.

classes.name: Minn\Feed\Tree
classes.doc:
A feed document parsed into the nested arrays plugin code reads through
get_item_tags() and friends: each element is a node holding its own text
("data", whitespace between children included), its attributes grouped
by namespace, the xml:base and xml:lang in force, and its children by
namespace and local name. Two shapes differ from plain XML: an Atom text
construct of type "xhtml" keeps its markup as text, and an RSS title is
stored HTML-escaped. Named HTML references are read as characters unless
the document brings its own DOCTYPE.

methods.name: parse
methods.doc: The document's elements under a root holding only "child".

methods.name: prepare
methods.doc: The document as the parser reads it: HTML references made numeric, the declaration on a line of its own.

methods.name: split
shapes: @return array{0: string, 1: string} namespace and local name

classes.name: Minn\Front\AdminBar
classes.doc:
The Minn bar on the public site: the same server-rendered chrome the
app ships (assets/js/bar.js and assets/css/bar.css from the bundle),
built here for a signed-in reader who can edit. There is no other bar
and no other admin on the engine, so it is on for everyone who passes
the edit_posts gate; the app's per-person opt-in does not apply.

constructor.signature: __construct(Minn\Auth\Authenticated $session, Minn\Auth\Capabilities $capabilities, Minn\Content\Site $site, Minn\Front\Permalinks $permalinks, Minn\Admin\App $app, Minn\Admin\Appearance $appearance, Minn\Admin\AdminTypes $types)

properties.name: key
properties.doc:
The key this request's corner carries and MINN_BAR repeats, so bar.js
binds to the bar printed here. The bar comes after the post content,
and content keeps id, style and hidden for roles without
unfiltered_html, so a lookup by a fixed id would find the content's
copy first. Content cannot know a key minted per request.

methods.name: forReader
methods.signature: forReader(?Minn\Auth\Authenticated $session, Minn\Auth\Capabilities $capabilities, Minn\Content\Site $site, Minn\Front\Permalinks $permalinks, Minn\Admin\App $app, Minn\Admin\Appearance $appearance, Minn\Admin\AdminTypes $types): ?self
methods.doc: The bar for a signed-in editor, or null for anyone else.

methods.name: t
methods.doc: A string of Minn Admin's, in the site's language (its own text domain, as the plugin asks for it).

methods.name: siteMenu
methods.doc: The site menu: the app's main views this user may open.

methods.name: statusMenu
methods.doc: The status menu, only when the page carries a site status. @param array<string, mixed>|null $status

methods.name: notificationsMenu

The status chip: the one thing the engine can say about site
visibility is whether search engines are asked to stay away.
shapes: @return array{tone: string, label: string, title: string, sub: string, fix: ?array}|null

methods.name: siteMode
methods.doc: The site's default mode the app keeps (dark, light or system), for a reader who never chose one.

methods.name: editTarget
shapes: @return array{0: string, 1: string, 2: string} url (or ''), label, hint

methods.name: searchTypes
methods.doc: post type slug => editor route base, for the palette's content results.

methods.name: menuItem
methods.signature: menuItem(string $href, string $icon, string $title, string $sub = '', string $meta = ''): string

classes.name: Minn\Front\ArchiveAddresses
classes.doc:
The archives an address may stand for, as the reference answers them:
the front, a search, a term's (a category's, a tag's, a plugin
taxonomy's), an author's and a date's. Each is the archive when what it
names exists (a term by its path's last slug, a valid date; an author's for any
name); whether its page has posts is the main query's to say, and an
empty page past the first, or an empty date, is the 404 it decides
(Theme\FrontLifecycle::handle404).

shapes: @param Closure(PostRecord): bool $readable whether the reader may read a post

params.name: readable
params.doc: whether the reader may read a post

methods.name: search
methods.doc: A search's results page.

methods.name: home
methods.doc: The front: the static front page when there is one, else the posts listing.

methods.name: taxonomy
methods.doc:
A plugin taxonomy's term archive by its path; a 404 when no term is
at that path.

methods.name: term
methods.doc: A category's or tag's archive by its path; a 404 when no term is at that path. @param list<string> $slugs

methods.name: author
methods.doc: An author's archive by nicename: the archive for any name, the author's when one has it.

methods.doc: A date archive by year, month and day; a 404 when the date is not one. @param list<string> $segments

methods.doc: Whether a year, month and day (the last two optional, a day only with its month) name a date.

methods.name: at
methods.doc:
The term a slug path names: its last slug's, whatever the segments
before it say (the reference serves /category/any/child/ as the
child's archive, unmoved).

classes.name: Minn\Front\Archives
classes.doc:
The archive periods wp_get_archives lists: months, years, days and weeks
that hold a published post of a type, newest first, each with its post
count and archive URL, plus the post-by-post and alphabetical listings.
Labels come from the caller's date formatter so the site's locale and
week start apply; the week label joins the week's first and last day.

@param Closure(int, ?int, ?int): string $dateLink the year, month, or day archive URL
@param Closure(string): array{start: int, end: int} $week the week's first and last second around a datetime

The periods of one granularity: monthly, yearly, daily, or weekly; a

@return array{url: string, text: string, count: int}

classes.name: Minn\Front\AssetsController
classes.doc: The engine's own static assets, served under a reserved path.

constants.name: TYPES
constants.doc: Media types as the web server sends the reference's static files (scripts as text/javascript, with the charset).

constants.name: PLAYER_FILES
constants.doc:
The media player's files, by the names the reference registers them
under: MediaElement.js's own (MIT, in vendor/mediaelement) and the
engine's start-up, skin and migration script in their place.

constants.doc: The embed scripts, by the reference addresses a page and a card's sourceURL name them at.
