methods.name: embedScript
methods.doc: The engine's embed scripts at the addresses the reference serves its own from.

methods.name: player
methods.doc: The media player, at the paths the reference registers it under (wp_default_scripts, wp_default_styles).

methods.name: jquery
methods.doc: The MIT libraries the engine ships, served at the paths the reference registers them under.

classes.name: Minn\Front\AttachmentAddresses
classes.doc:
The addresses an attachment's page answers to besides those its rules
find (Front\RuleTable: a loose one by its slug at the top, any by its
slug under another address, "attachment/" between or not): by id or
slug in the query (?attachment_id=, ?attachment=), and as a post (?p=,
?page_id=), which moves to its own page. With
attachment pages off (wp_attachment_pages_enabled, the default) every
address moves to the file itself; with them on, one that is not its own
moves to its page. An attachment is readable as its parent is.

methods.name: names
methods.doc: Whether a resolution is an attachment's page.

methods.name: fromQuery
methods.doc: ?attachment_id= or ?attachment=: the attachment's page, or a 404; null when the request names neither.

methods.name: asPost
methods.doc: An attachment asked for as a post (?p=, ?page_id=): it moves to its own page whatever the setting; null for any other post.

methods.name: answer
methods.doc:
With attachment pages off (the default), a move to the file itself,
from every address, its embed and feed among them: the query along,
though an ?attachment_id= address leaves its id behind unless it asked
for an embed. With them on, the page as typed, or (the address not its
own) a move to its own: the other query arguments along, ?attachment=
among them; an embed stays where it was asked for.

methods.name: readable
methods.doc: An attachment is readable as its parent is; a loose one as it stands.

classes.name: Minn\Front\Calendar
classes.doc:
One month as the calendar widget and block draw it: a table whose caption
names the month, whose head lists the week from the site's first day, and
whose cells link the days a post was published on to that day's archive;
today's cell carries the id the stylesheet lights; the nav below links
the nearest months with posts on either side. Markup, whitespace and the
attribute order of the two padding cells follow the reference byte for
byte, since themes style the table by those hooks.

shapes: @param Closure(int, int, ?int): string $link the month archive URL, or the day's when a day is given

params.name: link
params.doc: the month archive URL, or the day's when a day is given

methods.name: render
methods.doc: The table and its navigation.
shapes: @param list<int> $postDays days of the month with a published post
@param array{int, int}|null $previous the nearest earlier month with posts, as [year, month]
@param array{int, int}|null $next the nearest later month with posts
@param array{int, int, int}|null $today the site's current date, as [year, month, day]

params.name: postDays
params.doc: days of the month with a published post

params.name: previous
params.doc: the nearest earlier month with posts, as [year, month]

params.name: next
params.doc: the nearest later month with posts

params.name: today
params.doc: the site's current date, as [year, month, day]

classes.name: Minn\Front\CalendarLabels
classes.doc:
The words a calendar prints: weekday names Sunday first, the short form
each column shows (an initial or an abbreviation), month names by number,
and the abbreviation the month navigation uses.

shapes: @param array<string, string> $weekdayShort full weekday name to the column heading
@param array<string, string> $monthAbbrev full month name to its abbreviation

params.name: weekdayShort
params.doc: full weekday name to the column heading

params.name: monthAbbrev
params.doc: full month name to its abbreviation

methods.name: english
methods.doc: The English tables, with weekday initials as the reference shows by default.

methods.name: englishAbbreviated
methods.doc: The English tables with three-letter weekday abbreviations.

methods.name: fromEnglish
shapes: @param Closure(string): string $short the column heading for a weekday name

params.name: short
params.doc: the column heading for a weekday name

classes.name: Minn\Front\Canonical
classes.doc:
Where a URL should redirect to, by the engine's own resolution: the
canonical form of a request (trailing slash, `?p=` to permalink, doubled
slashes, former slugs). The front controller applies this before any
plugin runs; the `redirect_canonical()` facade asks it again for a URL a
plugin names.

methods.name: location
methods.doc: The canonical URL of a request, or null when it already is one.

classes.name: Minn\Front\CommentPostController
classes.doc:
wp-comments-post.php: the comment form's target. The reference's
answers, captured: 302 to the comment's anchor (with unapproved and
moderation-hash when held), plain pages with 200 for a missing field,
403 when comments are closed, 409 for a duplicate, 429 for posting too
quickly, and 405 for anything but POST.

methods.name: post
methods.doc: The comment form's target.

methods.name: submit
methods.doc:
The reference's own submission and redirect (contracts/runtime.md "The
comment form"), so a spam plugin's checks, the notifications and the
commenter cookies are WordPress's: a refusal with a status is the
refusal page, one without is a blank page; else set_comment_cookies,
the comment's link (or redirect_to), the held comment's id and hash
when the commenter is not remembered, comment_post_redirect, and
wp_safe_redirect's checks.

methods.name: refusal
methods.doc: The reference's plain refusal page: the message and a way back.

classes.name: Minn\Front\CustomLogo
classes.doc:
The site logo a theme prints, as get_custom_logo builds it (probe
plugin-helpers): the custom_logo theme mod's image at full size, never
lazy, its alt its own or else the site's name, linked home (marked the
current page on the front page). A theme that unlinks the home page logo
gets a plain span there, the image then decorative (an empty alt). The
image's attributes go through get_custom_logo_image_attributes and the
whole through get_custom_logo; no logo is an empty string, or in the
Customizer a hidden placeholder it can fill in.

methods.name: html
methods.doc: The logo's markup, through get_custom_logo; empty when the site has none.

classes.name: Minn\Front\EmbedCard
classes.doc:
The parts of a post's embed card the reference's embed template prints,
as markup: the featured image and its shape (the widest of the image's
sizes; wide enough and it sits above the title, else beside it, both by
filter), the site's name and icon, the comments and sharing buttons, and
the sharing dialog (its ids the post's and a random number, as on the
reference). The facade's template tags print them.

methods.name: thumbnail
methods.doc:
The featured image the card shows: [attachment id, size, shape], or
null. A post's thumbnail, or an image attachment itself, through
embed_thumbnail_id, embed_thumbnail_image_size and
embed_thumbnail_image_shape.

methods.name: featuredImage
methods.doc: The featured image's block, when the card shows one of this shape.

methods.name: siteTitle
methods.doc: The site's name and icon, linking home, the whole block through embed_site_title_html.

methods.name: commentsButton
methods.doc: The comments button: the count, linking to the comments; none on a 404, or with neither comments nor comments open.

methods.name: sharingButton
methods.doc: The button that opens the sharing dialog; none on a 404.

methods.name: sharingDialog
methods.doc: The sharing dialog: the post's address and its embed code, each a tab; none on a 404.

classes.name: Minn\Front\EntryScriptsController
classes.doc:
The reference's other stand-alone scripts at the webroot, answered as it
answers them (contracts/front/probes.md, "Entry scripts"): the links
OPML and post by email load the site and nothing more; signup,
activation and trackback run the main query on their own address first,
which finds nothing, as the reference's do.

methods.name: linksOpml
methods.doc: wp-links-opml.php: the site's links as OPML.

methods.name: mail
methods.doc:
wp-mail.php: post by email. Refused (403) while the configuration is
turned off or names no mail server; a configured POP3 server is not
read, so it is refused the same way (the engine carries no POP3
client: the open items register).

methods.name: signup
methods.doc: wp-signup.php and wp-activate.php: a single site sends both to registration.

methods.name: trackback
methods.doc: wp-trackback.php asked directly: the address names no post, so the answer is the reference's "need an ID".

methods.name: stopped
methods.doc: What wp_die printed for a message, under its status, where the reference exits.

classes.name: Minn\Front\FeedController
classes.doc:
The feeds, wherever a request asks for one: the feed var of the rule its
address matched (the site's at /feed/, the comments' at
/comments/feed/, a post's or an archive's after its address, a plugin's
own) or ?feed= on any page. Each is WordPress's feed lifecycle: the main
query with the feed asked for, then do_feed, whose handler prints the
feed and its content type. A feed of something the address names but
the site does not have is an empty feed, as the reference serves it.

methods.name: asked
methods.doc: Whether a request asks for a feed of what it resolved to (the query form only of something that exists).

methods.name: serve
methods.doc: The feed a request asks for, of what its address resolved to.

methods.name: served
shapes: @param array<string, mixed> $vars what the request asks of the feed: its type and its comments

params.name: vars
params.doc: what the request asks of the feed: its type and its comments

methods.name: perFeed
methods.doc: How many items a feed carries (posts_per_rss).

classes.name: Minn\Front\FeedTags
classes.doc:
The template tags a feed is written with that take more than a line, as
the reference answers them in a feed's loop (probe feed-tags): a post's
categories and tags in each feed's markup, its enclosures for RSS and
Atom, the link to its comments feed, the feed's build date, and the site
icon a feed carries; and the small ones: the site's default feed, a feed's
content type and a post's title for a feed.

methods.name: wpTitleRss
methods.doc: The page's document title as a feed's title (get_wp_title_rss), as get_wp_title_rss leaves it.

methods.name: contentFeed
methods.doc: The content of the post being read, rendered for a feed item (get_the_content_feed): CDATA's close escaped, then the_content_feed.

methods.name: serve
methods.doc:
The feed the query asks for run by its do_feed_{feed} handlers
(do_feed): leading underscores dropped, the default for none; a 404
when nothing handles it.

methods.name: defaultFeed
methods.doc: The feed the site serves by default (get_default_feed): default_feed's, "rss" read as rss2.

methods.name: contentType
methods.doc: The content type a feed is served as (feed_content_type), the default feed's when none is named.

methods.name: titleRss
methods.doc: A post's title for a feed (get_the_title_rss), as the_title_rss leaves it.

methods.name: categories
methods.doc: A post's category and tag names (each once) in a feed type's markup, before the_category_rss.

methods.name: rssEnclosures
methods.doc: The current post's enclosures as RSS has them: address, length, and the type the third line starts with.

methods.name: atomEnclosures
methods.doc: The current post's enclosures as Atom links: the length a line that is a number, the type a line that is a known MIME type.

methods.name: postCommentsFeedLink
methods.doc: The address of a post's comments feed in a feed type (the default one bare), through post_comments_feed_link.

methods.name: buildDate
methods.doc:
When the feed last changed, in a format: the newest of its posts'
modifications (and comments, for a comments feed); once the loop has
run out, the site's last modification; failing both, now.

methods.name: rss2Icon
methods.doc: The site icon as an RSS 2.0 image (titled with the feed's title), or '' without one.

methods.name: atomIcon
methods.doc: The site icon as an Atom icon, or '' without one.

methods.name: enclosures
shapes: @return list<list<string>> the current post's enclosures, each as its lines, unless its password is wanted

classes.name: Minn\Front\FeedTemplates
classes.doc:
The feed templates do_feed_* loads, written from the reference's output
(suite feed-hooks, probes feed-templates): RSS 2.0, Atom, RDF and RSS
0.92 for posts, RSS 2.0 and Atom for comments. Each is written through
the template tags, so every feed filter has its say, and fires each feed
action where the reference fires it; the whitespace between is the
reference's. A template is written once a request, as require_once
loads it, and sends its content type through the header callback first.

methods.name: load
methods.doc:
A feed template by its name (rss2, rss2-comments, atom, atom-comments,
rdf, rss), between wp_before_load_template and wp_after_load_template.
shapes: @param Closure(string): void $send sends a header line (the Content-Type)

methods.name: syndication
methods.doc: What the period and frequency of updates are, as the syndication module says.

methods.name: commentsTitle
methods.doc: The heading of a comments feed: the post's, the search's, or the site's.

methods.name: commentTitle
methods.doc: A comment's heading in a comments feed: by whom, and on what when the feed is not a single post's.

methods.name: current
methods.doc: The comment the loop is on, with its post made the current one. @return array{0: object, 1: Post}

classes.name: Minn\Front\FeedWriter
classes.doc:
A feed as it is written: text as given, and what each template tag and
action prints, in the order the template asks for them.

methods.name: put
methods.doc: Text as written.

methods.name: tag
methods.doc: What a function that prints (a template tag) prints, called with its arguments.

methods.name: cdata
methods.doc:
What a template tag prints, for inside a CDATA section: a "]]>" in it
is split so it cannot close the section (a hardening rule; the
reference lets a stored name break out, contracts/front/probes.md).

methods.name: insideCdata
methods.doc: Text made safe inside a CDATA section: "]]>" becomes "]]]]><![CDATA[>", which a reader joins back into the same characters.

methods.name: act
methods.doc: What an action's callbacks print.

methods.name: text
methods.doc: Everything written so far.

classes.name: Minn\Front\FrontController
classes.doc:
The public site. One catch-all route: resolve the URL, then either
redirect or render, through the active block theme when there is one,
the classic PHP template runner when the theme is classic, and the
interim template otherwise.

constructor.signature: __construct(Minn\Front\Resolver $resolver, Minn\Theme\MainQueryBridge $bridge, Minn\Front\Renderer $renderer, ?Minn\Theme\PageRenderer $theme = NULL, ?Minn\Front\FeedController $feeds = NULL, ?Minn\Cron\Cron $cron = NULL, ?Minn\Theme\ClassicRenderer $classic = NULL, ?Minn\Front\SitemapController $sitemaps = NULL, ?Minn\Theme\EmbedRenderer $embeds = NULL)

methods.name: notFound
methods.doc: The themed (or interim) 404 page.

methods.name: themed
methods.doc:
The themed (or interim) page for a resolution, under its status: the
main query stood first, its 404 (an empty page past the first, an
empty date) taken as the page's.

methods.name: show
methods.doc: The public page for any path; when scheduled work is due, the run follows the response.

methods.name: legacyPackOffer
methods.doc:
A page builder's editor opened on the page it edits (Beaver Builder's
?fl_builder) that needs the Minn Legacy Pack while it is not active:
someone who may edit goes to Minn Admin's offer to install it, and
comes back here once it is. A visitor gets the page as it is.

methods.name: rendered
methods.doc: The page for a resolution: an embed, a sitemap's or feed's query form, else the theme's.

classes.name: Minn\Front\FrontParts
classes.doc:
What the front builds before its routes: the extensions' seams for the
request's reader, the Minn bar they may carry, and the admin's types and
appearance the bar and the shell read. Built once a request, whether the
runtime has booted or not (MINN_WP_API lets an extension route answer
without it), and the extensions register on it once.

methods.name: build
methods.signature: build(Minn\Db $db, Minn\Content\Site $site, Minn\Http\Request $request, Minn\Content\Reader $reader, Minn\Auth\Capabilities $capabilities, Minn\Content\Users $users, Minn\Admin\App $app, mixed $session, Minn\Front\Permalinks $permalinks, string $contentDir): self
methods.doc: The parts for one request's reader: seams carrying the bar, nothing registered on them yet.

methods.name: registered
methods.doc: The seams with every active extension registered on them; the first call registers.

classes.name: Minn\Front\Kind
classes.doc: What a public URL resolved to.

cases.name: Taxonomy
cases.doc: a term archive of a plugin's taxonomy

cases.name: PostTypeArchive
cases.doc: the archive of a plugin's post type

classes.name: Minn\Front\LinksOpml
classes.doc:
wp-links-opml.php: the site's links as an OPML outline, as the reference
prints it (contracts/front/probes.md, "Entry scripts"). The link
categories with links (all of them, or the one link_cat names), each
with its visible links by name; whatever opml_head prints (the generator
comment, by default) in the head. The whitespace is the reference's to
the tab: a category opens flush, each link sits after a tab, and the
run that closes one item opens the next.

methods.name: page
methods.doc: The page for a request's query (its link_cat), under its content type.

methods.name: categoryArgs
methods.doc:
What the categories are asked with: every link category, or the one
link_cat names by its whole number made positive; 'all' is passed on
as it is and finds none, and an empty or '0' link_cat asks for all.

methods.name: category
methods.doc: One category's outline, its visible links inside.

classes.name: Minn\Front\ListingLinks
classes.doc:
The prev/next links a paged listing prints: which page sits either side of
the one being read, and the anchor that points at it. Posts listings and
comment threads both come through here; only the URL builder differs.

methods.name: neighbours
methods.doc:
The page before and after the current one, null past either end. A
listing of one page has neither, which is how the navigation blocks
know to print nothing at all.

methods.name: anchor
methods.doc: The anchor the reference prints. Attributes go in verbatim after the href, and the space that separates them stays even when a caller supplied none, so the markup reads `text`.

methods.name: label
methods.doc:
A navigation label's bare ampersands become entities, while an ampersand
that already opens an entity is left as it is.

methods.name: bareCommentPage
methods.doc:
Which page of a comment thread the bare permalink shows: the first when
the site reads oldest comments first, the last when it reads newest
first. Every other page carries a comment-page-N segment.

The page count is whatever the caller passed and is never filled in from
the query: a caller that does not say how long the thread is gets no
collapse at all under newest-first, because no page matches an unknown
last page.

classes.name: Minn\Front\Maintenance
classes.doc:
Maintenance mode, as hosting tools and updaters switch it on: a
.maintenance file in the webroot whose $upgrading is less than ten minutes
old. While it holds, every request gets the site's own maintenance.php
(which prints its page and stops) or the 503 page; an older file is ignored.

methods.name: answer
methods.doc: The answer while maintenance holds, or null when the site is open.

classes.name: Minn\Front\PageLinks
classes.doc:
The links between the pages of a post split with <!--nextpage-->, as
wp_link_pages writes them (probe placeholders-a). By number: the before
markup, each page (the current one a span, unless the whole post is not
being shown and this is its first page) after a space for the first and
the separator for the rest, the after markup. By next and previous, only
where the whole post is shown: the previous page's link, the separator,
the next page's. Nothing for a post in one page.

methods.name: render
methods.signature: render(array $args, int $page, int $pages, int $more, Closure $open, Closure $filter): string
methods.doc: The links for the page being shown of a split post.
shapes: @param array<string, mixed> $args wp_link_pages's arguments with their defaults
@param Closure(int): string $open the opening anchor of page $i
@param Closure(string, int): string $filter a link through wp_link_pages_link

params.name: more
params.doc: the reference's $more global: 1 when the whole post is shown

classes.name: Minn\Front\Pagination
classes.doc:
Numbered page links in the reference's shape: previous, the end and
middle runs with one ellipsis per gap, the current page as a span, next.

methods.name: links
methods.doc: The page links the reference's paginate_links builds, or null for one page.
shapes: @param Closure(int): string $link the URL for a page number
@return list<string>|null the link elements, null with fewer than two pages

params.name: link
params.doc: the URL for a page number

methods.name: format
methods.doc: The links in the requested shape.

classes.name: Minn\Front\Permalinks
classes.doc:
Builds public URLs from the site's permalink structure. With an empty
structure every link is a query-string form (?p=, ?cat=); with a
structure, published and private posts get their pretty form and every
other status keeps the query form, which is what the reference emits.

constructor.signature: __construct(Minn\Content\Posts $posts, Minn\Content\Terms $terms, string $home, string $structure, int $frontPageId = 0, int $postsPageId = 0, ?Closure $registry = NULL)

constants.name: QUERY_ONLY
constants.doc: Core taxonomies with no front-end archive: their terms link by query only.

methods.name: typeSlug
methods.doc: The rewrite slug a plugin gave its post type, else the type's name.

methods.name: taxonomySlug
methods.doc: The rewrite slug a plugin gave its taxonomy; null for one the engine does not know.

methods.name: forPostTypeArchive
methods.doc: A post type archive's address: its has_archive slug, or the type's slug when has_archive is true.

methods.name: fromDb
methods.doc: Link building from the site's own settings.

methods.name: isPretty
methods.doc: Whether the site uses a permalink structure.

methods.name: url
methods.doc: A URL under the home.

methods.name: feedPath
methods.doc:
A feed's address under a base path ("/", "/category/news/",
"/hello-world/"): feed/ for the default feed (rss2, and rss with it),
feed/<type>/ for another; a comments-<type> feed is its <type>.

methods.name: link
methods.doc:
A post's link as plugins and clients are given it: once the runtime
runs, the reference's, through its link filters (post_link, page_link,
post_type_link, as get_permalink() answers); before, the engine's own.

methods.name: forComment
methods.doc:
A comment's link as plugins and clients are given it: once the
runtime runs, get_comment_link()'s (its paging and its filter, over
the post's filtered link); before, the post's own with the anchor.

methods.name: forPost
methods.doc: A post's permalink, by the engine's own rules (no plugin filters: address matching uses it).

methods.name: forPage
methods.doc: A page's permalink, the home for the front page.

methods.name: pagePath
methods.doc: A page's own pretty path, even for the static front page (its comments feed lives there).

methods.name: forAttachment
methods.doc:
An attachment's public link: its slug under the parent's permalink
when attached, at the root when not, or the query form under plain
permalinks.

methods.name: forTerm
methods.doc: A term's archive URL.

methods.name: forAuthor
methods.doc: An author's archive URL.

methods.name: forDate
methods.doc: A date archive's URL.

methods.name: forSearch
methods.doc: A search's URL.

methods.name: forPaged
methods.doc: A listing URL for a page number.

methods.name: filtered
methods.doc: Whether links go through the reference's filters: once plugins can hook them.

classes.name: Minn\Front\PostEmbed
classes.doc:
A post as other sites embed it, the oEmbed provider side, as the
reference answers (probe oembed): the data (version, the site as
provider, the author or else the site, the title) through
oembed_response_data, whose default makes it "rich" with the embed
markup: a blockquote linking the post, a sandboxed iframe of its /embed/
page carrying a fresh secret, and the inline script that sizes it. Only
a publicly viewable post is embeddable; the width is held between 200
and 600 (oembed_min_max_width) and the height is a 16:9 share of it, at
least 200.

methods.name: data
methods.doc: get_oembed_response_data: the data, or false when the post cannot be embedded. @return array<string, mixed>|false

methods.name: rich
methods.doc: get_oembed_response_data_rich: the size, the markup, and a thumbnail when the post has one. @param array<string, mixed> $data @return array<string, mixed>

methods.name: html
methods.doc: get_post_embed_html: the blockquote, the iframe and its script, through embed_html; false for no post.

methods.name: url
methods.doc: get_post_embed_url: the post's /embed/ address (?embed=true without pretty links), through post_embed_url.

methods.name: xmlDocument
methods.doc: The data as an oEmbed XML document (_oembed_create_xml); false for no data.

methods.name: xml
methods.doc: _oembed_create_xml: the data as an oembed document (or under the root given), nested arrays as nested elements. @param array<string, mixed> $data

classes.name: Minn\Front\PostNavigation
classes.doc:
The links to the posts either side of this one, and the nav block that
wraps them. The caller's format wraps the anchor: `%link` is the whole
anchor, `%title` the post's title and `%date` its date, and the anchor carries rel="prev"
or rel="next".

Titles arrive already filtered; this only assembles.

methods.name: previous
methods.signature: previous(string $url, string $title, string $format, string $linkFormat, string $date = ''): string
methods.doc: A previous or next post link in the reference's format.

methods.name: next
methods.signature: next(string $url, string $title, string $format, string $linkFormat, string $date = ''): string
methods.doc: The next-post link in the reference's format.

methods.name: ariaLabel
methods.doc:
The aria-label a navigation block carries: an explicit one wins,
otherwise a caller-supplied screen-reader text stands in for it, and
only with neither does the default apply.
shapes: @param array<string, mixed> $args the caller's own arguments

methods.name: link
methods.signature: link(string $url, string $title, string $format, string $linkFormat, string $rel, string $date): string

classes.name: Minn\Front\PrintedResponse
classes.doc:
A response WordPress's handlers print themselves (a sitemap, robots.txt),
as the reference serves them: the main query stood with the request's own
variables and the front-end steps around it, then $print; what was
printed, under the status and headers the handlers sent. A handler that
ends the request early (Printed, where the reference exits) ends it here
too; when none did and there is nothing to print, null, and the theme
renders the page on the query as it stands.

methods.name: stand
methods.doc: The request served this way, or null for the theme to render.
shapes: @param array<string, mixed> $vars the request's own query variables

classes.name: Minn\Front\ProbeController
classes.doc:
The surface monitors, crawlers, and hosting checks hit that is not a
page: robots.txt, the XML-RPC and cron endpoints, the admin entry point,
and the favicon. Feeds and sitemaps have controllers of their own.

methods.name: robots
xmlrpc
methods.doc: XML-RPC is not served; GET answers the way the reference does, POST is refused outright.

methods.name: cron
methods.doc:
wp-cron.php: runs what is due. DISABLE_WP_CRON stops only the runs page
loads start; a host that sets it calls this from its own scheduler, and
the call still runs, as on the reference (cron suite).

methods.name: admin
methods.doc: The admin is Minn Admin; the reference's admin path lands there.

methods.name: favicon
methods.doc: The site icon, or the reference's default.

classes.name: Minn\Front\QueryMoves
classes.doc:
Where the root's archive query forms move under pretty permalinks, as
the reference's canonical redirect answers them (suite permalinks): a
feed (?feed=) first, then a date (?m=, ?year=), then an author by id, then a term when the
query names exactly one taxonomy (?cat= or ?category_name=, ?tag=,
?taxonomy= with ?term=, a registered taxonomy's own var; ?post_format=
counts as one but never moves itself), each to its pretty address with
the other arguments along. A page of listing asked as ?paged= (a
feed's first page aside) moves to the pretty page instead: a term's to
that page of the term, anything else, a date or an author too, to that
page of the root with the date's and author's arguments left behind
(/?m=2026&paged=2 to /page/2/, /?paged=1 to /). Nothing moves while a
search is asked for (?s=, even empty), or to something the site does not
have. The singles' forms are SingleQueries'.

methods.name: for
methods.doc: The move a root request's query string makes; null when it makes none.

methods.name: paged
methods.doc:
The move a root request asking for a page of listing as ?paged= makes
(the caller asks only when the page as typed is one the site has): a
term's to that page of the term, anything else to that page of the
root, a date's and an author's arguments left behind. Null when it asks
for none, or for a search.

methods.name: askedPage
methods.doc:
The page of listing a query string asks for as ?paged=, as a whole
number read the way the reference reads it (02, -2 and 2x are 2); 0
when it asks for none (absent, 0, not a number, not one value).

methods.name: feed
methods.doc:
?feed=: the feed at its pretty address: a comments feed under
/comments/, one taxonomy's term's under the term, any other the
site's, an author or date asked with it left behind. A feed's later
page stays asked for (?paged=2), its first is dropped. An unknown kind
of feed moves nowhere.

methods.name: term
methods.doc: The one taxonomy's term the query names, at its pretty address.

methods.name: oneTerm
methods.doc:
The term of the one taxonomy the query names, with the arguments that
name it; null when it names none, more than one, or a term the site
does not have.

classes.name: Minn\Front\RecordedRedirect
classes.doc:
The redirect the runtime recorded for this request (wp_redirect and its
safe variant record it, the reference exits after sending it), as the
response the engine sends: the location under its status with the
X-Redirect-By a caller named, or a blank page when a plugin's filter
emptied the location.

methods.name: response
methods.doc: The recorded redirect as a response, or a blank page when there is no location left to send.

classes.name: Minn\Front\Redirects
classes.doc:
Whether a resolution may answer with a canonical redirect. A GET or HEAD
follows them (the trailing slash, the pretty permalink for ?p=, the
guessed destination); any other method holds and resolves the path as
typed, as the reference's redirect_canonical bails on a POST.

methods.name: forMethod
methods.doc: The mode a request's method allows.

methods.name: forRequest
methods.doc: The mode for a request: its method's (a feed's query form moves too, under the site's own host).

methods.name: follows
methods.doc: Whether a canonical redirect may be answered.

classes.name: Minn\Front\Renderer
classes.doc:
The interim public theme: one clean template until the block-theme
reader lands. The body-class tokens are the contract (stylesheets and
crawlers key off them); the markup around them is engine-defined.

constants.name: CSS
constants.value: ':root { color-scheme: light dark; } body { margin: 0; font: 17px/1.6 "Hanken Grotesk", "Helvetica Neue", sans-serif; background: #fbfbfc; color: #1a1a1f; } @media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) { body { background: #0b0b0d; color: #ececed; } } .site-header, main, .site-footer { max-width: 680px; margin: 0 auto; padding: 0 24px; } .site-header { padding-top: 32px; } .site-title { font-weight: 800; letter-spacing: -0.02em; text-decoration: none; color: inherit; font-size: 20px; } main { padding-top: 40px; padding-bottom: 40px; } h1 { font-size: 36px; letter-spacing: -0.02em; line-height: 1.15; margin: 0 0 24px; } .post-list { list-style: none; margin: 0; padding: 0; } .post-list li { padding: 18px 0; border-top: 1px solid rgba(128,128,140,0.25); } .post-list a { font-weight: 600; color: inherit; text-decoration: none; font-size: 20px; } .post-list time { display: block; font-size: 13px; opacity: 0.6; } .post-list p { margin: 6px 0 0; opacity: 0.85; } .entry-content img { max-width: 100%; height: auto; } .site-footer { padding-bottom: 32px; font: 12px/1.6 "JetBrains Mono", monospace; opacity: 0.6; }'

methods.name: bodyClasses
methods.doc:
The body classes the main query stands for (Theme\QueryClasses);
none before one stands.

methods.name: render
methods.doc: The interim page for a resolution, without a theme: a listing shows the main query's page of posts.

methods.name: archive
shapes: @return array{0: string, 1: string} title and markup

classes.name: Minn\Front\RequestParse
classes.doc:
The query vars the reference's request parse sets for an address
(WP::parse_request), which plugins read off $wp->query_vars and
get_query_var: each public var the query string or form carries, else
the one the matched rewrite rule set (Front\RuleTable), all in the
public vars' order (a plugin's own after the core ones); a post type's
own var brings post_type and name; a path no rule matches is error=404
(the query string's error is ignored).

methods.name: vars
methods.doc: The parse's vars, in the reference's order.
shapes: @param array<string, string> $rule the matched rule's vars
@param list<string> $publicVars the public query vars, after the query_vars filter
@param array<string, mixed> $given the query string's and the form's values

params.name: publicVars
params.doc: the public query vars, after the query_vars filter

params.name: given
params.doc: the query string's and the form's values

methods.name: mismatch
methods.doc:
Whether the query string and the form give a public var two different
values: the reference refuses such a request (A variable mismatch has
been detected, a 400) before it reads either.

methods.name: queryString
methods.doc: The reference's query string for parse vars (WP::build_query_string): each one with a value, encoded.

classes.name: Minn\Front\Resolution
classes.doc:
The outcome of resolving a public URL: which kind of thing it names,
the record behind it, the page number for paginated views, and the query
vars of the rewrite rule the address matched (what the request parse
hands plugins). Redirects carry their target instead.

constructor.signature: __construct(Minn\Front\Kind $kind, Minn\Content\PostRecord|Minn\Content\UserRecord|Minn\Content\TermRecord|array|null $record = NULL, int $paged = 1, ?string $location = NULL, int $status = 200, ?string $search = NULL, ?array $date = NULL, ?string $authorName = NULL, bool $front = false, bool $preview = false, bool $postsPage = false, array $vars = array ( ))
shapes: @param array<string, mixed>|PostRecord|UserRecord|null $record the post, term, or user row

params.name: record
params.doc: the post, term, or user row

properties.name: front
properties.doc: the static front page (show_on_front = page), rendered as a page that is also home

properties.name: preview
properties.doc: a preview: the reader's autosave replaces the stored content

properties.name: postsPage
properties.doc: the posts page (page_for_posts): the record is the page, the listing is the blog

methods.name: asPreview
methods.doc: The same resolution marked as a preview.

methods.name: withVars
methods.doc: The same resolution reached through a rule with these query vars. @param array<string, string> $vars

methods.name: home
methods.doc: The home listing.

methods.name: single
methods.doc: A single post or page.

methods.name: frontPage
methods.doc: The static front page.

methods.name: postsPage
methods.doc: The page that stands for the blog: a home listing whose record is the page.

methods.name: term
methods.doc: A category or tag archive.

methods.name: taxonomy
methods.doc: A plugin taxonomy's term archive; the record is the term row (with its taxonomy).

methods.name: postTypeArchive
methods.doc: A plugin post type's archive; the record is the registered type (name, label, ...).

methods.name: author
methods.doc: An author archive.

methods.name: date
methods.doc: A date archive.

methods.name: search
methods.doc: A search.

methods.name: redirect
methods.doc: A redirect.

methods.name: id
methods.doc: The record's id, post or term.

classes.name: Minn\Front\Resolver
classes.doc:
Turns a public URL into a Resolution the way the reference's request
parse does: the root by its query string, any other path by the first
of the site's rewrite rules it fits (Front\RuleTable), whose query vars
name what it is (Front\RuleRoutes). What is left here are the
reference's canonical answers around that (redirect_canonical,
wp_old_slug_redirect):

- Unpaged content and archives without a trailing slash redirect to the
slashed form, as typed (case kept), as do an embed's and an endpoint's
addresses; paged views, search, and 404s do not.
- Query-var forms redirect to the pretty form when the target is
public: a single's (?p=, ?page_id=, ?name=, ?pagename=; SingleQueries)
and an archive's (?m=, ?year=, ?author=, one taxonomy's term;
QueryMoves), unless a search is asked for.
- A single asked for under a category it is not in (where the
structure names one), or with an old-style page number, moves to its
own address; a trackback address goes to the post; the front page
answers only at the root.
- A name the site no longer has: the post that used to have it, else the
closest published page or post whose name starts with it, pages before
posts, newest first. Archives never guess.
- Non-public posts are 404 to anonymous readers and served to a reader
who can edit them.

methods.name: fromDb
methods.doc: A resolver over the site's own settings.

methods.name: permalinks
methods.doc: The link builder.

methods.name: perPage
methods.doc: Posts per page.

methods.name: resolve
viewableTypes
methods.doc:
The post types a guess looks among: those a reader can view that
searches include.

methods.name: canonical
methods.doc:
The canonical answer for what a path's rule found: the found thing
as typed, or where it should be asked for instead.

methods.name: pagedMove
methods.doc:
A listing page that is not one: a post (not a page) asked for with a
page of listing (/hello-world/page/2/, ?paged=2) moves to the post, the
rest of the query along but that; a page of listing or of a page asked
as ?paged= moves to its pretty page, the query's number over the
path's (/2026/?paged=2 to /2026/page/2/, /page/3/?paged=1 to /); the
first page of any listing or page drops its /page/1/. Null when none
applies.

methods.name: missing
methods.doc:
A name the site does not have: where the post that used to have it
lives now (as typed too, where wp_old_slug_redirect makes the move),
else, on a single's rule, the closest match. Null when there is none.

methods.name: endpointIn
methods.doc: Whether the vars carry a rewrite endpoint's var. @param array<string, string> $vars

methods.name: resolveQueryVars
methods.doc:
The root by its query string, in the grammar a path's rule vars are
read in (RuleRoutes): a single's vars first (SingleQueries makes
their moves), then the archive forms that move (QueryMoves), then
what the vars name, an id form read as the name it stands for.

methods.name: rootVars
methods.doc:
The root's query vars as RuleRoutes reads them: the query string's
(error is not the query string's to set), ?cat= as the category's
slug, ?author= as the author's name, ?m= as its year, month and day.
Null when an id names nothing the site has.

methods.name: archives
methods.doc: The archives a request may stand for.

methods.name: attachments
methods.doc: The addresses an attachment's page answers to.

methods.name: elsewhere
methods.doc: The addresses a single answers to besides its own.

classes.name: Minn\Front\ResourceHints
classes.doc:
The resource hint links wp_head prints (wp_resource_hints): each relation
(dns-prefetch, preconnect, prefetch, prerender) handed to the filter with
what the engine found, its entries printed once each. A plain address
prints rel first; an entry given as attributes prints its href, the
attributes the reference keeps (as, crossorigin, pr, type; a bare word
for a numeric key) and rel last. dns-prefetch names only the host,
preconnect the scheme and host, the others the whole address (probe
media-template-doubts).

methods.name: render
methods.doc: The links, one a line.
shapes: @param list<string> $dnsPrefetch the external hosts the queued assets use
@param Closure(array, string): mixed $filter the wp_resource_hints filter

params.name: dnsPrefetch
params.doc: the external hosts the queued assets use

methods.name: address
methods.doc: An entry's address as its relation names it.

classes.name: Minn\Front\RuleRoutes
classes.doc:
What a matched rewrite rule's query vars name, as the reference's main
query reads them (suites permalinks, plugin-rules, request-vars): a post
or page by id, an attachment by name, a page (or an attachment) by its
path, a post by name (of the type the vars give), a registered type's
item by its own var; else a search, a category's, tag's, post
format's or registered taxonomy's archive, an author's, a date's, a
post type's; else the front. A rule that set error is a 404, as is a single
the reader may not read. Under a name the date or category the rule also
captured does not narrow the find: where the post really lives is the
canonical redirect's business.

shapes: @param Closure(PostRecord): bool $readable whether the reader may read a post

params.name: readable
params.doc: whether the reader may read a post

methods.name: resolve
methods.doc: The resolution the vars stand for. @param array<string, string> $vars

methods.name: single
methods.doc: A single the vars name; null when they name none. @param array<string, string> $vars

methods.name: archive
methods.doc:
The archive the vars name, the front when they name none: a search
first (whatever else they name, as the reference's templates
choose), a term's, an author's, a date's, a post type's when they
give one and nothing else.

methods.name: typeArchive
methods.doc: A post type's archive, when it has one; the front's listing (of that type) when it has none.

methods.name: found
methods.doc:
A found post as the reader may see it: the static front page, the
posts page (the blog's listing), any other post or page; a 404 when
there is none or the reader may not read it (an attachment as its
parent is).

methods.name: readable
methods.doc: Whether the reader may read a post; an attachment as its parent is, a loose one as it stands.

methods.name: registered
methods.doc:
The registered post types or taxonomies that answer to a var of their
own, among those a visitor may query (the reference keeps no other's
var public): name => var.

classes.name: Minn\Front\RuleTable
classes.doc:
An address read as WordPress's request parse reads it (suites
permalinks, request-vars, plugin-rules): against the site's rewrite
rules (made and stored when there are none, a plugin's own among them,
each place's endpoints too), the first rule the address fits winning, as
typed or decoded; a page's rule fits only when a page stands at the path
it captured, under verbose page rules. A match is the rule's query vars
with the matches put in. Which of them count is the request parse's
business (the public vars, after the query_vars filter).

methods.name: vars
methods.doc:
The vars the site's rules give a path, or null when no rule fits it
(or the site has none: plain permalinks).

methods.name: match
methods.doc:
What the request parse makes of a path (WP::parse_request): the path
under the home's, the rule it fits and that rule's query with the
matches put in, and its vars; the rule and query empty when none
fits. Null when the site has no rules (plain permalinks).
shapes: @return array{request: string, rule: string, query: string, vars: array<string, string>}|null

methods.name: subject
methods.doc: The address as the rules read it: under the home's own path, without the slashes at its ends.

methods.name: first
methods.doc:
The first rule an address fits, as typed or decoded; a page's rule
only when a page is at the path it captured, under verbose page rules.
shapes: @param Closure(string): bool $pageAt whether a page stands at a path

params.name: pageAt
params.doc: whether a page stands at a path

methods.name: queryOf
methods.doc:
A matched rule's query with the matches put in (urlencoded, so a
captured "&x=1" cannot split into extra vars).

methods.name: pageAt
methods.doc: Whether a page stands at a path (not one in the trash).

classes.name: Minn\Front\SingleAddresses
classes.doc:
The addresses a single answers to besides its own, as the reference
treats them: a slug the post used to have (alone, with a page number, or
with an embed or trackback suffix), and an address that puts it under a
category it is not in.

methods.name: formerSlug
methods.doc:
A slug a post used to have redirects to where the post lives now,
keeping the page number and dropping the query string; the lookup
ignores status because the reference does (unreadable posts land on
their `?p=` form and answer 404 there).

methods.name: misplaced
methods.doc:
Whether a post was asked for under a category it is not in, where
the structure names the category: the category the address names is
none at that path, or not one of the post's. The reference finds the
post by its name whatever the category, then moves to its own
address (a post in two categories answers under either).

methods.name: formerSuffix
methods.doc:
A former slug asked for with a suffix: embed follows the post to its
new embed address, trackback goes to the post itself. The front
page's redirect to the root keeps its own handling.

classes.name: Minn\Front\SingleQueries
classes.doc:
The single a query string asks for, as the reference's request parse and
canonical redirect answer it: by id (?p=, ?page_id=, any viewable type's;
an attachment's goes to its own page), an attachment by id or slug (?attachment_id=,
?attachment=), a post by slug (?name=), a page by path (?pagename=).
With canonical redirects on, an address that is not the single's own
moves there, the other query arguments along; without, each var is
strict about the type it finds.

methods.name: find
methods.doc: The resolution the query's single vars amount to; null when it has none of them.

methods.name: byId
methods.doc: ?p= or ?page_id=: the post or page (an attachment to its own page), moving to its pretty address.

methods.name: byPath
methods.doc: ?pagename=: the page at that path (the front page moves to the root), else one by the last slug.

classes.name: Minn\Front\SitemapController
classes.doc:
The sitemap index, its pages, and the two stylesheets, as the
reference serves them: the request's sitemap variables stand
in the main query and the sitemaps server answers at template_redirect
(SitemapRequest), through every filter a plugin hooks, any provider it
registers among them; what it does not print, the theme renders (a 404,
or the page a stray address amounts to).

methods.name: sitemapIndex
methods.doc: The sitemap index.

methods.name: sitemap
methods.doc: One sitemap page: a provider's name, its subtype when it has them, and the page.

methods.name: sitemapStylesheet
methods.doc: The sitemap stylesheet.

methods.name: sitemapIndexStylesheet
methods.doc: The sitemap index stylesheet.

methods.name: queried
methods.doc: The query form (?sitemap=, ?sitemap-stylesheet=) on the front page, with plugins loaded.

methods.name: served
methods.doc:
The reference's answer: what the sitemaps server printed, else the
theme's page on the query as it stands (a 404 when the server made it
one).

classes.name: Minn\Front\SitemapRequest
classes.doc:
A sitemap request at template_redirect, as the reference's sitemaps
server answers it: a sitemap address asked for another way (the query
form, page 0) moves to its own; with the sitemaps off, a provider nobody
registered, or a subtype or page that has nothing, the request is a 404
the theme renders; otherwise the stylesheet, the index or the provider's
page is printed and the request ends. Since 7.1.3 this is where a
sitemap page is judged: the main query no longer makes an empty page a
404 first, so a page a plugin fills past the page count still prints.

methods.name: url
methods.doc: A sitemap's address (get_sitemap_url): the index, or a provider's page of a subtype; false for one that is not there.

methods.name: canonical
methods.doc: The canonical step: a sitemap asked for by another address is sent to its own.

methods.name: serve
methods.doc: What the sitemaps server does with the request (render_sitemaps).

methods.name: page
methods.doc: One provider's page: printed, or a 404 when it has nothing (a subtype not the provider's gives nothing).

methods.name: notFound
methods.doc: The main query made a 404, which the theme renders.

classes.name: Minn\Front\SitemapXml
classes.doc:
The two sitemap documents, index and URL set, from entry maps; one
builder for the engine's routes and the facade's renderer. An element
with nothing inside closes itself, at every level, as the reference's
XML writer prints it (probe sitemap-classes).

methods.name: index
methods.doc: A sitemap index document.
shapes: @param list<array<string, string|null>> $entries each a map of element name => text; null values are skipped

params.name: entries
params.doc: each a map of element name => text; null values are skipped

methods.name: urlset
methods.doc: A sitemap urlset document.

methods.name: stylesheet
methods.doc: The processing instruction naming a stylesheet, as the renderer keeps it; nothing for no address.

methods.name: element
methods.doc: One element: closed on itself when empty.

methods.name: document
methods.doc: The document: the XML declaration, the stylesheet instruction when there is one, the body.

classes.name: Minn\Front\Sitemaps
classes.doc:
What the sitemaps share with WP_Sitemaps, which serves them: the two
stylesheets browsers get when they open a sitemap, their CSS
(wp_sitemaps_stylesheet_css filters it), the date form an entry's
lastmod takes, and the line robots.txt names the index by.

constants.name: CSS
constants.doc: The stylesheets' own CSS (wp_sitemaps_stylesheet_css filters it when plugins are loaded).

methods.name: robots
methods.doc: robots.txt with the index's Sitemap line after it, on a public site; as it was on one hidden from search.

methods.name: stylesheet
methods.doc: The engine's own stylesheet for browsers that open a sitemap.

methods.name: indexStylesheet
methods.doc: The stylesheet the sitemap index links: one column, the sitemaps.

methods.name: w3c
methods.doc: A GMT date as a sitemap dates it: W3C, in the site's timezone (probe blocks-rest-widget-doubts).

classes.name: Minn\Front\TermLists
classes.doc:
A term's parent chain and the tag cloud, built from term rows the caller
already fetched and links the caller resolves. The category list and
select are the walkers' (Walker_Category, Walker_CategoryDropdown).

methods.name: parentChain
methods.doc:
The chain of names from the outermost ancestor down to the term itself,
each one separated and optionally wrapped in its own link. The separator
trails the last name too, so a breadcrumb reads "Root/Mid/Leaf/".
shapes: @param list<array{name: string, slug: string, link: string}> $line outermost first, the term itself last

params.name: line
params.shape: list<array{name: string, slug: string, link: string}>
params.doc: outermost first, the term itself last

methods.name: tagCloud
methods.doc:
The tag cloud the reference prints, or null for none: the tags sorted
and cut to the number asked for (cloudTags), each one's entry
(cloudData), and the links (cloudMarkup). Each row brings its "id"
(for the tag-link class; its key when it has none), "scaled" (its count
through the scale callback), "text" (the count in words, for the
label), and its link already escaped.

methods.name: cloudTags
methods.doc:
The tags in the cloud's order (by name, or by count; RAND shuffles)
and cut to the number asked for. Keys survive the sort; taking the
first N renumbers the numeric ones before they name the tags.

methods.name: cloudData
methods.doc:
Each tag's entry, as wp_generate_tag_cloud_data is handed them (probe
filter-inputs): id, url, role, name, the count in words and as a
number, the link class, the font size, the label attribute and the
shown count. Sizes step from smallest to largest across the scaled
counts; a reversed range steps by one unit; an empty one leaves every
tag the same size and drops the label, unless the counts are shown.
shapes: @param array<array-key, array<string, mixed>> $tags in the cloud's order

methods.name: cloudMarkup
methods.doc:
The cloud from its entries (whatever wp_generate_tag_cloud_data made
of them), in the format asked for, or null for none.

methods.name: sorted
methods.doc:
By name (natural, case-insensitive) only for "name"; every other value
sorts by count. Only "DESC", in capitals, reverses; the order "RAND"
shuffles (probe taxonomy-blocks-user-doubts).

classes.name: Minn\Front\ToolbarMarkup
classes.doc:
WP_Admin_Bar's markup, piece by piece, as the reference prints it (probe
admin-bar): the wrapper (a skip link until the page has opened its body,
a class for phones), a group's list (named by the menu it opens from),
and an item: a link or an empty div, its focus order, its attributes
from meta, an arrow when it opens a menu below the top level, and any
markup a plugin hangs after it.

constants.name: ATTRIBUTES
constants.doc: The meta keys an item carries onto its link or div, in the reference's order.

methods.name: open
methods.doc: The bar's wrapper up to its first group.

methods.name: close
methods.doc: The bar's wrapper after its last group.

methods.name: groupOpen
methods.doc: A group's opening list tag, labelled by the menu it opens from when that has a menu title.

methods.name: itemOpen
methods.doc: An item up to its submenu: the list item, then its link (or a div when it has none) with its title.

methods.name: itemClose
methods.doc: An item after its submenu: any markup a plugin hangs on it, and the list item's end.

classes.name: Minn\Front\ToolbarMenus
classes.doc:
The nodes WordPress puts on the toolbar itself, as the reference adds
them on the front end for whoever is signed in (probe admin-bar): the
account menu, the WordPress menu, the site menu with its appearance
group, the site editor and customizer links, updates, comments, new
content, the edit link for what the page shows, the shortlink, the
secondary groups, and the search box. Each is one admin_bar_menu
callback, so plugins can unhook any of them by name.

classes.name: Minn\Front\ToolbarTree
classes.doc:
WP_Admin_Bar's nodes bound into the tree they print as, as the reference
binds them (probe admin-bar): each gains its children and its type; an
item's children go into its "-default" group, made when the first one
arrives; a group inside a group sits next to it in a "-container", put
where the outer group was; a node whose parent is missing is left out.
The bar's own node accessors are used throughout, so a subclass that
overrides them still sees every node it is asked for.

methods.name: bind
methods.doc:
The root of the bound tree, for nodes (the bar's, a root among them)
reached through the bar's accessors.

methods.name: place
methods.doc: A node into its parent's children, through a default group or a container when it needs one.

methods.name: defaultGroup
methods.doc: The group an item's child items go into, made the first time.

methods.name: container
methods.doc: The container a group shares with the groups inside it, put where the group was.

classes.name: Minn\Html
classes.doc:
HTML, the front door for escaping and cutting markup: plain static calls,
one import away (use Minn\Html;), the way Minn\Http and Minn\Json are.
Escaping at output boundaries goes through here.

constants.name: SPLIT
constants.doc: Markup's pieces of HTML: comments and CDATA whole (to the end when unclosed), else from "<" to the next ">".

methods.name: checked
methods.doc: The checked attribute when the two agree as text (checked), else nothing.

methods.name: selected
methods.doc: The selected attribute when the two agree as text (selected), else nothing.

methods.name: chosen
methods.doc: An attribute of the given name when the two agree as text, else nothing.

methods.name: split
methods.doc:
Markup cut into text and HTML pieces, the HTML ones at the odd
positions (wp_html_split): a comment or CDATA section is one piece
whatever it holds, and a "<" in text starts a piece that runs to the
next ">".

methods.name: esc
methods.doc: Text escaped for HTML.

methods.name: encodeAll
methods.doc: Every special and both quotes encoded, references included (an invalid UTF-8 string gives nothing): esc_textarea's encoding.

methods.name: attr
methods.doc: Text escaped for an attribute value.

methods.name: addClasses
methods.doc:
Appends classes to the first element in a fragment (or to the first
element already carrying $onClass), adding a class attribute when
the element has none. Existing classes keep their order.

methods.name: stripAllTags
methods.doc: Drops script and style elements with their contents, then every other tag; whitespace runs optionally collapse to one space.

methods.name: textField
methods.doc:
A single line of plain text from user input: tags stripped, control
whitespace folded, percent escapes removed. The caller passes its own
UTF-8 check and less-than encoder so its filters keep applying.

methods.name: scriptBody
methods.doc:
The code inside markup that is exactly one bare script element once the
surrounding whitespace is gone, or null for anything else: a tag with
attributes, an empty element, a missing end. The tag names match in any
case and the code is returned as written.

classes.name: Minn\Html\Decoder
classes.doc:
Character reference decoding for text and attribute values: numeric and
named references, the legacy names that work without a semicolon (not in
an attribute when an "=" or alphanumeric follows), unknown ones left as is.

constants.name: LEGACY
constants.doc: The named references that decode without a semicolon (the HTML standard's legacy list).

methods.name: text
methods.doc: Text with its character references decoded.

methods.name: attribute
methods.doc: An attribute value with its character references decoded.

methods.name: reference
methods.doc:
The character reference at $at in a context ("data" or "attribute"):
its text and how many bytes it spans, or null when none decodes there.

methods.name: char
methods.doc: The UTF-8 text for a code point, U+FFFD for one that cannot be a character, Windows-1252's for the C1 range.

classes.name: Minn\Html\Edits
classes.doc:
The edits pending on the current token: attribute sets and removals,
class additions and removals, and a text replacement, in call order.
They answer reads before they are written, and become the source
replacements the reader splices in when it moves on.

methods.name: validName
methods.doc: Whether an attribute name may be set at all, by the reference's rules.

methods.name: setAttribute
methods.doc: Records a set; setting class outright forgets the class edits before it.

methods.name: setEscapedAttribute
methods.doc: Records an attribute value that comes already escaped (a URL through esc_url), written as it is.

methods.name: removeAttribute
methods.doc: Records a removal of an attribute the source has.

methods.name: cancelAttribute
methods.doc: Forgets a pending set that never reached the source: cancelling an addition is not a removal.

methods.name: attribute
methods.doc: The pending set or removal for a lowercase name, or null when there is none. @return array{name: string, value: string|true|null}|null

methods.name: addClass
methods.doc: Records a class to add; a later removal of the same class wins.

methods.name: removeClass
methods.doc: Records a class to remove; a later addition of the same class wins.

methods.name: hasClassEdits
methods.doc: Whether any class edit is pending.

methods.name: hasTagEdits
methods.doc: Whether any attribute or class edit is pending.

methods.name: classesAfter
methods.doc:
The class list after the pending edits: additions appended once,
removals gone.

methods.name: closesComment
methods.doc: Whether text holds a comment closer, "-->" or "--!>".

methods.name: setTextFor
methods.doc:
Records a text replacement for a token of a kind that takes one: text
(escaped), an ordinary HTML comment, or a raw-text element's body
(script and style bodies get their closers escaped). False when the
kind takes none, or the text would end the element early.

params.name: tagName
params.doc: the lowercase tag name of an opening tag, null for anything else

methods.name: takeText
methods.doc: The pending text replacement, taken: it is cleared on read.

methods.name: takeReplacements
methods.doc:
The source replacements the attribute and class edits amount to, and
forgets them: a changed attribute is rewritten in place (its duplicates
removed), a removed one is cut, a new one is inserted after the tag name
(several in the order of their text).
shapes: @param list<array{name: string, lower: string, start: int, end: int, value: ?string}> $attributes the tag's own
@return list<array{int, int, string}> start, end, text

params.name: attributes
params.shape: list<array{name: string, lower: string, start: int, end: int, value: ?string}>

methods.name: clear
methods.doc: Forgets everything pending.

methods.name: splice
methods.signature: splice(string $html, array $replacements, array $bookmarks, int $tokenStart, int $tokenEnd): array
methods.doc:
Splices replacements into the source, ascending, and moves the bookmarks
and the cursor by what the token at [$tokenStart, $tokenEnd] gained or lost.
shapes: @return array{0: string, 1: array<string, array{0: int, 1: int}>, 2: int} the source, the bookmarks, the cursor

methods.name: classValue
methods.doc: The class attribute's decoded value before class edits: a pending set, else the source's; null when there is none.

methods.name: classList
methods.doc: The class names before class edits.

methods.name: rebuiltClassValue
methods.doc: The class attribute after edits: source order and inner whitespace kept, removed classes gone with the space before them, additions appended.

classes.name: Minn\Html\Escaped
classes.doc: An attribute value that comes already escaped (a URL through esc_url), written as it is.

classes.name: Minn\Html\Scanner
classes.doc:
Reads one token's shape out of raw HTML at an offset: a tag with its
name and attributes, a comment of one of the reference's kinds, a
doctype, or a processing instruction. Pure and stateless; null means the
input ends before the token does, which is where a streaming reader pauses.

methods.name: tag
methods.doc:
A tag starting at $at, its name from $nameStart (one byte in for an
opener, two for a closer): the name, where it ends, the end offset,
the attributes with their source offsets, and the self-closing flag.
shapes: @return array{name: string, nameEnd: int, end: int, attributes: list<array{name: string, lower: string, start: int, end: int, value: ?string, quoted: bool}>, selfClosing: bool}|null

methods.name: rawText
methods.doc:
A raw-text element's body (script, style, textarea, ...): from $from to
its closing tag, or null when the closer never comes.
shapes: @return array{textStart: int, textLength: int, end: int}|null

methods.name: markupDeclaration
methods.doc:
What "<!" opens at $at: an HTML comment (abruptly closed or not), a
doctype, a CDATA lookalike, or a bogus comment.
shapes: @return array{kind: string, start: int, end: int, textStart: int, textLength: int, commentType?: string, fullStart?: int, fullLength?: int}|null

methods.name: question
methods.doc:
What "<?" opens at $at: a processing instruction when an ASCII
alphanumeric target (not "xml") is followed by space, "?" or ">"
(its text after the space, up to "?>" or ">"); a PI lookalike comment
for another XML name closed by "?>"; otherwise an invalid comment.
shapes: @return array{kind: string, start: int, end: int, textStart: int, textLength: int, target?: string, commentType?: string, fullStart?: int, fullLength?: int}|null

methods.name: attributeValue
methods.doc: A source attribute's decoded value (true when it has none), or null when the tag lacks it.

methods.name: opensMarkup
methods.doc: Whether the "<" at $at opens markup: a tag, a closer, "<!" or "<?".

methods.name: textEnd
methods.doc: Where text starting at $at ends: at the next "<" that opens markup, before a "<" ending the input, or at the end.

methods.name: cdata
methods.doc: A CDATA section in foreign content, "<![CDATA[" to "]]>"; null when it does not close.
shapes: @return array{kind: string, start: int, end: int, textStart: int, textLength: int}|null

methods.name: doctype
methods.doc: A doctype's body split into its name and public and system identifiers.

methods.name: isSpace
methods.doc: Whether a byte is HTML whitespace.

methods.name: attribute
methods.doc:
One attribute from $i: its name (a leading "=" is part of it), then an
optional quoted or bare value. Null when the input ends first.
shapes: @return array{int, string, int, int, ?string, bool}|null offset after, name, start, end, value, quoted

methods.name: comment
methods.signature: comment(int $start, int $end, int $textStart, int $textLength, string $type, int $fullStart, int $fullLength): array
shapes: @return array{kind: string, start: int, end: int, textStart: int, textLength: int, commentType: string, fullStart: int, fullLength: int}

classes.name: Minn\Html\TagQuery

A tag processor's next_tag() query: a tag name (any case), a class, the
nth match to stop at, and whether closers count.

methods.name: from
methods.doc: The query read from the array a caller passes.
shapes: @param array{tag_name?: ?string, class_name?: ?string, match_offset?: int, tag_closers?: string} $query

params.name: query
params.shape: array{tag_name?: ?string, class_name?: ?string, match_offset?: int, tag_closers?: string}

classes.name: Minn\Html\Tags
classes.doc:
A streaming HTML tokenizer with in-place edits: every token in document order, attributes decoded,
edits applied to the source without reserialising the rest, bookmarks to seek back to (probe html-tag-processor).

constants.name: RAW_TEXT
constants.doc: Elements whose body is raw text up to the closer.

properties.name: afterPre
properties.doc: Whether a text token here drops one leading line break (it follows a PRE or LISTING opener).

methods.name: nextToken
methods.doc: Advances to the next token; false at the end or at an incomplete one.

methods.name: nextTag
methods.doc: Advances to the next tag matching the query; false when none. @param array{tag_name?: ?string, class_name?: ?string, match_offset?: int, tag_closers?: string} $query
shapes: @param array{tag_name?: ?string, class_name?: ?string, match_offset?: int, tag_closers?: string} $query

params.name: query
params.shape: array{tag_name?: ?string, class_name?: ?string, match_offset?: int, tag_closers?: string}

methods.name: pausedAtIncompleteToken
methods.doc: Whether the scan stopped inside an unfinished token.

methods.name: tokenType
methods.doc: The current token's kind.

methods.name: tokenName
methods.doc: The current token's name.

methods.name: tag
methods.doc: The current tag name, upper-cased; a processing instruction's target, or a PI lookalike's, as written.

methods.name: isCloser
methods.doc: Whether the current tag is a closer.

methods.name: selfClosing
methods.doc: Whether the current tag has the self-closing flag.

methods.name: commentType
methods.doc: The current comment's kind.

methods.name: fullCommentText
methods.doc: The current comment's whole text (a funky comment's is its text).

methods.name: modifiableText
methods.doc: The current token's text as a reader sees it.

methods.name: doctype
methods.doc: Doctype pieces, or null when the token is not a doctype. @return array{name: ?string, public: ?string, system: ?string}|null

methods.name: attribute
methods.doc: The decoded value, true for a bare attribute, null when absent; a pending edit answers first.

methods.name: attributeNames
methods.doc: The current tag's attribute names with a prefix, lower-cased, in source order; null off a tag. @return list<string>|null

methods.name: classes
methods.doc: The current tag's classes. @return list<string> distinct class names after pending edits
shapes: @return list<string> distinct class names after pending edits

methods.name: hasClass
methods.doc: Whether the current tag has a class.

methods.name: setAttribute
methods.doc: Sets an attribute on the current tag.

methods.name: removeAttribute
methods.doc: Removes an attribute from the current tag.

methods.name: addClass
methods.doc: Adds a class to the current tag.

methods.name: removeClass
methods.doc: Removes a class from the current tag.

methods.name: setModifiableText
methods.doc: Replaces the current token's text, when its kind allows it.

methods.name: setBookmark
methods.doc: Names the current token's position.

methods.name: releaseBookmark
methods.doc: Forgets a bookmark.

methods.name: hasBookmark
methods.doc: Whether a bookmark exists.

methods.name: seek
methods.doc: Moves to a bookmark.

methods.name: parseAs
methods.doc: What follows as a namespace's content: outside HTML "<![CDATA[" opens a section; tag bodies read as HTML ("html", raw text elements whole) unless foreign ("foreign").

methods.name: allowBookmarks
methods.doc: Raises how many bookmarks may be held at once.

methods.name: rewind
methods.doc: Back to the start of the document, with every update written in and the bookmarks kept.

methods.name: splitText
methods.doc: The current text token cut to its first bytes; the rest is read next.

methods.name: tokenSpan
methods.doc: Where the current token sits in the document: [start, end].

methods.name: textSpan
methods.doc: Where the current text token's text sits: [start, length].

methods.name: source
methods.doc: The source between two offsets, updates written in.

methods.name: bookmarkSpan
methods.doc: Where a bookmark sits: [start, end], or null when there is none of that name.

methods.name: replaceAfter
methods.doc: Replaces a span at or after the current token's end, updates written in first: the new text is read next, and bookmarks past the span move with it.

methods.name: html
methods.doc: The document with every update written in.

methods.name: setToken
methods.signature: setToken(string $type, string $name, int $start, int $end, int $textStart, int $textLength): void

methods.name: takeTag
methods.doc: A tag the scanner read at $at becomes the current token; a raw-text element carries its body to its closer.

methods.name: take
methods.doc: A comment, doctype, or processing instruction the scanner read becomes the current token; null pauses.

methods.name: flush
methods.doc: Writes every pending update into the source, keeping bookmarks and the current token aligned.

methods.name: rescanCurrent
methods.doc: Re-reads the current token so attribute offsets match the new source.

classes.name: Minn\Html\TokenMap
classes.doc:
A map from words to replacements that reads the longest word at a place
in a text (as character reference names are read): words shorter than
the key length stand alone, the others are grouped by their first bytes,
longest first.

methods.name: keyLength
methods.doc: How many leading bytes group the words.

methods.name: contains
methods.doc: Whether the word is in the map ("case-sensitive" or "ascii-case-insensitive").

methods.name: read
methods.doc: The replacement for the longest word at $offset, and the word's length; null when none starts there.

methods.name: toArray
methods.doc: Every word and its replacement: the short words first, then each group longest first.

classes.name: Minn\Html\Tree\BodyRules
classes.doc:
The "in body" insertion mode, with select handled in body as the current
spec does (no "in select" mode). The adoption agency runs its simple
cases (the formatting element is closed with nothing special inside it);
the reference stops on the others, and on an end tag for a formatting
element that is not active.

methods.name: process
methods.doc: Processes one token in the "in body" insertion mode.

methods.name: isSpecial
methods.doc: Whether the node is in the spec's "special" category.

methods.name: adoptionAgency
methods.doc: The adoption agency algorithm in the cases the reference runs: the formatting element closes with nothing special opened inside it.

classes.name: Minn\Html\Tree\Builder
classes.doc:
The HTML tree construction algorithm over the engine's tokenizer, as the
reference's HTML processor runs it: tokens go through the insertion
modes (HeadRules, BodyRules, TableRules) or the foreign content rules,
and every node opened or closed becomes an Event with its breadcrumbs.
Text is read one kind at a time (NUL bytes, white space, the rest). At
the end of the input every open element closes; nothing implied is
added. Where the reference does not build a tree (Unsupported), the walk
stops with that error.

methods.name: reset
methods.doc: Back to the state before the first token.

methods.name: next
methods.doc: The next opened or closed node, or null at the end, at an incomplete token, or once unsupported markup stopped the walk.

methods.name: halt
methods.doc: Stops the walk for good (a failed seek leaves the processor like this).

methods.name: error
methods.doc: Why the walk stopped early, if it did.

methods.name: breadcrumbs
methods.doc: The breadcrumbs of the open elements now.

methods.name: token
methods.doc: The token being processed.

methods.name: stack
methods.doc: The stack of open elements.

methods.name: formatting
methods.doc: The list of active formatting elements.

methods.name: isFragment
methods.doc: Whether this builder parses a fragment (in a BODY context) rather than a document.

methods.name: mode
methods.doc: The insertion mode.

methods.name: switchTo
methods.doc: Switches the insertion mode.

methods.name: reprocessIn
methods.doc: Switches the insertion mode and processes the current token again under it.

methods.name: process
methods.doc: Processes a token under the current insertion mode, or the foreign content rules when they apply.

methods.name: processIn
methods.doc: Processes a token using the rules of an insertion mode other than the current one.

methods.name: framesetOk
methods.doc: Whether the frameset-ok flag is still set.

methods.name: framesetNotOk
methods.doc: Clears the frameset-ok flag.

methods.name: compat
methods.doc: The document's compatibility mode ("no-quirks", "limited-quirks", "quirks").

methods.name: setCompat
methods.doc: Sets the compatibility mode the doctype indicated.

methods.name: headPointer
methods.doc: The head element pointer.

methods.name: formPointer
methods.doc: The form element pointer.

methods.name: setFormPointer
methods.doc: Sets (or clears) the form element pointer.

methods.name: templateModes
methods.doc: The stack of template insertion modes.

methods.name: pushTemplateMode
methods.doc: Pushes a template insertion mode.

methods.name: popTemplateMode
methods.doc: Pops the current template insertion mode.

methods.name: adjustedCurrent
methods.doc: The adjusted current node: the context element when only the fragment's root is open.

methods.name: insert
methods.doc: Inserts an element for the current start tag, real, in the namespace.

methods.name: insertImplied
methods.doc: Inserts an element the markup implied.

methods.name: insertLeafElement
methods.doc: Inserts and at once closes an element for the current start tag: a void element, one read whole, or self-closed foreign content.

methods.name: insertLeaf
methods.doc: Inserts a leaf (text, comment, CDATA, processing instruction) for the current token, in the namespace.

methods.name: insertDocumentLeaf
methods.doc: Inserts a leaf at the top of the document (a doctype or a comment before or around the html element).

methods.name: pop
methods.doc: Closes the current node as implied.

methods.name: popUntil
methods.doc: Pops until an HTML element of one of the names closes; when the current end tag names it, that last close is real.

methods.name: popUntilNode
methods.doc: Pops until this very node closes.

methods.name: generateImpliedEndTags
methods.doc: Generates implied end tags, leaving an element of the name open.

methods.name: generateAllImpliedEndTags
methods.doc: Generates all implied end tags thoroughly (table parts as well).

methods.name: closeP
methods.doc: Closes a P element: implied end tags but P's, then pops through the P.

methods.name: closePInButtonScope
methods.doc: Closes a P element when one is in button scope.

methods.name: reconstructFormatting
methods.doc: Reconstructs the active formatting elements; the reference stops when any would have to be reopened.

methods.name: skipNextNewline
methods.doc: Asks the parser to drop one leading line feed from the next token (after PRE, LISTING).

methods.name: resetInsertionMode
methods.doc: Resets the insertion mode from the stack of open elements.

methods.name: unsupported
methods.doc: Stops: the reference's processor does not build a tree for this markup.

methods.name: attribute
methods.doc: The current tag's attribute, decoded; null when absent.

methods.name: doctype

methods.name: read

with a system identifier), no quirks otherwise.
