classes.name: Minn\Http
classes.doc:
Outgoing HTTP, a client handed to the code that uses it. An extension
finds one on $minn->http, bound to the hosts its minn.json asks for under
needs.http; an engine class takes one in its constructor, the real network
unless a test passes a fake's:

$data = $minn->http->get('https://api.example.com/status')->json();
$this->http->post($url, json: ['email' => $email], timeout: 10)->throw();

Every verb answers with an Exchange (->ok(), ->failed(), ->json(),
->header(), ->cookie(), ->throw(), ->code, ->body) and takes the same
named arguments, each optional:

- `query`: array added to the URL's query string
- `headers`: `name => value` (a list value repeats the header), or "Name: value" lines
- `json`, `form`, `body` (post, put, patch): an array sent as JSON, an array
form-encoded, or a string sent as it is; one of the three, and the first
two set the Content-Type
- `timeout`: seconds for the whole exchange, 5 by default
- `redirects`: how many to follow, 5 by default; 0 hands back the 3xx
- `hosts`: URL prefixes every hop must start with (`['https://api.github.com/']`)
- `private`: hosts allowed to reach a private address. Loopback, LAN,
link-local and cloud-metadata addresses are refused otherwise, at every
hop and after DNS, so a URL someone typed is safe to fetch
- `maxBytes`: the largest body accepted; a longer one fails the exchange
- `userAgent`: Minn/{version} by default

A misspelt argument is an error at the line that has it. Credentials
(Authorization, Cookie) are dropped when a redirect leaves the origin.
A fake (new Http\Fake([...])->http()) answers only the client it made,
so a test shares nothing with the rest of the process.

constructor.doc:
The network, or $fake answering in its place. With $within, every hop
of every request must also start with one of those URL prefixes,
whatever a call's own hosts: say (an extension's needs.http).

classes.name: Minn\Http\Access
classes.doc:
Who a route is for. The six answers every route gives, so the
authorization surface of the engine reads as a list of these.

cases.name: Public
cases.doc: Anyone, signed in or not; the caller is never resolved.

cases.name: SignedIn
cases.doc: A signed-in caller, whoever they are.

cases.name: Cap
cases.doc: A signed-in caller holding the named capability (and every extra one).

cases.name: Floor
cases.doc: The Minn Admin floor: signed in, may edit posts, and holds every extra capability named; refused as rest_forbidden.

cases.name: Own
cases.doc: A signed-in caller holding a capability on the object a pattern capture names.

cases.name: CommentEditor
cases.doc: A signed-in caller who may change the comment a capture names: a moderator, or one who may edit its post; a note only the latter.

cases.name: Type
cases.doc: Any caller, on a route whose {base} capture must name a declared post type; the route declines otherwise and the handler judges the rest.

cases.name: Taxonomy
cases.doc: Any caller, on a route whose {base} capture must name a taxonomy plugin code registered to show in REST; the route declines otherwise and the handler judges the rest.

classes.name: Minn\Http\Args
classes.doc:
The parameters a route accepts, as the reference describes them in the
REST index: name => {description, type, ...}. The descriptions, types,
enums and bounds were captured from the reference, so a client that
reads either index is told the same thing, and the router refuses a
value the way the reference refuses it, before it judges the caller.

A route declares only what it really reads. An argument published here
that the handler ignores would be worse than none at all, because a
client reading the index would build a request around it, so each set
below names the code that consumes it. The sets keep the reference's
order, because a refusal lists the invalid parameters in that order.
`_fields` and `_embed` are read everywhere and declared nowhere, as the
reference lists neither and validates neither.

constants.name: SHARED
constants.doc:
The shared collection parameters, judged first: the reference answers
a refusal among these alone, and reads the route's own parameters
only once these pass.

constants.name: HANDLER_VALIDATES
constants.doc: The key an argument carries when its handler judges it (a status the caller may not read is refused before the enum is).

constants.name: SANITIZE_ROUND
constants.doc:
The key an argument carries when the reference judges it only once
every other argument has passed, in the round its sanitize callbacks
run, and lets it be empty: the comment author's address.

constants.name: BARE_REFUSAL
constants.doc: The key an argument carries when the reference's own check refuses it with a bare "Invalid parameter." and no details: a comment's meta.

constants.name: PASSWORD
constants.doc: The key a user's password carries: its type judged with the others, then, in the sanitize round, refused empty or with a backslash (probe rest-users-controller).

constants.name: INSTALLED_LOCALE

classes.name: Minn\Http\CertificateName
classes.doc:
Whether a TLS certificate names a host: a wildcard only as a whole first
label with at least two labels after it, matching exactly one label; an
IP address never matches by name; the subjectAltName DNS entries win over
the common name when present.

methods.name: valid
methods.doc: Whether a certificate's reference name is one a host can match.

methods.name: matches
methods.doc: Whether the host matches the reference name.

methods.name: certificateMatches
methods.doc: Whether a parsed certificate (openssl_x509_parse) names the host.

classes.name: Minn\Http\CookieText
classes.doc:
Set-Cookie text and the matching rules a cookie jar applies: parsing a
header into name, value and attributes; normalizing attributes (expires
and max-age as timestamps, the domain without its leading dot); whether
a cookie belongs to a domain and a path (RFC 6265).

methods.name: parse
methods.doc:
A Set-Cookie value split up. With a name given, the first part is
all value; a first part without "=" is a value with an empty name.
shapes: @return array{name: string, value: string, attributes: array<string, string|true>}

methods.name: normalizeAttribute
methods.doc: One attribute normalized, or null when it should go: dates become timestamps, the domain loses its leading dot.

methods.name: hostMatches
methods.doc: Whether a host-only cookie with this domain attribute (none means any) belongs to the domain: the same text only.

methods.name: domainMatches
methods.doc: Whether a cookie with this domain attribute (none means any) belongs to the domain or one of its subdomains (never an IP address).

methods.name: pathMatches
methods.doc: Whether a cookie with this path attribute (none means any) is sent for the request path.

methods.name: defaultPath
methods.doc: The path a cookie without one gets: the request path up to its last slash, or "/".

methods.name: fields
methods.doc:
A cookie's fields, as WP_Http_Cookie sets them: from a Set-Cookie
value (the value URL-decoded; expires, path, domain and port from its
attributes; the domain and path it names none of from the URL it came
from: the host, and the URL's directory), or from given fields that are
among $properties (an expiry given as a date becomes a timestamp); the
path "/" when nothing gives one.

classes.name: Minn\Http\Destination
classes.doc:
Where Minn\Http lets a request go. Only http and https; when hosts are
named, every hop must start with one of them (and with one of the
client's own, when it is bound); and an address outside the
public internet (loopback, private and shared ranges, link-local, cloud
metadata, reserved) is refused unless its host is listed in $private. A
name is resolved here and curl is pinned to the addresses that were
checked, so DNS cannot answer one way to the check and another to the
connection.

constructor.signature: __construct(array $hosts = array ( ), array $private = array ( ), ?Closure $lookup = NULL, array $within = array ( ))
shapes: @param list<string> $hosts URL prefixes every hop must start with; none means any public host
@param list<string> $private host names or addresses allowed to reach a private address
@param (Closure(string): list<string>)|null $lookup a host's addresses; DNS when null
@param list<string> $within URL prefixes the client itself is bound to (an extension's needs.http); none means unbound

params.name: hosts
params.doc: URL prefixes every hop must start with; none means any public host

params.name: private
params.doc: host names or addresses allowed to reach a private address

params.name: lookup
params.doc: a host's addresses; DNS when null

params.name: within
params.doc: URL prefixes the client itself is bound to (an extension's needs.http); none means unbound

methods.name: refusal
methods.doc: Why $url may not be requested, or null when nothing about the URL itself refuses it (a name is judged again once resolved).

methods.name: pinned
methods.doc:
The request with curl pinned to the addresses its host resolves to,
or the failed exchange when the name does not resolve or resolves
somewhere private it was not allowed.

methods.name: host
methods.doc: A URL's host, lower-cased, without the brackets around an IPv6 address.

methods.name: nonGlobalSix
methods.doc:
IPv6 ranges PHP's global-range flag lets through that reach no public
host: NAT64 (64:ff9b::/96 and 64:ff9b:1::/48, which carry an IPv4
address, a private one included), site-local fec0::/10 and multicast
ff00::/8 (security review 2026-10-22).

methods.name: dns
methods.doc: A name's IPv4 addresses, or its IPv6 ones when it has none.

classes.name: Minn\Http\DiePage
classes.doc:
The page wp_die shows a browser, as the reference draws it (probe
functions-remaining): its stylesheet word for word, the html element's
language (or dir='rtl' for a right-to-left message, which also sets a
Tahoma font), the charset, the robots tag, the title and the message as
given, then any links. The caller escapes what needs escaping. The
stylesheet is kept here with four spaces for each of its tabs.

written for the person who asked for the download.

classes.name: Minn\Http\Envelope

What runs around a matched route once the router knows the route takes
the request: the place a host lets other code refuse, answer or edit it
(the runtime's REST server filters). The router hands over the argument
check's refusal and the policy's, unthrown, because that code may clear
the one and must never run the handler past the other. Without an
envelope the router throws them itself.

classes.name: Minn\Http\Failure
classes.doc:
What the public sees when the engine cannot answer: a plain page with no
detail, while the detail goes to the log. Installed once per request,
it sets PHP's error settings from the debug constants (display stays off
unless WP_DEBUG and WP_DEBUG_DISPLAY ask for it) and catches the fatal
errors PHP would otherwise print.

properties.name: display
properties.doc: Whether errors display for this request: display_errors, once the debug constants set it.

properties.name: armed
properties.doc: Whether a failure right now may be recorded against an extension: only while the extensions boot.

methods.name: armRecovery
methods.doc:
Opens the window in which a failure is an extension's fault: while
the plugins and the theme's functions file load and the boot actions
fire, code that fails fails for every visitor, so pausing it heals
the site. A failure after that (a route, a shortcode, a template)
answers to one request's input and is never grounds for a pause;
it is logged and the request ends in the error page.

methods.name: disarmRecovery
methods.doc: Closes the window armRecovery() opened.

methods.name: onFatal
methods.doc:
What to do with a fatal beyond showing the page: the engine records
the extension it came from so the next request loads without it.
Installed once the runtime is up, since it needs the database.

methods.name: install
methods.doc:
Sets PHP's error settings from the debug constants as the reference's
boot does (Runtime\DebugMode), and installs the error handlers. With
WP_DEBUG off, or for a request that answers a machine, errors never
display. In the first case the reference leaves php.ini's setting;
the engine never shows a visitor PHP's errors. Detail is shown only
while display_errors is on.
shapes: @param array<string, mixed> $constants the debug and request constants, by name
@param array<string, mixed> $server the request's server variables

params.name: constants
params.doc: the debug and request constants, by name

methods.name: report
methods.doc: Logs the cause; the page says only that something went wrong.

methods.name: reportJson
methods.doc:
The same, for a request that asked for JSON: a client that speaks REST
is answered in REST, never handed the HTML error page.

methods.name: internal
methods.doc: The 500 page.

methods.name: databaseUnavailable
methods.doc: The 503 page the reference shows when the database cannot be reached.

methods.name: maintenance
methods.doc: The 503 page while maintenance mode holds; monitors read the status, the retry hint, and the title.

methods.name: detailed
methods.doc:
The same page with the cause on it, for a site that asked to see
errors. Only ever reached when WP_DEBUG_DISPLAY (or WP_DEBUG) is on:
a site that has not asked never learns this much from a response.

methods.name: discardOutput
methods.doc: Whatever a half-finished render left in the output buffers goes; the error page must stand alone.

methods.name: note
methods.doc: Logs the failure, clears whatever a half-finished render left, and offers it to recovery.

methods.name: record
methods.doc:
Hands the failure to the recorder, and never lets recovery itself
take the request down: a site that cannot record a pause should
still answer with the error page.

classes.name: Minn\Http\Fake
classes.doc:
Answers requests in place of the network, and keeps what was sent. A test
makes one and hands its client to the code it tests:

$fake = new Fake(['api.example.com/*' => ['ok' => true]]);
$result = (new StatusCheck($fake->http()))->run();
$fake->sent('api.example.com/status');   // the requests that went there

Only that client is answered, so there is nothing to put back and nothing
else in the process sees the fake.

constructor.doc:
Keys are URL patterns (* matches anything; the scheme and query may be
left off); values are an array (sent as JSON), a string (the body), a
status code, an Exchange from reply(), or a closure taking the
Outbound and returning one of those. A request no pattern matches
fails as if nothing were listening.

methods.doc:
A client this fake answers, bound to $within as an extension's is by
its needs.http. The destination rules still run, but names are not resolved.

methods.doc: The answer for one request, which is recorded as sent.

methods.doc: The requests sent so far, oldest first; with a pattern, only those whose URL matches it.

methods.doc: A response made by hand, for a fake to answer with. An array body is sent as JSON.

methods.name: write
methods.doc: The text, with $keep naming the extra byte ranges left unencoded.

The edge. Turns a request into a response through the router and turns
a RestError thrown anywhere underneath into the WordPress error shape.

methods.doc:
Headers every response carries: no content sniffing anywhere; the
sign-in and admin pages refuse framing (both headers), keep their
referrer to themselves and are never cached, as the reference's do.

classes.doc:
WP_Http's legacy readers, kept for plugins that still call them (probe
http-classes). They read a header block the old way, and decode a chunked
body with the reference's quirk. RawResponse does both properly for the
engine's own requests.

methods.doc:
A header block (a string, its folded lines joined, or a list of lines)
read into the last status line's code and message, lower-cased
headers (a repeated one as a list) and the Set-Cookie values. Each
status line starts the headers over.

methods.doc:
A chunked body decoded as the reference's WP_Http::chunkTransferDecode
decodes one. The CRLF after a chunk is not stepped over, so it decodes
only when chunks run into each other and a final 0 ends the body; any
other shape comes back as it was.

classes.doc: Where a redirect leads: a Location header made absolute against the URL that sent it.

methods.doc:
A redirect's address made safe, as wp_sanitize_redirect() makes it
(probe security-parity): spaces as %20, whole UTF-8 sequences
URL-encoded, any other character outside the URL set dropped, and an
encoded CR or LF taken out until none is left. Other encoded control
characters stay, as they do on the reference.

methods.doc:
The absolute URL $location names, read against $base as RFC 3986
reads a reference: a scheme keeps it as written, "//" takes the
base's scheme, a fragment or query alone keeps the base's path, and a
relative path joins the base's directory with "." and ".." resolved.

methods.doc: Whether two URLs share scheme, host, and port, so credentials may follow from one to the other.

methods.doc: A path with its "." and ".." segments resolved (RFC 3986 remove_dot_segments).

every method the same handler answers on that pattern (the reference
lists POST, PUT and PATCH together for one edit handler).

classes.name: Minn\Http\Policy
classes.doc:
What a route requires of its caller, as data on the route: the router
enforces it before the handler runs, so a grep over the attributes is
the authorization surface. The two refusals are the reference's: a
caller who is not signed in gets the sign-in code (401), a signed-in
caller who lacks the capability gets the refusal code (403); how a bad
nonce is answered belongs to whoever judges the policy. A policy that
names a subject has the record looked up first, and answers the
record's 404 before either refusal, which is the reference's order.

Written inline in the attribute with `new`, which is what an attribute
argument allows: `policy: new Policy(Access::Cap, 'upload_files',
refuse: 'rest_cannot_create', message: '...')`.

params.doc: the record the capture names, looked up before the caller is judged

An HTTP response as text, the way the Requests library hands it from
transport to parser: the status line and headers, a blank line, the
body. Built from an exchange, split back up, chunked bodies joined and
compressed ones inflated.

globals at the edge; handlers only ever see this object.

classes.name: Minn\Http\Route
classes.doc:
Declares a handler method as a route. The policy lives here, as
metadata the router enforces before the handler runs, so the
authorization surface of the engine is a grep away; a route with no
policy is one the ratchet in the style suite counts down. The parameter
sets it reads live here too, judged before the policy is (the reference
refuses a bad argument before it refuses a caller), so the REST index can
tell a client what a route takes as well as what it requires of them.

Patterns: "/wp/v2/posts/{id}" captures one segment, "{id:\d+}" constrains
it, and "/{path*}" captures the rest of the path (slashes included).

constructor.signature: __construct(Minn\Http\Method $method, string $pattern, ?Minn\Http\Policy $policy = NULL, array $args = array ( ), bool $index = true, array $body = array ( ), ?string $name = NULL, ?string $params = NULL, ?string $refuse = NULL, ?array $allowBatch = NULL)
shapes: @param list<array<string, array<string, mixed>>> $args the parameter sets this route reads, from Args
@param list<array<string, array<string, mixed>>> $body the parameter sets this route reads from the JSON body, from Args or the shape that owns them
@param array<string, bool>|null $allowBatch whether a batch may carry the route, by batch version, as the index lists it (['v1' => false]); unsaid when null

under the same namespace, say) instead of answering "no route" itself.

This is the row the REST index, the docs, and contracts/api/routes.json

classes.name: Minn\Http\Router
classes.doc:
Matches a request to a #[Route] on one of the registered handler
objects, has the check refuse a bad argument, has the gate judge the
route's policy, and invokes the method with the request plus the named
pattern captures. That order is the reference's: an invalid parameter is
answered before the caller is looked at. The gate is the one
thing a router cannot be built without: a policy nobody judges is a
route nobody may call.

shapes: @param Closure(Policy $policy, Request $request, array<string, string> $captures): void $gate throws when the policy refuses the caller
@param Closure(Route $route, Request $request): void|null $check throws when a declared argument is missing or invalid; judged before the gate

params.name: envelope
params.doc: what runs around a matched route instead of the router throwing its refusals itself

methods.name: register
methods.doc: Registers every #[Route] method of the given handlers; returns the router for chaining.

methods.name: routes
methods.doc: The routes that list in an index: pattern => methods. @return array<string, list<string>>

methods.name: table
methods.doc:
Every registered route as a row: what it is, who it is for, what it
takes. The same rows Rest\Catalogue reads from the classes alone.

methods.name: allowed
methods.doc:
The methods the caller may use on this path, for the Allow header:
every route matching the path (a route with no captures that names
the path exactly claims it alone), its policy judged for the caller
without dispatching. A route that states no policy counts for GET
only, until it states one. Empty when nothing matched or nothing
is allowed, and the header is then left out, as the reference does.

methods.name: matching
methods.doc:
The routes a request's method and path match, policies unjudged, in
the order dispatch tries them, with their captures: what a batch
reads to tell a route that does not take part from no route at all.

methods.name: claims
methods.doc:
Whether a #[Route] on any of these classes matches the request's
method and path, read from the classes alone: nothing is built,
judged or dispatched.

methods.name: dispatch
methods.doc: Null when nothing matched, so the caller can fall through.

methods.name: overridden
methods.doc:
The path's captures, each replaced by the request's own value of that
name where the route declares an argument by it: the reference reads a
parameter from the body and the query before the path, so
/wp/v2/users/1?id=2 is user 2, judged and answered as user 2. Replacing
the capture before anything reads it keeps the gate and the handler on
the same object. A value that is not a scalar is left to the argument
check, and an integer argument is handed over as the integer it reads as.

methods.name: arguments
methods.doc:
The captures a handler takes, by parameter name; a capture spelled as
the reference spells it (user_id) binds to its camelCase parameter.

methods.name: enveloped
methodsOf
methods.doc:
The methods one handler answers on one pattern alongside the request's,
grouped as the reference registers them: reading alone, deleting
alone, and creating or editing together (POST, PUT, PATCH).

methods.name: literal
methods.doc: The one path a route spells, a capture it fixes ({base:media}) read as its word; null for a route with a real capture.

methods.name: spells
methods.doc:
Whether a route names a path in so many words: its captures, if any,
only choose among words ({base:categories|tags}), so the path is one of
the routes it spells rather than a value it captures.

classes.name: Minn\Http\Subject
classes.doc:
The record a route capture names, so a policy can have it looked up
before the caller is judged: the reference answers "no such post" ahead
of "you may not", and the 404 it sends is the record's own. A kind that
reads its post type or taxonomy from the {base} capture says so.

classes.name: Minn\Http\Transport
classes.doc:
The engine's outgoing HTTP transport over curl: it sends exactly what an
Outbound says and nothing else decides. Redirects are followed by curl, so
the header lines of every hop arrive in order; only the last response's
block is kept, the way plugin code expects to read it. Code calling out
goes through Minn\Http, which owns the rules about where a request may go.

methods.name: send
methods.doc: Performs one outgoing request over curl and returns the exchange, a transport error included.

methods.name: options
methods.doc: The curl options every request carries, the header lines collected into $lines as they arrive.

methods.name: limit
methods.doc:
Stops a body that grows past $maxBytes: curl refuses up front when the
length is announced, and the progress callback aborts when it is not.

methods.name: lastHead
methods.doc: The last response's status line and header lines, line endings removed.

classes.name: Minn\Http\TrustedProxies
classes.doc:
Which addresses in front of the engine may speak for the client.

By default none do: a forwarded header is a request header, and a request
header is the client's word. Behind a proxy or CDN that terminates TLS,
`REMOTE_ADDR` is then the proxy's, which makes every visitor look like one
address (the sign-in throttle would lock them all out together) and every
request look insecure (the auth cookie would lose its Secure flag).

A site says who to believe in `wp-config.php`:

define('MINN_TRUSTED_PROXIES', '10.0.0.0/8, 2400:cb00::/32');
define('MINN_TRUSTED_PROXIES', '*');   // any: only when nothing but the proxy can reach PHP

The client is then the right-most address in `X-Forwarded-For` that is not
itself trusted, which is what a proxy chain appends, so a client that sends
its own `X-Forwarded-For` cannot put an address the engine believes to the
right of the proxy's. `*` trusts whoever connects, not every forwarded
hop: the client is the address that proxy appended (with it every hop,
the client's own included, would be skipped as trusted, and every visitor
would be the proxy again).

shapes: @param list<string> $ranges addresses or CIDR ranges, or ['*'] for any

params.name: ranges
params.doc: addresses or CIDR ranges, or ['*'] for any

methods.name: none
methods.doc: Nobody in front of the engine speaks for the client.

methods.name: configured
methods.doc: What the site declared in wp-config.php, or nobody.

methods.name: trusts
methods.doc: Whether the engine believes what this address says about the client.

methods.name: clientAddress
methods.doc:
The client's address, given who connected and what was forwarded: the
right-most forwarded address that is not itself a trusted proxy.

methods.name: forwardedSecure
methods.doc: Whether a forwarded scheme may be believed, and says https.

methods.name: coversHop
methods.doc: Whether a forwarded hop is a trusted proxy: one a declared range covers (`*` speaks for the connecting address only).

methods.name: bare
methods.doc: An address with a port or brackets stripped, as a forwarded list may carry them.

methods.name: covers
methods.doc: Whether a CIDR range or a plain address covers the address given.

classes.name: Minn\I18n\Catalog
classes.doc:
One translation file's contents: its headers as written, its messages
keyed the gettext way (the context, a 0x04 byte, then the original; the
original alone without a context), each with its translated forms and,
where the file says, the original plural, and the file's plural rule.
An empty translation is still a translation: it is what the file says.

methods.name: from
methods.doc: A catalog from headers and entries, its plural rule taken from the headers.

methods.name: key
methods.doc: The lookup key for an original in a context; an empty or missing context is no context.

methods.name: headerValue
methods.doc: A header's value, its name matched without case.

methods.doc: The translation of a message, empty when the file says so, or null when the file has no entry.

methods.name: translatePlural
methods.doc: The form of a message a count takes under this file's rule (the first form when the file has fewer), or null when the file has no entry.

methods.name: has
methods.doc: Whether the file has an entry for the message.

classes.name: Minn\I18n\Gettext
classes.doc:
Translation as plugins see it (__, _x, _n and the rest map here): the
message looked up in its domain's loaded files (loading the domain just
in time on first use, through the loader the runtime hands over), else
the English, then the gettext filters a plugin may change it through.
Engine code translates here rather than through the WordPress names;
with no runtime (an engine CLI verb) there is nothing loaded, and the
English stands.

methods.doc: The runtime's just-in-time loader for a domain's files. @param Closure(string): mixed $loader

methods.doc: A message (__).

methods.name: inContext
methods.doc: A message in a context (_x).

methods.name: plural
methods.doc: The form a count takes (_n): the domain's own plural, else English's.

methods.doc: The form a count takes in a context (_nx).

methods.doc: A domain's translation of a message key in the locale lookups are made in, or null (no runtime to have loaded one, no file, no entry).

classes.name: Minn\I18n\LegacyPluralForms
classes.doc:
The plural expression reader the old POMO library carries (Plural_Forms),
kept apart from PluralExpression because plugins see its quirks: it reads
only n, whole numbers, parentheses, % and the comparisons, && and ||, and
the ternary, skipping spaces and tabs alone. It turns the expression into
postfix tokens once (operators of equal strength group to the left, the
ternary to the right) and runs them on a stack per number: an operand the
stack lacks is null, == and != compare strictly, values stay as PHP left
them until the answer is cast to an integer, and % is PHP's own, so a zero
divisor throws. Every refusal is an Exception with the reference's words
(probe translation-files).

constants.name: LEVELS
constants.doc: The operators by how loosely they bind, loosest first; the parentheses below everything.

methods.name: chooser
methods.doc:
The form chooser a translation file makes of an expression
(make_plural_form_function): closing semicolons dropped, the
expression read as above, and English (n != 1) for one it refuses. A
chooser that cannot run a number throws, as the reference's does
(probe blocks-rest-widget-doubts).

methods.name: parse
methods.doc: The expression as postfix tokens: ['var'], ['value', int] or ['op', string].

methods.name: execute
methods.doc: The value of postfix tokens for one number.

methods.name: token
methods.doc: Reads one token at an offset onto the output or the operator stack; the offset after it.

methods.name: operator
methods.doc: Reads the one- or two-character operator at an offset; its length.

methods.name: closeTernary
methods.doc: A ":" moves operators out until its "?", which becomes the whole ternary.

methods.name: apply
methods.doc: Runs one operator on the values it pops, rightmost first.

methods.name: strengths
methods.doc: Each operator's strength: its level's place in LEVELS.

classes.name: Minn\I18n\LocalDates
classes.doc:

PHP's format, with the weekday and month names (D, l, F, M) and the
meridiems (a, A) in the language's own words, and a month written after
its day in the genitive where the language declines month names.
Backslashed characters stay as written.

methods.name: format
methods.doc: The date in the format given, its names translated.

classes.name: Minn\I18n\LocaleStack
classes.doc:
The locales a request switched into, innermost last, each with the user
whose locale it is (false when a locale was named outright). Empty means
the request speaks its own locale.

methods.doc: Enters a locale, a user's or one named outright.

methods.name: switched
methods.doc: Whether any locale is switched in.

classes.name: Minn\I18n\MoFile
classes.doc:
The GNU gettext binary catalog (.mo), read and written. The file opens
with a magic number that also says its byte order, then a revision, the
message count, and the offsets of two tables of (length, offset) pairs:
the originals, then the translations. The entry with an empty original
carries the headers; a plural original is "singular NUL plural" and its
translations are NUL-separated; a context precedes the original with a
0x04 byte.

methods.name: read
methods.doc: The catalog in a .mo file's bytes, or null when they are not one.

methods.name: write
methods.doc:
A .mo file's bytes for headers and entries, little-endian, entries in
the sorted order gettext expects.

A .mo file's bytes for a header block and its originals and
translations as written (MO::export with its export_* steps), sorted.

A .mo file's bytes for headers and entries kept in the order they are
held, the header block first (WP_Translation_File_MO::export, probe
blocks-rest-widget-doubts).

methods.doc: "V" for a little-endian file, "N" for a big-endian one, null for anything else.

classes.doc: Numbers written for people: grouped by thousands, to the decimals asked.

classes.name: Minn\I18n\PhpFile

The PHP translation file (.l10n.php): a file that returns an array of its
lower-cased headers and a "messages" map from the gettext key to the
translation, plural forms joined by NUL bytes. It is the site's own data,
read the way the reference reads it, by including it.

methods.doc: The catalog a .l10n.php file returns, or null when it returns no messages.

classes.name: Minn\I18n\PluralExpression
classes.doc:
The C subset a Plural-Forms header writes its rule in: the number n,
integer literals, parentheses, ! and unary minus, * / %, + -, the four
comparisons, == and !=, && and ||, and the ternary, with C's precedence
and the ternary binding to the right. Parsed into a small tree once and
evaluated per number; nothing is ever handed to PHP to run.

methods.doc: The expression as a tree, or null when it is not a whole expression.

methods.name: evaluate
methods.doc: The value of a parsed expression for one number; true is 1 and false 0.

methods.doc: One level of left-associative binary operators, and every tighter level under it.

classes.name: Minn\I18n\PluralRule
classes.doc:
A language's plural rule from its Plural-Forms header: how many forms it
has and which form a number takes. A file without the header follows
English (two forms, n != 1); an expression that does not parse sends
every number to the first form, as the reference does.

methods.doc: English: one form for 1, the other for everything else.

methods.name: fromHeader
methods.doc: The rule a Plural-Forms header states.

methods.doc: A rule from a form count and an expression in n.

methods.doc:
An expression with each ternary's branches parenthesized, as
parenthesize_plural_exression() writes it: "?" becomes " ? (", ":"
becomes ") : (", the open parentheses closed at each ";" and at the
end, trailing semicolons dropped.

methods.name: index
methods.doc: The form a number takes.

methods.name: pair
methods.doc: The form count and the expression, as nplurals_and_expression_from_header() answers them. @return array{0: int, 1: string}

methods.name: chooser
methods.doc: The form a number takes, as the function make_plural_form_function() hands back. @return \Closure(mixed): int

classes.name: Minn\I18n\ScriptTranslations
classes.doc:
Where a script's JSON translations are found, and how they reach the
page. A script is placed by its URL: inside a plugin or a theme, its path
there; elsewhere on the site, its path from the site root; off the site,
nowhere. The JSON files are named by the md5 of that path (with ".min.js"
read as ".js"), or by the script's handle in a folder a plugin names.

methods.name: place
methods.doc:
A script's path inside its plugin, theme or site, and the languages
subfolder for it ("plugins", "themes", or "" for the site); the path
is false for a script off the site.

methods.name: absolute
methods.doc: The script made absolute the way place() reads it, for the filter that may move it.

methods.name: fileHash
methods.doc: The md5 a translation file is named by: a minified script shares its source's file.

methods.name: prefix
methods.doc: The start of a translation file's name: the core domain goes by locale alone.

methods.name: block
methods.doc: The inline script that hands a script's translations to wp.i18n before the script runs.

classes.name: Minn\I18n\SiteLanguage
classes.doc:
The site's language as pages declare it: the locale in force (a switched
one first, then what the WPLANG option gives, through the locale filter) and the html element's dir and lang
attributes, which a plugin may change through language_attributes.

methods.name: locale
methods.doc:
The locale in force (get_locale): a switched one, else the configured
one. pre_determine_locale is determine_locale's, not this one's (probe
text-domain-timing); the reference asks it while registering the media
player's strings, as the engine now does (probe default-scripts).

methods.name: configured
methods.doc:
The site's locale through the locale filter: the $locale global once
set, else the WPLANG option read as get_option reads it (its filters
included), the WPLANG constant when the option names none, then en_US,
kept in the global unfiltered for the next ask (probe locale-reads).

methods.name: tag
methods.doc: The language tag pages carry: the locale in force (determine_locale; probe sweep-1020) with a hyphen, plain "en" read as en_US.

methods.name: isRtl
methods.doc: Whether the site's language is written right to left (is_rtl).

methods.name: attributes
methods.doc: The html element's dir and lang attributes (lang for html, xml:lang for xhtml or a non-HTML html_type).

classes.name: Minn\I18n\TextDomains
classes.doc:
The text domains this request knows: each domain's files in the order they
were loaded, and the domains looked for and not found (known, with no
files), all in the order they first appeared, which is the order a locale
switch reloads them in. Each file is kept with the locales it was loaded
for, and a lookup for a locale asks only those files (probe
translation-locales): the domain's files in load order, the first one with
a translation answering, each under its own plural rule.
The registry also remembers the folder a plugin or theme named for its
domain (and how files there are named), and the domains unloaded for good.

properties.name: turns
properties.doc: How many files have been loaded for a locale so far: a file's turn among a locale's files.

properties.name: locale
properties.doc: The locale lookups are made in: the translation controller's, en_US until it is set.

methods.name: useLocale
methods.doc: Sets the locale lookups are made in (the translation controller's set_locale).

methods.name: locale
methods.doc: The locale lookups are made in.

methods.name: add
methods.doc: Adds a loaded file to a domain for a locale; a file already loaded there is not added twice, only its locale noted.

methods.name: has
methods.doc: Whether any file is loaded for the domain, for the locale when one is given.

methods.name: unload
methods.doc: Forgets a domain and its files; true when it had any.

methods.name: accept
methods.doc:
Records that load_textdomain() loaded a file for the domain. A file
that does not parse adds nothing to look up, yet the reference's
global functions count its domain as loaded, while its translation
controller does not (probe translations-early-wplang).

methods.name: opened
methods.doc: Whether the global functions count the domain as loaded: a file loaded, or one load_textdomain() accepted.

methods.name: markKnown
methods.doc: Records that a domain was asked for, so it is looked for once and reloaded on a switch.

methods.name: waiting
methods.doc:
Whether a translation lookup should look for the domain's files: it was
never looked for, or nothing was found and a folder has been named for
it since (the reference looks again after each load_plugin_textdomain;
probe plugin-data).

methods.name: known
methods.doc: Whether the domain was loaded or looked for.

methods.name: knownDomains
methods.doc: Every known domain, in the order it first appeared.

methods.name: unloadFile
methods.doc:
Drops one file from a domain for a locale, the first it was loaded for
when none is given (probe translation-locales); the file stays for its
other locales. True when it was loaded.

methods.name: catalogs
methods.doc:
The domain's files and catalogs, first loaded first: those loaded for
the locale when one is given, in the order they were loaded for it,
else all of them.

methods.name: translate
methods.doc: The first loaded translation of a key in the domain (among the locale's files when one is given), or null.

methods.name: translatePlural
methods.doc:
The first loaded plural form for a count (among the locale's files when
one is given), or null: each key is looked for in every file before the
next key (the full "singular NUL plural" key, then the singular alone).

methods.name: rememberFolder
methods.doc:
Records the folder a plugin or theme named for its domain: files there
are "{domain}-{locale}", or named by the locale alone at or below the
active theme's folder, whichever domain names it (probe
text-domain-timing).

methods.name: rememberTheme
methods.doc: Records a folder of the active theme (its template's or its stylesheet's).

methods.name: folderFile
methods.doc: The .mo path a domain's named folder would hold for a locale, if a folder was named.

methods.name: close
methods.doc: Keeps an unloaded domain from loading again on its own.

methods.name: closed
methods.doc: Whether the domain was unloaded for good.

methods.name: domains
methods.doc: The domains with files loaded.

classes.name: Minn\I18n\TranslationFiles
classes.doc:
Which file a request for a .mo path reads, and reading it. Asked for
"x.mo", the reference reads "x.l10n.php" when the format is php and that
file is there, and the .mo only otherwise; asked for the mo format, only
the .mo.

methods.name: candidates
methods.doc: The files to try for a requested .mo path, in order.

methods.name: languages
methods.doc:
The languages a folder holds core translations for (each .mo but the
time zone names, the network admin's and the admin's), as
get_available_languages lists them, through its filter ($asked: the
folder as the caller named it, null for the site's own).

methods.name: read
methods.doc: A translation file's catalog by its extension, or null when it cannot be read as one.

classes.name: Minn\Json
classes.doc:
JSON in and out, for the engine and for code written for Minn:

use Minn\Json;

Json::encode($rows);              // {"url":"https://example.com/a","name":"Café"}
Json::decode($text);              // objects as arrays; JsonException when it is not JSON
Json::decode($stored, or: []);    // the fallback, for text that may be empty or broken
Json::file($path);                // the same, read from a file; the error names the file

encode() writes slashes and characters as themselves unless flags say
otherwise (Json::ESCAPED is the form WordPress writes, which REST bodies
keep). A string cut mid-character still encodes: each invalid byte becomes
"?", as wp_json_encode() does it (probe functions-utils). What cannot be
encoded even then (NAN, nesting past the depth) throws a JsonException.

constants.name: READABLE
constants.doc: Slashes and non-ASCII characters written as themselves: encode()'s default.

constants.name: ESCAPED
constants.doc: Slashes and non-ASCII characters escaped, as wp_json_encode() and the REST API write them.

methods.name: encode
methods.doc: A value as JSON; invalid UTF-8 is repaired, never a reason to fail.

params.name: flags
params.doc: json_encode() flags; JSON_THROW_ON_ERROR here skips the repair, as it does for wp_json_encode()

methods.name: decode
methods.doc: The value the text holds, objects as arrays; with `or:` given, that comes back instead of an exception.

methods.name: objects
methods.doc: The value the text holds with its objects kept as objects, or null when the text is not JSON.

methods.name: file
methods.doc: The value a JSON file holds, objects as arrays; with `or:` given, a missing or broken file gives that instead.

methods.name: repair
methods.doc: A value with every string and key made valid UTF-8, each invalid byte becoming "?", objects read as plain objects of their public properties.

methods.name: decodeKeepingEmptyObjects
methods.doc:
JSON as arrays, but an empty object stays an object: an in-process
REST answer keeps `{}` where the reference's data holds an empty
object (a global style's emptied settings), which decoding to arrays
would turn into `[]`.

methods.name: member
methods.doc: One member of an array or object: a nested one goes a level deeper, a string is repaired.

methods.name: text
methods.doc: A string made valid UTF-8: each invalid byte becomes "?", the valid characters stay.

classes.name: Minn\Login\LoginController
classes.doc:
Signing in. The page people see is /minn-admin/login: the form, the
lost-password and reset flows, and logout all live there and link there.
/wp-login.php stays as the address tooling knows (one-time login links,
uptime probes, scripted sign-ins) and answers in place with the same
shapes; a bare GET of it sends a browser to the clean page. Sessions
and cookies validate on the engine AND on WordPress either way.

constants.name: SEGMENTS
constants.doc: Clean path segment => the action wp-login.php spells with ?action=.

methods.name: form
methods.doc: The sign-in, lost-password, reset, and logout pages.

methods.name: signIn
methods.doc: Handles the posted form for each of those pages.

methods.name: page
methods.doc: The page a GET asks for: the sign-in form, or the action it names.

methods.name: landingFor
methods.doc: Where a sign-in from this page lands, through login_redirect: the address asked for, or the admin, with who the sign-in found.

methods.name: asked
methods.doc: The address a sign-in from this page asks for, and where it lands without one (the admin). @return array{0: string, 1: string}

methods.name: checkEmail
methods.doc: The check-your-email page's word, as the reference's: the confirmation link is on its way, or the registration is done.

methods.name: signInNotices
methods.doc: A sign-in page's notices after wp_login_errors, handed where a sign-in would land (the admin, unless the page names a landing).

methods.name: lostPassword
methods.doc: POST lostpassword mints a key and mails the link; POST resetpass saves the new password. Null for other actions.

methods.name: retrieve
methods.doc:
A reset asked for with plugins loaded, as the reference asks for it
(retrieve_password, its hooks and mail): the page again with the
refusal in its words, or on to "check your email". An unknown
account still counts against the address's attempts.

methods.name: openResetLink
methods.doc:
The link from the email: the key moves into a cookie scoped to
wp-login.php and the browser lands on the form without the key in
its address bar, as on the reference.

methods.name: resetSession
methods.doc: The user and key from the reset cookie, when the key is still good. @return array{0: ?array, 1: string}

methods.name: register
methods.doc:
Registration, when the site allows it (else off to the sign-in page
saying so): the form (its landing as registration_redirect says), or
a POST through register_new_user, landing where the form said (else
on the sign-in page, to check the email), or back on the form with
every refusal in its words.

methods.name: validateReset
methods.doc:
A new password judged as the reference judges it: the mismatch, then
whatever validate_password_reset adds.

methods.name: parts
methods.signature: parts(string $action, string $title, string $siteName, ?Minn\Content\UserRecord $user = NULL, ?Minn\Login\LoginNotices $notices = NULL): array
methods.doc:
What plugins put on one of the sign-in pages (LoginHooks::page()), for
a page titled $title, with its notices printed; without plugins, the
notices alone. @return array<string, string>

methods.name: tokenLogin
methods.doc:
The one-time login link `wp user login` and `minn login` print
(OneTimeLink), on this page or wp-login.php: spent on use, then on to
redirect_to when it names this site, else the admin. Any failure reads
the same so ids cannot be probed.

methods.name: submitted
methods.doc: What a POST does: signs in, or runs the action it names.

methods.name: adminEmail
methods.doc:
The administration email check (action confirm_admin_email): the
screen, or on to where the sign-in was going once the address is
confirmed or the reminder put off; someone who may not answer it is
sent to sign in.

methods.name: withTestCookie
methods.doc:
A wp-login.php answer with the test cookie set ahead of any other,
as the reference's login page sets it on every request but the bare
address (which the engine sends to its own sign-in page): for the
session, on the cookie path and the site path when that differs,
secure on HTTPS, HTTP only.

methods.name: testCookies
methods.doc: The test cookie as the login page sets it: for the session, on the cookie path and the site path when that differs. @return list<array{0: string, 1: string, 2: array<string, mixed>}>

methods.name: safeRedirect
methods.doc:
Only this site's own URLs are sign-in destinations: a path, or an
absolute URL on the home host. Anything else lands in the admin.

methods.name: logout
methods.doc:
Logging out ends the server-side session as well as the cookies, and
needs the session's own nonce so a stray link cannot do it; without
the nonce the reader is asked first.

methods.name: confirmLogOut
methods.doc:
The reference's confirmation for a log out that brings no valid nonce
(wp_nonce_ays): its die page, a 403, asking again with a link that
carries one; the request ends here.

methods.name: action
methods.doc:
The action asked for: a clean path segment (/minn-admin/login/reset)
or wp-login.php's ?action=. The reset flow's two halves share the
"reset" segment; a POST there saves the password.

methods.name: actionUrl
methods.doc: An action's address on the page this request came in on: a path under the clean page, a query on wp-login.php.

methods.name: siteName
methods.doc: The site's name, as the sign-in pages head themselves ("Site" when it has none).

methods.name: base
methods.doc: The sign-in page this request arrived at: the clean page, or wp-login.php for the tooling that still names it.

methods.name: tooManyAttempts
methods.doc: A guessed-at address waits out the window; the page says so and the status lets tooling see it.

methods.name: render
methods.doc: The sign-in page, its notices through wp_login_errors first.
