classes.name: Minn\Login\LoginHooks
classes.doc:
The sign-in as plugins see it, when they are loaded. The credentials go
through the reference's authenticate chain, so a plugin may refuse a
sign-in (a breached password, a second factor, a locked account) or
accept one the password alone would not; wp_login_failed is the chain's
own report. wp_login follows a good sign-in and wp_logout a sign-out.
The refusal is shown as the page's notices (LoginNotices): the chain's
own as one vague sentence, a plugin's in its own words.

methods.name: authenticate
methods.doc:
The credentials through wp_authenticate and the authenticate filters,
as the reference's sign-in runs them: the user, or the refusal (a
WP_Error, or null when the chain gave none).

methods.name: signedIn
methods.doc:
After a good sign-in. The chain read the user through the runtime,
which cached their meta before the new session was written, so the
cache is let go first: a plugin reading session_tokens on wp_login
(CleanTalk keeps the first session's address) must see the new one.

methods.name: enter
methods.doc: A sign-in page request arriving, as wp-login.php announces it: login_init, then login_form_{action}.

methods.name: page
methods.signature: page(string $action, string $title, string $siteName, string $homeUrl, ?Minn\Content\UserRecord $user = NULL, ?Minn\Login\LoginNotices $notices = NULL): array
methods.doc:
What plugins put on the sign-in page, where the reference's page puts
it: the title (login_title), the head (login_enqueue_scripts, then
login_head, which prints the styles and scripts), the body classes
(login_body_class), the header's link and words (login_headerurl,
login_headertext), the message above the form (login_message), the
page's notices (login_errors, login_messages), the fields inside the
form (login_form, lostpassword_form or resetpass_form, as the page
is), and the footer (login_footer).
shapes: @return array{title: string, head: string, bodyClass: string, headerUrl: string, headerText: string, message: string, errors?: string, messages?: string, form: string, footer: string}

methods.name: landing
methods.doc: Where a sign-in lands, as login_redirect says (the requested address beside it, and the user it found or why not).

methods.name: leaving
methods.doc: Where a sign-out lands, as logout_redirect says.

methods.name: signedOut
methods.doc: After a sign-out ended the session.

methods.name: signInFurniture
methods.doc:
What the sign-in page asks plugins about its own furniture, as the
reference's page asks: the word beside Remember Me
(login_remember_me_help_text), the lost-password link
(lost_password_html_link), what stands between the page's links
(login_link_separator), and whether the name field takes the focus
(enable_login_autofocus).
shapes: @return array{rememberHelp: string, lostLink: string, separator: string, autofocus: bool}

methods.name: lostPasswordPage
methods.doc:
The lost-password page's questions, as the reference's page asks them:
what stands between its links, where the form sends a reader once the
mail is out (lostpassword_redirect, kept in the form), and lost_password
with the page's errors. Returns the address the form keeps.

methods.name: postPasswordExpiry
methods.doc: When a post password's cookie runs out (post_password_expires; 0 is when the browser closes).

classes.name: Minn\Login\LoginNotices
classes.doc:
What a sign-in page tells the reader, held as the reference's pages hold
it: notices by code, each an error or (severity "message") a message,
their words as HTML. Printed, the errors are one paragraph, or a list
when there are several, and the messages a paragraph each; with plugins
loaded the sign-in page hands them through wp_login_errors first, and
every page prints them through login_errors and login_messages. The
authenticate chain's own refusals read as the engine's one sentence, so
a page never says which half of a sign-in was wrong.

shapes: @param list<array{0: string, 1: string, 2: string}> $notices code, HTML, severity ('' or 'message')

constants.name: REFUSALS
constants.doc: The chain's own refusals, which the page words as one.

constants.name: REFUSED
constants.value: 'Error: The username or password you entered is incorrect.'
constants.doc: The one sentence for any of them.

methods.name: none
methods.doc: No notices.

methods.name: plain
methods.doc: The engine's own plain words as one notice; an "Error:" lead takes the reference's strong label.

methods.name: refused
methods.doc: A sign-in refused: the chain's refusal, or (none given, or not one) the engine's one sentence.

methods.name: of
methods.doc: The notices a WP_Error holds (a plugin may have handed back something else: then none).

methods.name: with
methods.doc: These notices and one more.

methods.name: isEmpty
methods.doc: Whether there are none.

methods.name: wpError
methods.doc: As the WP_Error plugins are handed.

methods.name: forSignIn
methods.doc: The sign-in page's notices after wp_login_errors, which is handed where a sign-in would land.

methods.name: areas
methods.doc:
The error and message areas' HTML ('' for an area with none),
through login_errors and login_messages.

methods.name: words
methods.doc: Plain words as notice HTML.

classes.name: Minn\Login\OneTimeLink
classes.doc:
The one-time sign-in link hosting tools mint (the captaincore helper's
contract, which Cove and CaptainCore share): a token in the user's meta,
good once, for fifteen minutes. `wp user login` and `minn login` mint it;
the sign-in page spends it. Five wrong guesses at one user's token burn
it, as the helper's own validator does, because a helper-minted token is
only seven hex characters and reaches the engine too.

constants.name: LIFETIME
constants.doc: Seconds a token stays good after it is minted.

constants.name: MISS_LIMIT
constants.doc: Wrong guesses at one token before it is burnt.

methods.name: mint
methods.doc:
Mints a fresh token for the user and hands back the link's query
string. The token is 128 bits, stored raw (the helper's format, which
it compares verbatim when a hide-login plugin keeps the engine's page
from answering); a database read yields the link, which the window
and the single use bound.

methods.name: redeem
methods.doc: Whether the token given is the user's live one; a match is spent, a miss counted, a stale token cleared.

methods.name: clear
methods.doc: Forgets the user's token, its mint time and its miss count.

classes.name: Minn\Login\ServeLogin
classes.doc:
Thrown by the wp-login.php shape file when plugin code require's it
mid-request (a hide-login plugin serving its own sign-in URL, the
perfmatters pattern). Engine::respond() catches it and answers the
current request with the sign-in surface.

classes.name: Minn\Mail\AddressRules
classes.doc:
Email addresses: the checks a mailer can apply (PHP's filter, the
RFC 5322 grammar with comments, quoted local parts and domain literals,
the HTML5 form rule), parsing an address list, and the domain of an
address in ASCII.

constants.name: EAI
constants.doc:
The html5 check with letters, marks and numbers of any script beside
ASCII's (email address internationalization): what the validator
becomes once an address with such a local part is added. A domain
label is at most 63 characters, counted as characters.

methods.name: adding
methods.doc:
The validator once an address is added as a recipient or reply-to:
the default ("php") becomes "eai" for good when the address's local
part has 8-bit characters, whether or not the address then passes;
any other validator, a domain alone with 8-bit characters, and the
From address leave it as it is (measured on the reference).

methods.name: valid
methods.doc: Whether the address passes the named check ("php", "pcre", "pcre8", "html5", "eai", "noregex").

methods.name: parseList
methods.doc:
The addresses in a comma-separated list, as the reference's simple
parser reads one: split at every comma, quoted or not, each entry
with its display name (encoded words decoded into $charset); entries
that are not valid addresses are left out. Each call raises the
reference's notice that the simple parser is in use.

methods.name: asciiDomain
methods.doc: The address with its domain in ASCII (IDNA), the domain read from $charset first; unchanged when it cannot be.

methods.name: quoted
methods.doc: The text as an RFC 822 quoted string when it holds a character that needs one.

methods.name: rfc5322
methods.doc: RFC 5322 addr-spec with comments and folding white space, a quoted local part or a domain literal; local part 64, label 63 characters.

classes.name: Minn\Mail\ChangeNotices
classes.doc:
The notices the reference mails a user when their password or email
address changes, as templates: plugins filter them (password_change_email,
email_change_email) with the placeholders still in them and the site name
still a %s in the subject, and fill() finishes them after.

methods.name: password
methods.doc: The password notice: subject and message, placeholders unfilled. @return array{subject: string, message: string}

methods.name: email
methods.doc: The email-address notice, sent to the address being left: subject and message, placeholders unfilled. @return array{subject: string, message: string}

methods.name: fill
methods.doc: A template's placeholders filled with their values. @param array<string, string> $values placeholder name (USERNAME, ...) => value

classes.name: Minn\Mail\Composer
classes.doc:
A message as the reference's mailer writes it: the header block (Date,
the address lines, Subject, Message-ID, X-Mailer, custom headers,
MIME-Version), the MIME header for its type, and the body, multipart
when it has an alternative, inline parts or attachments. Boundaries are
"b1=_{id}" to "b3=_{id}"; a 7-bit-clean body declared 8bit goes out as
7bit us-ascii, and a body with a line past 998 characters as
quoted-printable.

methods.name: body
methods.doc: The body and the encoding a single-part message declares.

methods.name: headers
methods.doc: The header block, MIME-Version and the MIME header included.

methods.name: mimeHeaders
methods.doc: The MIME header for the message's type: the content type (with its boundary) and the transfer encoding.

methods.name: mailOnlyHeaders
methods.doc: The To and Subject lines PHP's mail() takes as arguments, written after the headers in the sent copy; no To is undisclosed recipients.

methods.name: addressLine
methods.doc: "Name: a, b" for a list of [address, name] pairs.

methods.name: address
methods.doc: One address as a header writes it: the address alone, or the name (as a phrase) and the address in angle brackets.

methods.name: secure
methods.doc: Header text with any line break taken out.

methods.name: messageId
methods.doc: The message id given when it is well formed, else one made from the id and the host name.

methods.name: encodingFor
shapes: @return array{0: string, 1: string} the encoding and charset a body part declares

methods.name: partHead
methods.signature: partHead(Minn\Mail\Draft $d, string $boundary, string $charset, string $contentType, string $encoding): string

methods.name: calendar
methods.doc:
A text/calendar part when the message carries one, followed by $after;
its method is the calendar's own (upper-cased) when it is a known one.

methods.name: date
methods.doc: The date given when it reads as a moment already past, else now; either way as RFC 5322 writes it.

methods.name: attachAll
methods.doc: Every attachment of one disposition as parts of the boundary, then the boundary's end; an identical one, or a repeated inline id, goes once.

methods.name: extraLines
shapes: @return list<string> X-Priority, X-Mailer, Disposition-Notification-To and the custom headers

classes.name: Minn\Mail\CustomHeaders
classes.doc:
A mailer's custom headers changed in place (PHPMailer::replaceCustomHeader,
probe db-mail-rewrite-doubts): the first header of the name takes the new
value and the others of that name go; a name nothing has is not added. A
name or value with a line break, or an empty name, changes nothing and
refuses without an error when a header would have taken it.

methods.name: replace
methods.doc: Whether the replacement held, and the headers after it.
shapes: @param list<array{0: string, 1: string}>|array<int, array{0: string, 1: string}> $headers
@return array{0: bool, 1: array<int, array{0: string, 1: string}>}

params.name: headers
params.shape: list<array{0: string, 1: string}>|array<int, array{0: string, 1: string}>

classes.name: Minn\Mail\DataLines
classes.doc:
A message cut into the lines SMTP DATA sends. Any line break (CRLF, CR
or LF) ends a line. A line longer than 998 characters is cut at its last
space within the first 998 (the space dropped), or at 997 when there is
none; in the header block (when the first line reads "Name: ..." with no
space in the name, up to the first empty line) each continuation starts
with a tab. Dot stuffing is the sender's job, after the cut.

methods.name: split
methods.doc: The lines to send, without their line endings.

classes.name: Minn\Mail\DebugOutput
classes.doc:
Where a mailer's debug text goes, as its Debugoutput setting names it: "echo" (a timestamp and a tab, continuation lines indented under the text), "html" (entity-escaped, line breaks dropped, ending in
), "error_log", a PSR-3 logger's debug(), or any other callable, which gets the text and its level. The two printed forms come back as text for the caller to print; the others are delivered here and return null.

methods.name: smtp
methods.doc: Debug text from the SMTP client: the text to print, or null once delivered; its html form carries a timestamp.

methods.name: mailer
methods.doc: Debug text from the mailer itself: the text to print, or null once delivered; its html form has no timestamp.

classes.name: Minn\Mail\Dkim
classes.doc:
DKIM signatures (RFC 6376) as the reference's mailer writes them:
rsa-sha256, relaxed header and simple body canonicalization, the
standard headers signed in the order they appear (plus any extra ones
the caller names), an optional identity, the signed headers copied into
z= when asked, and the signature folded in 73-character pieces.

methods.name: copyingHeaders
methods.doc: The same signer, copying the signed headers into z= as well.

methods.name: quotedPrintable
methods.doc: Text with everything outside the DKIM-safe printable set written as =XX.

methods.name: headers
methods.doc: Relaxed header canonicalization: unfolded, names lower-cased, runs of space collapsed, values trimmed.

methods.name: body
methods.doc: Simple body canonicalization: CRLF line endings and exactly one at the end.

methods.name: sign
methods.doc: The base64 RSA-SHA256 signature of the text, or null when the key cannot be read.

methods.name: signatureHeader
methods.signature: signatureHeader(string $headerBlock, string $subject, string $body, int $time, array $extra, string $eol): ?string
methods.doc: The DKIM-Signature header for a message, signed at $time.
shapes: @param list<string> $extra lower-case names of further headers to sign

params.name: extra
params.doc: lower-case names of further headers to sign

methods.name: signedHeaders
shapes: @return array{0: list<string>, 1: list<string>, 2: list<string>} names, header lines and z= copies

classes.name: Minn\Mail\Draft
classes.doc:
Everything a message is composed from: the transport it goes out on
(which decides the line ending, the header line length, and where To,
Subject and Bcc are written), the envelope, the content, the headers,
and the attachments as [path or data, file name, name, encoding, type,
is data, disposition, content id]. $toHeader is "list" (To, or
undisclosed-recipients when there is neither To nor Cc) or "omit" (one
message per recipient, the address given to each send instead).

constructor.signature: __construct(string $mailer, string $eol, string $charset, string $contentType, string $encoding, string $subject, string $body, string $altBody, string $ical, string $from, string $fromName, array $to, array $cc, array $bcc, array $replyTo, string $messageId, string $messageDate, ?int $priority, string $xMailer, string $confirmReadingTo, array $customHeaders, array $attachments, string $toHeader = 'list')
shapes: @param list<array{0: string, 1: string}> $to address and name pairs, as are $cc, $bcc and $replyTo
@param list<array{0: string, 1: string}> $customHeaders name and value pairs

params.name: to
params.doc: address and name pairs, as are $cc, $bcc and $replyTo

methods.name: lineLength
methods.doc: The longest header line the transport takes before it must fold.

methods.name: encodeHeader
methods.doc: Header text encoded for this message's charset and transport.

methods.name: messageType
methods.doc: Which parts the message has: plain, or "alt", "inline", "attach" joined by "_".

classes.name: Minn\Mail\HeaderWords
classes.doc:
Header text as mail carries it (RFC 2047): left alone when it is plain
and short enough, quoted when a phrase needs it, otherwise encoded words
in Q (mostly ASCII) or B (mostly not), folded to the line length the
transport allows: 63 for PHP's mail(), 998 otherwise. Plain text only
becomes an encoded word to be folded when it is too long for one line.

methods.name: encode
methods.signature: encode(string $text, string $position, string $charset, int $lineLength, string $eol): string
methods.doc: The header text encoded for its position ("text", "phrase" or "comment").

methods.name: q
methods.doc: RFC 2047 "Q" encoding for a position: spaces as "_", and the characters the position cannot carry as =XX.

methods.name: base64Lines
methods.doc:
Base64 lines of at most 63 characters cut at whole characters, so a
multibyte character is never split across encoded words.

methods.name: decode
methods.doc: Encoded words decoded (adjacent ones joined) and converted into $charset; other text passes through.

methods.name: specials
methods.doc: How many characters the position counts as needing encoding.

methods.name: qLines
methods.signature: qLines(string $text, string $position, string $charset, int $width, string $eol): array

classes.name: Minn\Mail\HostEntry
classes.doc:
One entry of a mailer's Host setting ("host", "host:port",
"ssl://host:465", "tls://host"; entries are separated by semicolons):
the security prefix, the host and the port. Only ssl:// and tls:// are
prefixes; anything else stays part of the host and fails the host check.

methods.name: parseAll
methods.doc: The entries of a Host setting, null where one cannot be read.
shapes: @return list<array{0: string, 1: self|null}> the trimmed entry text and its reading

methods.name: portOr
methods.doc: The port to connect on: the entry's own when it is one (1 to 65535), else the mailer's Port (probe db-mail-rewrite-doubts).

methods.name: takesOfferedTls
methods.doc: Whether a server's STARTTLS offer is taken on its own: never for localhost, nor without OpenSSL.

methods.name: serverName
methods.doc:
The name the mailer gives itself (serverHostname): the configured
Hostname, else the request's SERVER_NAME when one is set (even empty),
else the machine's; one that is not a valid host is
localhost.localdomain.

methods.name: validHost
methods.doc: Whether a host name, IPv4 address or bracketed IPv6 address is well formed.

classes.name: Minn\Mail\HtmlMessage
classes.doc:
What a mailer reads out of an HTML message: the images it can carry
inline (a src or background naming a file under the base directory, or
a data: URI of a raster image), the content id each one gets (the first
32 hex digits of a SHA-256 of the URL, or of a data URI's bytes, at
"phpmailer.0"), and the plain-text version (head, style and script
dropped, tags stripped, entities decoded into the charset).

constants.name: NO_TEXT
constants.value: 'This is an HTML-only message. To view it, activate HTML in your email application.'

methods.name: images
methods.doc: Every quoted src or background value, in document order.

methods.name: dataImage
methods.doc: A data: URI's bytes and type when it is a raster image, else null.

methods.name: localPath
methods.doc: A relative path with no scheme and no step up out of the base directory, or null.

methods.name: cid
methods.doc: The content id the mailer gives an image.

methods.name: text
methods.doc: The plain-text version of an HTML message.

classes.name: Minn\Mail\MailHeaders
classes.doc:
The headers argument of wp_mail() read the way the reference reads it:
a string split into lines (CRLF or LF) or a list of lines; a line
without a colon is skipped. From gives an address and a name (quotes
dropped); Cc, Bcc and Reply-To add comma-separated entries (a comma
inside quotes still splits); Content-Type gives a type and either a
charset or a boundary (a boundary leaves the charset empty); every
other header is kept by name, the last of a name winning.

methods.name: parse
methods.doc: The headers argument, as a string of lines or a list of them.

methods.name: recipient
methods.doc: One recipient entry as [address, name]: "Name <address>" (the name as written) or a bare address.

classes.name: Minn\Mail\MailLog
classes.doc:
The engine's development transport: each message as one JSON line
(time, from, to, subject, body) appended to wp-content/minn-mail.log.php,
nothing sent. The file opens with a line that returns from any request
for it, so a web server that runs PHP never serves the reset links it
holds (audit Low: it was a plain .log under the webroot).

constants.name: GUARD
constants.doc: The first line of the file: PHP that returns before the rest is sent.

methods.name: forSite
methods.doc: The site's log file.

methods.name: read
methods.doc: The messages a log file holds, oldest first (its guard line aside).

methods.name: write
methods.signature: write(string $file, string $from, string $fromName, array $to, string $subject, string $body): bool
methods.doc: Appends one message; false when the file cannot be written.

classes.name: Minn\Mail\MailSettings
classes.doc:
How mail leaves the site, from the minn_mail option (JSON or a serialized
array): the PHP mail
function by default, SMTP when configured, or a log file for development.
The sender defaults to the site name at a no-reply address on the home host.

constructor.signature: __construct(string $transport = 'mail', string $host = '', int $port = 587, string $encryption = 'tls', string $username = '', string $password = '', string $fromEmail = '', string $fromName = '')

methods.name: stored
methods.doc:
What the minn_mail option holds, without defaults: empty when the site
has not configured mail.

methods.name: fromSite
methods.doc: The site's mail settings from its minn_mail option, or the defaults.

methods.name: toArray
methods.doc: The option's JSON, secrets included, for the settings surface.

classes.name: Minn\Mail\Mailer
classes.doc:
Sends a Message through the configured transport. Failures are logged
and reported as false; nothing here throws into a request.

methods.name: forSite
methods.doc: A mailer using the site's own settings.

methods.name: mail
methods.doc:
The one-line send: a recipient, a subject, a body, through the site's
transport and sender, with nothing to construct at the call site.

methods.name: commentHeaders
methods.signature: commentHeaders(string $author, string $email, string $host, string $charset, string $siteName): string
methods.doc:
The headers a comment notice is sent with, as the reference writes
them: from the commenter's name (the site's when they gave none) at
wordpress@ the site's host (no www.), plain text in the site's
charset, replies to the commenter's address when there is one, the
bare address for a nameless commenter (probe functions-formatting-doubts).

methods.name: noticesFor
methods.doc: The engine's own notices, worded once, from this site's name and address.

methods.name: send
methods.doc:
Sends one message; false on failure. With WordPress's mail function
loaded the message goes through wp_mail(), so its filters and the
phpmailer_init hook (an SMTP plugin's way in) apply as they do on the
reference; otherwise through the configured transport directly.

methods.name: draft
methods.signature: draft(string $mailer, string $from, string $fromName, array $to, Minn\Mail\Message $message): Minn\Mail\Draft

classes.name: Minn\Mail\MailerStrings
classes.doc:
The mailer's English messages, keyed as plugins look them up
("authenticate", "provide_address", ...): the base set, and the set
WordPress's own mailer subclass loads, which words four of them
differently. Captured from the reference into data/mailer-strings.json.

methods.name: base
methods.doc: The base mailer's messages.

methods.name: wordpress
methods.doc: The messages WordPress's mailer subclass loads.

methods.name: word
methods.doc:
One message by key from a loaded set (PHPMailer::lang): the key itself
when the set lacks it; a failed SMTP connect points to the
troubleshooting page.

classes.name: Minn\Mail\Message
classes.doc: One outgoing plain-text email.

methods.name: to
methods.doc: One recipient or several, and the two things every mail has.

classes.name: Minn\Mail\MimeTypes
classes.doc:
The MIME type a mailer gives an attachment by its file extension (the
table the reference's mailer answers with); anything else is
application/octet-stream.

methods.name: forExtension
methods.doc: The type for an extension, in any case.

methods.name: forFilename
methods.doc: The type for a file name or path: its last extension (a query string ignored).

classes.name: Minn\Mail\Notices
classes.doc:
The messages the engine itself sends, worded as the reference words them
and built in one place, so a controller and a CLI verb that announce the
same thing say the same thing.

methods.name: passwordReset
methods.doc: The password reset link, with the requester's address as the reference prints it.

methods.name: moderation
methods.doc: A comment waiting in the queue, announced to the site's address.

methods.name: newComment
methods.signature: newComment(string $authorEmail, string $postTitle, string $author, string $comment, string $link): Minn\Mail\Message
methods.doc: An approved comment on a post, announced to the post's author.

methods.name: newNote
methods.signature: newNote(string $authorEmail, string $postTitle, string $author, string $note, string $editLink): Minn\Mail\Message
methods.doc: A post's author told of a note on it, with where the post is edited (notes live in the editor).

methods.name: subject
methods.doc: Every notice the reference sends carries the site's name in brackets.

classes.name: Minn\Mail\PathParts
classes.doc:
A path's parts the way a mailer names attachments, safe for multibyte
names: the directory ('' when there is none), the last segment, its
extension (after the last dot, so ".hidden" is all extension) and the
name before it. Either slash separates; trailing ones are ignored.

methods.name: of
methods.doc: The path's four parts.
shapes: @return array{dirname: string, basename: string, extension: string, filename: string}

classes.name: Minn\Mail\SendmailLine
classes.doc:
The command a mailer pipes a message to for sendmail and qmail (probe
db-mail-rewrite-doubts): sendmail reads the recipients from the message
and ignores lone dots (-i -t), qmail takes nothing more; the envelope
sender goes as -f only when it is a valid, shell-safe address, whatever
the sendmail options say.

methods.name: command
methods.doc: The command line for a mailer kind ("sendmail" or "qmail"), the sender given only when it may be passed.

classes.name: Minn\Mail\Smime
classes.doc:
S/MIME signing of a composed MIME entity with a certificate and key on
disk: the entity goes through OpenSSL as a detached signature and comes
back as new MIME headers (multipart/signed) and the signed body.

methods.name: sign
methods.doc: The signed entity's MIME headers and body, or null when signing fails.

methods.name: entityHeaders
methods.doc:
The MIME headers of the entity that is signed: a multipart entity whose
body is 7-bit clean is not declared 8bit (probe db-mail-rewrite-doubts).

classes.name: Minn\Mail\Smtp
classes.doc:
Delivery over SMTP for the engine's own mail when WordPress's mail
function is not loaded: the site's server, SSL or STARTTLS, a sign-in
when a user name is set, one message per connection, through the same
SmtpSession the PHPMailer SMTP class speaks with.

methods.name: sendRaw
methods.doc:
Sends one composed message (headers, a blank line, the body) to the
envelope recipients; false on any refusal.

classes.name: Minn\Mail\SmtpSession
classes.doc:
One SMTP conversation as the reference's client holds it: the socket,
the last reply, the server's extensions from EHLO, and the last error as
{error, detail, smtp_code, smtp_code_ex}. Every command names itself in
its error ("RCPT TO command failed"); a command sent before connecting
fails as "Called X without being connected". Debug text goes to the
given closure with its level: 1 client lines, 2 server replies, 3
connection events, 4 raw inbound lines. Credentials never reach it.

methods.name: limits
methods.doc: How long one read may wait and how long a whole reply may take, in seconds.

methods.name: connect
methods.doc: Opens the connection and reads the greeting.

methods.name: startTls
methods.doc: Asks for TLS and turns it on.

methods.name: authenticate
methods.doc:
Signs in with the named mechanism, or the strongest the server offers
when it is empty or not offered.

params.name: oauth
params.doc: a ready XOAUTH2 token, base64, when there is one

methods.name: connected
methods.doc: Whether the connection is open; a socket closed at the far end is closed here too.

methods.name: close
methods.doc: Closes the socket and forgets the server's greeting and extensions; the last error stays.

methods.name: data
hello
methods.doc: EHLO, falling back to HELO; the extensions come from the EHLO reply.

methods.name: mail
methods.doc: MAIL FROM, with the given parameters (" XVERP", " SMTPUTF8") after the address.

methods.name: quit
methods.doc: QUIT; the connection closes when it succeeds, or anyway unless told to keep it.

methods.name: recipient
methods.doc: RCPT TO, with the delivery notifications asked for (NEVER, SUCCESS, FAILURE, DELAY).

methods.name: xclient
methods.doc: XCLIENT with the named attributes that are in $allowed; others are dropped.

methods.name: turn
methods.doc: TURN is refused here, as the reference refuses it.

methods.name: command
methods.doc:
Sends one command and reads the reply; a reply outside $expect fails
with "{name} command failed" and the reply's detail and codes.

methods.name: send
methods.doc: Writes raw text to the server; credential commands show as hidden in the debug text.

methods.name: error
methods.doc: The last error; every field is empty after a command that succeeded.
shapes: @return array{error: string, detail: string, smtp_code: int|string, smtp_code_ex: string}

methods.name: extensions
methods.doc: The extensions from the last EHLO (or the HELO greeting), null before one.

methods.name: extension
methods.doc: One extension's value: true for a bare one, a string or list for one with arguments, false when absent, null before EHLO.

methods.name: lastReply
methods.doc: The server's last reply, every line.

methods.name: transactionId
methods.doc: The queue id the server gave the last message: null before one was sent, false when none was recognised.

methods.name: parseReply
methods.doc: The reply's code, enhanced code (when present) and the text after them.

classes.name: Minn\Mail\TextWrap
classes.doc:
Word wrapping for mail text. Lines break at spaces once they would pass
the length; existing line breaks stay; a word longer than the line stays
whole in plain text, and in quoted-printable text is cut into pieces
ending in a soft break ("="), never inside an =XX escape or (for UTF-8)
inside an encoded character. A line broken at a space keeps the space
and, in quoted-printable text, a soft break after it.

methods.name: plain
methods.doc: Plain text wrapped to the length, every line ending in $eol.

methods.name: quotedPrintable
methods.doc: Quoted-printable text wrapped to the length with soft breaks, every line ending in $eol.

methods.name: utf8Boundary
methods.doc:
Where to cut quoted-printable UTF-8 text at or before $max without
splitting an encoded character.

methods.name: wrapWith

and video streams, its playing time and bitrate, and its tags. The
format is found by the file's first bytes; a file named .mp3 with none

reader measures them (probe media-meta). The movie header gives the
playing time and the time it was made; each track's first sample entry
gives its codec. Only AAC ("mp4a") is read as audio, and it alone makes a
file audio/mp4 (or video/mp4 beside a video track); anything else is
video/quicktime. A video entry with a vendor is read the QuickTime way
(its compressor's name, lossless false); one without, the ISO way (a
named codec, and "mp4" as the format for the codecs it knows). Only H.264
and MPEG-4 video have the bitrate the audio leaves.

classes.doc:
MPEG audio (MP3, and layers 1 and 2) as the reference's audio reader
measures it (probe media-meta). The first frame gives the version,
layer, sample rate and channels. An Xing or Info frame (written by LAME
and most encoders) gives the frame and byte counts: a variable bitrate is
the bytes over the frames' duration, and the playing time is the audio's
bytes less one average frame, at that bitrate. Without one the bitrate is
the first frame's and the playing time is every byte at it.

The audio from $start (after any ID3v2 tag) to $end (before any
ID3v1 tag): the stream's description, its bitrate and playing time,
and where its frames lie; null when no frame is found.
shapes: @return array{audio: array<string, mixed>, bitrate: int|float, playtime_seconds: int|float, avdataoffset: int, avdataend: int}|null

methods.name: frameHeader
methods.doc:
A frame header's fields; null for one that is not valid MPEG audio:
no sync, a reserved version or layer, a free or bad bitrate, or a
reserved sample rate.
shapes: @return array{version: int, layer: int, bitrate: int, sampleRate: int, padding: int, mode: int, channels: int, samples: int, length: int}|null

methods.name: scan
methods.doc:
The frames of a stream from an offset to an end, as the reference
measures them inside another container (probe media-meta): data
that does not begin with a frame has none; the stream starts where
51 frames follow one another (or fewer that run to the end), the
first of them its first; when those frames share a
rate it is the stream's, and otherwise every frame to the end counts
toward the mean, past any bytes between them. Null when no frame is
found.
shapes: @return array{first: array<string, int>, bitrate: float, variable: bool}|null

methods.name: firstFrame
methods.doc: Where the first frame starts: a header the next one follows, at or after $start.

methods.name: run
methods.doc:
The rates of the frames that follow one another from an offset, up to
a number of them, and where the run stops.

methods.name: nextFrame
methods.doc: Where the next frame header is from an offset (read a block at a time), or null before the end.

methods.name: infoFrame
methods.doc:
The Xing or Info frame's counts and the LAME tag after them, read from
the first frame; null when the first frame is audio.

classes.name: Minn\Media\Av\Ogg
classes.doc:
Ogg files as the reference's media reader measures them (probe
media-meta): Vorbis, Opus, or FLAC in its first packet. The audio is
counted from the end of the comment header to the start of the last
page, and the last page's granule position over the rate is the playing
time (Opus's pre-skip included). A Vorbis stream's options are the
quality its nominal bitrate stands for, when libVorbis made it in stereo
at 44.1 or 48 kHz, and otherwise the nominal bitrate itself.

methods.name: read
methods.doc: The file's analysis.

methods.name: page
methods.doc:
A page at an offset: where it starts and ends, its header length,
granule position, its whole body and its first packet.
shapes: @return array{start: int, end: int, head: int, granule: int, body: string, packet: string}|null

methods.name: lastPage
methods.doc: The last page of the file, found from its end.
shapes: @return array{start: int, end: int, head: int, granule: int, body: string, packet: string}|null

methods.name: vendor
methods.doc: The vendor string a comment header carries after its $skip-byte signature.

methods.name: flacVendor
methods.doc: The vendor of an Ogg FLAC stream's comment block, in the page after its first.

methods.name: vorbisOptions
methods.doc: A Vorbis stream's options: its quality, or its nominal bitrate, or none without one.

classes.name: Minn\Media\Av\Riff
classes.doc:
RIFF files, WAV audio and AVI video, as the reference's media reader
measures them (probe media-meta). A WAV's format chunk describes its
stream (the codec named by its format tag, lossless only for PCM) and
its data chunk times it. An AVI's headers give the frames and their
rate, each stream's format, and the movie list that holds the data; its
video has the bitrate the audio's leaves. MP3 audio in an AVI (or in a
WAV that states its rate) is described from its first frame.

classes.name: Minn\Media\AvifInfo
classes.doc:
An AVIF file's primary image as wp_get_avif_info reports it (probe
media-tags): width and height from its spatial-extent property, bit depth
and channel count from its pixel-information property. The file is an
ISO base media file: an ftyp box naming the avif or avis brand, then a meta
box whose primary item (pitm) is tied to its properties (ipco) by the
association table (ipma). Anything else, or a file it cannot follow, is
unknown in every field.

methods.name: read
methods.doc: The primary image's size, bit depth and channels from a file's first bytes.
shapes: @return array{width: int|false, height: int|false, bit_depth: int|false, num_channels: int|false}

methods.name: isAvif
methods.doc: Whether the ftyp box names the avif or avis brand, as its major brand or a compatible one.

methods.name: primaryItem
methods.doc: The primary item's id from a pitm box: 16 bits in version 0, 32 after.

methods.name: associations
methods.doc: The 1-based property indices the ipma box ties to one item.
shapes: @param array{0: int, 1: int} $ipma the box's content span

methods.name: boxes
methods.doc:
The boxes between two offsets by type, each as its content span (after
the header). A box of size 1 carries a 64-bit size; size 0 runs to the end.

methods.name: ordered
methods.doc: The boxes between two offsets in file order: type, content start, end.

classes.name: Minn\Media\Canvas
classes.doc:
One GD bitmap and the operations the media layer needs on it. Every
operation returns a new canvas; alpha is preserved throughout, which is
what makes PNG and WebP sub-sizes match the reference's.

methods.name: of
methods.doc: A canvas over a GD image already in hand (what WP_Image_Editor_GD::_save is given).

methods.name: image
methods.doc: The GD image behind the canvas (what WP_Image_Editor_GD::_resize hands back).

methods.name: open
methods.doc:
A canvas from an image file, or null when it cannot be decoded or
would not fit in memory. The header names the dimensions before a
pixel is decoded, so a small file that claims a huge canvas is
refused instead of taking the request down.

methods.name: resample
methods.doc: Resamples a source box onto a destination box.
shapes: @param array{0: int, 1: int, 2: int, 3: int, 4: int, 5: int, 6: int, 7: int} $box dst x, dst y, src x, src y, dst w, dst h, src w, src h (the GD argument order)

params.name: box
params.shape: array{0: int, 1: int, 2: int, 3: int, 4: int, 5: int, 6: int, 7: int}
params.doc: dst x, dst y, src x, src y, dst w, dst h, src w, src h (the GD argument order)

methods.name: crop
methods.signature: crop(int $x, int $y, int $width, int $height, ?int $targetWidth = NULL, ?int $targetHeight = NULL): self
methods.doc: A canvas cut to a rectangle, resized to a target when given.

methods.name: rotate
methods.doc: A canvas turned by an angle, or null when GD refuses.

methods.name: flipVertical
methods.doc: A canvas mirrored on either axis.

methods.name: flipHorizontal
methods.doc: A canvas mirrored left to right.

methods.name: copy
methods.doc: An untouched copy of the canvas.

methods.name: write
methods.doc: Writes the bitmap in the given format; the directory is created when missing.

methods.name: progressive
methods.doc: The bitmap written progressively from now on (an interlaced JPEG).

methods.name: baseline
methods.doc: The bitmap written line by line from now on, as it is by default.

methods.name: stream
methods.doc: Writes the image to the output in a format, at a quality.

methods.name: affordable
methods.doc:
Whether a bitmap of these dimensions fits the memory left to this
request: five bytes a pixel for the decoded image (GD keeps four and
a little), twice over because every operation makes a second canvas,
under what memory_limit leaves after what is already in use.

methods.name: memoryLimit
methods.doc: memory_limit in bytes, or null when it is unlimited.

classes.name: Minn\Media\CompatFields
classes.doc:
The attachment's extra fields as the media modal's compat form prints
them (get_compat_media_markup), measured on the reference (probe
media-template-doubts): a hidden menu order, the required-fields note and
a table of rows, a field's own "tr" as given, then its hidden fields. A
text input's value is escaped; a textarea's value, a label and an html
field print as given; any other input prints the field's entry of that
name. Nothing at all when there are no fields.

methods.name: markup
methods.doc: The form's markup.

classes.name: Minn\Media\FileTypes
classes.doc:
File types as WordPress knows them (data/mime.json): every extension's
MIME type, the ones a user may upload, the kind each extension is (image,
audio, document...), and the type a file name's extension says, each
list through the filter plugins hook.

methods.name: table
methods.doc:
The table: mime (extensions => type), allowed (the ones uploads take
by default) and ext2type (kind => extensions).

methods.name: all
methods.doc: Every extension's MIME type (wp_get_mime_types), as mime_types leaves them.

methods.name: allowed
methods.doc:
The types a user (the request's, unless one is given) may upload
(get_allowed_mime_types): HTML and JavaScript too for one with
unfiltered_html; then upload_mimes.

methods.name: check
methods.doc:
The extension and type a file name has among the types given (the
allowed ones by default), false for each when none matches (wp_check_filetype).

methods.name: kinds
methods.doc: The extensions of each kind (wp_get_ext_types), as ext2type leaves them.

methods.name: kindOf
methods.doc: The kind an extension is (wp_ext2type), or null.

classes.name: Minn\Media\Gallery
classes.doc:
The classic `[gallery]` shortcode's markup. Every gallery on a page is
numbered from one shared per-request counter, and the wrapper names both
that number and the post the gallery sits in, so two galleries on one page
can be styled apart.

The single quotes around the wrapper attributes and the tab-indented item
body are the reference's, and themes have styled against them for long
enough that they are contract rather than formatting.

methods.name: render
methods.signature: render(array $items, array $args, int $instance, int $postId, ?string $opening = NULL): string
methods.doc: The gallery shortcode's HTML for these attachments.
shapes: @param list<array{icon: string, orientation: string, caption: string, caption_id: string}> $items
@param array{itemtag: string, icontag: string, captiontag: string, columns: int, size: string} $args

params.name: items
params.shape: list<array{icon: string, orientation: string, caption: string, caption_id: string}>

params.name: args
params.shape: array{itemtag: string, icontag: string, captiontag: string, columns: int, size: string}

methods.name: opening
methods.doc: The gallery's opening element: its instance id, its post, columns and size as classes.

methods.name: defaultStyle
methods.doc:
The style block printed before a gallery when use_default_gallery_style
asks for it (themes without HTML5 galleries), as the reference prints
it (probe filter-inputs-3): the items floated in equal whole-percent
columns, a border on the images, the caption flush left.

methods.name: tag
methods.doc: A caller's tag name, reduced to what may safely open an element.

methods.name: token
methods.doc: A size name reduced to a class token.

classes.name: Minn\Media\Icons
classes.doc:
The icon a file type is shown with, as wp_mime_type_icon finds it (probe
plugin-helpers): the icon folders (core's wp-includes/images/media, and
any icon_dirs adds) read once a request into a name => address map, an
icon of the asked kind (.png or .svg) preferred where both exist; then
the first name the type answers to: an attachment's file extension and
the kind of file it is, the type, its two halves, the type with an
underscore for the slash. Nothing answering (a post that is not there,
a type that is empty) is the default icon.

constants.name: CORE
constants.doc: Core's icons, each kept as .png and .svg.

methods.name: forType
methods.doc: The icon's address for a type or an attachment id.

methods.name: map
methods.doc: Every icon by name, read once a request with the first asker's preferred kind. @return array<string, string>

methods.name: files
methods.doc: A folder's icons by name; core's are known, a plugin's folder is read. @return array<string, string>

classes.name: Minn\Media\ImageMime
classes.doc:
An image file's real type from its first bytes, as the reference sniffs
it before trusting an upload's extension (probe hook-inputs-2): PHP's own
header check for the classic formats (JPEG, PNG, GIF, WebP, BMP, ICO,
TIFF, AVIF), then an ISO media file's major brand for the HEIF family
PHP does not know. A file too short or of another kind has no image type.

constants.name: BRANDS
constants.doc: An ISO base media file's major brand and the image type it declares.

methods.name: of
methods.doc: The image type the file's header declares, or null.

classes.name: Minn\Media\Kind
classes.doc: Whether an attachment is an image, audio or video (by its MIME type) or of a given extension.

constants.name: POST_MIME_TYPES
constants.value: array ( 'image' => array ( 0 => 'Images', 1 => 'Manage Images', 2 => 'Image (%s)', 3 => 'Images (%s)', ), 'audio' => array ( 0 => 'Audio', 1 => 'Manage Audio', 2 => 'Audio (%s)', 3 => 'Audio (%s)', ), 'video' => array ( 0 => 'Video', 1 => 'Manage Video', 2 => 'Video (%s)', 3 => 'Video (%s)', ), 'application/msword,application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document,application/vnd.ms-word.document.macroEnabled.12,application/vnd.ms-word.template.macroEnabled.12,application/vnd.oasis.opendocument.text,application/vnd.apple.pages,application/pdf,application/vnd.ms-xpsdocument,application/oxps,application/rtf,application/wordperfect,application/octet-stream' => array ( 0 => 'Documents', 1 => 'Manage Documents', 2 => 'Document (%s)', 3 => 'Documents (%s)', ), 'application/vnd.apple.numbers,application/vnd.oasis.opendocument.spreadsheet,application/vnd.ms-excel,application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet,application/vnd.ms-excel.sheet.macroEnabled.12,application/vnd.ms-excel.sheet.binary.macroEnabled.12' => array ( 0 => 'Spreadsheets', 1 => 'Manage Spreadsheets', 2 => 'Spreadsheet (%s)', 3 => 'Spreadsheets (%s)', ), 'application/x-gzip,application/rar,application/x-tar,application/zip,application/x-7z-compressed' => array ( 0 => 'Archives', 1 => 'Manage Archives', 2 => 'Archive (%s)', 3 => 'Archives (%s)', ), )
constants.doc:
The media library's filter groups: a MIME pattern (a top-level type, or
a comma list of full types) => its plural label, its manage label, and
the singular and plural count labels.

methods.name: matchWildcards
methods.doc:
Real mime types grouped under the wildcard patterns that match them
(image, audio/*, image/jpeg, *), the last pattern first; a pattern with
no matches is omitted (probe post-remaining).

methods.name: matches
methods.doc:
Whether a file is of a media type (wp_attachment_is): an image, audio
or video by its mime type alone, whatever its extension says; any
other type by the file's extension.

classes.name: Minn\Media\MediaModal
classes.doc:
WordPress's media modal, set up for a page that opens it (wp_enqueue_media):
a page builder's editor picks and uploads images through it. Its scripts,
styles, words and templates are WordPress's and come with the Minn Legacy
Pack. The engine queues them and tells them about the site, as the
reference does and through the same filters: the post being edited, the
file types and the months the library holds, the nonces, the upload
settings, and the templates printed in the footer. Without the pack's
scripts there is no modal to set up and nothing happens.

methods.name: enqueue
methods.doc: Queues the modal for the page, once a request.
shapes: @param array<string, mixed> $args 'post': the post being edited, an ID or a post object

params.name: args
params.doc: 'post': the post being edited, an ID or a post object

methods.name: uploadSettings
methods.doc:
The upload settings the modal's uploader reads (wp_plupload_default_settings):
where files go, how large, which types, with which nonce, added to the
data the uploader's script already carries.

methods.name: tabs
methods.doc: The upload tabs plugins add; WordPress's own four are the modal's views, not tabs. @return array<string, string>

methods.name: mimeTypes
methods.doc: The library's file-type filter: each kind's label, by its MIME pattern (get_post_mime_types). @return array<string, string>

methods.name: shows
methods.doc: Whether the library offers audio or video playlists: a plugin's answer, or whether it holds any such file.

methods.name: months
methods.doc: The months the library has files from, newest first, as the modal's date filter lists them. @return list<array{year: string, month: string, text: string}>
shapes: @return list<array{year: string, month: string, text: string}>

methods.name: embeds
methods.doc: The audio and video extensions the modal embeds, and the MIME type of each. @return array{list<string>, array<string, string>}

methods.name: maxUploadSize
methods.doc: The largest upload the server takes, the smaller of PHP's two limits, as plugins leave it (upload_size_limit).

methods.name: canUpload
methods.doc: Whether the browser can upload: every desktop, and iOS from 6.

classes.name: Minn\Media\Metadata
classes.doc:
The _wp_attachment_metadata blob: parsed by scanning for the shapes it
holds (top-level dims and file, the sizes map, the image_meta scalars)
and written back in the reference's stored form: a:6 at the top,
image_meta as a:13 with alt last.

methods.name: namesFile
methods.doc:
Whether an image location names the attachment's file, one of its
sizes, or its original (probe media-tags): the location, its query
dropped, must end with the stored path, or with the stored folder and
a size's or the original's file name. A bare file name with no folder
matches nothing.
shapes: @param array<string, mixed> $meta the attachment metadata as stored

methods.name: parse
methods.doc: The attachment metadata blob as an array, tolerant of anything missing.
shapes: @return array{width: int, height: int, file: string, filesize: int, sizes: array<string, array>, image_meta: ?array}

methods.name: blankImageMeta
methods.doc: The image_meta block a fresh upload carries.

classes.name: Minn\Media\PhotoMeta
classes.doc:
A photo's own description, read as the reference's wp_read_image_metadata
reads it (probe image-meta): IPTC first (headline or object name for the
title, caption, credit or byline, copyright, keywords, the date and time
it was made), then EXIF for what IPTC left empty (a short description as
the title, the user comment or description as the caption, the artist,
copyright, model, the digitized time, aperture, focal length, ISO,
exposure, orientation). Text that is not UTF-8 is read as Latin-1, and
every value is cleaned (the reference runs wp_kses_post) and made a
string; a short caption doubles as the title.

constants.name: EXIF_TYPES
constants.doc: EXIF is read for these image types only: JPEG and TIFF, both byte orders.

methods.name: read
methods.doc:
The metadata, the image type, the IPTC and EXIF it came from; null
when there is no such file.
shapes: @return array{meta: array<string, mixed>, type: int|null, iptc: array<string, mixed>, exif: array<string, mixed>}|null

methods.name: described
methods.doc:
The title and caption EXIF gives when IPTC left them empty: a short
description is the title, and the user comment (else the description)
the caption; a description that is not the title runs on into the
comment; a comment alone is the caption; a short caption doubles as the
title.

methods.name: fraction
methods.doc: "28/10" as 2.8; a zero denominator reads 0.

methods.name: exifTime
methods.doc: An EXIF time ("2024:05:06 07:08:09") as a Unix time read as UTC.

methods.name: cleaned
methods.doc: Text made UTF-8 (Latin-1 read as such) and cleaned, every value a string.

classes.name: Minn\Media\Player
classes.doc:
The media player's data as the reference gives MediaElement.js (probe
media-player): its strings in the language in force, and the site's
settings for it.

methods.name: register
methods.doc:
The player's scripts as the reference registers them: MediaElement.js
(MIT, served from minn/assets/vendor), the engine's migration script
and start-up in the reference's own files' place, all in the footer.
Their strings and settings come with data().

methods.name: registerStyles
methods.doc: The player's styles: MediaElement.js's own and the engine's skin.

methods.name: data
methods.doc: The strings (mejsL10n, before the library) and settings (_wpmejsSettings) given to the player's handles.

methods.name: strings
methods.doc: The script that defines mejsL10n: the language determine_locale names, and each string translated.

methods.name: settings
methods.doc:
_wpmejsSettings: where the player's files are, its class prefix and
stretching, and the shortcode libraries, through mejs_settings.

classes.name: Minn\Media\Sizing
classes.doc:
The image size arithmetic the media functions share: the crop or scale a
resize needs, the registered size a requested box picks, and the srcset
candidates an image's sizes yield. Behaviour pinned by contracts/fixtures/api/media.json.

methods.name: constrain
methods.doc:
The largest box inside the limits that keeps the ratio: only sides over
their limit shrink, the smaller ratio wins, and a result one pixel short
of a limit it was constrained by snaps to that limit.

methods.name: resize
methods.signature: resize(int $origW, int $origH, int $destW, int $destH, bool $crop, Closure $constrain): ?array
methods.doc:
The GD-style resize box (dst x, dst y, src x, src y, dst w, dst h, src w, src h),
or null when every asked dimension is larger than the image (nothing to make).
shapes: @param Closure(int, int, int, int): array{0: int, 1: int} $constrain scales a box into a maximum
@return array{0: int, 1: int, 2: int, 3: int, 4: int, 5: int, 6: int, 7: int}|null

params.name: constrain
params.shape: Closure(int, int, int, int): array{0: int, 1: int}
params.doc: scales a box into a maximum

methods.name: sameSize
methods.doc:
Whether a resize box makes the image's own size again, a pixel either
way counting as rounding.
shapes: @param array{0: int, 1: int, 2: int, 3: int, 4: int, 5: int, 6: int, 7: int} $box

params.name: box
params.shape: array{0: int, 1: int, 2: int, 3: int, 4: int, 5: int, 6: int, 7: int}

methods.name: intermediate
methods.doc:
The registered size that serves a request: by name, or for a
requested box the size of exactly that box, else the smallest larger
one in its proportion (the full size never counts), else the
thumbnail when it is wide enough; with its path and URL beside the
file's.
shapes: @param Closure(int, int, array): array{0: int, 1: int} $editorConstrain

params.name: editorConstrain
params.shape: Closure(int, int, array): array{0: int, 1: int}

methods.name: sources
methods.signature: sources(array $sizeArray, string $src, array $meta, Closure $matchesRatio, string $uploadsUrl, Closure $maxWidth): array
methods.doc:
The srcset candidates by width: every size on the image's ratio (and
the same edit, when the file was edited) no wider than the cap, the
source itself winning a width clash and passing the cap.
shapes: @param Closure(array{0: int, 1: int}): int $maxWidth the widest candidate (max_srcset_image_width; 0 for no cap), asked before the folder is checked
@return array<int, array{url: string, descriptor: string, value: int}>

params.name: maxWidth
params.doc: the widest candidate (max_srcset_image_width; 0 for no cap), asked before the folder is checked

methods.name: srcset
methods.doc: The srcset attribute for at least two sources; null for fewer.

methods.name: editorSizes
methods.signature: editorSizes(array $meta, string $baseUrl, string $fullUrl, array $names, Closure $downsize): array
methods.doc: The image sizes an attachment offers the editor, each with orientation. @param Closure(string): (array|false) $downsize

methods.name: oldThumbnail
methods.doc:
The old thumbnail an image's metadata names (its `thumb`), as a file
beside the image with its size, while it is still there (probe
image-downsize).
shapes: @return array{0: string, 1: int, 2: int}|null the file's name, width and height

methods.name: cropBox
methods.doc:
A cropped size's box: each side at most the original's, and a side asked as 0 drawn from the
other in the original's proportion.

classes.name: Minn\Media\Upload
classes.doc:
One file arriving for the library, on either transport: a multipart
field named "file" (a temporary upload to move) or a raw body whose
Content-Disposition names the file. The parent is read from the same
request, wherever the client put it.

methods.name: fromRequest
methods.doc: Null when the request carries no file.

methods.name: filenameFrom
methods.doc:
The file a Content-Disposition names, as the reference reads one
(probe rest-attachments-controller): the parameters after the
disposition type, split on semicolons as written; the last non-empty
filename= of all the headers, unquoted when double
quotes wrap it. "filename" is matched as written, and filename* is
not read. Null when none names one.

methods.name: refusal
methods.doc:
Why a raw body cannot be taken, in the reference's order: no data, no
Content-Type, no Content-Disposition, one naming no file, a
Content-MD5 the data does not match. Null when it can. The headers are
the REST request's, keyed by lower-case names with underscores.

methods.name: mime
methods.doc: The mime type the extension maps to, or null for one the library refuses.

methods.name: parentOf
methods.doc: The post the client wants the file attached to: form field, query, or JSON body.

classes.name: Minn\Media\Uploads
classes.doc: The uploads directory: paths, URLs, the allowed types, and landing a file.

constants.name: MIMES
constants.doc: extension => canonical mime

methods.name: baseDir
methods.doc: The uploads directory on disk.

methods.name: baseUrl
methods.doc: The uploads directory's URL.

methods.name: urlFor
methods.doc: The URL of a file by its relative path.

methods.name: pathFor
methods.doc: The path of a file by its relative path.

methods.name: sanitizeName
methods.doc:
A safe file name: one extension. Every dot-separated part between the
base and the last extension that is not itself an allowed extension
is joined with an underscore, so "shell.php.png" lands as
"shell_php.png" and no handler can be talked into running it.

methods.name: relativeOf
methods.doc: A stored file's path relative to the uploads folder, or null for a file outside it.

methods.name: attachmentFiles
methods.doc:
Every file an attachment owns, in deletion order: the legacy thumb, each
sub-size, the original image, the backup sizes, then the file itself.
shapes: @return list<string> absolute paths, unique, only the main file checked for existence

methods.name: layout
methods.signature: layout(string $uploadPath, string $uploadUrlPath, string $siteUrl, string $contentDir, string $contentUrl, string $abspath, bool $yearMonth, string $time): array
shapes: @return array{path: string, url: string, subdir: string, basedir: string, baseurl: string, error: false}

classes.name: Minn\Media\WebpInfo
classes.doc:
A WebP file's size and kind from its first 40 bytes, as wp_get_webp_info
reads them (probe plugin-queue8): a simple lossy frame (VP8), a lossless
one (VP8L), or the extended form (VP8X), which the reference names
animated-alpha whatever its flags say. Anything shorter or of another
chunk is unknown.

methods.name: read
methods.doc: The width, height and kind a file's first bytes declare. @return array{width: int|false, height: int|false, type: string|false}
shapes: @return array{width: int|false, height: int|false, type: string|false}

classes.name: Minn\Media\Writer
classes.doc:
Where the media library's files live, as a REST upload names them: a
stored file's address, its path on disk, and its path relative to the
uploads folder. The attachment itself is written through the runtime
(wp_handle_upload, wp_insert_attachment, wp_generate_attachment_metadata),
as the reference writes it.

methods.name: urlOf
methods.doc: A stored file's address.

methods.name: pathOf
methods.doc: A stored file's path on disk.

methods.name: relativeOf
methods.doc: A stored file's path relative to the uploads folder, or null for one outside it.

classes.name: Minn\Objects\BlockType
classes.doc:
A registered block type as the WordPress layer hands it to plugins
(WP_Block_Type): its attributes, supports, styles and render callback.
The engine knows these objects by this mark and finds them through
Runtime\Handoff, so it never names the WordPress layer's class.

classes.name: Minn\Objects\Comment
classes.doc:
A comment as the WordPress layer hands it to plugins (WP_Comment). The
engine knows these objects by this mark and makes them through
Runtime\Handoff, so it never names the WordPress layer's class.

classes.name: Minn\Objects\CommentsQuery
classes.doc:
A comments query as the WordPress layer hands it to plugins
(WP_Comment_Query). The engine knows these objects by this mark and makes
them through Runtime\Handoff, so it never names the WordPress layer's
class.

classes.name: Minn\Objects\Dependency
classes.doc:
A registered script or style as the WordPress layer hands it to plugins
(_WP_Dependency): its handle, source, dependencies, version and extra
data. The engine knows these objects by this mark, so it never names the
WordPress layer's class.

classes.name: Minn\Objects\Environment
classes.doc:
The request's environment as the WordPress layer hands it to plugins
(WP, the $wp global): the query variables parsed from the request and
the headers sent. The engine knows it by this mark, so it never names
the WordPress layer's class.

classes.name: Minn\Objects\Errors
classes.doc:
A list of errors as the WordPress layer hands it to plugins (WP_Error):
codes with their messages and data. The engine knows these objects by this
mark and makes them through Runtime\Handoff, so it never names the
WordPress layer's class.

classes.name: Minn\Objects\HttpResponse
classes.doc:
An HTTP response as the WordPress layer hands it to plugins
(WP_HTTP_Response): its data, status and headers. The engine knows these
objects by this mark and makes them through Runtime\Handoff, so it never
names the WordPress layer's class.

classes.name: Minn\Objects\Post
classes.doc:
A post as the WordPress layer hands it to plugins (WP_Post). The engine
knows these objects by this mark and makes them through Runtime\Handoff,
so it never names the WordPress layer's class.

classes.name: Minn\Objects\PostType
classes.doc:
A registered post type as the WordPress layer hands it to plugins
(WP_Post_Type): its labels, capabilities and settings. The engine knows
these objects by this mark and makes them through Runtime\Handoff, so it
never names the WordPress layer's class.

classes.name: Minn\Objects\Query
classes.doc:
A posts query as the WordPress layer hands it to plugins (WP_Query): its
variables, flags, posts and loop. The engine knows these objects by this
mark and makes them through Runtime\Handoff, so it never names the
WordPress layer's class.

classes.name: Minn\Objects\RenderedBlock
classes.doc:
A block being rendered as the WordPress layer hands it to plugins
(WP_Block): its parsed block, attributes, context and inner blocks. The
engine knows these objects by this mark and makes them through
Runtime\Handoff, so it never names the WordPress layer's class.

classes.name: Minn\Objects\RestRequest
classes.doc:
A REST request as the WordPress layer hands it to plugins
(WP_REST_Request): its route, method, parameters, headers and body. The
engine knows these objects by this mark and makes them through
