classes.name: Minn\Ops\Archive
classes.doc:
A zip unpacked the safe way, for the plugin and theme installer and for
the engine's own update alike: every entry stays inside its folder (no
absolute path, no "..", no backslash, no NUL), none is a symbolic link,
there are no more than 20,000 of them, they unpack to no more than
512 MB, and they all sit in exactly one top folder (macOS's __MACOSX
noise aside). Nothing is written until every entry has passed.

methods.name: unpackFolder
methods.doc: Unpacks a zip file into a new folder $stage; the path of the one folder the archive held.

methods.name: inspect
methods.doc: Checks every entry of a zip file without writing anything; the one folder it holds.

methods.name: holds
methods.doc: Whether a zip file holds an entry by that name.

methods.name: isFolderName
methods.doc: A plain folder name: no separators, never "." or "..".

methods.name: isSymlinkEntry
methods.doc: Whether a zip entry is recorded as a symbolic link (a Unix entry whose mode says so).

classes.name: Minn\Ops\Asking
classes.doc:
Why the engine asks the update service: the daily pass, once every 24
hours (marked X-Minn-Check: daily, which the service counts as one site
running that day), or anything else (a person checking, an update needing
a fresh answer), which goes unmarked.

methods.name: headers
methods.doc: The request headers, with the daily mark when this is the daily pass. @param list<string> $headers @return list<string>

classes.name: Minn\Ops\AutoUpdates
classes.doc:
Whether per-item auto-updates apply to plugins or themes, as the
reference decides it (contracts/rest/minn-admin-v1.md "Auto-updates"):
never when file mods are off (DISALLOW_FILE_MODS through file_mod_allowed,
context automatic_updater), never when the updater is disabled
(AUTOMATIC_UPDATER_DISABLED through automatic_updater_disabled, which a
plugin may turn back), and then the type's own filter has the last word.
Only plugins and themes can be on.

shapes: @param Closure(string, mixed, mixed...): mixed $filter applies a filter, as apply_filters does

params.name: filter
params.doc: applies a filter, as apply_filters does

methods.name: forSite
methods.doc: The gate as the site's plugins see it: through their filters (none before any plugin loads, so as configured).

methods.name: enabledFor
methods.doc: Whether per-item auto-updates apply to a type ("plugin" or "theme"; anything else is never on).

methods.name: updaterOff
methods.doc: Whether the automatic updater is off for the whole site: file mods refused, or the updater disabled.

classes.name: Minn\Ops\Changelog
classes.doc:
A changelog read from its repository rather than shipped: a Minn release
carries no notes, its own or Minn Admin's, for anyone to find on the
sites that run it. The update service reads changelog.md from the
repository's default branch on GitHub; the engine asks the service at most
once a day, and again when the version installed changes, and keeps the
copy in an option (JSON) with the time it came and the version it was read
for; sections still marked Unreleased are left out, so a site only reads
about releases that exist. A fetch GitHub does not answer keeps the last copy; a
404 (no such file, or a private repository) keeps nothing.

constructor.signature: __construct(Closure $load, Closure $save, string $source, Minn\Http $http = \Minn\Http::__set_state(array(    'within' =>    array (   ),    'fake' => NULL,    'refusal' => NULL, )))
shapes: @param Closure(): ?string $load the stored copy, as JSON
@param Closure(string): void $save keeps the copy, as JSON

methods.name: engine
methods.doc: Minn's changelog for a site, kept in its minn_changelog option.

methods.name: admin
methods.doc: Minn Admin's changelog for a site running Minn, kept in its minn_admin_changelog option.

methods.name: markdown
methods.doc:
The released sections as Markdown, fetched first when the copy is a day
old or was read for another version than $version (the one installed,
so an update shows its own notes at once); '' when there is none.

methods.name: released
methods.doc: The changelog without its Unreleased sections.

classes.name: Minn\Ops\CoreStatus
classes.doc:
The core the app's update banner and chip speak of, which on Minn is
Minn: the running engine's version, a newer release on offer
(Ops\Releases, asked of the update service once a day), and installing it
(Ops\EngineUpdate). WordPress's own offer (the update_core transient a
parked copy may write) is not Minn's to act on and is not shown.
dbUpgrade is false: the database is WordPress's, and a Minn release
never migrates it.

methods.name: data
methods.doc: Minn's version, any offer, and when the update service was last asked.

methods.name: due
methods.doc: Whether the update service was last asked a day ago or more.

methods.name: refresh
methods.doc: Asks the update service now.

methods.name: update
methods.doc: Installs the release on offer; the version now in place.

classes.name: Minn\Ops\Diagnostics
classes.doc:
The System view's facts about this install: the engine, PHP, the
database, and the server, with the health checks a site owner acts on.
Every number is read live; nothing is cached or fetched from outside.

constructor.signature: __construct(Minn\Db $db, Minn\Content\Site $site, Minn\Front\Permalinks $permalinks, Minn\Ops\InstalledSoftware $software, Minn\Ops\Logs $logs, string $engineVersion, string $webroot)

methods.name: payload
methods.doc: The System view: checks, config, logs, and the four info groups.

methods.name: config
methods.doc: The wp-config debug constants as they stand; the engine never rewrites the file.

methods.name: cron
methods.doc: The scheduled events: the cron option's hooks and the engine's own scheduled posts, soonest first.

methods.name: autoload
methods.doc: The autoloaded options: the summary and the largest rows.

methods.name: checks
methods.doc: The pass / warn / fail rows the System view leads with.

methods.name: wpApi
methods.doc:
The MINN_WP_API row: which mode the site runs in, and what it keeps out.
Auto and off with plugins active warn: on public pages a membership,
private-site, firewall or maintenance plugin no longer decides who reads
what (security sweep 2026-11-12, finding 2.9), and under off they never run.

methods.name: cronOptionEvents
methods.doc:
The cron option's events as rows, a recurring event's interval read
as its recurrence and a single event marked one-off.

methods.name: humanInterval
methods.doc: A recurrence interval as its two largest whole units.

classes.name: Minn\Ops\Directory
classes.doc:
The Minn update service, https://updates.minn.run: the one place the
engine asks about anything it does not have yet, so a site running Minn
talks to Minn and never to wordpress.org. The service speaks
wordpress.org's own endpoints under /v1/ (plugin and theme update checks,
directory search and information, translations) with every address a site
would fetch pointed back at itself: packages under /v1/download/, icons,
screenshots and emoji under /v1/assets/. It also serves Minn's own
releases and changelogs. Every request names the engine and the WordPress
version it is compatible with (which judges a plugin's "Requires at
least"), never the site's address. A development install says "(lab)"
after the version, so the service counts it apart from real sites.

constants.name: LAB_HOST
constants.doc: Host names only a development install answers to.

constants.name: PACKAGES
constants.doc: Where plugin, theme and translation packages download from.

methods.name: url
methods.doc: An address on the service: a path under /v1/, such as "plugins/info/1.2/".

methods.name: userAgent
methods.doc: How the engine introduces itself: its version, "(lab)" from a development install, and nothing about the site.

methods.name: lab
methods.doc:
Whether a site is a development install: its environment type is local
or development, or its address names a development host (localhost, a
.localhost, .test, .local, .example, .invalid or .internal name, a
private or loopback address). Staging counts as a real site.

methods.name: post
methods.signature: post(Minn\Http $http, string $path, array $form, Minn\Ops\Asking $asking = Minn\Ops\Asking::Now): array
methods.doc:
A form POST to the service (the update checks) over the caller's client, its answer decoded.
The daily pass's checks are marked (Asking::Daily): the service counts those, one a site,
as the sites running Minn that day, and keeps nothing else about it.

methods.name: home
methods.doc: The site's address (wp-config's WP_HOME, else the home option), through the options store; '' when it cannot be read.

classes.name: Minn\Ops\DirectoryApi
classes.doc:
plugins_api() and themes_api() as plugins call them and answer them
(probes plugins-api, themes-api), one class for both ($kind 'plugins' or
'themes'): the arguments as an object with the reader's locale and the
major.minor version beside them, through <kind>_api_args; then whatever a
plugin answers through <kind>_api (a seller's own information, or an
error) stands, and only when nobody answers is the directory asked,
through Ops\Packages (behind the Minn update service);
<kind>_api_result is handed what came back either way. A refusal is
<kind>_api_failed in the directory's own words.

shapes: @param Closure(string, mixed...): mixed $filter applies a filter, as apply_filters does

params.name: filter
params.doc: applies a filter, as apply_filters does

methods.name: ask
methods.doc: The answer for an action (plugin_information, query_themes, ...): an object, a WP_Error, or what a plugin returned.

methods.name: unexpected
methods.doc:
An answer that is not JSON. wordpress.org words an unknown theme
action as JSON to WordPress but as a paragraph to anyone else (the
update service), so the paragraph is read as the refusal WordPress
would have been given; anything else is the reference's own message
for an answer it cannot read, the body kept as its data.

classes.name: Minn\Ops\EngineChecksums
classes.doc:
Checks a Minn install's files against the release they claim to be, the
way `wp core verify-checksums` checks WordPress's against wordpress.org:
the update service describes the running version's release, its minn.zip
is downloaded from the service alone and must match its published sha256
and carry a signature from a key this engine trusts (EngineUpdate), and
then every file of the engine is compared with the archive's, as are the
shape files at the webroot with the archive's layout templates. A file
that differs, one the archive has and the install lacks, and one the
install has beyond the archive are all named. The install record
(.install.json) is the site's own and is not compared.

constructor.signature: __construct(string $engineDir, array $keys = Minn\Ops\EngineUpdate::KEYS, Minn\Http $http = \Minn\Http::__set_state(array(    'within' =>    array (   ),    'fake' => NULL,    'refusal' => NULL, )))
shapes: @param list<string> $keys the release keys to trust (tests pass their own)

params.name: keys
params.doc: the release keys to trust (tests pass their own)

constants.name: SOURCE
constants.doc: Where a version's release record is asked for.

methods.name: check
methods.doc:
The comparison: the version checked, and the paths (under minn/, or at
the webroot for shape files) that differ, are missing, or are extra.
shapes: @return array{version: string, changed: list<string>, missing: list<string>, extra: list<string>}

methods.name: release
methods.doc: The release the service describes for a version; it must be one Minn offers, of that version.

methods.name: archiveHashes
methods.doc: The sha256 of every file in the archive's engine folder, by its path inside that folder.

methods.name: treeHashes
methods.doc: The sha256 of every file under the engine folder, by its path inside it; the install record left out.

methods.name: layoutOf
methods.doc: The archive's layout templates by the webroot path each shapes.

methods.name: shapeHashes
methods.doc: The sha256 of the webroot's shape files that exist.

methods.name: compare
methods.doc: Expected against found: the paths that differ, are missing, and are extra, prefixed.
shapes: @return array{changed: list<string>, missing: list<string>, extra: list<string>}

classes.name: Minn\Ops\EngineUpdate
classes.doc:
Replaces the running engine with a published release. The release's
minn.zip comes from the Minn update service and nowhere else (every
redirect hop is judged), must match the sha256 its release records, and
must carry an Ed25519 signature made with a key this engine was built to
trust (KEYS; the secret half never leaves the release maintainer's
machine, so neither GitHub nor the service can stand in a build of their
own). It is unpacked beside the engine into a folder of its own, where it
is checked again: its bootstrap names the version on offer and bin/minn is
there. Then the swap, two renames in the folder the engine lives in: the
running engine moves aside, the new one moves in, and the old copy is
removed; when the second rename fails the first is undone. The webroot's
shape files are laid again from the new engine (ShapeFiles::refresh): one
still as the old engine wrote it, a stock empty placeholder above all, is
replaced, and one the site changed is left alone. The legacy
install record (.install.json, from installs that kept it inside the
engine) comes along. One update runs at a time. A development checkout (a
symbolic link, or a folder under git) is refused: git owns those. The
site keeps answering throughout.

constructor.signature: __construct(string $engineDir, array $keys = self::KEYS, Minn\Http $http = \Minn\Http::__set_state(array(    'within' =>    array (   ),    'fake' => NULL,    'refusal' => NULL, )))
shapes: @param list<string> $keys the release keys to trust (tests pass their own)

params.name: keys
params.doc: the release keys to trust (tests pass their own)

constants.name: KEYS
constants.doc:
The public halves of the keys that sign Minn releases (base64 Ed25519;
scripts/release-key.php). A new key ships here in a release signed by
an old one before it signs anything. The first is the working key; the
second is the recovery key, kept offline and used only to sign a
release that replaces a lost or exposed working key.

methods.name: apply
methods.doc: Downloads, checks and installs a release; the version now in place.

methods.name: install
methods.doc:
Installs an archive in hand once it matches its checksum and signature,
holds the version named, and that version is newer than the running
one: an older release signed in its day is still signed, and putting
it back would bring back what it was replaced for. The version now in
place.

methods.name: verify
methods.signature: verify(string $zip, string $sha256, string $signature, string $version, string $use = 'used'): void
methods.doc: Throws unless an archive matches the checksum its release publishes and carries a signature from a trusted key; $use says what would not happen.

methods.name: versionOf
methods.doc: The version a bootstrap.php names; "0.0.0" when it names none.

methods.name: isCheckout
methods.doc:
A link, or a folder inside a git working copy at any depth (the engine's
own repository keeps it two levels down). Folders open_basedir keeps
PHP out of are not looked in: asking there only warns, on every request
(a host such as Kinsta allows the webroot and not the site folder above it).

methods.name: reachable
methods.doc: Whether open_basedir lets PHP look inside a folder: when it is set, the folder must lie within one of its paths.

methods.name: swap
methods.doc: Unpacks, checks and swaps in the archive, one update at a time (install() holds the lock).

methods.name: signed
methods.doc: Whether one of the trusted keys made this signature over the archive.

classes.name: Minn\Ops\FilesystemCredentials
classes.doc:
How the site reaches its own files, and the connection it asks for when
it cannot write them itself (probes filesystem-credentials and
filesystem-credentials-constants).

The method (get_filesystem_method) is FS_METHOD when set; otherwise
direct when a file made in the folder (the content folder by default)
belongs to the owner of the running script, or when ownership is relaxed
and the file could be made at all; otherwise SSH2, the FTP extension or
FTP over sockets, whichever this PHP has; filesystem_method has the last
word.

The connection (request_filesystem_credentials): request_filesystem_
credentials may answer first; a direct method needs none. The stored
connection (ftp_credentials) is the start, each field then taken from its
FTP_* constant, else from the form posted with a good _fs_nonce when it
is not empty, else as stored; a host's ":port" is split off (kept only
when it is a number); the type is ssh under FTP_SSH, ftps under FTP_SSL,
else as posted, stored, or ftp. With no error to show, a host, a user and
a password (or, over SSH, both key paths) make it complete: it is stored
(not autoloaded) without the password, the keys or the port (the port
back on the host)
and returned. Otherwise the answer is false and the form is printed, as
the reference prints it, after the error's notice (the facade's
wp_admin_notice).

methods.name: method
methods.doc: The method the site's files are reached by (get_filesystem_method).
shapes: @param array{0?: mixed, 1?: mixed, 2?: mixed} $asked the arguments as given: the method's own, the folder, whether ownership is relaxed

params.name: asked
params.doc: the arguments as given: the method's own, the folder, whether ownership is relaxed

methods.name: request
methods.doc:
The connection, or false with the form to print
(request_filesystem_credentials); an error's notice is the caller's.
shapes: @param array{0: mixed, 1?: mixed, 2?: mixed, 3?: mixed, 4?: mixed, 5?: mixed} $asked the arguments as given: the form's address, the type, the error, the folder, the extra fields, whether ownership is relaxed
@return array{0: mixed, 1: string} the answer, then what is printed

params.name: asked
params.shape: array{0: mixed, 1?: mixed, 2?: mixed, 3?: mixed, 4?: mixed, 5?: mixed}
params.doc: the arguments as given: the form's address, the type, the error, the folder, the extra fields, whether ownership is relaxed

methods.name: credentials
methods.doc:
The connection as stored, its fields from the constants, the form or
what was stored, its port split from the host and its type settled.

methods.name: host
methods.doc: The host with its port, as stored and shown. @param array<string, mixed> $credentials

methods.name: types
methods.doc: The connection types this PHP can offer. @return array<string, string>

methods.name: ownsNewFiles
methods.doc: Whether a file made in the folder belongs to the running script's owner; null when none can be made there.

methods.name: scriptOwner
methods.doc:
The running script's owner, as getmyuid() reports it. Where a host
disables getmyuid() it is the owner of the engine's own code: the first
included file can be the host's auto_prepend_file (root-owned on
Kinsta), which made every update ask for an FTP connection.

methods.name: transport
methods.doc: The first remote transport this PHP has, or false.

methods.name: form
methods.signature: form(string $formPost, array $credentials, array $types, array $extraFields, array $posted): string
methods.doc:
The form asking for the connection, character for character as the
reference prints it.

classes.name: Minn\Ops\InstalledSoftware

What is installed, as the System view lists it: every extension and
WordPress plugin with whether it runs, the mu-plugins, the themes with
their parents, and the active theme's label.

methods.name: activeExtensionCount
methods.doc: How many Minn extensions are active.

methods.doc: Plugins, mu-plugins, and themes with their versions and whether each is active.

classes.name: Minn\Ops\Logs
classes.doc:
The log files the System view can read and clear: the debug log the
engine's failure handler writes, and PHP's own error log when it is a
separate file inside the site. Anything outside the site is named but
never read; it may be another tenant's.

methods.name: sources
methods.doc: Every log the engine knows about, with its path and group.
shapes: @return array<string, array{label: string, group: string, path: string}>

methods.name: listPayload
methods.doc: The logs list as the System view shows it.
shapes: @return list<array> the sources that exist, debug first

methods.name: read
methods.doc: One log's tail, by id.

methods.name: clear
methods.doc: Empties one log.

methods.doc: A byte count in KB, MB, or GB.

classes.name: Minn\Ops\Packages
classes.doc:
Putting plugins, themes and extensions on disk. Plugins and themes come
from the directory (wordpress.org's, asked through the Minn update
service, Ops\Directory) or an uploaded zip, and are installed through
WordPress's upgraders (UpgraderRun), so plugins hear every upgrader hook;
a Minn extension (a folder with a minn.json) is placed by the engine.
Every archive passes Archive's checks first: exactly one top-level
folder that is a plain name (never "." or ".."), no absolute or dotted
paths, no symbolic links, bounded entry count and size. Removal proves
the folder is a direct child of its kind's directory before anything is
deleted.

constants.name: THEMES_INFO
constants.doc: The largest archive fetched or unpacked, in bytes.

methods.name: searchThemes
methods.doc: Directory theme search, or the popular list for an empty query. @return list<array>

methods.name: searchPlugins
shapes: @return array{plugins: list<array>, page: int, pages: int, total: int}

methods.name: pluginInfo
methods.doc: The slim card for one directory plugin, cached twelve hours per slug.

methods.name: installPlugin
methods.doc: Installs a directory plugin by slug, through the upgrader; returns its folder.

methods.name: replacePlugin
methods.doc: Installs a directory plugin over the folder already there.

methods.name: directoryPlugin
methods.doc: One directory plugin record, or null when the slug is unknown.

methods.name: infoAction
methods.doc:
The directory's answer to a plugins_api() or themes_api() action
($kind 'plugins' or 'themes'), its request passed as given
(Ops\DirectoryApi), read whatever the status: a refusal is the
directory's own words ({"error": ...}); an answer that is not JSON
comes back as {"unexpected": body}. Null when the service did not
answer.

methods.name: queryThemes
methods.doc: A page of directory themes for `wp theme search`.

methods.name: queryPlugins
methods.doc: A page of directory plugins for `wp plugin search`.

methods.name: directoryTheme
methods.doc: One directory theme record, or null when the slug is unknown.

methods.name: installTheme
methods.doc: Installs a directory theme by slug, through the upgrader; returns its stylesheet folder.

methods.name: replaceTheme
methods.doc: Installs a directory theme over the folder already there.

methods.name: unpack
methods.doc:
Unpacks an uploaded or downloaded archive into wp-content/themes or
wp-content/plugins: a theme or a WordPress plugin through the upgrader,
a Minn extension (minn.json) placed by the engine; refused when its
folder is taken. @return array{folder: string, name: string, version: string, kind: string}
shapes: @return array{folder: string, name: string, version: string, kind: string}

methods.name: unpackReplacing

One published Minn release as the update service describes it (and as
the minn_release option keeps it, the same shape): the version, its notes
and page, when it went out, and its minn.zip with that file's sha256 and
its Ed25519 signature. Anything else is not a release Minn offers: a
version that is not major.minor.patch, a package anywhere but Minn's own
downloads, a missing checksum, or a missing signature.

Whether a newer Minn is out, asked of the Minn update service at most
once a day: its latest installable release (published on GitHub, read
by the service), kept in the minn_release option (JSON) with the time it
was asked. A check the service does not answer (offline, GitHub rate
limiting it) keeps the last answer and waits a day like any other; no
installable release (a 404) offers nothing. This is Minn asking Minn,
never wordpress.org, and never GitHub directly.

classes.name: Minn\Ops\ShapeFiles

The files an install lays at the webroot for tooling to find: the shape
files from layout/ (index.php, wp-settings.php, version.php and the rest),
a shape file under each of WordPress's request entry points
(data/entry-files.json: wp-cron.php, wp-admin/admin-ajax.php, ...), so a
host that runs only PHP files present on disk (nginx) still reaches the
engine, and one file for each of the reference's wp-includes and
wp-admin/includes files, an empty placeholder or, where layout/ ships one,
the engine's loader (wp-includes/pluggable.php is the engine's pluggable
functions themselves, Runtime\Pluggables). An engine update lays them again from the new engine:
a file still as the replaced engine wrote it is replaced, a missing one is
written, and one the site changed is left alone.

classes.name: Minn\Ops\Unzip
classes.doc:
An archive unpacked as unzip_file() unpacks it (probe unzip-file): into
the destination through the filesystem the site set up, every folder
made first (the destination and its missing parents included), resource-fork entries
(__MACOSX/) and entries whose names climb out or are absolute left out;
refused when the disk cannot take twice the unpacked size and a little
more. pre_unzip_file may answer first, and unzip_file is handed the
result, each with the folders to make and the space needed. An archive
the reader cannot open is refused in the words of the library the
reference falls back to.

shapes: @param Closure(string, mixed...): mixed $filter applies a filter, as apply_filters does

params.name: filter
params.doc: applies a filter, as apply_filters does

methods.doc: Whether a file is a zip archive that opens and passes its consistency check (wp_zip_file_is_valid).

methods.doc: The archive's files under the destination: true, a refusal, or what pre_unzip_file answered instead.

methods.doc:
The entries to write, the folders they need (each archive folder and
every parent of a file), and their unpacked size.
shapes: @return array{0: array<int, string>, 1: list<string>, 2: int} index => name, folders, bytes

methods.name: safe
methods.doc: Whether an entry's name stays inside the destination: no climbing segment, not absolute, no drive.

classes.name: Minn\Ops\Updates
classes.doc:
Update offers for the site's plugins and themes from the directory, asked
through the Minn update service (Ops\Directory), which answers with
wordpress.org's own offers and serves their packages: the update-check
endpoints asked with the installed headers (each plugin's Name, Version
and Update URI, so a plugin that updates from elsewhere is never offered
the directory's plugin of the same folder name), the answer kept in the
minn_updates option (JSON) for 24 hours, and the offers applied by
downloading the release archive through the one package unpacker. A
plugin or theme the directory does not know keeps its folder untouched
and is never offered anything. The per-item
auto-update lists are the site's own auto_update_plugins and
auto_update_themes options, in the shape the app already reads.

The directory is not the only source. A plugin that hosts itself answers
for its own version through the update transient's filter, which is where
WordPress reads it too, so Runtime\PluginUpdates asks the runtime the same
question and its answer is merged in. Applying such an offer goes through
the publisher: a package outside the directory is unpacked only when
`upgrader_pre_download` hands back a copy it verified.

constructor.signature: __construct(Minn\Content\Site $site, Minn\Content\Inventory $inventory, Minn\Ops\Packages $packages, string $contentDir, Minn\Http $http = \Minn\Http::__set_state(array(    'within' =>    array (   ),    'fake' => NULL,    'refusal' => NULL, )))

methods.name: forSite
methods.doc: The updater over a site's wp-content.

methods.name: checkForWordPress
methods.doc:
wp_update_plugins and wp_update_themes: the service asked when the
stored answer is old (or a fresh one is wanted), and the offers left
in the update transients when they are not there already.

methods.name: state
methods.doc: The stored answer, refreshed when older than the TTL or absent.

methods.name: refresh
methods.doc: Asks the directory now, whatever the cache says, and keeps the answer; the daily pass says so.

methods.doc: Asks the directory now and stores the answer.

methods.doc:
The offers in WordPress's update transients, update_plugins and
update_themes, in the shape wp_update_plugins and wp_update_themes
leave there: where plugins, the facade's update helpers and the
upgraders read them. Written after every check and after an update.

methods.doc: Plugin file => offered version, only where the installed version is older. @return array<string, string>

methods.name: themeOffers
methods.doc: Stylesheet => offered version. @return array<string, string>

methods.doc: Plugin file => slug, icon, directory URL, for every plugin the directory knows. @return array<string, array{slug: string, icon: string, url: string}>

methods.doc: Whether the directory knows this theme.

methods.doc: Applies the offer for one plugin file; returns the installed version afterwards.

methods.name: updateTheme
methods.doc: Updates one theme to its offer; the new version.

methods.doc: The auto-update list for plugins or themes, trimmed to what is installed. @return list<string>

methods.doc: Turns auto-updates on or off for one plugin or theme.

methods.doc: Takes one plugin or theme off the auto-update list; the list after.

Applies every offer on the auto-update lists: what was updated, and
what was refused with the reason, by plugin file or theme slug.

methods.doc: Stylesheet => style.css headers. @return array<string, array<string, string>>

methods.doc:
The locales a check asks about, as the reference asks: the languages
installed (their .mo files, through get_available_languages), then
the check's own filter (plugins_update_check_locales,
themes_update_check_locales); none for an English-only site.

methods.name: supplied
methods.doc:
What the site's own plugins offer for themselves. A check that runs
without a booted runtime (a cron trigger that loads no plugins) asks
nobody, so the last answer rides across rather than the offer
vanishing until the next request.
shapes: @return array{plugins: array<string, array<string, mixed>>, no_update: array<string, array<string, mixed>>}

methods.doc:
Stores an auto-update list, kept to assets that exist; the asset being
changed must be one of them.

methods.doc: Plugin file => the headers the update check sends, in WordPress's keys.
shapes: @return array<string, array{Name: string, Version: string, UpdateURI: string}>

methods.name: apply
methods.doc:
Applies one offer through the upgrader (UpgraderRun): the update
transients carry the offers first, as they do on WordPress when an
update starts. The archive's SHA-256 is kept under "archives" in the
state when the package came from the update service, so an audit can
ask what code arrived.

methods.name: consume
methods.doc:
An applied offer moves to the current bucket so the next read agrees
with the folder, and the offers left go back into the update
transients the upgrader cleared, as Minn Admin puts them back on
WordPress.

methods.name: map
methods.doc: The directory answers an empty bucket as a list; a map either way.

classes.name: Minn\Ops\UpgraderRun
classes.doc:
The engine's own installs and updates, run through the reference's
upgraders (Plugin_Upgrader, Theme_Upgrader) so plugins hear every hook a
WordPress install or update tells them: the REST plugin route, Minn
Admin's install, upload and update routes, the CLI verbs and the
automatic updates all come here. The Minn update service's packages are
fetched over the engine's own client (Packages::fetch: https, the
service's host, a size cap) and handed to the upgrader as a file through
upgrader_pre_download, so where Minn gets code is never the
plugin-filterable HTTP API's to change. A package from anywhere else is
installed only when its publisher answered upgrader_pre_download with a
copy it checked (or refused it): nobody's word, no install. A package
from the service passes Archive's checks before the upgrader unpacks it;
a local file (an upload, checked by Packages) is the upgrader's to read. The upgrader's refusals come back
as the engine's REST errors, in the words its routes already use.

methods.name: install
methods.doc:
Installs a package (or, with overwrite_package, replaces the folder it
lands on): its folder and the sha256 of a package fetched from the
service, '' otherwise.
shapes: @param array<string, mixed> $args the upgrader's install arguments

methods.name: update
methods.doc:
Applies the offer the update transient holds for one plugin (file) or
theme (folder), as Minn Admin does on WordPress: a plugin through
bulk_upgrade, a theme through upgrade. The sha256 of the package, ''
when it did not come from the service.

methods.name: guarded
methods.doc:
Runs $call with the engine's say over the download: the service's
package fetched here, any other remote one only on its publisher's
answer. $sha256 is set when the service's package was fetched.

methods.name: refusal
methods.doc: The upgrader's refusal in the engine's words: a taken folder says what is there and what came.

methods.name: unreachable
methods.doc:
The refusal for an upgrader that stopped without a word because it
could not reach the site's files (fs_connect answers false and records
nothing); null when the files are reachable directly.

methods.name: taken
methods.doc: The refusal for a folder already taken, naming what is there and what the package holds.

classes.name: Minn\Query\AuthorPostsSql

get_posts_by_author_sql as the reference writes it: for each type, its
published posts, and its private ones the reader may see (all of them
with the cap to read others', their own otherwise), OR'd; an author
narrows it; WHERE in front when asked.

WP_Comment_Query's ORDER BY and LIMIT as the reference writes them
(probe wp-comment-query-sql): no orderby means comment_date_gmt in the
order asked; a list, a string of keys or a map of keys to directions
each become a column, a meta value or the FIELD() list comment__in
gives; a key it does not know is dropped (none left means
comment_date_gmt), and unless comment_ID or comment__in is among them a
comment_ID tiebreak follows, in the first date clause's direction or
DESC.

methods.doc: ASC when asked for, DESC for anything else.

methods.signature: clause(string $by, array $qv, string $table, string $metaTable, array $metaClauses): string
methods.doc:
One orderby key as SQL, or '' when the reference does not take it: a
column, the meta value (as a number when asked), a named meta
clause's cast value, or the FIELD() list keeping comment__in's order.

classes.name: Minn\Query\DateSql
classes.doc:
The WHERE fragment of a date query in the reference's shape: before and
after bounds as full datetimes (inclusive bounds close the day), the
date parts as MySQL functions compared or listed, groups joined by
their relation, columns validated against the known date columns.

shapes: @param array<string, string> $tables table key to prefixed table name

params.name: tables
params.doc: table key to prefixed table name

constants.name: RANGES
constants.doc: The ranges a date part is checked against, in the order the reference reports them (week's top depends on the year).

methods.name: week
methods.doc: The week of a column as the reference counts it from the site's first day of the week.

methods.name: validate
methods.doc:
Whether a clause's date values are valid, with a notice for each part
out of range (week up to the given year's ISO weeks, 53 without one)
and for a month and day that make no date (in a leap year when no year
is given, and only once every part is in range); before and after given
as parts are checked too (probes
query-clauses, query-clause-internals). An empty clause is not valid.

methods.name: sanitize
methods.doc: Sanitises to the reference's shape: every level carries column, compare and relation.

methods.name: isFirstOrder
methods.doc: Whether a date query is one clause rather than a group of them.

methods.name: validateColumn
methods.doc: A column name as "table.column", the default for anything unknown.

methods.name: checkColumnsWith
methods.doc: Has the valid columns pass through a filter (WP_Date_Query hands it date_query_valid_columns).

methods.name: build
methods.doc: The WHERE fragment for a date query.

methods.name: forQuery
methods.doc: A query or group as the reference's get_sql_for_query returns it, indented for its depth. @return array{join: string, where: string}

methods.name: clauseParts
methods.doc:
One clause's pieces, before they are joined: the bounds, the date parts
in order (a part whose value builds to nothing, or to 0, is left out),
then the time.

methods.name: buildValue
methods.doc:
A value as the comparison wants it (build_value): a list of numbers
for IN, exactly two for BETWEEN, one number otherwise; false when the
value does not fit.

methods.name: buildTime
methods.signature: buildTime(string $column, string $compare, mixed $hour, mixed $minute, mixed $second): string|false
methods.doc:
The time of day (build_time_query): listed or ranged parts each on
their own; a single part by its function; an hour with a second and no
minute not at all; otherwise the parts as one decimal, DATE_FORMAT( col,
'%H.%i%s' ). False when no part is given.

methods.name: datetime
methods.doc:
A full datetime from a string or a parts array. A string as precise as
a year, a month, a day or a minute is read as those parts, so an end
bound reaches the end of its unit; any other string is read as a time
in the site's zone. Missing parts start (or end) the unit.

methods.doc: A comparison upper-cased, = for anything the reference does not know.

methods.name: validDate
methods.doc: Whether a clause's month and day make a date, in its year or a leap year; a notice names them when they do not.

methods.name: partExpressions
methods.doc: The date parts a clause gives, each as its SQL expression; monthnum and w stand in for month and week only when those are not given. @return array<string, string>

methods.name: clause
methods.doc: One clause as the reference writes it: its pieces, more than one joined by AND inside parentheses.

classes.name: Minn\Query\MetaSql
classes.doc:
The JOIN and WHERE fragments of a meta query in the reference's shape:
one meta-table join per clause (the first under the table's own name,
then mt1, mt2, ...), INNER joins unless an OR relation or a NOT EXISTS
clause needs LEFT ones, and casts by the clause's declared type. Under
an OR relation a clause shares an equality-shaped sibling's join.

shapes: @param array<string, array{0: string, 1: string}> $tables meta type to [table, object column]

methods.name: sanitize
methods.doc:
Normalises a raw meta_query: clauses get key/value/compare/type
defaults, a nested group its relation, and a "relation" key sits on
every level. Named clauses keep their names.

methods.doc: A clause rather than a group: it names a key or a value.

methods.name: build
methods.doc: The JOIN and WHERE fragments for a meta query.

A group's JOIN and WHERE (get_sql_for_query), indented for its depth;
each clause is given its alias in place, so its siblings can share it.

methods.doc:
One clause's JOIN and WHERE pieces (get_sql_for_clause): the clause is
settled in place (compare, compare_key, then its alias and cast), its
alias shared with a compatible sibling or a new join.

methods.doc: Has every clause's shared alias (or false) pass through a filter (WP_Meta_Query hands it meta_query_find_compatible_table_alias).

methods.doc:
The alias of a sibling the clause can share (find_compatible_table_alias):
under OR, the first sibling already given an alias whose comparison,
like the clause's, reads the same join; false otherwise.

methods.name: cast

methods.doc: A clause with its compare and compare_key settled: upper case, IN for a list, = for anything unknown. @return array<string, mixed>

methods.doc: An OR group holding a NOT EXISTS clause makes every join a LEFT one.

The SQL WP_Site_Query and WP_Network_Query build from their variables

table (blogs); every other column stands bare. A network query names each
column through its table (site). On one site both tables are unnamed, so

and stopwords dropped, ten or more terms or none left searched as one
sentence), each term a group of LIKEs over the searched columns (NOT LIKE

The headers the reference's server adds to every REST answer over

methods.doc:

takes it; the runtime's table is never consulted. This is what the
runtime's server calls for a core route, so a route the engine
declines cannot bounce between the two. $as is the caller's own
request object, which the route's parameters are set on.

policy is judged, the way the reference does: a required parameter that
did not arrive is rest_missing_callback_param; the shared collection
parameters (context, page, per_page, search) are judged first and a
refusal among them is answered alone; then every other invalid one is
listed in rest_invalid_param, in the order the route declares them, with
the schema's own refusal under details (none for an argument whose
refusal is bare, Args::BARE_REFUSAL). An argument judged in the
sanitize round (Args::SANITIZE_ROUND) is read only once all the others
passed. The query is read against the route's args, the JSON body
against its body set, and a JSON body that does not parse is refused on
every route first. An argument its handler judges
(Args::HANDLER_VALIDATES) is left to the handler.

in batches may be asked: posts, pages and the other post types shown in
REST (not media, templates, global styles or fonts), the taxonomies,
users, widgets, and a plugin's routes that opt in with allow_batch. Any
other route answers rest_batch_not_allowed with its Allow header, a path

methods.doc: One namespace's block types.

methods.name: single
methods.doc: One block type.

methods.name: fields
methods.doc:
A block type's fields in the reference's order, as the route and
WP_REST_Block_Types_Controller show them: its registration (supports
{} when it has none), its styles (its own, then those registered for
it), its variations as built when asked, and the first handle of each
asset kind as the old single field (probe rest-block-controllers).

methods.name: requireViewer
methods.doc: Only someone who edits a type shown in REST may read block types; the runtime holds them.

classes.name: Minn\Rest\BlocksController
classes.doc:
wp/v2/blocks: synced patterns and reusable blocks, stored as wp_block
posts. The reading and writing is the posts machinery with the post
type's own capabilities and the posts list's parameters; what is this
type's alone is the reading rule: a pattern is read only by one who may
read it (read_post), published or not, so without that the list counts
the patterns and shows none, and a single one is refused.

methods.name: list
methods.doc: The blocks, each shown to a caller who may read it.

methods.name: single
methods.doc:
One block. Editing context is the posts machinery's own gate
(rest_forbidden_context); a view is refused to anyone who may not read
the block, and an unknown one is not found rather than refused.

methods.name: create
methods.doc: Creates a block: a pattern's create_posts is publish_posts.

routes: POST /wp/v2/blocks/{id:[\d]+} (cap edit_post on {id}; block {id} must exist)
PUT /wp/v2/blocks/{id:[\d]+} (cap edit_post on {id}; block {id} must exist)
PATCH /wp/v2/blocks/{id:[\d]+} (cap edit_post on {id}; block {id} must exist)
methods.name: update
methods.doc: Updates a block.

routes: DELETE /wp/v2/blocks/{id:[\d]+} (cap delete_post on {id}; block {id} must exist)
methods.name: delete
methods.doc: Trashes or deletes a block.

methods.name: readable
methods.doc: Whether the caller may read a pattern: read_post, whatever its status.

classes.name: Minn\Rest\Caller
classes.doc:
Who is making this REST call. Resolved once from the cookie and nonce;
an anonymous or failed caller has id 0 and every capability check fails.

methods.name: resolveAs
methods.doc:
Settles the caller as a session already proven elsewhere: an
in-process request a plugin makes through rest_do_request() carries
no nonce, so it runs as whoever the outer request resolved.

methods.name: resolveAnonymous
methods.doc: Settles the caller as nobody: plugin code (determine_current_user) signed the request out.

methods.name: cookieBound
methods.doc:
Whether a sign-in cookie vouches for this caller (or failed to, for
want of its nonce): a cookie's nonce vouches for its own user only.

methods.name: recheck
methods.doc: Has the cookie and nonce checked again on the next question: a plugin's nonce lifetime (nonce_life) is heard only once plugins load.

methods.name: resolveInvalidNonce
methods.doc: Settles the caller as one whose cookie's nonce does not vouch for the user plugin code named.

methods.name: session
methods.doc: The session, or null for an anonymous or refused caller.

methods.name: id
methods.doc: The caller's user id, 0 when anonymous.

methods.name: mayChangeComment
methods.doc:
Whether the caller may edit or delete a comment: a moderator any
ordinary one, and whoever may edit its post (edit_comment) any one; a
note belongs to its post's editors alone (probe patch-714).

methods.name: can
methods.doc:
Whether the caller holds a capability, on a post when given. With
plugins loaded the answer is WordPress's: the same mapping, then
map_meta_cap and user_has_cap, where role editors and lock plugins
have their say.

methods.name: editsAnyRestType
methods.doc:
Whether the caller can edit posts of some type shown in REST: what
the reference asks before showing statuses, block types and the
active theme. A plugin's types count once plugins are loaded.

methods.name: capabilities
methods.doc: The capability engine.

methods.name: require
methods.signature: require(string $code = 'rest_not_logged_in', string $message = 'You are not currently logged in.', int $status = 401): Minn\Auth\Authenticated
methods.doc:
The session, or the reference's refusal: a bad nonce is always 403
rest_cookie_invalid_nonce; no identity is the caller-supplied error.

methods.name: requireFloor
methods.doc:
The floor every Minn Admin route shares: a signed-in caller who can
edit posts, plus any further capability named, all refused with the
same rest_forbidden the reference uses. Returns the caller's id.

methods.name: requireCap
methods.doc: 403 rest_forbidden unless the caller holds every capability named.

methods.name: refuse
methods.doc: 401 for an anonymous caller, 403 for one who is signed in but refused.

classes.name: Minn\Rest\Catalogue
classes.doc:
The route table read from the classes alone: every #[Route] under
src/Minn, as rows, with no request, database, or site behind it. This is
what contracts/api/routes.json is written from, so an agent can read
which routes exist, who may call them, and what they take, without
booting the engine. The per-request router builds the same rows for the
handlers it actually registered, which is what the live index serves.

methods.name: scan
methods.doc:
Every route declared by a class under the source directory, in file
order, then declaration order.

methods.name: document
methods.doc: The rows as the JSON catalogue: a version line and one entry per route.

methods.name: classes
methods.doc:
The fully qualified names of the classes under the directory, from
their paths (PSR-4: Minn\A\B is A/B.php), sorted.

classes.name: Minn\Rest\ClientSchema
classes.doc:
A JSON schema trimmed for a client (probe json-schema): only the keywords
a profile allows, in the order given, at every level a sub-schema sits.

A property's boolean required becomes its object's required list (names
whose required is true), kept where the object's own required is not a
list, appended last otherwise, even where the profile drops required
itself; an object's own list wins. A boolean required is always dropped.
Sub-schemas are trimmed where they are objects: a keyword's value, a
list's members, a map's entries; anything else stays as given.

constants.name: MAPS
constants.doc: Keywords whose value maps names to sub-schemas.

constants.name: SCHEMAS
constants.doc: Keywords whose value is a sub-schema or a list of them.

methods.name: keywords
methods.doc:
The keywords a profile keeps: draft-04's whole set, the REST API's for
any other profile.

methods.name: trim
methods.doc:
A schema with only the allowed keywords, keyed by keyword (the values
do not matter), trimmed all the way down.

methods.name: position
methods.doc: A sub-schema's place: an object trimmed, a list's object members trimmed, anything else as given.

methods.name: member
methods.doc: A list member or map entry: trimmed when it is an object schema.

methods.name: requiredNames
shapes: @return list<string> the properties whose required is true

classes.name: Minn\Rest\CommentListArgs
classes.doc:
The WP_Comment_Query arguments a comment list request makes, as the
reference makes them before rest_comment_query (probe
rest-comment-lists): each declared parameter the request carries under
its query name, an empty email and search when none is given, the
orderby name mapped to the query's, the found rows counted, the posts
loaded, the date bounds as one clause, the offset the page makes when
none is given, and ids alone for a HEAD request.

methods.name: of
methods.doc:
The arguments before plugins see them: a parameter maps when the
collection (as rest_comment_collection_params left it) still has it.

classes.name: Minn\Rest\CommentObject
classes.doc: The wp/v2 comment object; edit context adds the moderation-desk fields.

methods.name: build
methods.doc: A comment in the context asked for, through rest_prepare_comment when a plugin hooks it.

methods.name: url
methods.doc: The REST URL builder.

methods.name: buildFields
methods.doc: The wp/v2 comment shape, with the edit-context fields when asked.

classes.name: Minn\Rest\CommentsController
classes.doc:
wp/v2/comments: the status tabs with pagination headers, single,
signed-in replies, moderation updates, trash, and force delete.

methods.name: list
methods.doc:
The comments list as the reference serves it: the request's
WP_Comment_Query through rest_comment_query, its totals (counted again
when a page comes back empty), and the comments the caller may read.

methods.name: single
methods.doc: One comment, if the caller may read it: one on a protected post only with the post's password, or for one who may edit the post.

methods.name: create
methods.doc: A signed-in reply; the author fields come from the user.

routes: POST /wp/v2/comments/{id:[\d]+} (moderate_comments (not on a note) or edit_comment on {id}; comment {id} must exist)
PUT /wp/v2/comments/{id:[\d]+} (moderate_comments (not on a note) or edit_comment on {id}; comment {id} must exist)
PATCH /wp/v2/comments/{id:[\d]+} (moderate_comments (not on a note) or edit_comment on {id}; comment {id} must exist)
methods.name: update
methods.doc: Status flips and content or author edits, for moderators.

routes: DELETE /wp/v2/comments/{id:[\d]+} (moderate_comments (not on a note) or edit_comment on {id}; comment {id} must exist)
methods.name: delete
methods.doc: Trash remembers where the comment came from; force removes it outright.

methods.name: totals
methods.doc:
The total and the page count: the query's own, or, when it found
nothing (a page past the end), a count without the page.

methods.name: events
methods.doc: Tells plugins about the writes, through the runtime's comment functions.

methods.name: allowed
methods.doc:
What this caller may ask the list for: the edit context and other
statuses are for moderators and editors; comments without a post
belong to moderators, an unreadable post's to those who may read it
(or who give its password); type, author, author_exclude and
author_email to anyone who can edit posts (the email judged as sent,
before sanitizing empties a bad one).

methods.name: readablePost
methods.doc:
A post whose comments this caller may read: a protected one only with
its password or for someone who may edit it, as the reference reads
it; otherwise one it may read, or any published one.

methods.name: readable
methods.doc:
A listed comment this caller may read: a note only someone who may
edit its post (security review 2026-10-22); otherwise a moderator any,
its author their own, anyone an approved one on a post they may read.

methods.name: commentOrNote
methods.doc: A comment or a note by id, the 404 for anything else.

methods.name: note
methods.doc:
A note read by id: its post's editors' alone, in any context; anyone
else is refused the edit context, or the note (probe patch-714).

methods.name: editsListed
methods.doc:
Whether the caller may list in the edit context: notes of the posts
named are their editors' (a moderator's say does not reach them), any
other list a moderator's (probe patch-714).

methods.name: prepared
methods.doc:
The fields a request sends, as the reference's controller prepares
them for the runtime: the content, the author (a user's own details
unless the author fields say otherwise), the address (a moderator may
name one) and the browser.

classes.name: Minn\Rest\Context
classes.doc:
The view a REST caller asked for. View is the public shape, edit adds the
raw halves and the caller's own action links, embed is the reduced shape
a linked resource carries when it rides inside another response.

methods.name: of
methods.doc: The context a request names, view when it names none or names one the route does not serve.

methods.name: isEdit
methods.doc: Whether this is the edit context.

classes.name: Minn\Rest\DeclaredPostsController
classes.doc:
wp/v2/{rest_base} for extra post types declared by an active extension.
Registered last so core collections (users, comments, menus, ...) match
first; an unknown base is declined, so a plugin's own route under wp/v2
(answered by the runtime after the engine's routes) is not shadowed.

methods.name: list
methods.doc: A declared type's list.

methods.name: single
methods.doc: A declared type's single post.

methods.name: create
methods.doc: Creates a post of a declared type.

methods.name: update
methods.doc: Updates a post of a declared type.

methods.name: delete
methods.doc: Trashes or deletes a post of a declared type.

classes.name: Minn\Rest\DeclaredRevisionsController
classes.doc:
wp/v2 revisions and autosaves under a post type plugin code or an
extension registered, at its rest_base (RevisableTypes says which take
which). The {base} declines any other base, so the next route may take
it; the answers, and the parent's checks, are RevisionsController's.

methods.name: revisions
methods.doc: Every revision of the parent.

methods.name: revision
methods.doc: One revision of the parent.

methods.name: deleteRevision
methods.doc: Deletes one revision of the parent.

methods.name: autosaves
methods.doc: The parent's autosaves.

methods.name: autosave
methods.doc: The parent's newest autosave.

methods.name: createAutosave
methods.doc: Saves the caller's autosave of the parent.

classes.name: Minn\Rest\DeclaredTermsController
classes.doc:
wp/v2/{rest_base} for the taxonomies plugin code registers to show in
REST (probe rest-plugin-types), answered as the core taxonomies are.
Registered after the declared post types; a base no such taxonomy names
declines, so a plugin's own route under wp/v2 is not shadowed.

methods.name: list
methods.doc: A registered taxonomy's terms.

methods.name: single
methods.doc: One term of a registered taxonomy.

methods.name: create
methods.doc: Creates a term in a registered taxonomy.

methods.name: update
methods.doc: Updates a term of a registered taxonomy.

methods.name: delete
methods.doc: Deletes a term of a registered taxonomy.

classes.name: Minn\Rest\Embed
classes.doc:
The _embed decoration and the embed context. Every embeddable link in an
object's _links is answered in-process as the same caller with
context=embed and placed under _embedded[rel], an error as the error
itself; a rel whose every embed came back empty is left out, while an
empty list beside a full one stays (wp:term keeps its empty tags list
next to the categories).
Lists have _fields applied per item before the links are read, so a
_fields value without _links embeds nothing there; a single object embeds
first and is filtered afterwards. The embed context is the view object
cut to the reference's key set for that kind of item.

methods.name: decorate
methods.doc: Decorates a finished response: the embed context, then _embedded, then the deferred _fields.

methods.name: embedded
methods.doc:
A response's data with its embeddable links answered (the runtime's
WP_REST_Server::embed_links): every rel when none is named.

methods.name: halves
methods.doc:
A post's view object with the nested halves its type's embed shows:
a navigation post's title and content keep their raw halves and the
content its block version, for any caller; a pattern's title, which
has only a raw half, shows empty.

methods.doc: An item cut to the embed shape of its object type (a post type, a taxonomy, attachment, user or comment); any other kept whole. @param array<string, mixed> $item @return array<string, mixed>

methods.doc: The linked object in embed context; an error answer as the error itself (probe rest-server-methods); null when nothing came back.

methods.name: target
methods.doc: A REST href in either URL form, as the route path and its query. @return array{0: string, 1: array<string, string>}

methods.name: kind
methods.doc: Which key set a route's objects take in embed context; null for routes without one.

methods.name: typeAt
methods.doc: The post type a wp/v2 path serves, so the embed shape holds when _fields leaves out the item's type.

methods.name: context
methods.doc: The embed shape, with the fields plugin code registered for the item's type to show in embed.

classes.name: Minn\Rest\EngineRoutes
classes.doc:
The engine's own REST routes in the reference's regex form, for the
index and for the runtime's server, whose route table plugin code reads
to learn what the site answers (a missing /wp/v2/comments there reads as
"comments are off").

methods.name: map
methods.doc: The router's routes as route => methods, the way the index lists them.
shapes: @param list<string> $declaredBases the rest_base of every declared type

params.name: declaredBases
params.doc: the rest_base of every declared type

methods.name: forms
methods.doc:
A route attribute pattern as the reference writes routes: `{id:\d+}`
becomes `(?P<id>\d+)`, a bare capture matches one segment, a `{rest*}`
capture the remainder, and a literal constraint (`{base:posts}`, or
the alternation `{base:posts|pages}`) expands to one route per
literal. The declared-type routes are written once as a `{base:[...]}`
catch-all; they list per declared type under its rest_base (as the
reference lists a registered type) and not at all when no type is
declared, so nothing listed answers no-route.

classes.name: Minn\Rest\ExistingPost
classes.doc:
A post created with an id names one that exists: refused with
rest_post_exists before the caller is judged, even signed out (probe
patch-security). An id of 0 passes here and is refused later, as an
invalid post id.

methods.name: refuse
methods.doc: Throws rest_post_exists for a non-empty id in the body or the query.

classes.name: Minn\Rest\Fields
classes.doc:
The _fields response filter. Dot paths descend ("title.rendered"); the
object's own key order is kept. Applied per item on list responses and to
the whole payload otherwise, which is why _fields on the associative
types response strips every key and yields [] over HTTP, a reference
quirk the engine reproduces by construction.

constructor.doc: embedded first and filtered by Embed afterwards

params.name: deferred
params.doc: true when _embed rides along: a single object is

methods.name: fromQuery
methods.doc: The _fields selection a query carries, or null for everything.

methods.name: withLinksForEmbedded
methods.doc: The same paths plus _links whenever _embedded is among them: the reference's single-object rule under _embed.

methods.name: wants
methods.doc:
Whether a top-level field is among the selection: named whole, below
one of its paths (title.rendered), or above one (a path into it).

methods.name: apply
methods.doc: The object with only the selected fields.

methods.name: select
methods.doc:
The fields a response keeps when a caller names some: known fields as
given, dotted paths whose root is known, and `id` whenever it exists.

(font families, font faces, font collections), in its order, each read

exact-search switch, ordered by id or by include alone, and only a

classes.name: Minn\Rest\FontSettings
classes.doc:
The settings a font family or face is written with, judged and cleaned as
the reference does (probe font-writes). A POST sends them as a JSON
string: one that is not a string is refused by type, one that is not
JSON (or is null) as not "a valid JSON string", and what it holds is held
to the settings' schema (required keys first, then each key in the order
sent: its type, or that it is not a property), then each key that must
not be empty. A family's update names no slug and needs none of the
rest; a face's sources must each be an address the site may fetch or a
file the request uploads, and every file it uploads must be one of
them. Only the first refusal is answered, under the settings' name, its
own data moved under additional_data beside a 400 status. A PUT or a
PATCH reads the settings as the object itself, which the reference
cannot save (it fails with a fatal error); here such an update saves as
a POST would.

updated, a face created under its family, each saved as the reference

only someone who may edit theme options writes. A family is stored as
its name (the title), its slug and the rest of its settings as JSON
content, refused when another family has the slug (an empty slug matches
any); its update merges what it names over what is stored. A face is

folder in the order its sources name them (a refused file leaves the

save fires the post's own hooks, then rest_insert_{type},
