plugin's file and headers as written, an extension's key and fields.

methods.name: find
methods.doc: One plugin's item, built alone: an item reads (and loads the text domain of) only its own plugin.

methods.name: statusOf
methods.doc: Whether a plugin is active, read without building its item (nothing translated, no text domain loaded).

methods.name: pluginItem
methods.doc:
A WordPress plugin as the reference's item shows it: its headers read,
translated and cut to the allowed markup once for the fields and once
more, marked up, for the rendered description (probe plugin-data).

methods.name: refuse
methods.doc: An activation the plugin refused, as the reference's REST answer carries it: HTTP 500, the refusal's own data kept beside.

classes.name: Minn\Rest\PolicyGate
classes.doc:
Judges a route's policy against the caller, with the reference's
refusals: a caller who is not signed in gets the policy's sign-in code
at 401, a bad nonce is always 403 rest_cookie_invalid_nonce, and a
signed-in caller who lacks a capability gets the refusal code at 403.
A subject the policy names is looked up first and answers its 404
before any of those. The edit-context policy, when the request asks
for it, is judged before the route's own, as the reference refuses the
context first (the menus).

methods.name: closure
methods.doc: The judge as the router takes it.

methods.name: judge
methods.doc: Throws the refusal the policy names, or returns.

methods.name: subject
methods.doc:
The record's 404 when it does not exist. "me" names the caller, who
must then be signed in; the reference answers that with its plain
sign-in refusal whatever the route's own code is.

methods.name: type
methods.doc:
A {base} that names no declared type declines the route, so the next
one may take it. A write is judged with the type's own capabilities
(probe rest-plugin-caps): a missing post first (404), then the
caller (401 signed out, 403 refused).

methods.name: taxonomy
methods.doc:
A {base} that names no registered taxonomy declines the route. A
write is judged with the taxonomy's own capabilities (probe
rest-plugin-caps): a missing term first (404), then the caller.

methods.name: opened
methods.doc:
Whether a policy's opener lets any caller through: the filter it names,
handed false, the request, and the controller the reference passes, by
its kind (built with the argument given).

methods.name: registered
methods.doc: A capability as the post type or taxonomy the policy names registered it, or as given.

classes.name: Minn\Rest\PostCollectionParams
classes.doc:
A post type's collection parameters as the reference builds them for its
list (probe rest-post-lists): the shared four, dates, authors when the
type supports them, ids, menu order and its orderby for page attributes,
parents for a hierarchical type, search columns and semantics, slugs,
statuses (every registered one, and any), each REST taxonomy's term
filter (a list, or a query with children for a hierarchical one and an
operator for the include side) under a relation, stickies for posts, and
formats for a type with post formats. Plugins change them through
rest_{type}_collection_params, asked once a request.

methods.name: for
methods.doc: The parameters of the list a {base} capture names; none for a base no REST post type has.

methods.name: ofType
methods.doc: The parameters of a post type's list, by the type's name. @return array<string, array<string, mixed>>

methods.name: listed
methods.doc:
A post type's list parameters asked afresh, as the reference's list
asks for them each time it runs: rest_{type}_collection_params runs
again.

methods.name: built
methods.doc:
A post type's list parameters as built, for the type in any
namespace: before rest_{type}_collection_params and the optional
marks, for the facade's controller class, which adds its callbacks
and runs the filter itself.

methods.name: mediaTypes
methods.doc:
The allowed MIME types by media type (the part before the slash), in
the order the site allows them, each once.

methods.name: named
methods.doc:
A REST post type by its name, in whatever namespace it lists itself
(a plugin's type under a namespace of its own has the same list as one
under wp/v2); posts and pages by name before plugins load.
shapes: @return array{name: string, object: ?PostType, author: bool, attributes: bool, hierarchical: bool, formats: bool, taxonomies: array<string, bool>}|null

methods.name: forType
shapes: @param array{name: string, object: ?PostType, author: bool, attributes: bool, hierarchical: bool, formats: bool, taxonomies: array<string, bool>}|null $type @return array<string, array<string, mixed>>

params.name: type
params.shape: array{name: string, object: ?PostType, author: bool, attributes: bool, hierarchical: bool, formats: bool, taxonomies: array<string, bool>}|null

methods.name: filtered
methods.doc: The parameters built, through rest_{type}_collection_params, each marked optional. @param array{name: string, object: ?PostType, author: bool, attributes: bool, hierarchical: bool, formats: bool, taxonomies: array<string, bool>} $type @return array<string, array<string, mixed>>
shapes: @param array{name: string, object: ?PostType, author: bool, attributes: bool, hierarchical: bool, formats: bool, taxonomies: array<string, bool>} $type @return array<string, array<string, mixed>>

params.name: type
params.shape: array{name: string, object: ?PostType, author: bool, attributes: bool, hierarchical: bool, formats: bool, taxonomies: array<string, bool>}

methods.name: type
methods.doc:
The type a REST base names, with what its parameters depend on. Posts
and pages are known before plugins load; other types once they have.
shapes: @return array{name: string, object: ?PostType, author: bool, attributes: bool, hierarchical: bool, formats: bool, taxonomies: array<string, bool>}|null

methods.name: described
shapes: @return array{name: string, object: ?PostType, author: bool, attributes: bool, hierarchical: bool, formats: bool, taxonomies: array<string, bool>}

methods.name: build
shapes: @param array{name: string, author: bool, attributes: bool, hierarchical: bool, formats: bool, taxonomies: array<string, bool>} $type @return array<string, array<string, mixed>>

params.name: type
params.shape: array{name: string, author: bool, attributes: bool, hierarchical: bool, formats: bool, taxonomies: array<string, bool>}

methods.name: taxonomies
methods.doc: The term filters: a relation, then each taxonomy's include and exclude.

methods.name: termFilter
methods.doc: One term filter: an id list, or a query object with these properties beside its terms. @param array<string, array<string, mixed>> $properties @return array<string, mixed>

classes.name: Minn\Rest\PostListArgs
classes.doc:
The WP_Query arguments a post list request makes, as the reference makes
them before rest_{type}_query (probe rest-post-lists): each registered
parameter the request carries under its query name, the date bounds,
per_page, stickies (only them, or none of them), an exact search, each
taxonomy's include and exclude under the request's relation, formats
(standard as no format at all), the type, and ids alone for a HEAD
request. Then each through rest_query_var-{name}, the orderby names
mapped to the query's, and stickies left where they fall unless asked.

methods.name: of
methods.doc: The arguments before plugins see them.

methods.name: queryVars
methods.doc:
The query variables from the arguments plugins left: each through
rest_query_var-{name}, and the list's orderby names as the query's.

methods.name: mimeTypes
methods.doc:
A media list's MIME types, set after plugins have seen the query:
every one of the media types asked for, then each MIME type asked for
that the site allows (probe sweep-1020b).

methods.name: sticky
methods.doc: Only sticky posts (those among the ids asked for), or none of them. @param array<string, mixed> $args @return array<string, mixed>

methods.name: taxonomies
methods.doc: Each REST taxonomy's include (ids, or a query with children and an operator) and exclude, under the request's relation. @param array<string, mixed> $args @return array<string, mixed>

methods.name: termClause
methods.doc: One term filter as a clause: its terms, whether children count, and its operator (an include may ask for all). @return array<string, mixed>|null

methods.name: formats
methods.doc:
Formats as an OR of their terms, standard as no format at all; beside
other term filters, a group of their own.

classes.name: Minn\Rest\PostObject
classes.doc:
Builds the wp/v2 post and page objects in the reference's shape: the
view context, the edit context (raw+rendered dual fields, editor-only
fields, and cap-gated wp:action-* links), and their _links blocks.

constants.name: NAVIGATION
constants.doc: The one post type whose REST shape is not post-shaped.

constants.name: BLOCK
constants.doc: The other: a pattern carries its content raw, its category, and its sync status.

methods.name: view
methods.doc:
The view-context object, through rest_prepare_{type} when a plugin
hooks it; with a _fields selection, the rendered title, content and
excerpt only when it asks for them, as the reference renders only
what is asked.

methods.name: embed
methods.doc: The embed-context object before Embed cuts it to the kind's keys, with the nested halves its type's embed shows (Embed::halves).

methods.name: viewWithPassword
methods.doc:
The view-context object for a post read with a password: a protected
post's content and excerpt rendered when the password is its own
(still marked protected), as the reference's can_access_password_content
allows; otherwise the plain view.

methods.name: edit
methods.doc:
The edit-context object, its raw content given its hooked blocks,
through rest_prepare_{type} when a plugin hooks it; with a _fields
selection, rendered only as far as it asks.

methods.name: permalink
methods.doc: A post's permalink as of now: pretty once live with a slug, ?p= (or ?page_id=) before.

methods.name: restBase
methods.doc: The rest_base of a type.

methods.name: links
methods.doc: The _links of a post in the view context.

methods.name: modifiedUnsaved
methods.doc: Whether a live post carries an autosave newer than its saved revision.

methods.name: lockHolder
methods.doc: The OTHER user holding a live _edit_lock (150 second window), or null.

methods.name: editLinks
methods.doc: The view links plus the caller's verbs and cap-gated wp:action-* entries.

methods.name: date
methods.doc: A MySQL datetime in the reference's ISO form.

methods.name: meta
methods.doc:
The meta field: the keys registered to show in REST (probe rest-meta),
or the footnotes alone without the runtime.

methods.name: navigationView
methods.doc:
A navigation menu is a post with almost nothing on it: no author, no
excerpt, no featured image, no comments, no taxonomies, and so no
class list either. What it does carry is a template field and the
rendered menu.

methods.name: blockView
methods.doc:
A pattern (wp_block) is read by editors only, so its title and
content come raw even in view context: no rendered title, no rendered
content. It carries an excerpt, the footnotes meta, its pattern
categories, and the sync status core registers beside meta.

methods.name: viewFields
methods.doc: The view-context object: the shared fields, then the type's own, then class_list and _links.

methods.name: viewTerms
methods.doc:
The taxonomies a non-page carries, each as [term_id, slug] pairs; the
format terms only for posts.

methods.name: template
methods.doc: The custom template a post names (_wp_page_template), '' for none; the classic editor's 'default' is none.

methods.name: typeFields
methods.doc:
Pages carry parent and menu_order first; posts carry their term ids,
and only the post type has sticky and format, among the shared fields.

methods.name: classList
methods.doc:
The reference's class_list order: identity, type, status, format (posts
only), password, thumbnail, hentry, then one class per term.

methods.name: termLinks
methods.doc: The taxonomy links a type carries: posts their categories and tags, patterns their pattern categories, pages and menus none.

methods.name: editFields
methods.doc:
The edit-context object for a given caller: raw+rendered dual fields,
password, permalink_template, generated_slug, block_version, Minn
Admin's registered list fields, and the cap-gated action links.

methods.name: allow
methods.doc:
What the caller may do to this post, which the reference reports in
every context: a reader sees GET, an editor of the post sees the
write verbs, and DELETE only when they may delete it too.

methods.name: gmt
methods.doc:
A gmt timestamp for the wire: the stored one, or, when it is the
draft zero, the local time converted through the site's offset, the
way the reference derives it.

classes.name: Minn\Rest\PostsController
classes.doc: wp/v2 posts and pages, read side.

methods.name: list
methods.doc: The posts or pages list.

methods.name: serveList
methods.signature: serveList(Minn\Http\Request $request, string $type, ?Closure $shape = NULL, ?Closure $readable = NULL, ?array $registered = NULL): Minn\Http\Response
methods.doc:
The list for any post type as the reference serves it (probe
rest-post-lists): the caller and the statuses judged, the request's
parameters sanitized, the query arguments through rest_{type}_query
and rest_query_var-*, a WP_Query (so pre_get_posts and every query
filter run), then each post the caller may read (or edit, in the edit
context) shaped (by $shape when the type has its own object, as
media does). The totals are the query's, counted again without the
page when a later page came back empty. A media search also matches
file names, as the reference's does. A type whose posts are read by
a rule of its own names it ($readable, by post id: a pattern needs
read_post, published or not), its rows still counted; a type whose
list takes parameters of its own names them ($registered, as menu
items do); a shape that answers null leaves the post out.

methods.name: requestedStatuses
methods.doc:
The statuses a list request names, null when it names none: a list
given as one (status[]=draft), its members that are not plain values
dropped, or a comma-separated string.

routes: GET /wp/v2/{base:posts|pages}/{id:[\d]+} (public; post {id} must exist; edit context: cap edit_post on {id})
methods.name: single
methods.doc: One post or page.

methods.name: serveSingle
methods.doc:
One post of any type, with the reference's read rules: the edit
context for one who may edit it, then the password (any given that is
not the post's own is refused, protected or not, before the post's
readability is judged), then the read itself, by the type's own rule
when it has one ($readable, by post id) and otherwise a published post
or one the caller may read. The excerpt is cut to the excerpt_length
asked for, and the right password opens the content and the excerpt.

methods.name: withAlternate
methods.doc: A viewable type's single post points at its page on the site.

methods.name: shaped
methods.doc:
A list's posts as objects: each the caller may read (or edit, in the
edit context), shaped by the type's own shape or the post object.

methods.name: totals
methods.doc:
The total and the page count: the query's own, or, when a later page
came back with nothing counted, a count without the page. A page past
the last is refused.

methods.name: readable
methods.doc: Whether the caller may read a post: published, readable to them, a public status, or an attachment of one they may.

methods.name: visibleStatuses
methods.doc:
The statuses this caller may list. Public callers see only 'publish';
any other status and the edit context need a caller who can edit this
type, and a status beyond publish is a parameter error without that cap.
Answers the statuses the list reads, publish (or inherit) when none is named.

classes.name: Minn\Rest\PostsWriteController
classes.doc:
wp/v2 posts and pages, write side: create, update, trash, and force
delete, each gated by the capability engine and answering with the
edit-context object the reference returns.

constructor.signature: __construct(Minn\Content\Posts $posts, Minn\Content\PostWriter $writer, Minn\Content\Site $site, Minn\Rest\PostObject $object, Minn\Rest\RestUrl $url, Minn\Rest\Caller $caller, ?Minn\Theme\TemplateIndex $templates = NULL)

constants.name: LIVE
constants.doc: The statuses that make a post live: they need the publish capability and give the post its slug.

constants.name: FIELD_SUPPORTS
constants.doc: What a plugin's type must support for its posts to take a title, content or excerpt: a field its schema lacks is not saved (probe rest-plugin-types).

methods.name: create
methods.doc: Creates a post or page; one asked for with an id is refused before the caller is judged (patch-security).

methods.name: serveCreate
methods.doc: Creates a post of any type from the body.

routes: POST /wp/v2/{base:posts|pages}/{id:[\d]+} (cap edit_post on {id}; post {id} must exist)
PUT /wp/v2/{base:posts|pages}/{id:[\d]+} (cap edit_post on {id}; post {id} must exist)
PATCH /wp/v2/{base:posts|pages}/{id:[\d]+} (cap edit_post on {id}; post {id} must exist)
methods.name: update
methods.doc: Updates a post or page.

methods.name: serveUpdate
methods.doc: Updates a post of any type from the body.

routes: DELETE /wp/v2/{base:posts|pages}/{id:[\d]+} (cap delete_post on {id}; post {id} must exist)
methods.name: delete
methods.doc: Trashes or deletes a post or page.

methods.name: serveDelete
methods.doc: Trashes a post of any type, or deletes it with force.

methods.name: checkMeta
methods.doc: A body's meta must be an object of keys (probe rest-meta). @param array<string, mixed> $body

methods.name: field
methods.doc: A field that may arrive as a scalar or as {raw: ...}.

methods.name: takes
methods.doc: Whether a type's posts take a title, content or excerpt from a request: posts and pages take all three (a page's schema has an excerpt it does not support).

methods.name: hasParent
methods.doc: Whether a type's posts take a parent: pages, and a plugin's hierarchical type.

methods.name: hasOrder
methods.doc: Whether a type's posts take an order: pages, and a plugin's type with page attributes.

methods.name: events
methods.doc: Tells plugins about the writes, through the runtime's lifecycle.

methods.name: newColumns
methods.signature: newColumns(array $body, string $type, int $author, string $status, string $slug, string $date, string $dateGmt, string $modified, string $modifiedGmt, string $title): array
methods.doc: The row of a new post, from the body and what the create settled.

methods.name: writeNewPost
methods.doc:
Writes a new post's row as the insert does: its guid becomes the
permalink as of now (pretty only when live). The default category
follows, and the body's own terms come after rest_insert_{type}, so
categories: [] leaves none.

methods.name: checkAssignTerms
methods.doc:
Every existing term the body names must be one the caller may assign
(assign_term, through map_meta_cap), as the reference's permission
check asks before anything is written (audit Low); an id that names no
term is left to the save to report.

methods.name: rememberOld
methods.doc:
After a save: a post brought back from the trash under a new slug has
its wanted slug back and stops waiting for it. The old slug and date a
published post keeps are the reference's post_updated hooks'.

methods.name: floatingDate
methods.doc:
A draft that was never given a date (its GMT date is zero) has a
floating one: every save moves it to now, and the GMT date stays zero
until the post leaves draft or pending, as on the reference.

methods.name: scheduledIfFuture
methods.doc:
A date in the future turns a publish into a schedule, whether the
status was sent or kept; a schedule given a date that has come
(or reset to now) is published (probe hook-inputs-2).

methods.name: askedDate
methods.doc:
The dates a write asks for, as [local, gmt, timestamp]: date (site
local) before date_gmt; null when neither is sent.

methods.name: updatedDate
methods.doc:
The dates an update asks for: as askedDate(), or now when either date
is sent as null, which resets the post's date (probe hook-inputs-2).

methods.name: fieldColumns
methods.doc:
The columns the body's fields change, minus the status: author (gated
by edit_others_*), the two flags, password, the page attributes, the
date, the three markup fields through the caller's filter, the slug.

methods.name: statusColumns
methods.doc:
The status change and what rides with it: going live needs the
publish cap and gives a slugless post one from its title; the first
move to publish stamps the publish date.

methods.name: checkStickyChange
methods.doc:
Making a post sticky, or no longer sticky, takes the type's
edit_others_posts since 7.1.3; asking for what it already is does not
(rest-sticky). Only posts are sticky.

methods.name: checkBody
methods.doc: The body's meta and template, checked before anything is written.

methods.name: checkTemplate
methods.doc:
A template field must name a custom template the type's posts may use
(TemplateIndex::customFor), or be '' to clear the choice; anything else
is refused with the names allowed, as the reference refuses it. Under a
classic theme the engine does not list PHP page templates yet, so a
name is kept as given.

methods.name: checkStickyPasswordConflict
methods.doc: The reference refuses a sticky and password combination outright.

methods.name: clean
methods.doc: Markup from a caller without unfiltered_html goes through the allowlist filter.

classes.name: Minn\Rest\RegisteredFields
classes.doc:
The fields plugin code adds to an object type with register_rest_field,
as the reference serves them (probe rest-fields). A get callback's value
follows the item's own fields, before its links. It is handed the item
so far (without links, cut to the fields asked for, id kept), the
field's name, the request and the object type. A field is left out when
_fields does not name it or its schema's context does not include the
request's. A write runs the update callbacks for the fields its body
names, with the saved object, before rest_after_insert; an error one
returns is the write's answer.

methods.name: add
methods.doc: The item with the type's registered fields added, answering the request. @param array<string, mixed> $item @return array<string, mixed>

methods.name: update
methods.doc: Runs the update callbacks for the fields the request's body names; an error one returns is thrown as the write's answer.

methods.name: context
methods.doc:
The context the item is answered in, set on the request as the
reference's controllers set it: a write and a delete answer in edit
(a term's delete in view); a read in the one asked for, or view.

methods.name: shownIn
methods.doc: The names of the fields registered for the type that show in the context. @return list<string>

methods.name: args
methods.doc:
The type's registered fields as a write's parameters, each from its
schema as the reference derives an item schema's (a read-only field,
or one without a schema, takes none).

methods.name: withSchemas
methods.doc:
An item schema with the type's registered fields added after its own
properties, each by its schema (one without a schema adds none).

methods.name: wanted
methods.doc: The fields _fields names, or null when it names none. @return list<string>|null

methods.name: inContext
methods.doc: A field without a schema, or one whose schema names no context, shows in every context. @param array<string, mixed> $options

classes.name: Minn\Rest\RegisteredPostFields
classes.doc: The REST object of a post whose type plugin code registered (probe rest-plugin-types), built by what the type supports.

methods.name: view
methods.doc:
A plugin's type in the view context (probe rest-plugin-types): the
shared fields, then only what the type supports (title, editor,
excerpt, author, thumbnail, page attributes, comments, formats, custom
fields), its parent when hierarchical, each REST taxonomy's term ids
under its REST base, the class list and links.
shapes: @param Closure(int): list<string> $allow the methods the caller may use on a post
@param Closure(string, string): string $gmt a GMT date as the object writes it

params.name: allow
params.doc: the methods the caller may use on a post

params.name: gmt
params.doc: a GMT date as the object writes it

methods.name: links
methods.signature: links(Minn\Content\PostRecord $p, Minn\Rest\RegisteredType $type, int $featured, array $taxonomies, Closure $allow): array

classes.name: Minn\Rest\RegisteredType
classes.doc:
A post type plugin code registered, as its REST object follows it
(probe rest-plugin-types): what it supports, whether it is hierarchical,
and the taxonomies it shows in REST under their REST bases. Only once the
runtime has loaded the plugins that register it.

methods.name: of
methods.doc: The type when plugin code registered it (not a built-in), or null.

methods.name: supports
methods.doc: Whether the type supports the feature (title, editor, author...).

methods.name: hierarchical
methods.doc: Whether the type's posts have parents.

methods.name: base
methods.doc: The REST base the type's routes live under, with its namespace.

methods.name: taxonomies
methods.doc: The taxonomies the type shows in REST, REST base => taxonomy, in registration order. @return array<string, string>

classes.name: Minn\Rest\RenderedFields
classes.doc:
A post's rendered title, content and excerpt as a REST response carries
them. Without plugins they are Minn's own render. With plugins loaded
they pass the filters the reference's controller runs, with the post set
up as it sets it up: the_title over the stored title, the engine's
render of the content then the rest of the_content (shortcodes and every
plugin's callback), and get_the_excerpt then the_excerpt.

methods.name: title
methods.doc: The rendered title.

methods.name: content
methods.doc: The rendered content.

methods.name: excerpt
methods.doc: The rendered excerpt.

methods.name: setUp
methods.doc: The post made current and set up for a response that renders none of its text, as the reference sets up every item it prepares.

methods.name: classes
methods.doc:
A post's class list as get_post_class hands it back once plugin code
filters post_class (WooCommerce drops hentry and adds a product's
stock and type): the filter's answer without repeats, in order.

classes.name: Minn\Rest\Reply
classes.doc:
JSON responses in the reference's shape: its header set, its json_encode
flags (slashes escaped), the _fields filter, and the pagination headers
on lists.

constants.name: HEADERS
constants.value: array (   'Content-Type' => 'application/json; charset=UTF-8',   'X-Content-Type-Options' => 'nosniff',   'Access-Control-Expose-Headers' => 'X-WP-Total, X-WP-TotalPages, Link',   'Access-Control-Allow-Headers' => 'Authorization, X-WP-Nonce, Content-Disposition, Content-MD5, Content-Type', )

methods.name: answer
methods.doc: One item, shaped by the request's own _fields: what nearly every handler ends with.

methods.name: item
methods.doc: One object as a response, the selected fields applied.

methods.name: alternate
methods.doc: A post's answer pointing at its page on the site, as a viewable type's single item does.

methods.name: list
methods.doc: A list response with the total and page-count headers.

methods.name: rows
methods.doc: A list response without paging headers, each row's fields selected.

methods.name: error
methods.doc: A REST error as the reference's error body.

classes.name: Minn\Rest\Responses
classes.doc:
REST answers as the WordPress layer shapes them: any value made a
response, a list of errors made one (its status from the errors' data),
the REST server (made, and rest_api_init told, the first time it is
asked), the fields a request asked for kept, and the status that tells
a signed-out caller from one who may not.

methods.name: ensure
methods.doc: A value as a REST response (rest_ensure_response): errors and responses as they are; an HTTP response's parts carried over.

methods.name: fromErrors
methods.doc:
A list of errors as a REST response (rest_convert_error_to_response):
the first error the body, the rest as additional_errors; the status
the last one the errors' data name, 500 when none does.

methods.name: server
methods.doc: The REST server (rest_get_server): made the first time, of the class wp_rest_server_class names, and rest_api_init told.

methods.name: fieldIncluded
methods.doc: Whether a field is among those asked for (rest_is_field_included), a nested one by its parent or child.

methods.name: filterFields
methods.doc: A response with only the fields the request's _fields asks for (rest_filter_response_fields), a list item by item.

methods.name: authorizationRequiredCode
methods.doc: The status refusing a caller (rest_authorization_required_code): 403 for one signed in, 401 for one who is not.

methods.name: entries
methods.doc:
Each error as the REST body writes it: code, message, its code's last
data, and the earlier data as additional_data.

classes.name: Minn\Rest\RestMeta
classes.doc:
An object's meta field over REST, from the keys registered to show
there (probe rest-meta). Each key answers under its REST name (its own,
or show_in_rest's name): those for every subtype, then the object's
subtype's, left out of a context their schema does not name. A single
key reads its first stored value (its default, or its type's empty value,
when none), a multiple key each one; each value is checked against the
key's schema (null when it does not fit, the empty value of a scalar
type for '') and cast, or handed to the key's prepare callback. A write
goes key by key in registration order: null (or an empty list) deletes,
a value its schema refuses is a 400, and a key the user may not edit is
a 403 (an unchanged single value is left alone first). The errors are
gathered; the first is the answer, with the others beside it.

methods.name: read
methods.doc: The meta field of an object in a context (the one the request answers in, when none is named), keyed by REST name. @return array<string, mixed>

methods.name: value
methods.signature: value(string $objectType, int $objectId, string $key, array $field, Minn\Objects\RestRequest $request, ?callable $prepare = NULL): mixed
methods.doc:
One field's value for an object: a single key's first stored value (its
default when none), a multiple key's each one, prepared for the response.

methods.name: writeFrom
methods.doc: Applies the meta a write request names, when it names any.

methods.name: write
methods.doc: Applies a request's meta to an object; the gathered refusals are thrown.

methods.name: errors
methods.doc: Applies a request's meta to an object, key by key in registration order; the refusals come back. @return list<Errors>

methods.doc:
The refusals of writing a request's meta over the fields given, each
key deleted, stored or stored as a list through the step of that name
(WP_REST_Meta_Fields::update_value hands its own methods, so a
subclass's are the ones that run); a step's true is no refusal.
shapes: @param array{delete: callable, single: callable, multiple: callable} $steps

params.name: steps
params.shape: array{delete: callable, single: callable, multiple: callable}

methods.name: fields
methods.doc:
The keys registered to show in REST for an object type and subtype,
each with its REST name, whether it is single, its schema (a multiple
key's an array of its own) and its prepare callback; keys of a type
REST does not know are left out.
shapes: @return array<string, array{name: string, single: bool, schema: array<string, mixed>, prepare_callback: mixed}>

methods.name: prepare
methods.doc: A value for the response: through the field's prepare callback, or checked against its schema (null when it does not fit) and cast. @param array<string, mixed> $field

methods.name: store

methods.name: deleteKey

methods.doc: Whether a value sanitizes to what is stored (scalar types compared as the text the store keeps). @param array<string, mixed> $field

methods.name: emptyValue
methods.doc: A type's empty value: '' for a string, false, 0, or an empty list.

methods.name: update

methods.doc:
A multiple key set to a list: values already stored once are kept,

classes.name: Minn\Rest\RestUrl

REST URLs in the form the reference emits for the site's permalink mode:
{home}/wp-json/wp/v2/... when pretty, otherwise
{home}/index.php?rest_route=/wp/v2/... with the route value URL-encoded

classes.name: Minn\Rest\RevisableTypes
classes.doc:
The post types plugin code or an extension registered that answer
revisions and autosaves routes at their rest_base, as the reference
registers those controllers per type shown in REST under wp/v2:
autosaves for any type but attachments, revisions for a type that
supports them.

methods.name: typeOf
methods.doc: The registered post type a REST base names under wp/v2, or null. Asked only inside a REST request, where the runtime has booted.

methods.name: revisable
methods.doc: Whether a base's type answers the revisions routes: it supports revisions.

methods.name: autosaving
methods.doc: Whether a base's type answers the autosaves routes: any type but attachments.

classes.name: Minn\Rest\RevisionCollection
classes.doc:
A revisions list as the reference answers it (probe of the posts,
pages, patterns, menus, templates and global styles revisions routes):
the include list (which outranks exclude) or the exclude list, the
search (terms, quoted phrases and -exclusions over the title, excerpt
and content, as a post search reads them), the order, then the page. An
empty result is no pages at all. Without per_page every match is one
page. An offset sent (zero too) is where a page of per_page starts, in
the page number's place; one other than zero is refused at or past the
total, and without one a page past the last is refused.

methods.name: ofParent
methods.doc:
The revision a single route asks for, refused as the reference refuses
it: no revision by that id is an invalid id, one of another parent a
mismatch naming the parent asked for.

methods.name: filtered
methods.doc: The rows the request's filters keep, in its order.

methods.name: paged
methods.doc: The page the request asks for, with the total and the page count.

methods.name: ids
methods.doc: An id list argument as integers: a list, or a comma or space separated string.

methods.name: matches
methods.doc: Whether a revision matches every search term: an excluded term (a leading dash) in none of its columns, any other in one.

methods.name: sorted
methods.signature: sorted(array $rows, string $orderby, int $direction, array $include, string $search, array $terms): array
methods.doc:
The rows in the asked order: by date with the id breaking ties, by id,
by the include list's own order, by relevance (the whole search in
the title, then every term there, then any, then by date), or by
title or slug with ties left in id order.

methods.name: rank
methods.doc: A row's place in the relevance order, lowest first.

classes.name: Minn\Rest\RevisionsController
classes.doc:
wp/v2 revisions under posts, pages, patterns and navigation menus, and
autosaves under those and menu items (probes rest-revisions,
rest-autosaves). A revision carries the fields its parent's type
supports: a navigation menu's its title and content, a menu item's its
title alone.

constants.doc: The parents' REST bases and their post types.

constants.name: FIELDS

constants.value: 'Sorry, you are not allowed to delete revisions of this post.'

methods.name: deleteRevision
methods.doc:
A revision deleted for good, answered as it was; never trashed. The
reference grants deleting a revision to nobody by default, so a
request that passes the parent's check is refused at the revision's.

methods.name: autosaves
methods.doc: The autosaves of a post, every author's, in the asked context; the edit view names each one's preview.

methods.doc: The parent's newest autosave, whoever saved it and whichever autosave id is asked for; the edit view names its preview.

methods.doc: One autosave slot per author; the reply carries a preview link.

methods.name: object
methods.doc: One revision row as wp/v2 serves it (autosaves and revisions alike), in the view, edit or embed shape.

methods.name: selected
methods.doc:
One revision or autosave under the request's _fields: its links ride
along exactly when the parent field is asked for, as the reference
links one to its parent only then (and _links alone shows nothing).

methods.name: draftObject
methods.doc:
A draft saved in place by its autosave, as the reference replies with
it: a revision's fields with the post's own parent (linked only when
there is one), its own guid, no dates while it floats, and its plain
preview link.

methods.name: embedded
methods.doc:
The embed view of a revision: who, when, which and whose, its title and
excerpt; a navigation menu's carries its title and content with their
raw halves instead.

methods.name: withPreviewLink
methods.doc: The autosave POST reply names where to preview the draft, just before its links; a revision never carries it.

methods.name: previewLink
methods.doc:
Where to preview the parent with its autosave: its permalink once
published, its plain address before; none for a type that is never
viewed (a navigation menu, a menu item).

methods.name: meta
methods.doc: A revision's meta: the footnotes, and for a pattern the sync status core revisions too; none for a navigation menu or a menu item.

methods.name: requireParent
methods.doc: The revision surfaces are gated on edit_post of the parent.

The routes the engine serves, described in the reference's shape for the
index and for an OPTIONS request: every route's namespace, its methods
and the parameters it declares, gathered per concrete route from the
attributes so a client learns what really works on it, with the
namespaces they fall under. Routes are keyed as the reference spells them
('/wp/v2/posts/(?P<id>[\d]+)').

Every route the engine serves, the root and each namespace's index

The namespaces in the order the reference's index lists them, which

The namespace a route is listed under: its first two segments when the

classes.name: Minn\Rest\RuntimeEnvelope
classes.doc:
The REST server's filters around one of Minn's own routes, as the
reference runs them around every route (contracts/runtime.md, "The REST
server's envelope"): rest_request_before_callbacks is handed the argument
check's error or null and may refuse; the route's permission is the
next refusal; rest_dispatch_request may answer in place of the route;
rest_request_after_callbacks sees whatever came of it and may change it.
A value other than an error from the first filter does not answer: the
route still runs. With nothing hooked on any of the three, the route
answers as it would without plugins, unconverted; and before the runtime
boots (the API is built first) there are no plugins to ask.

params.name: types
params.doc: the declared types, for naming a {base} route as the reference does

methods.doc: The route's answer with the server's filters around it, or as the route gives it when no plugin can hear.

methods.doc: The route's answer as the server's filters hand it on: a response object, or the error it refused with.

methods.doc: The route as the reference names it in its table: the form of the pattern this request matched.

methods.name: handler
methods.doc:
The handler as plugins read it from the filters: its methods, its
arguments as the index publishes them, and callables for the route
and its permission.

methods.name: typed
methods.doc:
The captures as the reference holds them once its arguments passed:
a number is an integer.

classes.name: Minn\Rest\RuntimePrepare
classes.doc:
An item a REST response carries, through the filter the reference runs
as it prepares one (rest_prepare_{type}, rest_prepare_attachment,
rest_prepare_user, rest_prepare_comment, rest_prepare_{taxonomy}): the
item as a response object, its links on the response rather than in its
data, handed with the object it describes and the request; what the
filter leaves is the item. With nothing hooked, or a response handed back
untouched, the item is Minn's own, byte for byte. Fields plugin code
registers for the type are added first, as the reference adds them
before the filter runs.

hand plugins that one), then puts back the request it interrupted.

A post-shaped item (a post, a page, a pattern, a navigation, an
attachment, any other type) through rest_prepare_{type}, given its

it: a type it lists has its content's ignored hooked blocks marked, a

update_ignored_hooked_blocks_postmeta does; asked of every save.

the posts controller prepares, with the post it describes): a type it
lists has its raw content given its hooked blocks and rendered again
from that, a navigation's root list put in its meta, as the

classes.name: Minn\Rest\RuntimeRoutes
classes.doc:
Routes plugin code registered with register_rest_route(), answered
through the runtime's server after the engine's own routes have had
their turn; the runtime's say before the engine answers at all (an
authentication refusal, a pre-dispatch answer, a removed endpoint);
and the runtime's namespaces folded into the index.

constants.name: DISPATCH_DONE
constants.doc: rest_post_dispatch's defaults the engine does itself: every answer is cut to its _fields before it is served.

constants.name: ROUTE_SCOPED
constants.doc: rest_post_dispatch's defaults that touch one route only: elsewhere they hand the answer back as it came, so they are left out there.

methods.doc:
What plugin code decides before any route runs, engine routes
included, in the reference's order: rest_authentication_errors may
refuse the request, rest_pre_dispatch may answer it outright, and a
route a rest_endpoints filter removed is no route at all. Null lets
the engine's router proceed.

methods.name: predispatch
methods.doc:
What plugin code decides before a route runs, for a request inside
another (an embedded link) as for the first: rest_pre_dispatch may
answer it outright, and a route a rest_endpoints filter removed is no
route at all. Null lets the router proceed.

methods.doc: Null when the runtime has no route for the request either.

methods.doc: The methods of a plugin's route whose handler lets this request through (a handler with no permission callback does). @return list<string>

hints them on every self link it serves (targetHints.allow): the
route the link names, each of its methods whose handler lets this
caller through; null when no route of the runtime's takes the link.
A route the engine answers itself is judged by its policies, as its
Allow header is (probe rest-registry-controllers).

methods.name: described
methods.doc:
An engine route's description with what its core controller says of
the same endpoints (an endpoint listing the same methods): whether it
may be batched, and, for a write or a delete, or a read that declares
none, the parameters the controller publishes when they hold every
one the engine declares (a type's writes list its schema's fields).
A read's own parameters stay the engine's, as do the endpoints and
their methods: nothing the engine does not answer is listed.

methods.name: mergeIndex
methods.doc: The engine's index plus the namespaces and routes the runtime holds.

methods.name: adopt
methods.doc: An in-process call's own request object stands for the engine's request: the server sets its route's parameters on it, as the reference's dispatch does.

methods.name: sanitized
methods.doc:
The request as the list's handler reads it: its parameters with their
defaults, sanitized by their schemas, as plugins' filters see it too.

methods.name: wpRequest
methods.doc: The request as the runtime's server reads it, and as a REST filter or action hands it to plugins: the same object each time.

methods.name: matched
methods.doc: Keeps the route and handler a request matched, for the response plugins see at serving.

methods.name: toWpError
methods.doc: An engine refusal as plugins handle one.

methods.name: toWp
methods.doc:
An engine answer as plugins handle one: its data decoded (an empty
object stays one), its links on the response rather than in the data,
its status and headers.

methods.name: wpHeaders
methods.doc:
A route's own headers as the reference's response object holds them:
a list's totals are numbers, but the comments list's stay text.

methods.name: itemResponse
methods.doc:
One item a response carries, as a response object: its data without
_links, the links on the response.

methods.name: fromWp
methods.doc: Whatever the filters left, as the engine sends it; what they handed back untouched is the engine's own answer, byte for byte.

methods.name: serve
methods.doc:
The server's last word on any REST answer, engine or plugin route,
as the reference serves one: rest_post_dispatch may change it,
rest_pre_serve_request may serve it itself (what it prints is the
body), and rest_pre_echo_response may rewrite the data echoed. With
nothing hooked, the answer goes out as it is.

methods.name: servedAsXml
methods.doc:
Whether the answer went out as oEmbed's XML. The reference prints it
in rest_pre_serve_request ahead of rest_send_cors_headers, so none of
the CORS headers follow it, Vary: Origin among them.

methods.name: ensure
methods.doc: A callback's return as a response object, an error converted.

methods.name: server
methods.doc: The runtime's REST server, the one door to it (built, with rest_api_init, on first use).

methods.name: allow
methods.doc:
The Allow header a plugin's route answers with, as the reference's
rest_send_allow_header sets it: every method of the route whose
handler's permission callback lets this request through (a handler
with none counts). Left alone when the handler set one itself.

methods.name: describing
methods.doc:
What describes an engine route's endpoints: its own description, or,
for a template's autosaves, its update's, whose parameters the
reference lists for the autosave too.

methods.name: filled
methods.doc:
An engine route's description with what another description of it
says of the same endpoints, by described()'s rule; an engine endpoint
the other lists as several (settings' read and its update) is listed
as those.

methods.name: dispatchDone
shapes: @return array<string, int> the rest_post_dispatch callbacks this request leaves out: the engine's own, and the route-scoped ones off their route

methods.name: asksForXml
methods.doc: The embed route only: the proxy answers JSON whatever its format.

methods.name: oembedXml
methods.doc:
An embed asked for as XML (format=xml), as the reference's
_oembed_rest_pre_serve_request serves it over HTTP: the data, or the
error (its code, message and data), as an oembed document, text/xml,
with the status it had. Null for anything else.

methods.name: look
methods.doc: What a response looks like to the code that may change it. @return array<int, mixed>

methods.name: decode
methods.doc: JSON as arrays, as plugins read REST data, with an empty object kept an object so it is sent back as one.

methods.name: expand
methods.doc:
Compacted link relations ("wp:term") back to the relations a response
holds ("https://api.w.org/term"); the CURIE list itself is rebuilt
when the response is compacted again.

classes.name: Minn\Rest\Schema
classes.doc:
JSON-schema handling the way the REST API's argument validation does it:
validate a value against a schema (a Refusal names what failed), sanitise
it into the schema's type, filter a response by context, and the type
tests the schema vocabulary needs. Behaviour pinned by contracts/fixtures/api/rest.json.

shapes: @param Closure(string): bool $email the email test, so the reference's is_email filter applies
@param Closure(int|float): string $number the localised number formatter for messages
@param Closure(string, mixed): mixed $format the sanitiser for a string format (hex-color, email, uri, ...)

params.name: email
params.doc: the email test, so the reference's is_email filter applies

params.name: number
params.doc: the localised number formatter for messages

params.name: format
params.doc: the sanitiser for a string format (hex-color, email, uri, ...)

constants.name: KEYWORDS
constants.doc: Every keyword a route schema may carry, in the reference's order; the endpoint subset drops the three descriptive ones.

constants.name: ENDPOINT_KEYWORDS
constants.doc: An object schema that names its properties forbids the others unless it says otherwise, all the way down.

methods.name: validate
methods.doc: Whether a value satisfies a schema, or the reference's refusal.

methods.name: choices
methods.doc: A schema's anyOf and oneOf: which of their schemas a value matches, and the refusal when not as wanted.

methods.name: validateAs
methods.doc:
One type's own checks, as the per-type validators run them: a number's
bounds before an integer's wholeness, and no enum or format.

methods.name: validateEnum
methods.doc: Whether a value is one of the schema's enum, coerced to the schema's type first when it names one.

methods.name: sanitize
methods.doc: A value coerced to its schema's types.

methods.name: filterByContext
methods.doc: Drops the properties whose schema does not list the context; an array whose items do not is emptied.

methods.name: anyMatching
methods.doc: The first anyOf branch the value validates against.

methods.name: endpointArgs
methods.doc:
The argument map a route derives from an item schema: every writable
property with the default validators, its keywords, defaults and
required flags on the create route only, and any arg_options overrides.

methods.name: castEmptyObjects
methods.doc:
A value with each empty array the schema calls an object made one
(it encodes as {}), through properties, additional properties, list
items and the value as a whole (probe rest-view-config).

methods.name: closeObjects
methods.doc: The schema with additionalProperties closed on every object.

methods.name: validateInteger
methods.doc:
Numeric, within bounds and a multiple, then whole; null when the integer passes.
A value that is not numeric names the schema's own type, empty when the
schema names none (the reference words it "p is not of type .").

methods.name: validateString
methods.doc: Length and pattern; null when the string passes.

methods.name: validateNumber
methods.doc: Bounds and multipleOf; null when the number passes.

methods.name: firstMissing
methods.doc:
The first property an object schema requires and the value lacks. A list under 'required'
(draft 4) wins; without one, each property's own 'required' => true (draft 3) counts.

classes.name: Minn\Rest\SchemaChoices
classes.doc:
anyOf and oneOf the way the REST API's validation judges them (probe
rest-schema-choices): a choice's schemas without a type take the
choice's own; the refusal for matching none is named from the closest
schema, or lists the titles, or is plain; several matches are named by
their titles. Schema::validate() asks here first, then applies the
schema's own keywords.

methods.name: matchAny
methods.doc:
The first of an anyOf's schemas the value matches, each without a type
taking the choice's own, or the refusal for matching none (probe
rest-media-actions).

methods.name: matchOne
methods.doc:
The one of a oneOf's schemas the value matches, each without a type
taking the choice's own; "first" settles for the first match. Matching
none is refused as matchAny() refuses it; matching several names them
when every one has a title, with their positions.

methods.name: combiningError
methods.doc:
The refusal for a value no schema of a choice matched (probe
rest-media-actions). With one schema, its refusal is named. Otherwise
the refusals that say only the value is not the schema's type are set
aside, and one left is named. Of several left, when the first is an
object's, the one whose properties share the most keys with the value
is named (the first of a tie, none when none share). Then, when every
schema has a title, they are listed; else the plain refusal.
shapes: @param list<array{0: Refusal, 1: array<string, mixed>, 2: int|string}> $errors refusal, schema, position

methods.name: combiningFailure
methods.doc:
The refusal for a value that matched none of a combinator's schemas,
worded from the one that came closest: its title when it has one (an
empty title still reads as one), and that schema's own reason.

methods.name: closestObject
methods.doc:
Of several object schemas' refusals, the one whose properties share
the most keys with the value; null when the first is not an object's
or none shares a key.

methods.name: listed
methods.doc: Names in a sentence: "A and B", "A, B, and C". @param list<string> $names

classes.name: Minn\Rest\SchemaData
classes.doc:
REST schemas captured from the reference for the facade's controller
classes (data/rest-schemas.json): an item schema, a collection's
parameters or a route argument, by name. Callbacks are not data, so a
controller adds its own.

methods.name: of
methods.doc: One captured schema by name; an empty array when there is none. @return array<string, mixed>

classes.name: Minn\Rest\SchemaValues
classes.doc:
The value side of JSON Schema, as the reference applies it: what counts
as a boolean, integer, array, or object, the coercions to each, the
comparisons and date, colour, and uuid parsers the formats use, and the
combining walk anyOf and oneOf share. Schema holds the rules; this holds
what they are applied to.

methods.name: isBoolean
methods.doc: Whether a value reads as a boolean, the strings included.

methods.name: toBoolean
methods.doc: The boolean a value reads as.

methods.name: isInteger
methods.doc: Whether a value is a whole number.

methods.name: isArray
methods.doc: Whether a value reads as a list, a comma-separated string included.

methods.name: toArray
methods.doc: The list a value reads as.

methods.name: isObject
methods.doc: Whether a value reads as an object.

methods.name: toObject
methods.doc: The object a value reads as, as an array.

methods.name: bestType
methods.doc: The first of the schema's types, in the order it lists them, that the value reads as (an empty string is a string when that is allowed); '' when none.

methods.name: valuesEqual
methods.doc: Whether two values are equal by the reference's loose rules.

methods.name: patternProperty
methods.doc: The schema of the patternProperties entry a property name matches, or null.

methods.name: matchesPattern
methods.doc: Whether a value matches a schema pattern, read as the reference reads one: unanchored, # escaped, UTF-8.

methods.name: hasUniqueItems
methods.doc: Whether no two items are equal once their keys are sorted; types stay apart, so 1 and "1" differ.

methods.name: intersectKeys
methods.doc: The first array's entries whose keys the second has too, at every level where both hold an array.

methods.name: stabilize
methods.doc: Keys sorted at every level, so two equal structures serialise the same.

methods.name: parseDate
methods.doc: A timestamp for an RFC3339-shaped date, false otherwise; $forceUtc reads the offset as Z.

methods.name: parseHexColor
methods.doc: A hex colour as given, or false.

methods.name: isUuid
methods.doc: Whether a value is a version-4 uuid.

methods.name: list
methods.doc: A comma- or space-separated string as a list.

methods.name: objectOf
methods.doc:
A value as an object's properties: '' is the empty object, a stdClass its properties, a
JsonSerializable what it serializes to; null when it is no object.

classes.name: Minn\Rest\SearchController
classes.doc:
wp/v2 search over published content: id, title, url, type, and the
post type as subtype. Ordered the way the reference orders a search:
a title holding every term first, then a title holding any term, then
an excerpt match, then a content match, newest first within a rank.

force that copy goes to the trash, which already hands the theme's
file back; with force the row goes for good. A template that exists
only as a theme file has nothing to remove.

version 1 is taken, and only the documented keys: each is set (its value
replaced), merged (maps merged key by key, lists joined with their
members matched by identity), replaced (merged, but lists replaced
whole) or removed (keys from a map, members from a list by identity).
A null in a patch removes what it names. What a caller got wrong comes
back as problems: the function to name and the words.

remove), and the problems met: [function or null for the mode's own
method, words].

methods.name: merge

methods.name: remove
methods.doc: Keys removed from a map (a list of keys, or a key mapped to what to remove inside it); members removed from a list by identity.

methods.name: update

Saves a widget's settings through its own update and registers it:

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\Abilities
classes.doc:
The abilities registry behind WP_Abilities_Registry,
WP_Ability_Categories_Registry and the wp_*_ability facade, as the
reference keeps it (probes abilities-registry, abilities-classes). The
categories init and then the abilities init fire once each, lazily, on
the first lookup of their kind, each handed its registry. The registries
themselves take a registration at any time; only the wp_register_*
functions insist on the init action. A registration is checked as the
reference checks it (name shape, duplicates, a known category, then the
properties the ability and category classes check) and refused with its
notice. An ability's meta gains the default annotations, show_in_rest
(public's value when unset) and public.

methods.name: initializeCategories
methods.doc: Fires the categories action once.

methods.name: initialize
methods.doc: Fires the categories action, then the abilities action, each once.

methods.name: registerCategory
methods.doc: Registers a category; its row, or null with the reference's notice. @return array<string, mixed>|null

methods.name: register
methods.doc: Registers an ability; its row, or null with the reference's notice. @return array<string, mixed>|null

methods.name: unregister
methods.doc: Removes an ability; its row, or null with the reference's notice. @return array<string, mixed>|null

methods.name: unregisterCategory
methods.doc: Removes a category; its row, or null with the reference's notice. @return array<string, mixed>|null

methods.name: find
methods.doc: One ability, or null with the reference's notice. @return array<string, mixed>|null

methods.name: ability
methods.doc: One ability, or null, asked after without a notice. @return array<string, mixed>|null

methods.name: findCategory
methods.doc: One category, or null with the reference's notice. @return array<string, mixed>|null

methods.name: category
methods.doc: One category, or null, asked after without a notice. @return array<string, mixed>|null

methods.name: all
methods.doc: Every ability, by name. @return array<string, array>

methods.name: allCategories
methods.doc: Every category, by slug. @return array<string, array>

methods.name: abilityRefusal
methods.doc: Why an ability's properties are refused, as WP_Ability::prepare_properties says it, or null. @param array<string, mixed> $args

methods.name: categoryRefusal
methods.doc: Why a category's properties are refused, as WP_Ability_Category::prepare_properties says it, or null. @param array<string, mixed> $args

methods.name: meta
methods.doc:
An ability's meta with the reference's defaults: the three annotations
first, show_in_rest (public's value when unset), then public.

methods.name: state
shapes: @return array{categoriesFired: bool, abilitiesFired: bool, categories: array<string, array>, abilities: array<string, array>}

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\AbilityRun
classes.doc:
The checks of an ability's run, as the reference makes them (probes
abilities-registry, abilities-classes); WP_Ability::execute strings them:
input left out takes the input schema's default, input given to an ability
without an input schema is refused, input that its schema refuses is
ability_invalid_input; a permission callback that does not answer true is
ability_invalid_permissions (an error it returns is reported as a notice);
then wp_before_execute_ability, the callback
(an error it returns is the answer), the output checked against the
output schema (ability_invalid_output), and wp_after_execute_ability.

methods.name: input
methods.doc: True, or why the input does not fit.

methods.name: allowed
methods.doc: True, or the error a permission answer other than true becomes (an error it returns is reported as a notice).

methods.name: output
methods.doc: True, or why the output does not fit the output schema.

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\AccountFlows
classes.doc:
The account functions a sign-in page and plugins call, with the
reference's checks, words, hooks and mail (probe account-flows): asking
for a password reset (retrieve_password), resetting one
(reset_password), registering (register_new_user), and telling the site
and the new user about a registration (wp_new_user_notification).

constants.name: NO_ACCOUNT
constants.value: 'Error: There is no account with that username or email address.'

methods.name: retrievePassword
methods.doc:
A reset link mailed to the account a login or email names: true, or
the refusal (no name, no such account, a plugin's error, reset not
allowed, or the mail failing). $link makes the link from the account's
login and the key when the reset page is someone else's (an
extension's own); without it the link opens the sign-in page's.
$words writes the mail's subject, body and (optionally) headers from
the link and the account's display name, for a site whose people never
see a login (an HTML mail sends its Content-Type header); without it
the mail is the reference's. Plugins' filters still have the last word
either way.

methods.name: resetPassword
methods.doc: A new password for a user, announced before (password_reset) and after (after_password_reset).

methods.name: registerNewUser
methods.doc:
A new account for a login and an email, with a generated password and
the nag to change it: its id, or every refusal at once (the name
empty, illegal, taken or barred; the email empty, malformed or taken;
whatever register_post and registration_errors add).

methods.name: registerWithPassword
methods.signature: registerWithPassword(string $login, string $email, string $password, string $shownAs = '', string $role = ''): Minn\Objects\Errors|int
methods.doc:
A new account whose holder chose the password (a sign-up form of an
extension's own): the same checks as registerNewUser, then the account
with that password (as a form sends it, slashed) and, when one is
given, the name shown for it (display name and nickname) and the role
(else the site's default role), and the site told. The holder is
mailed nothing: there is no password to set.

methods.name: accountWithPassword
methods.signature: accountWithPassword(string $login, string $email, string $password, string $shownAs = '', string $role = ''): Minn\Objects\Errors|int
methods.doc:
The account registerWithPassword makes, with nobody told: for a
sign-up whose accounts the site's address has no need to hear about
one by one (the players of a game).

methods.name: newUserNotification
methods.doc:
A new account announced: to the site's address (unless only the user
is told), then to the user with a link to set their password (unless
only the site is, or the old call shape asks for nobody).

methods.name: vetRegistration
methods.doc:
The name and email a registration asks for, judged as the reference
judges them: the sanitised name, the filtered email, and the refusals
(none when the registration may go ahead).

methods.name: registerFailed
methods.doc: The refusal when the account row could not be written.

methods.name: resetLink
methods.doc: The link that opens the password form for a user's key.

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\AdminActionController
classes.doc:
The wp-admin pages a plugin answers itself. The admin is Minn Admin, so
the engine draws no wp-admin screen, but a page builder opens its editor
from one: Elementor's "Edit with Elementor" is post.php?post=N&action=elementor,
whose handler (admin_action_elementor) prints a whole page of its own and
ends the request before any screen is drawn.

A request to a wp-admin page that names an action boots as an admin
request, as the reference's does. The admin cookie (scoped to /wp-admin)
is asked for, for the user the request is read as; without it the
visitor signs in and comes back. admin_init fires, then the action's
handlers. When no plugin handles the action, or its handlers return, the
request lands in Minn Admin, where every other wp-admin address goes.

One page is an endpoint instead: the media modal's uploader posts its files
to async-upload.php (action upload-attachment), which the reference answers
as an ajax request, in plain text. After the page's action the upload runs
the handlers registered for the upload-attachment ajax action, as
admin-ajax.php would: WordPress's own answer comes with the Minn Legacy Pack,
the plugin that brings the modal.

methods.name: claims
methods.doc: Whether a request is for a wp-admin page with an action to run, which the runtime boots as an admin request.

methods.name: uploads
methods.doc: Whether a request is the media modal's upload, which the reference answers as an ajax request (DOING_AJAX).

methods.name: dispatch
methods.doc: Runs the handlers a plugin hooked for the action, or sends the visitor on.

methods.name: post
methods.doc:
admin-post.php, where plugins' forms post, as the reference answers it
(runtime suite, "admin-post.php"): an admin request with the admin
headers, admin_init, then admin_post_{action} for someone signed in
(by the admin cookie, else the front end's) or admin_post_nopriv_{action}
for a visitor, and
admin_post or admin_post_nopriv when no action is named. A named action
nobody handles is a 400; what the handlers print is the page, and a
handler that redirects and exits sends its redirect.

methods.name: upload
methods.doc:
The upload, answered in plain text from the first byte a handler prints.
A handler ends the request with its answer; when none does, the answer
is admin-ajax.php's for an action nobody handles.

methods.name: action
methods.doc: The action the request names, the posted field over the query's, or null when there is none.

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\AjaxController
classes.doc:
admin-ajax.php, the endpoint plugins post their front-end work to: a form
submitted without a reload, a spam check, a background job. The action a
request names runs the handlers registered as wp_ajax_{action} for a
signed-in visitor and wp_ajax_nopriv_{action} for anyone else, answered as
the reference answers them (contracts/runtime.md "admin-ajax.php").

It is an admin request: is_admin() is true while the plugins load and
admin_init fires before the handler. A handler usually ends the request
itself (wp_send_json, wp_die, exit), so the endpoint's headers go out
before it runs; one that returns is followed by the reference's "0".

constants.name: CORE
constants.doc: The core actions the endpoint answers itself, under the prefix for who is asking: the action => the handler.

constants.name: ADMIN_FILTERS
constants.doc: The filters the reference's admin includes add once plugins have loaded: the hook, the callback.

methods.name: claims
methods.doc: Whether a request is for the endpoint, which the runtime boots as an admin request.

methods.name: doing
methods.doc: Whether the reference answers a request as an ajax one (DOING_AJAX): this endpoint, and the media modal's uploads.

methods.name: dispatch
methods.doc: Runs the handlers registered for the action the request names.

methods.name: action
methods.doc: The action the request names, the posted field over the query's, or null when there is none to run.

methods.name: allowedOrigin
methods.doc: The two cross-origin headers, for an Origin that is this site's own address; empty for any other.

methods.name: registerCore
methods.doc: The reference registers its own actions after admin_init, only those for who is asking, ahead of a plugin's.

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\AllowedOptions
classes.doc:
The settings-page allowlist plugins extend: option group => the option
names a settings form in that group may save. The engine renders no
settings pages, so the list is only recorded, never enforced.

methods.name: merge
methods.doc:
The allowlist with each new name appended to its group once, groups
created as needed. A group handed as anything but a list adds nothing.

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\ApplicationPasswordEvents
classes.doc:
Application password changes made over REST, as the reference makes them
(probe rest-application-password-hooks): the prepared item (the name,
and an app id a new one is given) through
rest_pre_insert_application_password, then WP_Application_Passwords
(which tells plugins through wp_create_, wp_update_ and
wp_delete_application_password), then rest_after_insert_application_password.

methods.name: create
methods.doc:
A new password: its record and its plain text in groups of four, or
the reference's refusal.

methods.name: update
methods.doc: A password renamed (when the body names it): its record as it stands.

methods.name: prepared
methods.doc: The item the request prepares (its name; a new one's app id), through rest_pre_insert_application_password. @param array<string, mixed> $fields

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\ApplicationPasswordRecords
classes.doc:
A user's application passwords as WordPress's API keeps them
(WP_Application_Passwords), over the engine's store
(Minn\Auth\ApplicationPasswords, the reference's format): made, found,
renamed, used, removed one by one or all together, with the reference's
answers and actions.

constants.name: IN_USE
constants.doc: The site option saying any password was made.

methods.name: inUse
methods.doc: Whether any user has made an application password (is_in_use).

methods.name: create
methods.doc:
A new password for the user (create_new_application_password): [the
password, its record], or the reference's error for a nameless one.

methods.name: all
methods.doc: A user's passwords (get_user_application_passwords).

methods.name: find
methods.doc: One of a user's passwords by its uuid (get_user_application_password), or null.

methods.name: nameExists
methods.doc: Whether one of a user's passwords has the name (application_name_exists_for_user).

methods.name: update
methods.doc: A password renamed, the only field the reference changes (update_application_password): true, or its not-found error.

methods.name: recordUsage
methods.doc: A use recorded, when and from where (record_application_password_usage): true, or the not-found error.

methods.name: delete
methods.doc: A password removed (delete_application_password): true, or the not-found error.

methods.name: deleteAll
methods.doc: Every password of the user removed, each told to wp_delete_application_password (delete_all_application_passwords); how many went.

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\ApplicationPasswordSignIn
classes.doc:
wp_authenticate_application_password as the reference answers it (probe
application-passwords-api): a user found already stands; outside an API
request (application_password_is_api_request) nothing is tried; then the
user by login or email, the feature's availability (for the site, for
the user), and each of the user's passwords, a match passing through
wp_authenticate_application_password_errors, recorded, and announced
(application_password_did_authenticate); every refusal announced
through application_password_failed_authentication.

methods.name: authenticate
methods.doc: The signed-in user, the input unchanged, or the refusal.

methods.name: validate
methods.doc:
determine_current_user's application password step: an earlier
answer stands; else the user the REST request's application password
signed in (the engine checked the password before plugins loaded),
heard again as the reference hears it: the feature's availability,
wp_authenticate_application_password_errors, then
application_password_did_authenticate; a refusal is announced and
leaves the request signed out.

methods.name: refusal
methods.doc: Why the user may not sign in by application password, or null when they may.

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\ArchiveLinks
classes.doc:
A post type's archive address and its feed, as the reference gives them
(probe archive-links). The posts' archive is the posts page when the
front is a page with one, else the bare home; a type with an archive
lives under its named archive or its rewrite slug (after the
structure's front unless it declines it), or at ?post_type= without
rewrites or pretty permalinks; any other type has none (false, no
filter). Its feed is the archive's /feed/ (/feed/{type}/ for one not the
default) when the type's rewrite takes feeds, else ?feed= with the type
spelled out.

methods.name: archive
methods.doc: get_post_type_archive_link.

methods.name: feed
methods.doc: get_post_type_archive_feed_link.

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\AssetEdits
classes.doc:
What a plugin did to $wp_scripts->registered or $wp_styles->registered
directly, as wp_default_scripts callbacks do (a dependency dropped, a
source swapped, an entry unset or added), handed to the registry: each
handle as the view showed it last against the view as the plugin left
it.

methods.name: apply
methods.doc:
The edits applied, for every handle or only the one named. The view
changes with each edit the registry takes, so the edited view is read
from the copy handed in.
shapes: @param array<string, mixed> $edited the view as the plugin left it
@param array<string, array{0: mixed, 1: list<string>, 2: mixed, 3: mixed, 4: mixed}> $synced each handle as the view last showed it (source, dependencies, version, args, data)

params.name: edited
params.doc: the view as the plugin left it

params.name: synced
params.shape: array<string, array{0: mixed, 1: list<string>, 2: mixed, 3: mixed, 4: mixed}>
params.doc: each handle as the view last showed it (source, dependencies, version, args, data)

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\AssetQueue
classes.doc:
The scripts and styles a request queues, as WordPress's asset functions
queue them: each kind's registry kept for the request, a handle queued
(with the notice for one queued before init), and a script's element,
from a file or inline, through the attribute filters.

methods.name: follow
methods.doc:
The registry the page's functions work on: the one held by the object
in the global a plugin may replace ($wp_scripts, $wp_styles), as the
reference's functions follow that global. Elementor's editor starts
from a new registry of each kind, leaving every other plugin's assets
out; from then on that one is the page's, the engine's own printing
included. Without such an object, the request's own.

methods.name: of
methods.doc: The engine queue a registry object holds (a WP_Scripts or WP_Styles), null for anything else.

methods.name: forFunctions
methods.doc: The registry a page's script or style function works on (follow), a script one used first (used).

methods.name: snapshot
methods.doc: The scripts, styles and script modules queued now, to compare with once a block has rendered.

methods.name: dequeueSince
methods.doc:
Takes off the queues what joined them since the snapshot: what a block that rendered nothing enqueued, as
the reference takes it off.

methods.name: settleBlock
methods.signature: settleBlock(array $before, string $html, string $name, Closure $enqueue, mixed $type = NULL): void
methods.doc:
After a block has rendered: when a named block rendered nothing, whitespace aside, and its render enqueued
something or its own assets are not all queued yet, enqueue_empty_block_content_assets is asked; unless it
keeps them, what the render enqueued is taken off the queues again and the block's own are not added.
Otherwise $enqueue adds its own. The text between blocks (no name) is never asked about, as on the reference.

methods.name: assets
methods.doc: The request's registry of one kind of asset, script or style, made the first time it is asked for.

methods.name: warnTooEarly
methods.doc:
The notice (doing it wrong, 3.3.0) for an asset function run before
init and before any of the enqueue actions
(_wp_scripts_maybe_doing_it_wrong), naming the handle when there is one.

methods.name: linedUp
methods.doc:
The scripts lined up for printing, as print_scripts_array leaves them.
WordPress's own scripts among them that the engine has no file for are
noted for the Minn Legacy Pack (LegacyPack::noteScripts).

methods.name: enqueueScript
methods.doc: A registered script queued (wp_enqueue_script with a handle alone).

methods.name: used
methods.doc:
The page's script registry used, as rendering a block or queuing a
script uses the reference's (it is made then, and what it is told as it
is made, it is told now): the facade's callback runs once and is gone.

methods.name: onFirstUse
methods.doc: What the page's script registry is told on its first use (the facade's wp_scripts()); null for nothing.

methods.name: enqueueStyle
methods.doc: A registered style queued (wp_enqueue_style with a handle alone).

methods.name: tag
methods.doc: A script file's element (wp_get_script_tag), its attributes through wp_script_attributes first.

methods.name: inlineTag
methods.doc: Inline code's element (wp_get_inline_script_tag): the code trimmed between newlines, wp_inline_script_attributes asked.

methods.name: pending
methods.doc: Whether a block type has assets of its own not queued yet (its scripts, view scripts and modules, styles).

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\AssetView
classes.doc:
A registry's view in the shape plugins read and edit it: the public
arrays of WordPress's dependency classes ($wp_scripts->registered, ->queue,
->done), kept current from Runtime\Assets one handle at a time. What a
plugin edits in the view is handed back (Runtime\AssetEdits) before the
registry changes or reads that handle, and for every handle before the
view is rebuilt or printed from. Rebuilding the whole view at each change
cost a page that registers hundreds of handles tens of milliseconds.

methods.name: sync
methods.doc: Rebuilds the whole view from the registry, after handing back what a plugin edited in it.

methods.name: push
methods.doc: Hands back what a plugin edited in place (every handle, the queue, the printed list).

methods.name: refresh
methods.doc: One handle of the view (none: null), the queue and the printed list, kept current after the registry changed them.

methods.name: show
methods.doc: A handle as the registry holds it, in the view and remembered as shown; gone from both when the registry has none.

methods.name: handBack
methods.doc: Hands back what a plugin edited in place for one handle (none: null), and in the queue and the printed list.

methods.name: reconcile
methods.doc: What a plugin did to the view's handles directly, for one handle or (null) every one, handed to the registry.

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\Assets
classes.doc:
The registry behind wp_register_/wp_enqueue_ for scripts and styles:
handles, sources, dependencies, versions, inline additions, localized
data, and the head/footer split. Printing follows the reference's tag
shapes as far as captured; see contracts/runtime.md.

methods.name: watch
methods.doc:
A listener told after every change which handle changed (null when
only the queue or the printed list did), so a plugin-facing view keeps
that handle current without rebuilding the rest; and one told before a
handle is changed or read, so what a plugin edited in that view for it
lands first.

methods.name: setQueue
