methods.doc: The queue as a plugin left it after editing the view directly.

methods.name: register
methods.signature: register(string $handle, string|false $src, array $deps, string|bool|null $ver, mixed $extra): bool
methods.doc: Registers an asset under a handle.

methods.name: revise
methods.signature: revise(string $handle, string|false $src, array $deps, string|bool|null $ver, mixed $extra): bool
methods.doc: An existing handle's source, dependencies, version and arguments replaced, its data, inline code and place in the queue kept.

methods.name: externalHosts
methods.doc: The hosts the queued assets load from, other than the site's own.
shapes: @return list<string> hosts of enqueued sources (dependencies first) away from the given host, for dns-prefetch hints

methods.name: deregister
methods.doc: Forgets an asset.

methods.name: enqueue
methods.doc:
Queues an asset for printing (probe placeholders-admin). One that is
neither registered nor among the reference's own handles waits, and
joins the queue when it is registered; one of the reference's own the
engine ships no file for is queued as the reference would queue it.

methods.name: dequeue
methods.doc: Removes an asset from the queue, or from the handles waiting for registration.

methods.name: registered
methods.doc: Whether a handle is registered, by the site or as one the reference registers itself (data/default-assets.json).

methods.name: unshipped
methods.doc: Whether a handle is one the reference registers itself that nothing here registered: the engine carries no file for it.

methods.name: dependencies
methods.doc: A handle's dependencies: as registered, or as the reference registers it. @return list<string>

methods.name: dependents
methods.doc: The registered handles that name a handle among their dependencies. @return list<string>

methods.name: reaches
methods.doc:
Whether a handle is a dependency, however deep, of any of the given
handles.

methods.name: enqueued
methods.doc:
Queued directly, or pulled in as the dependency of something queued,
however deep. The reference answers the same way, and plugin code
leans on it: WooCommerce only attaches its settings blob when it
finds `wc-settings` "enqueued", and nothing queues that handle by
name, it only ever rides in as a dependency.

methods.name: doneList
methods.doc: The handles printed so far.

methods.name: setDone
methods.doc: The printed handles as a plugin left them after editing the view directly.

methods.name: done
methods.doc: Whether a handle has been printed.

methods.name: addInline
methods.doc: Attaches inline code to an asset.

methods.name: addData
methods.doc: Attaches a data key to an asset.

methods.name: setTranslations
methods.doc: Names the text domain and folder a script's translations come from, and makes the script depend on wp-i18n.

methods.name: data
methods.doc: A data key of an asset, or false.

methods.name: localize
methods.doc: Attaches a localized object to a script.

methods.name: toPrint
methods.doc: Every queued handle not yet printed, dependencies first. @return list<string>

methods.name: withPath
methods.doc:
Enqueued handles that name a file on disk, mapped to that path. A style
registered with a `path` datum is saying it can be inlined; whether it
is small enough to be worth inlining is the caller's decision.

methods.name: unsource
methods.doc: Drops a handle's source so it prints as markup rather than a link.

methods.name: markDone
methods.doc: Records a handle as printed.

methods.name: item
methods.doc: One registered asset, or null.

methods.name: items
methods.doc: Every registered asset.

methods.name: queue
methods.doc: The handles queued.

methods.name: kind
methods.doc: Whether these are scripts or styles.

methods.name: held
methods.doc:
Whether a handle is an item to attach to: one registered here, or a
stylesheet the reference registers itself, held from then on with no
file (the engine ships none of those) so what a plugin attaches to it
still prints. A core script is not held: its inline code without the
library would only fail in the browser.

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\AttachmentImages
classes.doc:
An attachment's image as WordPress's media functions make it: the
registered sizes, a size fitted to a box, the file for a size (or an
icon), the srcset and sizes pair, the loading attributes an image earns
where it sits, the img element itself, and the site icon.

methods.name: sizes
methods.doc:
The registered sizes (_minn_image_sizes): the four from the options,
then the ones add_image_size added.

methods.name: additionalSizes
methods.doc:
The sizes plugins and themes added (wp_get_additional_image_sizes),
kept where they read them: $_wp_additional_image_sizes.

methods.name: constrain
methods.doc:
Dimensions fitted inside a box (wp_constrain_dimensions), through
wp_constrain_dimensions when there is a box.

methods.name: matchesRatio
methods.doc: Whether two sizes share a ratio (wp_image_matches_ratio): the wider one, fitted into the other's box, comes within a pixel of it.

methods.name: constrainForEditor
methods.signature: constrainForEditor(mixed $width, mixed $height, mixed $size = 'medium', mixed $context = NULL): mixed
methods.doc:
Dimensions fitted for the editor to a named or given size
(image_constrain_size_for_editor), within editor_max_image_size.

methods.name: intermediate
methods.doc: An attachment's file for a size (image_get_intermediate_size), as image_get_intermediate_size leaves it; false for none.

methods.name: downsize
methods.doc:
An image attachment at a size (image_downsize): its address, width,
height and whether that is a resized copy, unless image_downsize
answers first; false for no image.

methods.name: src
methods.doc: An attachment's image at a size, or its icon when asked (wp_get_attachment_image_src), as wp_get_attachment_image_src leaves it.

methods.name: sizeFromMeta
methods.doc:
A named size's dimensions from an image's metadata
(_wp_get_image_size_from_meta): full for the original; false for one
it lacks.

methods.name: srcset
methods.doc: The srcset of an image's sizes with its ratio (wp_calculate_image_srcset), as wp_calculate_image_srcset leaves the sources; false for none.

methods.name: subsizes
methods.doc:
The sizes get_intermediate_image_sizes names (its
intermediate_image_sizes filter heard), each with its width, height
and crop: a name no size is registered under is read from its
options, and one of neither width nor height is left out (probe
media-template-doubts).
shapes: @return array<string, array{width: int, height: int, crop: bool|array<mixed>}>

methods.name: browserProcessing
methods.doc:
Whether images are processed in the browser before upload (probe
rest-attachments-controller): in a secure context, which is HTTPS or
a host of localhost or under .localhost (its port aside; 127.0.0.1
is not one), through wp_client_side_media_processing_enabled.

methods.name: sizesAttribute
methods.signature: sizesAttribute(mixed $size, mixed $imageSrc = NULL, mixed $imageMeta = NULL, mixed $attachmentId = 0): mixed
methods.doc: The sizes attribute for an image's width (wp_calculate_image_sizes), as wp_calculate_image_sizes leaves it; false without a width.

methods.name: startsWithAuto
methods.doc: Whether a sizes list starts with auto, alone or before a comma, in any case (wp_sizes_attribute_includes_valid_auto).

methods.name: dimensionAttributes
methods.doc: The width and height attributes for an image (image_hwstring), each when set.

methods.name: lazyLoading
methods.doc: Whether lazy loading is on for a tag in a context (wp_lazy_loading_enabled): images and iframes, as wp_lazy_loading_enabled leaves it.

methods.name: loadingAttributes
methods.doc:
The loading attributes an image or iframe earns
(wp_get_loading_optimization_attributes), unless a plugin answers
first: decoding async for an image; with both dimensions set, the
caller's own priority and loading, else where it sits.

methods.name: earnedPriority
methods.doc:
Fetch priority high for an image large enough to deserve it, while no
other image has taken it.

methods.name: imageAttributes
methods.signature: imageAttributes(int $attachmentId, array $attr, string $src, int $width, int $height, string $context = 'wp_get_attachment_image'): array
methods.doc:
The loading attributes and the srcset and sizes pair an attachment's
image carries unless the caller set them.

methods.name: image
methods.signature: image(mixed $attachmentId, mixed $size = 'thumbnail', mixed $icon = false, mixed $attr = ''): mixed
methods.doc:
An attachment's img element at a size (wp_get_attachment_image): its
class, alt text, loading attributes and srcset, through
wp_get_attachment_image_attributes and wp_get_attachment_image; empty
for none.

methods.name: siteIconUrl
methods.doc: The site icon's address at a size (get_site_icon_url), the address given when the site has none; as get_site_icon_url leaves it.

methods.name: hasSiteIcon
methods.doc: Whether the site has an icon (has_site_icon).

methods.name: omitThreshold
methods.doc:
How many images in a page's content load eagerly
(wp_omit_loading_attr_threshold): 3, as the filter leaves it, asked
once and then kept unless forced (probe: the loading threshold).

methods.name: asked
methods.doc:
What a caller's own fetchpriority high or loading settles; null when it
named neither. Only an image takes high priority, and an element that
names a loading other than lazy is never made lazy.

methods.name: byPlace
methods.doc:
Where an element sits settles the rest. One in a header context is in
view: never lazy, one of the eager images. Inside a page's template, or
its main loop, an image shares the budget wp_omit_loading_attr_threshold
leaves (three eager images), the first one large enough to deserve it
high priority. Anything else
waits, where lazy loading is on.

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\AttachmentModel
classes.doc:
An attachment as the media modal's scripts read it
(wp_prepare_attachment_for_js): its fields, its file and its sizes, and
what the visitor may do with it. The nonces the modal saves, deletes and
edits with, the links to edit the attachment and its author, and the post
it was uploaded to are there only for a visitor allowed each, as the
reference gives them. The model passes through wp_prepare_attachment_for_js.

constants.name: FIELDS
constants.doc: The model's first fields, in the order the reference sends them.

methods.name: forJs
methods.doc: The model, or null for anything that is not an attachment.

methods.name: people
methods.doc:
Who uploaded the attachment and to which post: the author's name, and
a link to edit them where one may (none for an author no longer a
user); the post's title and edit link for a visitor who may read it.

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\Attachments
classes.doc:
Attachments as WordPress's media functions keep them: the uploads folder
and its address, an attachment's file (stored relative to the folder),
its address and metadata, and what kind of file it is; each as its
filter leaves it.

methods.name: uploadDir
methods.doc:
The uploads folder and its address for a time, the month's folder too
when uploads go by month (_wp_upload_dir, wp_get_upload_dir), as
upload_dir leaves them.

methods.name: uploadDirMade
methods.signature: uploadDirMade(mixed $time = NULL, mixed $createDir = true, mixed $refreshCache = false): mixed
methods.doc: The uploads folder made on disk when asked (wp_upload_dir), and returned.

methods.name: makeDir
methods.doc: A folder made with its parents (wp_mkdir_p): whether it is there and may be written to.

methods.name: relativePath
methods.doc: A path under the uploads folder made relative to it (_wp_relative_upload_path), as _wp_relative_upload_path leaves it.

methods.name: file
methods.doc: An attachment's file on disk (get_attached_file), the uploads folder before a relative one; through get_attached_file unless asked not to be.

methods.name: setFile
methods.doc: An attachment's file recorded (update_attached_file), relative to the uploads folder; an empty one removes the record.

methods.name: url
methods.doc:
An attachment's address (wp_get_attachment_url): its file under the
uploads address, else its guid; false for no attachment or no address.

methods.name: metadata
methods.doc:
An attachment's metadata (wp_get_attachment_metadata), the post being
read's for none; one stored in a shape the meta reader refuses is
parsed from its row; false for none; through
wp_get_attachment_metadata unless asked not to be.

methods.name: setMetadata
methods.doc: An attachment's metadata stored (wp_update_attachment_metadata) as wp_update_attachment_metadata leaves it; an empty one removed.

methods.name: is
methods.doc: Whether an attachment is a kind of file (wp_attachment_is): image, audio, video, or a MIME type or extension.

methods.name: isImage
methods.doc: Whether an attachment is an image (wp_attachment_is_image).

methods.name: audioExtensions
methods.doc: The audio file extensions the player takes (wp_get_audio_extensions), as wp_audio_extensions leaves them.

methods.name: videoExtensions
methods.doc: The video file extensions the player takes (wp_get_video_extensions), as wp_video_extensions leaves them.

methods.name: insert
methods.signature: insert(mixed $args, mixed $file = false, mixed $parentPostId = 0, mixed $wpError = false, mixed $fireAfterHooks = true): mixed
methods.doc:
An attachment stored (wp_insert_attachment): the arguments over a file
and no parent, the parent given, saved as a post of type attachment.

methods.name: delete
methods.doc:
An attachment deleted (wp_delete_attachment): to the trash first
unless forced or the media trash is off; unless pre_delete_attachment
answers, its terms, comments and meta removed, the row between
delete_post and deleted_post, then its files. The post, or null.

methods.name: deleteFiles
methods.doc: An attachment's files deleted, its sizes and backups too (wp_delete_attachment_files); false when any was missing or outside the uploads folder.

methods.name: readImageMetadata
methods.doc:
A photo's own description from its IPTC and EXIF (wp_read_image_metadata),
through wp_read_image_metadata_types and wp_read_image_metadata; false
when there is no such file.

methods.name: fileUrl
methods.doc:
Where an attached file is served from, by where its stored path
points: inside the uploads folder, its folder swapped for the uploads
address; through an old uploads folder elsewhere, the part after that
folder, reached from a level under the uploads address; otherwise
relative to the uploads address.

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\Autosaves
classes.doc:
An autosave as the reference's REST autosave makes it (probes
rest-autosaves, hook-inputs-2; tests/tools/side-effects.php): the
author's own draft is saved in place through wp_update_post; anyone
else's post gets the author's one autosave slot, made through
wp_insert_post and _wp_put_post_revision, or updated through
wp_update_post after wp_creating_autosave. A slot already there is left
alone when every field given matches the post. An autosave request
(save) defines DOING_AUTOSAVE for the rest of the request, so plugins'
save hooks can tell, and no revision is saved while it is; a slot saved
on its own (create_post_autosave) defines nothing.

methods.name: save
methods.doc:
Saves the given revision fields (post_title, post_content,
post_excerpt) as the user's autosave of the post: the post's own id
when the draft itself was saved, the slot's otherwise, or the save's
refusal.

methods.name: saveSlot
methods.doc:
Saves the given revision fields in the user's autosave slot of the
post (create_post_autosave): the slot's id, or the save's refusal.

methods.name: inPlace
methods.doc: Whether an autosave saves the post itself: the author's own draft (or auto-draft), while no one else holds its lock.

methods.name: slot
methods.doc: The id of the user's autosave of a post, or null.

methods.name: matchesPost
methods.doc: Whether every field given matches the post's own, whitespace evened out. @param array<string, string> $fields

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\AvMetadata
classes.doc:
An audio or video file's metadata as WordPress's media readers keep it
(wp_read_audio_metadata, wp_read_video_metadata; probe media-meta), from
the engine's own analysis (Media\Av): an audio file's stream described
whole, a video's size, format and codec with its audio beside, the
playing time rounded and as a clock, when it was made, its ID3 tags and
cover, each through the reader's filter.

methods.name: audio
methods.doc: An audio file's metadata (wp_read_audio_metadata); false when there is no such file.

methods.name: video
methods.doc: A video file's metadata (wp_read_video_metadata); false when there is no such file.

methods.name: withTags
methods.doc:
Metadata with an analysis's ID3 tags added (wp_add_id3_tag_data): the
first value under each name of the ID3v2 tag, or of the ID3v1 tag when
there is no ID3v2 one, cleaned as post content; the length is left
out, and a terms-of-use notice the tag cut short is mended.

methods.name: withCover
methods.doc:
An audio or video attachment's metadata with its cover kept as an
attachment of its own, as wp_generate_attachment_metadata keeps it:
where the attachment type or the theme supports thumbnails, the
cover (found again by its digest, or written beside the file as
"name-ext-image") becomes the attachment's thumbnail; the cover's
bytes leave the metadata either way.

methods.name: creationTimestamp
methods.doc:
When an analysed file was made (wp_get_media_creation_timestamp): a
Windows Media file's creation date, a Matroska or WebM file's creation
time (false when it is no date) or its date, or the time the first box
of an MPEG-4 or QuickTime movie gives; false for any other.

methods.name: coverType
methods.doc:
A cover's extension and type, read from its bytes whatever the tag
names (probe media-cover): a JPEG, PNG or GIF is what it is; anything
else is kept as a .jpg of no type.

methods.name: cover
methods.doc: The attachment a cover is kept as: one an earlier file made from the same bytes, or a new one.

methods.name: common
methods.doc: The size, type and playing time both readers record.

methods.name: finished
methods.doc:
What both readers add last: when the file was made, its tags and its
cover (an ID3v2 picture with its size, any other without).

methods.name: withoutStreams
methods.doc: A stream's description without its per-stream list.

methods.name: cleaned
methods.doc: A tag's value cleaned as post content, text inside a list included.

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\Avatar
classes.doc: Avatars the way get_avatar_data and get_avatar decide them: the argument defaults, the email an id, user, post, or comment names, the Gravatar URL, and the attributes. Behaviour pinned by contracts/fixtures/api/functions.json.

methods.name: dataArgs
methods.doc: The data arguments normalised: sizes to integers, the default token, the rating lowercased.

methods.name: hash
methods.doc: The Gravatar hash an email yields; '' for no email.

methods.name: hashFromAddress
methods.doc: A hash given as an md5.gravatar.com address, else null.

methods.name: urlArgs
methods.doc: The Gravatar URL's query arguments for the data arguments. @return array<string, string|int|false>

methods.name: classes
methods.doc: The classes: the size class, a default marker, the caller's own. @return list

methods.name: extraAttributes
methods.doc: The extra attribute string with loading and decoding added when the caller did not set them.

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\BlockFilters
classes.doc:
The block-level filters plugin code hooks (pre_render_block,
render_block_data, render_block, render_block_{name}), applied around the
engine's own renderer so a plugin sees every block the page renders, not
only the ones it registered.

constants.name: NATIVE_DATA_DONE
constants.doc:
The data filters the engine's renderer does itself for a block it
renders natively: a gallery's image ids. Element styles and style
variations are left to their own filters, which name the classes in
the block's className as plugins' later filters read it (probe
block-class-stages).

constants.name: NATIVE_RENDER_DONE
constants.doc:
The render filters it does itself: none. The element, layout, style
variation and paragraph classes reach the markup at their own filters,
as a plugin's earlier filters see it without them (probe
block-class-stages).

methods.name: active
methods.doc: Whether any block filter is registered.

methods.name: toArray
methods.doc: A block as the parsed array plugins receive.
shapes: @return array<string, mixed> the parsed-array shape plugin code reads

methods.name: fromArray
methods.doc: A block from the parsed array plugins hand back.

methods.name: data
methods.doc:
A parsed block through render_block_data, without the callbacks done
already (NATIVE_DATA_DONE for a block the engine's renderer renders).

params.name: parent
params.doc: the WP_Block rendering it, when there is one

methods.name: rendered
methods.doc:
A rendered block through render_block and its per-name filter, without
the callbacks done already (NATIVE_RENDER_DONE, with its stand-ins, for
a block the engine's renderer renders).

methods.name: before
methods.doc:
A block about to render, begun as the reference begins it (probe
block-instances): one with no parent block (a document's, a part's, a
pattern's) is asked pre_render_block, render_block_data and
render_block_context with none, then made a WP_Block with the post's
context; an inner one is made a WP_Block from what its parent gives its
inner blocks first (its type asked get_block_type_uses_context), then
asked the three with its parent (the context filter handed the
context its type uses), and adopts what they made of it.
A short-circuit from pre_render_block, or the block as
render_block_data left it.
shapes: @param array<string, int|array{0: int, 1: string}> $done the data filters done already

methods.name: made
methods.doc:
A block begun as the reference's block list makes one its parent
renders without asking the block filters first (a navigation's own
items): its WP_Block, with what the parent gives its inner blocks.

methods.name: begun
methods.doc: The WP_Block a block began as and the context render_block_context gave it.

methods.name: after
methods.doc:
A rendered block through render_block and its per-name filter, with
the WP_Block it began as.
shapes: @param array<string, int|array{0: int, 1: string}> $done the render filters done already

methods.name: context
shapes: @return array<string, mixed> the context render_block() gives a document's top block: the global post's, as get_post() reads it

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\BlockHooks
classes.doc:
The Block Hooks API on the engine's own front end: a plugin asks for its
block to be inserted next to an anchor block in a template part or a
pattern (WooCommerce puts the mini-cart after the navigation in a
header), and the markup the renderer reads carries those insertions.

The facade owns the traversal (wp-api/blocks.php); this is the seam the
theme blocks call, and it stays inert until a plugin actually hooks
something, so a site without such a plugin parses nothing extra.

methods.name: withSingleInstances
methods.doc:
Content's blocks written out by $serialize under the single-instance
rule (apply_block_hooks_to_content): a hooked type that does not
support multiple goes in at the first anchor position that names it
only, and nowhere when the content has one already, however deep
(probe taxonomy-blocks-user-doubts).

methods.name: nextPosition
methods.doc: The traversal moves on to the next anchor position (each before, after, first_child and last_child the visitors ask).

methods.name: hooked
methods.doc:
The blocks hooked to each anchor, by position (get_hooked_blocks), as
the registered block types' block_hooks name them.

methods.name: active
methods.doc: Whether block hooks are registered (the runtime's functions are there only once it is up).

methods.name: insert
methods.doc:
The blocks hooked to an anchor at a position (insert_hooked_blocks),
each as the filters leave it, serialized; a type a filter suppresses,
or one the anchor lists as ignored, goes in nothing (probe
post-block-hooks).

methods.name: markIgnored
methods.doc:
The anchor's ignoredHookedBlocks with the types hooked to it at a
position added (set_ignored_hooked_blocks_metadata): those a filter
leaves standing, the list keeping the keys it had (probe
post-block-hooks). Nothing is inserted: the markup is empty.

methods.name: registeredPattern
methods.doc:
A plugin-registered pattern's content, hooks already applied by the
registry, for a slug the theme does not carry. Null when the runtime
is not up or nothing registered that name.

methods.name: forPattern
methods.doc:
A theme pattern's markup with its hooked blocks inserted, with the
pattern array as the context (blockTypes and categories are how a
plugin recognises a header pattern).

methods.name: forPost
methods.doc:
A post's blocks with the blocks hooked to them, as the reference reads
a navigation's or a synced pattern's
(apply_block_hooks_to_content_from_post_object): the hooked blocks the
post says to leave out left out; as stored with no WordPress layer to
ask.

methods.name: filtered
methods.doc:
The types hooked_block_types names for an anchor at a position, each
with the block hooked_block and hooked_block_{type} make of it (null
when one suppresses it).

methods.name: admitted
methods.doc: Whether a hooked type may go in at this position: always, unless it is single-instance and already in the content or put in at another position.

methods.name: names
methods.doc: Every block name in parsed blocks, however deep.

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\BlockMetadata
classes.doc:
block.json to the settings a block type registers with: the property
renames, the script and style handles (registered through the closures,
one per entry), the view script modules, the block hooks positions, and
the render template as a callback. Behaviour pinned by contracts/fixtures/api/blocks.json.

constants.name: I18N
constants.value: array (   'title' => 'block title',   'description' => 'block description',   'keywords' =>    array (     0 => 'block keyword',   ),   'styles' =>    array (     0 =>      array (       'label' => 'block style label',     ),   ),   'variations' =>    array (     0 =>      array (       'title' => 'block variation title',       'description' => 'block variation description',       'keywords' =>        array (         0 => 'block variation keyword',       ),     ),   ), )
constants.doc: The block.json strings a text domain translates, each with its context (get_block_metadata_i18n_schema).

methods.name: translated
methods.doc:
A block.json's strings in its text domain, each asked in its context
(title as "block title", keywords as "block keyword"...); a block
without a text domain is left as it is (probe taxonomy-blocks-user-doubts).

methods.name: settings
methods.signature: settings(array $metadata, Closure $scriptHandle, Closure $styleHandle, Closure $moduleId, Closure $render): array
methods.doc: Block settings from a block.json, the way the reference maps its properties.
shapes: @param Closure(array, string, int): (string|false) $scriptHandle registers one script entry, answering its handle
@param Closure(array, string, int): (string|false) $styleHandle registers one style entry
@param Closure(array, string, int): (string|false) $moduleId registers one view script module entry
@param Closure(string): ?Closure $render the render callback for a template path, or null when the file is missing

params.name: scriptHandle
params.doc: registers one script entry, answering its handle

params.name: moduleId
params.doc: registers one view script module entry

params.name: render
params.doc: the render callback for a template path, or null when the file is missing

methods.name: assetHandle
methods.doc: The script or style handle a block.json field registers under; core blocks keep the `wp-block-` spelling.

methods.name: translatedValue
methods.doc: One value by its piece of the schema: a string in its context, a list item by item, an object key by key.

methods.name: handles
methods.doc: The registered handles for one asset field: every entry when the field lists several; null when the field is absent. @return list<string>|null

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\BlockQueries
classes.doc:
The query arguments the query and comments blocks run, as WordPress's
block functions build them from a block's context: a query block's post
query, and the comment query a post's comments block shows.

constants.name: FORMATS
constants.doc: The post formats a query block may ask for, by slug.

methods.name: posts
methods.doc:
A query block's post query for a page (build_query_vars_from_query_block),
through query_loop_block_query_vars when the block has a query context.

methods.name: comments
methods.doc:
The comment query a comments block shows (build_comment_query_vars_from_block):
approved comments oldest first, the reader's own held ones too, the
post's, threaded and paged as the discussion settings say.

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\BlockTemplates
classes.doc:
Block templates plugins register at runtime, by their namespaced name
("plugin//slug"). A theme file or a saved template of the same slug
wins; otherwise the registered content renders for that slug.

methods.name: register
methods.doc: The registered row, or the refusal code the reference reports.

methods.name: unregister
methods.doc: Forgets a registered template; the row, or null.

methods.name: all
methods.doc: Every registered template.
shapes: @return array<string, array<string, mixed>> by registered name

methods.name: get
methods.doc: One registered template, or null.

methods.name: bySlug
methods.doc: A registered template by slug, or null.

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\BlockWidget
classes.doc:
A block widget's legacy class name. Every widget the block editor saves
is one block of markup, and a classic theme styles it by the widget
class the equivalent legacy widget used, so the wrapper carries a
second class named after the FIRST block in the content. A block with
no legacy equivalent adds nothing.

constants.name: LEGACY_CLASSES
constants.doc: First block name => the legacy widget class a theme styles.

methods.name: classNameFor
methods.doc: The legacy widget class a block widget maps to.

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\Bookmarks
classes.doc:
The site's links as the link functions find them (get_bookmarks): the
Links repository asked with the caller's arguments, each row an object,
through the get_bookmarks filter.

methods.name: find
methods.doc:
The links asked for (get_bookmarks): a category by name narrows them to
that category, or to none when no link category has the name; a list
of links to include sets any category aside.

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\BrowserGlobals
classes.doc:
The browser and web server a request names, as the reference's globals
have them from boot ($is_chrome, $is_safari, $is_IE, $is_apache,
$is_nginx, …; probe vars-matrix): one browser at most, read from the
user agent in the reference's order (Lynx, Edge, Opera, Chrome, Safari,
Internet Explorer on a Mac then elsewhere, Gecko, Netscape 4), an
iPhone being a mobile Safari; the server from SERVER_SOFTWARE, IIS 7 and
up apart. Chrome Frame's switch is the facade's (use_google_chrome_frame).

constants.name: NAMES
constants.doc: The globals, in the order the reference sets them.

methods.name: detect
methods.doc: Each global's value for this user agent and server software.

methods.name: browser
methods.doc: The one browser global the user agent sets, or null.

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\CommentChecks
classes.doc:
What WordPress checks of a comment before and after it is stored: the
lengths the table allows its fields, each field through its pre_comment_
filter, the status a stored comment has in words, and whether a new
post of a type starts open to comments or pings.

methods.name: fieldMaxLengths
methods.doc:
How long each comment form field may be
(wp_get_comment_fields_max_lengths), as the table allows, through
wp_get_comment_fields_max_lengths.

methods.name: maxLengths
methods.doc: Whether a comment fits its columns (wp_check_comment_data_max_lengths): true, or the error naming the first field too long.

methods.name: filter
methods.doc:
Each field through its pre_comment_ filter (wp_filter_comment), in the
reference's order (the user first, the email last), marked filtered.

methods.name: status
methods.doc: A comment's status (wp_get_comment_status): approved, unapproved, spam or trash; false for an unknown comment or status.

methods.name: defaultStatus
methods.doc:
Whether a new post of a type starts open (get_default_comment_status):
a page starts closed; another type follows the site's default when it
supports comments (or trackbacks, for pings).

methods.name: passes
methods.signature: passes(mixed $author, mixed $email, mixed $url, mixed $comment, mixed $userIp, mixed $userAgent, mixed $commentType): bool
methods.doc:
Whether a comment needs no moderation (check_comment): never while
moderation is on; the links counted in the comment as comment_text
shows it (comment_max_links_url may recount) against comment_max_links;
the moderation words; and, when asked, an earlier approved comment from
the same author (a pingback from one of the site's own posts, as
wp_auto_approve_ping decides; a trackback never).

methods.name: disallowed
methods.signature: disallowed(mixed $author, mixed $email, mixed $url, mixed $comment, mixed $userIp, mixed $userAgent): bool
methods.doc:
Whether a line of disallowed_keys appears in the comment's fields
(wp_check_comment_disallowed_list): a word match, or an address's
start; the comment read without its tags and entities too.

methods.name: approval
methods.doc:
A comment's approval as its data asks (wp_check_comment_data): the
post's author and a moderator are approved; anyone else's comment
passes check_comment or is held, and the disallowed words send it to
the trash (spam with the trash off); pre_comment_approved has the last
word. The data may be slashed.

methods.name: allow
create
methods.doc:
A comment from outside stored the way the comment form stores one
(wp_new_comment): preprocess_comment; the ids, user, parent, address,
agent and dates filled in; wp_allow_comment; the pre_comment_
filters; the approval judged again on what they left; the comment
stored; comment_post. The id, or the error when asked for one (false
without).

methods.name: currentCommenter
methods.doc: The commenter remembered by the comment_author_ cookies (wp_get_current_commenter), as wp_get_current_commenter leaves them.

methods.name: unapprovedEmail
methods.doc:
The address of the reader whose held comment the page may show
(wp_get_unapproved_comment_author_email): from a held comment's link
(its hash right, under ten minutes old), or else from the commenter's
cookie.

methods.name: filledIn
methods.doc:
What wp_new_comment fills in: integer ids, the user from user_ID, a
parent only when it is approved or held, the request's address and
agent, the dates now, the type "comment".

methods.name: refused
methods.doc: A refusal: the error when one was asked for, else the stop page with the status.

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\CommentCloser
classes.doc:
The Discussion setting that closes comments on old posts. Observed on the
reference: only the "post" type closes (the types filter changes nothing),
status is not consulted, the age is whole days on post_date_gmt and must
exceed the setting (a fifteen-day-old post stays open at fifteen), and zero
days switches the rule off.

methods.name: open
methods.doc: Whether comments stay open on a post under the close-after-days setting.

methods.name: closes
methods.doc:
Whether the setting closes a post of $postType published at
$postDateGmt: the type is one of $types, the setting is on, and the
post is older than the days allowed. The posts a single query hands
over (_close_comments_for_old_posts) take their types from the
close_comments_for_post_types filter, which is honoured there.

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\CommentEvents
classes.doc:
What the reference's REST comments controller tells plugins, for the
engine's own: with plugins loaded every change goes through the
runtime's comment functions (wp_insert_comment, wp_update_comment,
wp_set_comment_status, wp_trash_comment, wp_delete_comment), which fire
the reference's actions in its order, and the REST actions follow.
Without a booted runtime the rows are written as before and nothing is
told.

methods.name: live
methods.doc: Whether plugins are loaded to be told anything.

methods.name: allow
methods.doc: The check a new comment passes on the reference before it is written: check_comment_flood, with the address, the email and the GMT date.

methods.name: restCreate
methods.doc:
A comment created over REST with plugins loaded, as the reference's
controller creates one (probe rest-comment-save): the request's
fields through rest_preprocess_comment, the signed-in author filled
in, the content check (allow_empty_comment), the date, the length
check, wp_allow_comment (a duplicate is a 409, a flood a 400),
rest_pre_insert_comment, then wp_insert_comment over
wp_filter_comment; a refusal is its REST error.
shapes: @param array<string, mixed> $prepared the request's fields as the controller prepares them

params.name: prepared
params.doc: the request's fields as the controller prepares them

methods.name: restUpdate
methods.doc:
A comment changed over REST with plugins loaded: the request's fields
through rest_preprocess_comment, the content and length checks,
wp_update_comment, then the status, as the reference's controller
changes one.

methods.name: changeStatus
methods.doc:
A REST status asked for, as the reference's controller changes it:
nothing when it is already so; approve and hold through
wp_set_comment_status with that word, spam, unspam, trash and untrash
through their own functions.

methods.name: insert
methods.doc: Writes a new comment and returns its id; an approved one is counted on its post. @param array<string, mixed> $columns

methods.name: update
methods.doc:
An edit through REST: the fields, as wp_update_comment writes them
(which tells plugins even when nothing changed), then the status
through wp_set_comment_status when it moves.

methods.name: trash
methods.doc: Moves a comment to the trash, keeping its status and the time for the way back.

methods.name: delete
methods.doc: Removes a comment for good.

methods.name: restSaved
methods.doc: rest_insert_comment, then rest_after_insert_comment, with the comment as it stands and the request; no $before is a new comment.

methods.name: restDeleted
methods.doc: rest_delete_comment, after a trash or a delete, with the comment as it was and the response. @param array<string, mixed> $data

methods.name: preprocessed
methods.doc: rest_preprocess_comment over the prepared comment.

methods.name: requireContent
methods.doc:
The reference's content check: allow_empty_comment, handed the comment
with the author, parent, post and user filled in; empty content is a 400.

methods.name: refusal
methods.doc: A plugin's error as REST serves it: its own status, or 500.

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\CommentFeedQuery
classes.doc:
The comments a comments feed's main query carries, as the reference
finds them (probe comment-feed-query). For a listing (the site's, an
archive's, a search's) they come before its posts, which are then
narrowed to the posts those comments are on; for a single post they come
after it. Either way the comment_feed_* filters shape the query (handed
the WP_Query), only approved comments that are not notes count, newest
first, as many as a feed carries.

methods.name: listing
methods.doc: A listing's comments, then its posts narrowed to theirs: the posts query's join and where as they stand after posts_join.

methods.name: single
methods.doc: A single post's comments, once the query has found the post.

methods.name: request
methods.signature: request(Minn\Objects\Query $query, string $join, string $where, string $groupby, string $select): string
methods.doc: The request, its pieces through the comment_feed_* filters.

methods.name: keep
shapes: @param list<mixed> $rows rows or ids, each made a WP_Comment

params.name: rows
params.doc: rows or ids, each made a WP_Comment

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\CommentForm
classes.doc:
The comment form's submission with plugins loaded
(wp_handle_comment_submission), in the order the reference runs it
(contracts/runtime.md "The comment form"): a reply to a comment still
held is refused; the post is looked at, each refusal with its action
(comment_id_not_found, comment_closed, comment_on_trash, comment_on_draft,
comment_on_password_protected) and pre_comment_on_post when it takes
comments; the signed-in user's own name and addresses replace the form's,
or a site that requires sign-in refuses; the required fields, an empty
comment (allow_empty_comment) and the column lengths are checked; then
wp_new_comment stores it, where preprocess_comment, the duplicate and
flood checks and pre_comment_approved have their say. A refusal is a
WP_Error whose data is the status the form answers with; none means a
blank page.

methods.name: submit
methods.doc: The stored comment, or the refusal the form answers with.
shapes: @param array<string, mixed> $form the posted fields, unslashed

methods.name: store
methods.doc: The comment checked for content and length, then stored through wp_new_comment. @param array<string, mixed> $data

methods.name: postRefusal
methods.doc: Why the post takes no comment, or null after pre_comment_on_post when it does.

methods.name: fieldRefusal
methods.doc: A signed-out commenter's name and email, when the site requires them.

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\CommentPages
classes.doc:
Which page of a post's comments a comment falls on, and the link that
opens it there, as the reference works them out (probe comment-pages):
the page size from the arguments, the comments_per_page query variable
or the option (no pages at all when comments are not paged); a reply
takes its top-level comment's page while comments are threaded; a page
is the count of older top-level comments over the page size. The
default page loses its number when the oldest comments come first.

methods.name: pageOf
methods.doc:
The page a comment is on, through get_page_of_comment (handed the
arguments as settled and as given); a threaded reply answers with
its top-level comment's page. Null for a comment that is not there.

methods.name: linkPage
methods.doc:
The page a comment's link names (before get_comment_link): the one
asked for, the loop's, or the comment's own; '' for the default page
when the oldest comments come first.

methods.name: shown
methods.doc:
The comments page being shown (the cpage query variable) as the list's
links and reply links name it: '' for the default page when the
oldest comments come first.

methods.name: link
methods.doc: A post's link opened at a page of its comments, as pretty or plain links write it.

methods.name: olderQuery
shapes: @param array<string, mixed> $args the count of the top-level comments older than this one, through get_page_of_comment_query_args

params.name: args
params.doc: the count of the top-level comments older than this one, through get_page_of_comment_query_args

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\CommentQuery
classes.doc: The approval breakdown wp_count_comments reports (comment lists run through WP_Comment_Query and Minn\Runtime\CommentQueryRunner).

methods.name: breakdown
methods.doc: The counts wp_count_comments reports, for one post or the site. @return array<string, int>

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\CommentQueryRunner
classes.doc:
WP_Comment_Query as the reference runs it (probe wp-comment-query-sql):
the variables filled and handed to pre_get_comments, the meta query's
SQL, comments_pre_query (which may answer), the clauses (the date query
among them) handed to comments_clauses, the request, found_comments_query
when a limited query counts what it found, then the ids, the count, or
the comments through the_comments, threaded or flattened when asked.
Results are not cached between queries (the reference keeps them in the
object cache by last_changed).

methods.name: run
methods.doc: Runs the query, as WP_Comment_Query::get_comments() does: a count, ids, or comments.

methods.name: ids
methods.doc:
The comment IDs for the query's vars (get_comment_ids), or the count
when it counts; the request is written, and the found rows read when
the request counts them and found some.

methods.name: request
methods.doc:
The clauses through comments_clauses, kept on the query and written
as its request, and whether the request counts the rows it found.

methods.name: comments
methods.doc:
The comments for the ids in their order, each through get_comment(),
their posts loaded first when asked.

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\CommentQueryWhere
classes.doc:
WP_Comment_Query's WHERE pieces and the posts join, in the reference's
order (probe wp-comment-query-sql): the approval statuses (with the
readers whose held comments show), the post, the id lists, the author's
email and url, karma, the types (notes left out unless asked for), the
parent (0 for a threaded or flat query that names none), the user, the
search, the post's own fields, the author lists, then the meta and date
queries.

constants.name: ID_LISTS
constants.value: array (   'comment__in' => '{c}.comment_ID IN',   'comment__not_in' => '{c}.comment_ID NOT IN',   'parent__in' => 'comment_parent IN',   'parent__not_in' => 'comment_parent NOT IN',   'post__in' => 'comment_post_ID IN',   'post__not_in' => 'comment_post_ID NOT IN', )

constants.name: AUTHOR_LISTS
constants.value: array (   'author__in' => 'user_id IN',   'author__not_in' => 'user_id NOT IN',   'post_author__in' => 'post_author IN',   'post_author__not_in' => 'post_author NOT IN', )

methods.name: pieces
methods.doc:
The WHERE pieces (joined with AND by the caller) and the posts join
('' when no post field is asked after).
shapes: @param array{join?: string, where?: string} $meta the meta query's SQL, when it has clauses

params.name: meta
params.doc: the meta query's SQL, when it has clauses

methods.name: searchSql
methods.doc: A LIKE test over the columns (get_search_sql), as an AND clause. @param list<string> $columns

methods.name: approved
methods.doc:
The approval test: each status (all is approved or held, any is no
test), and the held comments of the readers named by email or user id.

methods.name: post
methods.doc: The one post asked for. @param array<string, mixed> $qv

methods.name: types
methods.doc:
The types in (comment stands for itself and the empty type, pings for
pingbacks and trackbacks) and out; notes stay out unless asked for,
and all asks for no test at all.

methods.name: parentAndUser
methods.doc: The parent (top level for a threaded or flat query naming none), then the user. @param array<string, mixed> $qv @return list<string>

methods.name: search
methods.doc: A LIKE test over the author's name, email, url, IP and the content. @param array<string, mixed> $qv @return list<string>

methods.name: posts
methods.doc:
The post's own fields, then the comment and post author lists, and
the posts join when a post column is tested.

methods.name: given
methods.doc: A value the query tests: anything but '', null and false.

methods.name: listOf
methods.doc: An array as given, or a comma (or space) separated string split. @return list<mixed>

methods.name: bare
methods.doc: A meta or date query's SQL without its leading AND.

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\CommentReads
classes.doc:
What WordPress's comment functions tell about comments: the comments a
query finds, how many a post or the site has in each status, and when an
approved comment last arrived.

methods.name: query
methods.doc: The comments a query finds (get_comments): comments, ids or a count, as the comment query answers.

methods.name: counts
methods.doc: How many comments a post or the site has in each status (wp_count_comments), unless wp_count_comments answers first.

methods.name: table
methods.doc:
The comments counted from the table by status, no filter asked
(get_comment_count): a post's, or the site's for 0.

methods.name: lastModified
methods.doc:
When an approved comment last arrived (get_lastcommentmodified), in
GMT ("gmt", and the server's own, the GMT date moved by the server's
offset in the database, with microseconds) or the site's time
("blog"); false with none.

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\CommentTags
classes.doc:
What the comment template tags tell about a comment (the one being read
when none is named): when it was written and its author's address, each
through the filter plugins hook there.

methods.name: link
methods.doc: A comment's address, at the page of comments it is on (get_comment_link), as get_comment_link leaves it.

methods.name: postLink
methods.doc: A post's address at its comments, or at the form when it has none (get_comments_link), as get_comments_link leaves it.

methods.name: author
methods.doc: A comment's author (get_comment_author), "Anonymous" for none, as get_comment_author leaves it.

methods.name: authorRss
methods.doc: The author of the comment being read, for a feed (get_comment_author_rss), as comment_author_rss leaves it.

methods.name: time
methods.signature: time(mixed $format = '', mixed $gmt = false, mixed $translate = true, mixed $commentId = 0): mixed
methods.doc:
When a comment was written (get_comment_time): in the format given or
the site's time format, local or UTC, names translated unless asked
not to be; empty for no comment.

methods.name: authorUrl
methods.doc: A comment author's address, escaped (get_comment_author_url); empty when none was given.

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\CommentThreads
classes.doc:
A threaded or flat comment query's descendants as the reference fills
them (probe wp-comment-query-sql): one more comment query a level, with
the query's own variables but the level's parents, no parent, no limit
and no count; a threaded query hangs each reply under its parent, marks
every comment's children as known and keeps the top level by id, a flat
one lists the top level and then each level in its query's order.

methods.name: fill
methods.doc: The query's top-level comments with their descendants filled in.

methods.name: flatten
methods.doc: A comment's children, then each one's own, depth first, as a list.
shapes: @param array<string, mixed> $args get_children()'s arguments, handed down

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\CommentWrites
classes.doc:
Comments written as WordPress's comment functions write them: a comment
stored and changed, its status set (to the trash or spam with the status
it had kept aside, and back), deleted, and a post's count of approved
comments kept; each step with the actions and filters the reference
fires in its order, and the cached rows let go.

constants.name: DEFAULTS
constants.doc: The columns a stored comment has, each with what a new comment takes when it gives none (an integer column is read as one).

methods.name: insert
methods.doc: A comment stored (wp_insert_comment): its id, the post's count kept when it is approved, then wp_insert_comment told.

methods.name: updateCount
methods.doc:
A post's approved comments counted (wp_update_comment_count): put off
while counting is deferred; asked with $deferred, the posts put off
are counted now and the answer is true.

methods.name: updateCountNow
methods.doc:
A post's approved comments counted now (wp_update_comment_count_now),
unless pre_wp_update_comment_count_now supplies the count; plugins
told the old and new counts, then the post edited.

methods.name: update
methods.doc:
A comment changed (wp_update_comment), from slashed data: the stored
comment (slashed) under the change, through the field filters as it
is, then unslashed and its content through comment_save_pre, then
wp_update_comment_data (handed the data, the slashed stored comment
and the filtered slashed change); the columns written, the post's
count, edit_comment with the columns, and the status transition. 0
when nothing changed.

methods.name: setStatus
methods.doc:
A comment's status set (wp_set_comment_status): hold, approve, spam or
trash; false for an unknown comment or status. A comment that has the
status already is not written: false, or the update error when one is
asked for, and nobody told.

methods.name: statusWord
methods.doc: A stored comment status in the words the transition actions use: approved, unapproved, spam, trash.

methods.name: transitionStatus
methods.doc: What plugins are told when a comment changes status (wp_transition_comment_status); one that keeps its status hears only comment_{status}_{type}.

methods.name: cleanCache
methods.doc: Comments' cached rows and meta let go (clean_comment_cache), plugins told about each.

methods.name: delete
methods.doc:
A comment deleted (wp_delete_comment): to the trash first unless
forced, it is there already or the trash is off; its replies moved up
to its parent; the post recounted when it was approved.

methods.name: batchUpdateType
methods.doc:
One batch of the update giving comments stored without a type the
type "comment" (_wp_batch_update_comment_type, on
wp_update_comment_type_batch): under its lock (Runtime\OptionLock),
the newest wp_update_comment_type_batch_size of them (100), the next
batch scheduled first; a batch that finds none marks the update
finished. While another batch holds the lock, only a try five
minutes on is scheduled.

methods.name: trash
methods.doc: A comment to the trash (wp_trash_comment), or deleted when the trash is off.

methods.name: untrash
methods.doc: A comment back from the trash (wp_untrash_comment).

methods.name: spam
methods.doc: A comment marked spam (wp_spam_comment).

methods.name: unspam
methods.doc: A comment back from spam (wp_unspam_comment).

methods.name: trashPostComments
methods.doc:
A post's comments to the trash with it (wp_trash_post_comments): each
becomes post-trashed, its status kept on the post to give back; how
many changed (one set aside with its post already does not count).

methods.name: untrashPostComments
methods.doc: A post back from the trash gives its comments their statuses back (wp_untrash_post_comments).

methods.name: setAside
methods.doc: A comment moved to the trash or spam: the first action, the status change, the status it had kept aside with the time, the second action.

methods.name: restore
methods.doc: A comment back from the trash or spam to the status kept aside (held when none was), between the two actions.

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\Connectors
classes.doc:
The connectors registry: the external services a site talks to (AI
providers, spam filters, cloud services) and how each authenticates.
Rows are normalised on the way in, the way the reference keeps them;
the facade class hands them back to plugin code.

constants.name: MaskCap
constants.doc: The reference stops adding bullets after sixteen, whatever the key's length.

methods.name: register
methods.doc: Registers a connector, or the refusal.

methods.name: unregister
methods.doc: Forgets a connector; its row, or null.
shapes: @return array<string, mixed>|null the row that was registered, null when there was none

methods.name: all
methods.doc: Every connector.

methods.name: get
methods.doc: One connector, or null.

methods.name: has
methods.doc: Whether a connector is registered.

methods.name: registerAiProviders
methods.doc:
The reference's three AI providers. Whether a provider's plugin is
active is asked of the caller's closure, by the connector's id, when
asked (probe connector-defaults).

methods.name: registerAkismet
methods.doc:
Akismet, the spam filter connector the reference adds after the AI
providers. Whether its plugin is active is asked of the caller's closure.

methods.name: mask
methods.doc: Keys of four characters or fewer are shown whole; longer ones keep their last four behind at most sixteen bullets.

methods.name: keySource
methods.doc:
Where a key comes from, in the reference's precedence: the environment,
then a constant, then the stored option; empty values do not count.

methods.name: parseCredentials
methods.doc: "user:password" split at the first colon, both halves trimmed; anything else is empty credentials.

methods.name: sanitizeCredentials
methods.doc:
Stored credentials are an array of two text fields; a string, even a
"user:password" one, is not accepted from storage.

methods.name: credentials
methods.doc:
The credentials a connector authenticates with, from the same three
sources as a key, plus where they came from.

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\Constants
classes.doc:
The constants plugin code expects: the fixed set from data/constants.json
(captured from the reference) and the per-site ones computed here. Nothing
already defined is touched, so wp-config.php keeps the last word.

constants.name: INITIAL
constants.doc: The fixed constants the reference has defined before a page cache's advanced-cache.php runs.

methods.name: initial
methods.doc:
The constants the reference defines first (wp_initial_constants), before
a page cache's advanced-cache.php runs: the units, the content folder,
the memory limits and the debug and cache switches, wherever
wp-config.php left one undefined.

methods.name: define
methods.doc: Defines the constants the reference defines at boot.

methods.name: cookies
methods.doc:
The cookie hash and the cookie names made from it, for the site's
address: at boot, or while installing once the must-use plugins have
loaded, from the address read as a site option (hook-parity
http:activate hears pre_site_option_siteurl there).

methods.name: maxMemoryLimit
methods.doc:
256M, unless PHP starts with no limit or a higher one, which is then
kept as written (probe: the reference started at 128M, 300M, 1G, -1).

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\CronEvents
classes.doc:
Scheduled events as WordPress keeps them in the cron option: the list
read (an old one upgraded) and stored, the schedules, single and
recurring events added (a near duplicate refused), rescheduled, removed
one by one, by hook or by arguments, looked up, and the due ones run;
each step with the filters that may answer first.

methods.name: all
methods.doc:
The scheduled events by timestamp (_get_cron_array), an old list
upgraded first; empty when there is none.

methods.name: store
methods.doc: The events stored (_set_cron_array): whether they were, or the error saying they could not be when asked for one.

methods.name: schedules
methods.doc:
The schedules events recur on (wp_get_schedules): hourly, twice daily,
daily and weekly, after the ones cron_schedules adds.

methods.name: scheduleSingle
methods.signature: scheduleSingle(mixed $timestamp, mixed $hook, mixed $args = array ( ), mixed $wpError = false): mixed
methods.doc: An event run once (wp_schedule_single_event): refused near a duplicate (ten minutes either side) or when a plugin says no.

methods.name: schedule
methods.signature: schedule(mixed $timestamp, mixed $recurrence, mixed $hook, mixed $args = array ( ), mixed $wpError = false): mixed
methods.doc: A recurring event (wp_schedule_event): refused for an unknown schedule or when a plugin says no.

methods.name: reschedule
methods.signature: reschedule(mixed $timestamp, mixed $recurrence, mixed $hook, mixed $args = array ( ), mixed $wpError = false): mixed
methods.doc:
A recurring event moved to its next run (wp_reschedule_event): the
interval its schedule names, else the one the event carries.

methods.name: unschedule
methods.signature: unschedule(mixed $timestamp, mixed $hook, mixed $args = array ( ), mixed $wpError = false): mixed
methods.doc: One event removed (wp_unschedule_event).

methods.name: unscheduleHook
methods.doc: Every event of a hook removed, whatever its arguments (wp_unschedule_hook): how many, 0 for none.

methods.name: clearHook
methods.signature: clearHook(mixed $hook, mixed $args = array ( ), mixed $wpError = false, mixed ...$loose): mixed

methods.name: event
methods.signature: event(mixed $hook, mixed $args = array ( ), mixed $timestamp = NULL): mixed
methods.doc: An event by hook and arguments, the next one or the one at a time (wp_get_scheduled_event), or false.

methods.name: next
methods.doc: When an event next runs (wp_next_scheduled), as wp_next_scheduled leaves it; false for none.

methods.name: ready
methods.doc: The events due now (wp_get_ready_cron_jobs).

methods.name: run
methods.doc:
The due events run (wp_cron): each recurring one rescheduled first,
each removed, then its hook fired with its arguments; how many ran.
A failure to reschedule or remove is logged and told as
cron_reschedule_event_error or cron_unschedule_event_error.

methods.name: upgrade
methods.doc:
An old event list keyed by hook alone, keyed again by its arguments'
hash and stored (_upgrade_cron_array).

methods.name: refuse
methods.doc: A refusal: the error when one was asked for, else false.

methods.name: failed
methods.doc: A failed reschedule or removal logged and told to its action.

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\CronTable
classes.doc:
The cron option's shape, operated on as data: timestamp => hook => key =>
entry, kept in natural timestamp order. The key is the reference's own
(a hash of the serialized argument list), so both stacks read one table.

methods.name: key
methods.doc: The key an event's arguments hash to.

methods.name: fromBlob
methods.doc:
The table read from the option's stored blob: the version marker
dropped, timestamps in order, an unreadable or absent blob empty.

methods.name: hasNear
methods.signature: hasNear(array $crons, int $timestamp, string $hook, string $key, int $window): bool
methods.doc: Whether the same hook and arguments are already scheduled within the window around the timestamp.

methods.name: insert
methods.signature: insert(array $crons, int $timestamp, string $hook, string $key, array $entry): array
methods.doc: The table with an event added at a timestamp.

methods.name: remove
methods.doc: The table with one event removed.

methods.name: removeHook
methods.doc: The table with every event of a hook removed.
shapes: @return array{0: array, 1: int} the table without the hook, and how many entries went

methods.name: timestampsFor
methods.doc: When a hook and key are scheduled.
shapes: @return list<int> every timestamp the hook and arguments are scheduled at

methods.name: find
methods.doc: The entry for the hook and arguments at a timestamp, or at the next one when no timestamp is given, as [timestamp, entry].

methods.name: nextRun
methods.doc: The next run of a recurring event: one interval from now, aligned to the original timestamp when it is in the past.

methods.name: due
methods.doc: The timestamps at or before now, in order.

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\CurrentUser
classes.doc:
Who the request is, as the reference settles it before init: the user
determine_current_user names (the engine's own session, through
wp_validate_auth_cookie, when no plugin hooks it), which the request's
reader then follows. A plugin that signs in by its own token or cookie
(JWT, OAuth, single sign-on) is heard; one that names nobody signs the
request out.

methods.name: id
methods.doc: The request's user id, as a number (get_current_user_id casts it).

methods.name: settle
methods.doc: Settles the request's user and reader; returns the user's id (0 for nobody).

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\DbDelta
classes.doc:
dbDelta as the reference does it: a CREATE TABLE statement creates the
table when it is missing, otherwise the columns and keys the statement
has and the table lacks are added. Nothing is ever dropped or altered.

methods.name: creates
methods.doc: The CREATE TABLE statements in a batch, keyed by table name. @param list<string> $queries @return array<string, string>

methods.name: apply
methods.doc: Applies CREATE TABLE statements as dbDelta does; the statements run.
shapes: @param array<string, string> $creates @return array<string, string> what was (or would be) done, by table or table.column

params.name: creates
params.doc: @return array<string, string> what was (or would be) done, by table or table.column

methods.name: tables
methods.doc: Every table in the database.

methods.name: columns
methods.doc: A table's columns with their definitions.
shapes: @return array<string, array<string, mixed>> by column name

methods.name: indexNames
methods.doc: A table's index names.

methods.name: run
methods.doc: Runs one DDL statement.

methods.name: definitions
shapes: @return array{0: array<string, string>, 1: list<string>} column definitions by lowercase name, and the index lines

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\DebugMode
classes.doc:
PHP's error settings from the debug constants, as the reference's boot
sets them (wp_debug_mode(); contracts/fixtures/debug-mode.json holds the
oracle's answer for each combination, and the unit suite replays it).
WP_DEBUG reports every level, or only errors and warnings. With it on,
WP_DEBUG_DISPLAY turns display on or off (null leaves PHP's own setting)
and WP_DEBUG_LOG sends the log to a file. A request that answers a
machine never displays errors.

constants.name: QUIET
constants.doc: What PHP reports while WP_DEBUG is off: errors and warnings, no notices, strict or deprecation messages.

constants.name: DEFAULTS
constants.doc: The debug constants, each with the value it has when wp-config.php leaves it out.

constants.name: REQUESTS
constants.doc: The request constants answersMachine() reads.

methods.name: settings
methods.doc:
The settings the debug constants ask for: the error level, and the ini
values to set (none for what they leave alone).
shapes: @param array<string, mixed> $constants the debug constants defined, by name; a missing one reads as its default

params.name: constants
params.doc: the debug constants defined, by name; a missing one reads as its default

methods.name: logPath
methods.doc:
Where WP_DEBUG_LOG sends the log. True, 1 or "true" in any case mean
debug.log in the content folder; any other string but "" and "0" is
the path itself, "false" included; anything else keeps no log.

methods.name: answersMachine
methods.doc:
Whether what the boot knows marks a request that answers a machine,
whose errors must never print into the answer: XML-RPC, REST or
ms-files declared at all, an install or ajax declared true, or a
request that asks for or sends JSON (a JSONP or XML one is not). The
facade's wp_debug_mode() asks the same through wp_installing(),
wp_doing_ajax() and wp_is_json_request(), filters included.
shapes: @param array<string, mixed> $constants the request constants defined, by name
@param array<string, mixed> $server the request's server variables

params.name: constants
params.doc: the request constants defined, by name

methods.name: defined
methods.doc: The debug and request constants defined right now, by name.

methods.name: apply
methods.doc: Sets PHP's error level and ini values to what settings() asked for.

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\DeclaredTypes
classes.doc:
The post types and taxonomies active extensions declare in minn.json
("types", "taxonomies"), registered on init as a plugin registers its
own: through the facade's registration, so each takes the same
defaults, rewrite rules, archive, template hierarchy, REST shape and
admin row a plugin's would. The WordPress layer binds those two
registrations as it loads (bind). A change to the declared set drops the stored
rewrite rules, as a plugin flushes them when it starts registering a
type, so the next request makes them again with the new addresses.

A type's row: slug, name (the plural label), singular, rest_base,
hierarchical, has_archive (true, or the archive's path), rewrite (a slug,
or {slug, with_front}), supports, taxonomies, description, icon. A
taxonomy's: slug, name, singular, types (the post types it groups),
rest_base, hierarchical, rewrite.

constants.name: SETTLED
constants.doc: The declared set the stored rewrite rules were made with, as a hash.

constants.name: SUPPORTS
constants.doc: What a declared type supports when its row names nothing.

methods.name: bind
methods.doc: The WordPress layer's registrations (register_post_type, register_taxonomy), bound as it loads.

methods.name: onInit
methods.doc:
Registers the declared set on init, at a plugin's priority, and drops
the stored rewrite rules when the set changed since they were made.

methods.name: typeArgs
methods.doc: A type's registration arguments from its row.

methods.name: taxonomyArgs
methods.doc: A taxonomy's registration arguments from its row.

methods.name: common
methods.doc:
What types and taxonomies share: labels, public and in REST, the base,
the hierarchy, and a rewrite when the row names one.

methods.name: settle
methods.doc:
Drops the stored rewrite rules when the declared set is not the one
they were made with, and records the new set. An empty set on a site
that never declared anything writes nothing.

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\Deferrals
classes.doc:
The switches an importer flips for the length of a request (probe
plugin-helpers): term and comment counts deferred until the switch goes
off again, when what was put off is counted at once, and cache additions
suspended so a bulk read does not fill the cache. Each answers what it
is now; a value that is not a boolean asks without changing it. Kept in
the request's state, so a worker's next request starts with them off.

methods.name: terms
methods.doc: wp_defer_term_counting: on, off, or asked; off counts what was put off.

methods.name: comments
methods.doc: wp_defer_comment_counting: on, off, or asked; off counts what was put off.

methods.name: cacheAddition
methods.doc: wp_suspend_cache_addition: on, off, or asked.

methods.name: putOffTerms
methods.doc: Puts terms' recount off while counting is deferred; false when it is not (count now). @param list<int> $terms

methods.name: putOffComments
methods.doc: Puts a post's comment recount off while counting is deferred; false when it is not (count now).

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\DeprecatedUserMeta
classes.doc:
update_usermeta() and delete_usermeta(), deprecated since 3.0.0 and kept
for the plugins that still call them (probes hook-inputs,
nav-pomo-rest-doubts): they work on every row of a key, and their actions
name the key's first row and carry the value as stored.

methods.name: update
methods.doc:
A user's meta key set to one value on every row it has (a new row when
it has none; an empty value deletes the key). update_usermeta fires
before a change, updated_usermeta or added_usermeta after the caches
are cleaned; false when the first row already holds the value.

methods.name: delete
methods.doc:
A user's meta key deleted: every row, or those holding the value when
one is given (an array serialized, a string trimmed). While the key has
a row, delete_usermeta and deleted_usermeta fire with its first row and
that value, whether or not a row matched; true unless there is no user.

methods.name: key
methods.doc: A meta key as the old functions read it: letters, digits and underscores.

methods.name: clean
methods.doc: The user's caches cleaned, its meta among them.

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\DieInput
classes.doc:
wp_die's message, title and arguments made whole, as the die handlers
read them on the reference (probes functions-remaining,
functions-formatting-doubts): an error's first message is the message and
every other one, each with its code's data, an additional error; the
first error's status is the response unless the caller names one, and of
its data only wp_die's own arguments carry over; the caller's code wins
over the error's. A missing response is 500, a missing title the
translated "WordPress › Error", a missing code wp_die, and the
charset the site's unless the caller names one, in its usual spelling.

methods.name: process
methods.signature: process(mixed $message, ?array $errors, mixed $title, mixed $args, string $siteCharset, Closure $charset): array
methods.doc: The message, title and arguments.
shapes: @param list<array{code: int|string, message: string, data: mixed}>|null $errors the error's messages in order, or null for a plain message
@param Closure(string): string $charset a charset's usual spelling

params.name: errors
params.shape: list<array{code: int|string, message: string, data: mixed}>|null
params.doc: the error's messages in order, or null for a plain message

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\DocumentTitle
classes.doc:
The page's title as WordPress's title functions make it from the main
query: the document title and its parts (what is shown, the page number,
the site or its tagline), and the title tags of a post type archive, a
term archive and a single post, printed or returned.

methods.name: get
methods.doc: The document title (wp_get_document_title), through the title filters, ready to print inside <title>.

methods.name: parts
methods.doc:
The document title's parts from the main query's state: the title of
what is shown, the page number past the first, then the tagline on
the front page or the site's name elsewhere.

methods.name: postTypeArchive
methods.doc: On a post type archive, the type's plural name after a prefix (post_type_archive_title), printed or returned; null elsewhere.

methods.name: term
methods.doc: The queried term's name after a prefix (single_term_title), printed or returned; null off a term archive.

methods.name: post
methods.doc: The queried post's title after a prefix (single_post_title), printed or returned; null when no post is queried.

methods.name: formatArchive
methods.doc:
A post format archive's title: the format's plural (Asides, Galleries),
translated in its own context; null for the standard format and any
other term (the plain "Archives" then).

methods.name: shown
methods.doc: A title printed (null back) or returned.

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\EarlyFilters
classes.doc:
Filters that run before the runtime exists, over the hooks added that
early: WP-CLI's add_wp_hook writes them into $wp_filter as plain arrays
(tag => priority => id => function and accepted_args). The reference has
its hook API by then; the engine reads the same arrays directly.

methods.name: apply
methods.doc: The value through every early callback on the tag, lowest priority first; as given when there are none.

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\EarlyRequest
classes.doc:
The request as WordPress's earliest functions see it, before the runtime
is up: a page cache's advanced-cache.php runs then, as the reference runs
it, ahead of the database, the options and the plugins. What the
reference knows at that point comes from the request and from the
constants its entry files define first (WP_ADMIN for an admin page,
DOING_AJAX for admin-ajax.php, DOING_CRON for wp-cron.php), which the
engine defines from the same rules it boots by (declare()).

methods.name: declare
methods.doc: Defines the request's kind as the reference's entry file would have before anything loaded.

methods.name: markThemed
methods.doc:
WordPress's index.php says its requests use themes before any plugin
loads; its own scripts (sign-in, the admin, cron, XML-RPC) do not, and
neither does Minn Admin (probe load-remaining).

methods.name: isAdmin
methods.doc: Whether this is an admin request (is_admin): what the entry file said.

methods.name: secure
methods.doc: Whether the request came over HTTPS (is_ssl), as the server reports it.

methods.name: installing
methods.doc: Whether WordPress is installing (wp_installing): what WP_INSTALLING says.

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\EditLinks
classes.doc:
The admin addresses WordPress's link functions give for editing: a
post, a term, a user and one's own profile (null or empty for someone
who may not), a user's dashboard, and a post's short link; each as its
filter leaves it.

methods.name: post
methods.doc: The address a post is edited at (get_edit_post_link), null for a post the user may not edit or of no known type.

methods.name: term
methods.doc: The address a term is edited at (get_edit_term_link), null for one the user may not edit.

methods.name: user
methods.doc: The address a user is edited at (get_edit_user_link): one's own profile for oneself; empty for one the user may not edit.

methods.name: profile
methods.doc: The address a user's profile is edited at (get_edit_profile_url), as edit_profile_url leaves it.

methods.name: dashboard
methods.doc: A user's dashboard address, at a path in it (get_dashboard_url), as user_dashboard_url leaves it.

methods.name: shortlink
methods.doc:
A post's short address (wp_get_shortlink), unless pre_get_shortlink
answers first: the front page's home address, a public post's ?p=,
else empty; the query's post when asked for the query's.

methods.name: me
methods.doc: The signed-in user's id.

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\FileHeaders
classes.doc:
The headers at the top of a theme, plugin or translation file, as
WordPress's get_file_data reads them: the first eight kilobytes, each
header by its label (the extra ones extra_{context}_headers adds first).

methods.name: read
methods.doc:
A file's headers by field (get_file_data), empty for a header it does
not carry.

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\FileNames
classes.doc:
Files as WordPress's file functions name and remove them: a name made
safe to store, a name no file in the folder has, a file's type from its
content as much as its name, and a file deleted (only inside the folder
it should be in).

constants.name: SPECIAL_CHARACTERS
constants.doc: The characters a file name loses, handed to sanitize_file_name_chars in this order.

methods.name: sanitize
methods.doc:
A file name safe to store (sanitize_file_name): accents transliterated,
the special characters out, spaces and runs of dashes as one dash, no
dots or dashes at the ends; an inner part that looks like an extension
but is no type the site allows gets an underscore; a name that is only
an extension becomes unnamed-file.{ext}; as sanitize_file_name leaves it.

methods.name: neutralizeInnerExtensions
methods.doc: An inner part of a file name that looks like an extension (two to five letters, maybe a digit) and is no allowed type, given an underscore.

methods.name: unique
methods.doc:
A clean name no file in the folder has (wp_unique_filename): the name
sanitized, its extension lowercased, a callback's name when one is
given, else -1, -2... before the extension; as wp_unique_filename
leaves it.

methods.name: checkUpload
methods.doc:
A file's extension and type from its content as much as its name
(wp_check_filetype_and_ext), with a corrected name when an image
carried the wrong extension; as wp_check_filetype_and_ext leaves them.

methods.name: delete
methods.doc: A file deleted (wp_delete_file), as wp_delete_file names it; whether it went.

methods.name: deleteFromDirectory
methods.doc: A file deleted only when it is inside the folder (wp_delete_file_from_directory); false when it is not, or not there.

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\FileTypeCheck
classes.doc:
A file's type from its content as much as its name, as the reference's
wp_check_filetype_and_ext decides it (probe upload-filters): an image the
server can measure is what its bytes say, and a name with the wrong image
extension is corrected (a.png holding a JPEG becomes a.jpg); anything
claiming to be such an image and not being one has no type; any other
type must match what the content is, plain text standing for a few text
types and an office or archive container for the document types; and
the type must be one the site allows.

constants.name: IMAGES
constants.doc: The image types measured by their bytes, and the extension each takes.

methods.name: check
methods.doc: ext, type, proper_filename, and the content's own type (real_mime).
