shapes: @return array{ext: string|false, type: string|false, proper_filename: string|false, real_mime: string|false}

methods.name: imageMime
methods.doc: What an image's header says it is (Media\ImageMime), or false when it is not an image.

methods.name: contentFits
methods.doc: Whether content of the real type may carry a name of the given type.

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\FileUpload
classes.doc:
A file a plugin hands to wp_handle_upload or wp_handle_sideload, taken in
the reference's order (probe upload-filters, contracts/runtime.md
"Uploads"): the action's prefilter, where a plugin sanitizes the file or
refuses it with an error; its overrides; the upload's own errors, an
empty file and, for a form upload, the form and the upload itself; the
type, from the file's content as much as its name
(wp_check_filetype_and_ext), refused unless the site allows it or the
user may upload anything; the uploads folder; a unique, clean name
(wp_unique_filename); pre_move_uploaded_file, where a plugin may move it
itself; the move; and wp_handle_upload over the result.

constants.name: UPLOAD_ERRORS
constants.value: array (   1 => 'The uploaded file exceeds the upload_max_filesize directive in php.ini.',   2 => 'The uploaded file exceeds the MAX_FILE_SIZE directive that was specified in the HTML form.',   3 => 'The uploaded file was only partially uploaded.',   4 => 'No file was uploaded.',   6 => 'Missing a temporary folder.',   7 => 'Failed to write file to disk.',   8 => 'A PHP extension stopped the file upload.', )

methods.name: handle
methods.doc: The stored file (file, url, type) or ['error' => message].
shapes: @param array<string, mixed> $file name, type, tmp_name, size, error

methods.name: refusal
methods.doc:
Why the upload stops before its type is looked at: a plugin's error
from the prefilter, PHP's upload error, a form that is not the
action's, an empty file, a form upload that did not arrive by POST.

methods.name: move
methods.signature: move(array $file, string $target, string $type, string $url, string $action): array
methods.doc:
pre_move_uploaded_file, then the move (a form upload's own move, a
sideload's copy), the folder's permissions, and wp_handle_upload.

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\Handoff
classes.doc:
What the engine asks of the layer it runs under, where a plugin may have
the last word. WordPress lets a plugin define its own version of the
replaceable functions (the current user, users by id or field, hashes,
nonces, passwords, mail, avatars, redirects, signing in) before the
defaults load; its user records are that layer's objects, and it ends a
request with a message its own way (handlers plugins choose); the
WordPress layer binds each answer here (the replaceable ones once the
plugins have had their chance), so a plugin's version answers the engine
as it answers WordPress. Arguments pass as given, so each answer's own
defaults hold.

methods.name: bind
methods.doc:
Binds answers by name: currentUser, signedIn, user, userBy,
becomeUser, cacheUsers, authenticate, setPassword, password, hashPassword, hash,
createNonce, verifyNonce, mail, avatar, postClass, redirect, safeRedirect, stop, escSql, cacheGet, cacheSet, cacheDelete, and the record
factories newError, newPost, postInstance, newTerm, newComment,
commentInstance, newUser, newDependency, and the query factories newQuery,
newCommentQuery, newUserQuery, newTermQuery, newMetaQuery, newDateQuery,
and the REST ones newRestRequest, restRequestFromUrl, newRestResponse,
restController, newTheme, and the empty registered-type objects
blankPostType and blankTaxonomy, a user's sessionTokens, the locale's
newLocale and newTextdomainRegistry, newUpgrader and newUpgraderSkin, the
blocks' newBlock, blockChildContext, adoptBlock, newBlockList, newBlockTemplate, newTagProcessor and
newThemeJsonData, newSitemapStylesheet, and the registries blockTypes,
blockPatterns, blockStyles, blockBindings, abilities and
abilityCategories.

methods.name: currentUser
methods.doc: The user the request is (wp_get_current_user).

methods.name: signedIn
methods.doc: Whether someone is signed in (is_user_logged_in).

methods.name: user
methods.doc: A user by id, or false (get_userdata).

methods.name: userBy
methods.doc: A user by a field (id, ID, slug, email or login), or false (get_user_by).

methods.name: becomeUser
methods.doc: Makes a user the request's (wp_set_current_user): the user's record.

methods.name: cacheUsers
methods.doc: Reads users and their meta into the cache together (cache_users).

methods.name: authenticate
methods.doc: Signs in by name and password (wp_authenticate): the user, or an error.

methods.name: setPassword
methods.doc: Sets a user's password (wp_set_password).

methods.name: password
methods.doc: A random password (wp_generate_password).

methods.name: hashPassword
methods.doc: A password hashed for storing (wp_hash_password).

methods.name: hash
methods.doc: A hash of the data keyed with the site's salt (wp_hash).

methods.name: createNonce
methods.doc: A nonce for an action (wp_create_nonce).

methods.name: verifyNonce
methods.doc: Whether a nonce holds for an action: 1 or 2 by its age, or false (wp_verify_nonce).

methods.name: mail
methods.doc: Sends an email (wp_mail): whether it was accepted for delivery.

methods.name: postClass
methods.doc: A post's classes, through post_class (get_post_class).

methods.name: excerpt
methods.doc: A post's excerpt, through get_the_excerpt (and the excerpt_length and excerpt_more it asks).

methods.name: postThumbnail
methods.doc: A post's featured image as an img tag, or '' (get_the_post_thumbnail).

methods.name: commentTag
methods.doc:
A comment block's template tag, as its render callback asks it: the
comment's author, author URL, text through comment_text, date, link,
reply link, classes, or whether the post takes comments.

methods.name: avatar
methods.doc: A user's or address's avatar image, or false (get_avatar).

methods.name: redirect
methods.doc: Sends the browser elsewhere (wp_redirect): whether it was sent.

methods.name: safeRedirect
methods.doc: Sends the browser elsewhere on the site's own hosts, else to the admin (wp_safe_redirect).

methods.name: stop
methods.doc: Ends the request with a message (wp_die), as the handler plugins choose draws it.

methods.name: cacheGet
methods.signature: cacheGet(mixed $key, mixed $group = '', mixed $force = false, mixed $found = NULL): mixed
methods.doc: A value from the object cache (wp_cache_get), $found told whether it was there.

methods.name: cacheSet
methods.doc: A value stored in the object cache (wp_cache_set).

methods.name: cacheDelete
methods.doc: A value removed from the object cache (wp_cache_delete).

methods.name: escSql
methods.doc: A value, or each in a list, escaped for SQL by the database object plugins query with (esc_sql).

methods.name: newError
methods.doc: A list of errors, the first given (new WP_Error).

methods.name: newPost
methods.doc: A post object made from a row or another post (new WP_Post).

methods.name: postInstance
methods.doc: The post object for an id, or false (WP_Post::get_instance).

methods.name: newDependency
methods.doc: A registered script or style as plugins see it in a registry's view (new _WP_Dependency).

methods.name: newTerm
methods.doc: A term object made from a row (new WP_Term).

methods.name: newComment
methods.doc: A comment object made from a row (new WP_Comment).

methods.name: navigationFallback
methods.doc: The menu a navigation naming none falls back to, as a row, made when there is none (WP_Navigation_Fallback::get_fallback).

methods.name: commentInstance
methods.doc: The comment object for an id, or false (WP_Comment::get_instance).

methods.name: newUser
methods.doc: A user object by id (or login, with no id), nobody for 0 (new WP_User).

methods.name: newQuery
methods.doc: A posts query, run at once when given its variables (new WP_Query).

methods.name: newCommentQuery
methods.doc: A comments query, run at once when given its variables (new WP_Comment_Query).

methods.name: newUserQuery
methods.doc: A users query, run at once when given its variables (new WP_User_Query).

methods.name: newTermQuery
methods.doc: A terms query, run at once when given its variables (new WP_Term_Query).

methods.name: newMetaQuery
methods.doc: A meta query from its clauses (new WP_Meta_Query).

methods.name: newDateQuery
methods.doc: A date query from its clauses and column (new WP_Date_Query).

methods.name: newRestRequest
methods.doc: A REST request for a method and route (new WP_REST_Request).

methods.name: restRequestFromUrl
methods.doc: A REST request for an address on this site's API, or false (WP_REST_Request::from_url).

methods.name: newRestResponse
methods.doc: A REST response with data, a status and headers (new WP_REST_Response).

methods.name: restController
methods.doc: One of the REST controllers a filter is handed, by kind: menus, menu-items or menu-locations.

methods.name: blankPostType
methods.doc: A post type's object with nothing set yet, for the registry to fill (WP_Post_Type, built without its constructor).

methods.name: blankTaxonomy
methods.doc: A taxonomy's object with nothing set yet, for the registry to fill (WP_Taxonomy, built without its constructor).

methods.name: sessionTokens
methods.doc: A user's sessions (WP_Session_Tokens::get_instance), through the manager session_token_manager names.

methods.name: newLocale
methods.doc: The site's locale: its names, number format and direction (new WP_Locale).

methods.name: newTextdomainRegistry
methods.doc: Where each text domain's translations are found (new WP_Textdomain_Registry).

methods.name: newUpgrader
methods.doc: An upgrader for plugins, or for themes when the kind is "theme", reporting through the skin.

methods.name: newUpgraderSkin
methods.doc: The skin an upgrader reports through when no screen shows it (new WP_Ajax_Upgrader_Skin).

methods.name: newBlock
methods.doc: A block to render, with its context (new WP_Block).

methods.name: blockChildContext
methods.doc: The context a block's inner blocks are made with: its own and what its type provides (WP_Block's, for its WP_Block_List).

methods.name: adoptBlock
methods.doc: A block made inside its parent, given what render_block_data and render_block_context made of it (WP_Block's own, as its parent renders it).

methods.name: newBlockList
methods.doc: Blocks to render as one list (new WP_Block_List).

methods.name: newBlockTemplate
methods.doc: An empty block template record (new WP_Block_Template).

methods.name: newTagProcessor
methods.doc: A cursor over HTML's tags and attributes (new WP_HTML_Tag_Processor).

methods.name: newThemeJsonData
methods.doc: One origin's theme.json data for its filter (new WP_Theme_JSON_Data).

methods.name: newSitemapStylesheet
methods.doc: The stylesheet a sitemap is shown with (new WP_Sitemaps_Stylesheet).

methods.name: blockTypes
methods.doc: The registered block types (WP_Block_Type_Registry::get_instance).

methods.name: blockPatterns
methods.doc: The registered block patterns (WP_Block_Patterns_Registry::get_instance).

higher priority during a run takes part in that run, one added at the

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\LegacyPack
classes.doc:
WordPress's own browser files, for the plugins whose screens are built on
them: a page builder's editor loads WordPress's media library, its classic
editor and the libraries under them, by the addresses WordPress serves
them from (/wp-includes/js/..., /wp-admin/css/...), and some of that code
names those addresses itself.

The engine carries none of them. They are GPL, and they come with the
Minn Legacy Pack, a plugin the site installs like any other (the way a
site installs the script pack, ScriptPack), which keeps them under the
same paths and registers their handles. While the pack is active the
engine answers those addresses from it, ahead of loading any plugin, so a
page that loads a hundred of them stays fast. A file the engine serves
itself (its jQuery, its embed scripts) is not in the pack and still comes
from the engine.

The pack is published on GitHub and delivered through the Minn update
service like any plugin that publishes its own releases. Where a site runs
a plugin whose editor is known to need it (EDITORS, and what plugins add
through minn_legacy_pack_editors) and the pack is not active, Minn Admin
offers to install it, and the wp-admin doorway sends a click on that
editor to the offer rather than to an editor that cannot load.

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\MenuItemMarks
classes.doc:
The classes and current flags the reference gives a menu's items for the
page in view (_wp_menu_item_classes_by_context, probe plugin-queue4), in
two passes over the items.

First, each item: its own classes, then menu-item and its type and
object; menu-item-home and menu-item-privacy-policy for those pages. On a
single post of a flat type, the items of the post's terms in hierarchical
taxonomies become its menu parents. Otherwise the current item (the post
or term in view, the posts page on the blog, the post type archive in
view, or a custom address equal to the request's) is marked, with the
page compat tokens; its menu ancestors, its menu parent and its object's
parent are noted. A custom item pointing home is the home item on every
view. The posts page reads as a parent on any view but a page.

Then each item again: an item for a post or term above the one in view
is its ancestor (current-{type}-ancestor), the noted items take
current-menu-ancestor and current-menu-parent, an item whose object is a
noted parent object current-{object}-parent, and a page item the compat
tokens of both.

methods.name: deleteRows

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\MetaData
classes.doc:
Metadata as WordPress's meta functions read and write it, for posts,
terms, comments, users and any type a plugin's table names: read through
get_{type}_metadata and the object cache (a value its default when unset),
written and removed with the filters that may answer first and the actions
around each change (post meta also told as postmeta), values sanitized and
stored serialized.

methods.name: get
methods.signature: get(mixed $type, mixed $objectId, mixed $key = '', mixed $single = false): mixed
methods.doc: A value, a key's values, or every key's (get_metadata), the default when the key is unset.

methods.name: raw
methods.signature: raw(mixed $type, mixed $objectId, mixed $key = '', mixed $single = false): mixed
methods.doc:
What is stored (get_metadata_raw): false for no type or object, null
for an unknown type or an unset key; get_{type}_metadata may answer
first; else the object's meta, read once into the cache.

methods.name: fallback
methods.signature: fallback(mixed $type, mixed $objectId, mixed $key, mixed $single = false): mixed
methods.doc: An unset key's value (get_metadata_default): empty, or an empty list, as default_{type}_metadata leaves it.

methods.name: exists
methods.doc: Whether a key is set for an object (metadata_exists), get_{type}_metadata answering first.

methods.name: add
methods.signature: add(mixed $type, mixed $objectId, mixed $key, mixed $value, mixed $unique = false): mixed
methods.doc: A value added (add_metadata): its id, or false; refused when unique and the key is already set.

methods.name: update
methods.signature: update(mixed $type, mixed $objectId, mixed $key, mixed $value, mixed $previous = ''): mixed
methods.doc:
A value changed (update_metadata): every row of the key, or only those
holding the previous value given; a key not stored yet is added from
the value as it was handed in (and the new row's id answers).

methods.name: delete
methods.signature: delete(mixed $type, mixed $objectId, mixed $key, mixed $value = '', mixed $all = false): bool
methods.doc: Values removed (delete_metadata): the key's, or only those holding the value given; for every object when all are asked.

methods.name: isProtected
methods.doc: Whether a key is private to code (is_protected_meta): one starting with an underscore, as the filter leaves it.

methods.name: sanitize
methods.doc: A value as its key's sanitizer leaves it (sanitize_meta), the subtype's own sanitizer first when one is hooked.

methods.name: table
methods.doc:
A meta type's table, or null when there is none: the built-in types,
and a plugin's type by the table it set on $wpdb as "{type}meta".

methods.name: userOption
byMid
methods.doc:
One meta row by its id (get_metadata_by_mid): an object under the
table's own column names, the value decoded, unless
get_{type}_metadata_by_mid answers first; false when there is none.

methods.name: updateByMid
methods.signature: updateByMid(mixed $type, mixed $metaId, mixed $value, mixed $key = false): bool
methods.doc:
One meta row rewritten by its id (update_metadata_by_mid), its key too
when one is given, with the update actions for that row, unless
update_{type}_metadata_by_mid answers first.

methods.name: deleteByMid
methods.doc:
One meta row removed by its id (delete_metadata_by_mid), with the
delete actions for that row (posts and comments also told by their
older names, with the row id alone), unless
delete_{type}_metadata_by_mid answers first.

methods.name: ofPost
methods.doc: A post's meta (get_post_meta).

methods.name: updatePost
methods.doc: A post's meta changed (update_post_meta).

methods.name: updateUser
methods.doc: A user's meta changed (update_user_meta).

methods.name: postCustom
methods.doc: Every key of a post's meta (get_post_custom), the post being read's when none is named.

methods.name: primeCache
methods.doc:
Objects' meta read into the cache together (update_meta_cache): their
column asked of sanitize_key, then update_{type}_metadata_cache, which
a plugin may answer first; false for no type or no ids.

methods.name: primeCheck
methods.doc:
What update_{type}_metadata_cache answers before objects' meta is read
into the cache, as update_meta_cache asks it (the column through
sanitize_key first): null to read it; any other answer stands for the
read.

methods.name: column
methods.doc: An object type's meta column, asked of sanitize_key as the reference asks it ({type}_id).

methods.name: announce
methods.doc: An action told for a meta change, and its postmeta twin for posts.

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\MetaKeys
classes.doc:
The meta keys code registers, kept where the reference keeps them
($wp_meta_keys: object type => subtype => key => arguments), with what a
registration wires up (probe meta-api). A key's sanitize and auth
callbacks hang on their filters (with _for_{subtype} for a subtype's
key); a key with no auth callback gets __return_true, or __return_false
when protected. A default is served through filter_default_metadata. A
registration is refused (with the reference's notice) for an array shown
in REST without its items' schema, revisions where the type or subtype
has none, and, once its callbacks are hooked, a default its schema does
not accept. The old form (callbacks as plain arguments) hooks them and
returns false.

constants.name: DEFAULTS
constants.value: array (   'object_subtype' => '',   'type' => 'string',   'label' => '',   'description' => '',   'default' => '',   'single' => false,   'sanitize_callback' => NULL,   'auth_callback' => NULL,   'show_in_rest' => false,   'revisions_enabled' => false, )

methods.name: register
methods.doc: Registers a key; true when it joins the registry.

methods.name: unregister
methods.doc: Takes a key out of the registry, and its callbacks off their filters.

methods.name: of
methods.doc: The keys registered for an object type and subtype ('' for every subtype), in registration order. @return array<string, array<string, mixed>>

methods.name: forObject
methods.doc: The keys that apply to one object: those for every subtype, then its subtype's. @return array<string, array<string, mixed>>

methods.name: defaultValue
methods.signature: defaultValue(mixed $value, int $objectId, string $key, bool $single, string $objectType): mixed
methods.doc:
The registered default for a key as filter_default_metadata answers:
the one for every subtype, else the object's subtype's; the value
handed in when neither registered one.

methods.name: subtype
methods.doc: The object's subtype: a post's type, a term's taxonomy, comment or user while they exist; '' otherwise.

methods.name: capabilities
methods.doc:
A meta capability (edit, add or delete a post's, comment's, term's or
user's meta) as the reference maps it: what editing the object needs,
then the capability itself when the key is not allowed (protected, or
refused by its auth filter); nothing for an object that does not
exist. Null for any other capability.
shapes: @param list<mixed> $args the object id, then the key

params.name: args
params.doc: the object id, then the key

methods.name: refusal
methods.doc: Why the reference refuses a registration before hooking anything, or null. @param array<string, mixed> $args

methods.name: defaultFits
methods.doc: Whether a default fits the key's type, and its REST schema when it has one. @param array<string, mixed> $args

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\MetaTypes
classes.doc:
Meta types a plugin brought, by the table it named on $wpdb as
"{$type}meta" (WooCommerce's order items keep theirs in
woocommerce_order_itemmeta). The reference reads any such table with
"{$type}_id" for the object and meta_id for the row; Meta does the same.

methods.name: register
methods.doc: Registers a meta type by its full table name; refused unless both are plain identifiers.

methods.name: table
methods.doc: The full table name of a registered meta type, or null.

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\NavMenu
classes.doc:
wp_nav_menu()'s menu: the one the arguments name, its items marked for
the page in view (MenuItemMarks), walked, wrapped in the container.

methods.name: menus
methods.doc: Every menu (wp_get_nav_menus): the nav_menu terms by name, empty ones too, as wp_get_nav_menus leaves them.

methods.name: menu
methods.doc: A menu by its term, id, slug or name (wp_get_nav_menu_object), or false, as the filter leaves it.

methods.name: items
methods.doc: A menu's items (wp_get_nav_menu_items), or false for no menu.

methods.name: walk
methods.doc: A menu's items printed through the walker its arguments name, else the default (walk_nav_menu_tree).

methods.name: locations
methods.doc: The menu set for each of the theme's locations (get_nav_menu_locations).

methods.name: build
methods.doc:
The whole menu for wp_nav_menu(): resolve, fetch, decorate, walk,
wrap, filter. Null when there is no menu (the caller's fallback
runs); false when the items filtered away to nothing.

methods.name: menuForArgs
methods.doc: The menu the args name: by menu, by assigned location, else the first menu that has items.

methods.name: wrapId
methods.doc: The ul id: the caller's, else menu-{slug}, counted up when the same menu renders twice on a page.

methods.name: container
methods.doc: The container wrap, when the args ask for one.

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\NavMenuItems
classes.doc:
Classic menu items as the reference serves them to walkers and plugins
(probe nav-menu-items). wp_setup_nav_menu_item dresses a nav_menu_item
post with the fields walkers read: its _menu_item_* meta (ids as
strings), kept when already set; then by its kind the label, address
and title of what it points at (a post's title through the_title, every
time, the item's own title winning when it has one; a post or term
gone, or a post trashed, marks it _invalid; a post not published is
labelled by its status; a post or term item left without a title reads
"#<object id> (no title)", and an archive item for a type not registered
has the address false); its title attribute and description through
their filters. A post or term of another kind is dressed as a would-be
item, as the admin's boxes use it: id 0, its own title, address and
parent. wp_get_nav_menu_items reads a menu's items through get_posts,
sets each up, drops the invalid ones outside the admin, and for ARRAY_A
output sorts them by the output key and numbers that key from 1, all
before its filter.

methods.name: prepare
methods.doc: A menu item made ready to print (wp_setup_nav_menu_item), unless pre_wp_setup_nav_menu_item answers first.

methods.name: setUp
methods.doc: The item dressed, whatever it was, then the filter (what wp_setup_nav_menu_item does past its pre filter).

methods.name: forMenu
methods.doc: wp_get_nav_menu_items for a menu found.

methods.name: menuItem
methods.doc: A nav_menu_item post: its meta, what it points at, its attribute and description.

methods.name: pointsAtPost
methods.doc: An item for a post: the post type's name (its status's for a post not published), the post's address and filtered title.

methods.name: pointsAtTerm
methods.doc: An item for a term: the taxonomy's name, the term's address and name.

methods.name: pointsAtArchive
methods.doc: An item for a post type's archive: the archives label, the archive's address.

methods.name: untitled
methods.doc: The title a post or term item falls back to when it has none, translated whether it is needed or not.

methods.name: custom
methods.doc: A custom link: its own title and stored address.

methods.name: post
methods.doc: A post of another kind, as a would-be item for it.

methods.name: term
methods.doc: A term, as a would-be item for it.

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\NavigationFallback
classes.doc:
The navigation menu a navigation block falls back to
(WP_Navigation_Fallback, and the block_core_navigation_* helpers the
reference keeps as deprecated): the newest published navigation menu, else
one made from the site's classic menu, else a default listing the pages
(probes navigation-fallback, nav-pomo-rest-doubts).

methods.name: fallback
methods.doc:
The navigation menu to fall back to: the newest published one; else,
unless wp_navigation_should_create_fallback says not, one made from the
classic menu or, without one, the default, then the newest again.

methods.name: classicMenu
methods.doc:
The classic menu a navigation falls back to: the one in the primary
location, else the one slugged primary, else the newest; null without menus.

methods.name: classicMenuBlocks
methods.doc: A classic menu's items as serialized navigation blocks, parsed by the callable given (else here).

methods.name: menuItemBlocks
methods.doc:
Menu items as navigation blocks: a link each, a submenu for an item with
children (its inner blocks serialized as its content), the children
parsed by the callable given (else here).

methods.name: newest
methods.doc: The newest published navigation menu, through the query's filters, or null.

methods.name: fromClassicMenu
methods.doc: The classic menu made a published navigation menu: the insert's answer, or null without a classic menu or with an empty one.

methods.name: createDefault
methods.doc: A published navigation menu titled Navigation, listing the site's pages while the page list block is registered.

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\Notices
classes.doc:
The debugging notices plugins and the engine raise: a deprecated function,
argument, hook, file, class or constructor, and a function called
incorrectly. Each is heard by its action first; then, only under WP_DEBUG
and while its own filter still says so, it is raised as a PHP notice worded
as the reference words it. Every raised message passes
wp_trigger_error_always_run, wp_trigger_error_trigger_error and
wp_trigger_error_run, and keeps only links (http and https), line breaks,
code and emphasis. Values reach the hooks exactly as they were given.

constants.name: MARKUP
constants.value: array (   'a' =>    array (     0 => 'href',   ),   'br' =>    array (   ),   'code' =>    array (   ),   'em' =>    array (   ),   'strong' =>    array (   ), )
constants.doc: The markup a raised notice keeps (each element with its attributes), and the protocols its links may use.

constants.name: DEPRECATIONS
constants.value: array ( 'function' => array ( 0 => 'deprecated_function_run', 1 => 'deprecated_function_trigger_error', 2 => 'Function %1$s is deprecated since version %2$s! Use %3$s instead.', 3 => 'Function %1$s is deprecated since version %2$s with no alternative available.', 4 => false, ), 'argument' => array ( 0 => 'deprecated_argument_run', 1 => 'deprecated_argument_trigger_error', 2 => 'Function %1$s was called with an argument that is deprecated since version %2$s! %3$s', 3 => 'Function %1$s was called with an argument that is deprecated since version %2$s with no alternative available.', 4 => false, ), 'hook' => array ( 0 => 'deprecated_hook_run', 1 => 'deprecated_hook_trigger_error', 2 => 'Hook %1$s is deprecated since version %2$s! Use %3$s instead.', 3 => 'Hook %1$s is deprecated since version %2$s with no alternative available.', 4 => true, ), 'file' => array ( 0 => 'deprecated_file_included', 1 => 'deprecated_file_trigger_error', 2 => 'File %1$s is deprecated since version %2$s! Use %3$s instead.', 3 => 'File %1$s is deprecated since version %2$s with no alternative available.', 4 => true, ), 'class' => array ( 0 => 'deprecated_class_run', 1 => 'deprecated_class_trigger_error', 2 => 'Class %1$s is deprecated since version %2$s! Use %3$s instead.', 3 => 'Class %1$s is deprecated since version %2$s with no alternative available.', 4 => false, ), )
constants.doc:
Each kind of deprecation: the action that hears it, the filter that may
silence it, its wording with an alternative and without one, and
whether a closing note follows the wording (and is heard after the
version).

methods.name: wanted
methods.doc: Whether a notice is raised: only under WP_DEBUG, and only while its filter (handed true and anything else given) still says so.

methods.name: deprecated
methods.signature: deprecated(string $kind, mixed $name, mixed $version, mixed $alternative = '', mixed $note = ''): void
methods.doc:
A deprecation of one kind (function, argument, hook, file or class): its
name, the version that deprecated it, the alternative (for an argument,
the message), and for a hook or a file a note added after the wording.

methods.name: constructor
methods.doc: A class still constructed through its old PHP 4 style constructor, in its parent class when one is named.

methods.name: doingItWrong
methods.doc: A function called incorrectly, with why, and the version that added the message.

methods.name: message
methods.doc:
A notice's message as it would be raised, or null when it is not:
wp_trigger_error_always_run hears every one; under WP_DEBUG, and unless
wp_trigger_error_trigger_error silences it, wp_trigger_error_run hears it
and it is cleaned to the markup a notice keeps.

methods.name: notify
methods.doc: One of the engine's own notices, raised when it is wanted.

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\OEmbed
classes.doc: oEmbed as data: provider matching against the wildcard table, response parsing, and the markup an oEmbed payload becomes.

methods.doc: The endpoint of the provider whose mask matches a URL, or null.
shapes: @param array<string, array{0: string, 1: bool}> $providers mask => [endpoint with {format}, mask is a regex]

params.doc: mask => [endpoint with {format}, mask is a regex]

methods.doc:
The provider endpoint a page names in its head: the first link of each
oEmbed type (the linktypes map type to json or xml), JSON before XML,
its address entity-decoded. Null when it names none.

methods.name: autoembed
methods.doc:
URLs standing alone on a line, or alone in a paragraph, handed to the
callback (WP_Embed::autoembed): a newline inside a tag (one split over
lines, or an attribute value) is kept from the line match, so a URL
there stays as written.

methods.name: stripNewlines
methods.doc: Drops newlines from embed markup while leaving the inside of <pre> blocks untouched.

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\ObjectCache
classes.doc: The per-request object cache behind wp_cache_*: groups of keys, nothing persistent.

methods.name: get
methods.doc: A cached value, or false.

methods.name: set
methods.doc: Stores a value.

methods.name: add
methods.doc: Stores a value only when the key is empty.

methods.name: delete
methods.doc: Removes a key.

methods.name: flush
methods.doc: Empties the cache.

methods.name: sizes
methods.doc:
Each group's size, its entries serialized, in bytes, in the order the
groups were first written: what WP_Object_Cache::stats prints.

methods.name: flushGroup
methods.doc: Empties one group.

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\ObjectTerms
classes.doc:
wp_get_object_terms's handling of taxonomies registered with their own
query arguments, as the reference handles them: among several, each such
taxonomy is asked on its own with its arguments over the caller's; alone,
its arguments join the caller's.

methods.name: byTaxonomyArgs
methods.doc: The terms asked for apart, the taxonomies left (keys as they were), and the arguments for those.
shapes: @return array{0: list<mixed>, 1: array<int, string>, 2: array<string, mixed>}

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\OptionLock
classes.doc:
A lock the reference keeps as an option row (the revision upgrade's
"revision-upgrade-{id}", the comment type batch's
"update_comment_type.lock"; tests/tools/side-effects.php): inserted only
when no row holds the name, its value the time it was taken; one held
for less than an hour keeps others out, an older one is taken over. The
holder writes the time again through update_option, and deletes the row
when done.

constants.name: HELD_SECONDS
constants.doc: How long a held lock keeps others out, in seconds.

methods.name: take
methods.doc: Takes the lock, inserting its row with the autoload value the reference gives it; false while another holds it.

methods.name: release
methods.doc: Lets the lock go.

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\OptionSanitizer
classes.doc:
A core option's value cleaned as the reference's sanitize_option cleans
it (probe sanitize-option), before sanitize_option_{$option}: counts as
whole numbers, the site's name and tagline escaped, formats and mail
settings stripped of markup, addresses checked and kept as they were
(with a settings error) when they are not addresses, word lists split
and trimmed, the timezone and language checked against what exists. Any
other option is left to its filter, where register_setting puts a
plugin's sanitize_callback.

constants.name: EMAIL
constants.value: 'The email address entered did not appear to be a valid email address. Please enter a valid email address.'

constants.name: ERRORS
constants.value: array ( 'siteurl' => 'The WordPress address you entered did not appear to be a valid URL. Please enter a valid URL.', 'home' => 'The Site address you entered did not appear to be a valid URL. Please enter a valid URL.', 'timezone_string' => 'The timezone you have entered is not valid. Please select a valid timezone.', 'permalink_structure' => 'A structure tag is required when using custom permalinks. Learn more', )

methods.name: clean
methods.doc: The value as sanitize_option leaves it, through sanitize_option_{$option}.

methods.name: rule
methods.doc: The option's own rule: the cleaned value, and the error that refuses it (null when it stands).

methods.name: perPage
methods.doc: A page size: a whole number, 1 when none, a negative one (but -1, all) made positive.

methods.name: languages
methods.doc: The languages the site may be set to: those installed, and the one wp-config names. @return list<string>

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\OptionWrites
classes.doc:
Options written the way add_option(), update_option() and delete_option()
write them: the name trimmed, alloptions and notoptions stopped, the
guarded ones refused, the value sanitized, and each change heard before
and after by the actions plugins hook.

methods.name: add
methods.doc:
A new option (add_option): refused when it already reads as anything
but its default; its autoload flag decided when not given.

methods.name: update
delete
methods.doc: An option removed (delete_option): false when it was not there.

methods.name: protect
methods.doc: Stops the request at alloptions or notoptions, which nothing may write (wp_protect_special_option).

methods.name: autoloadFlag
methods.doc:
The autoload flag an option is stored with (wp_determine_option_autoload_value):
"on" for on, yes or true, "off" for off, no or false; anything else is
decided by wp_default_autoload_value (auto-on, auto-off) or left "auto".

methods.name: setAutoload
methods.doc:
Options' autoload flags set (wp_set_option_autoload_values): per option,
whether its flag changed. Only false, no, off, auto-off and 0 mean off.

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\Options
classes.doc:
Options as plugin code sees them, kept where the reference keeps them:
wp_cache's options group (OptionsGroup) holds the autoloaded list, the
names known unset, and a key per option not autoloaded, so a plugin that
reads, writes or drops those keys is heard. get_option() and
wp_load_alloptions() pass the list through pre_wp_load_alloptions and
alloptions. A value written this request is held as it was written (an
int stays an int, true stays true), arrays and objects as stored. Each
stored text is decoded once while it stays the same, except one holding
an object, decoded afresh on every read as the reference does: a plugin
that changes the object it was handed and saves it must find the stored
copy still different, or its change is never written.

constants.name: GUARDED
constants.doc:
The options the engine keeps for itself: the symbol-gate cache a plugin
could otherwise rewrite to pass its own gate, the recovery strikes and
the token of recovery's own check, the cron lock, and the sign-in
throttle rows. The facade refuses to write them; the engine writes
them through this class directly.

constants.name: ON_DEMAND
constants.doc:
The engine's own caches, read on demand and written with autoload off
(Site::setOption). Rows an older engine wrote autoloaded are set right
the first time a loaded list holds them.

constants.name: AUTOLOAD_VALUES
constants.doc: The autoload column values that load an option with every request, in the reference's order.

constants.name: EVERY_REQUEST
constants.doc:
Options not autoloaded that are read on every request (the symbol
survey, recovery's paused plugins, the site language, the HTTPS
migration flag, the post types and taxonomies Minn Admin keeps and
registers as it loads, whether scripts may be compressed, which every
page that prints them asks, the site logo a block theme's header asks
for, and Minn Admin's maintenance switch the front door checks): read
together as a request begins, as one read rather than one each.

methods.name: isFor
methods.doc: Whether this store reads through the given connection.

methods.name: guarded
methods.doc: Whether plugin code is refused a write to this option.

methods.name: autoloaded
methods.doc:
The autoloaded list as wp_load_alloptions() gives it:
pre_wp_load_alloptions may answer first (told whether the cache was
forced), and then alloptions is not heard; otherwise the list the
group holds, through alloptions, which may add or change entries
without the group keeping them.

methods.name: filtered
methods.doc:
An option as get_option() reads it, through the filters plugins hook:
pre_option_{name}, then pre_option, may answer first; then the
autoloaded list is read through its filters on every read; an unset
option is its default (false when none is given) through
default_option_{name}, which is told whether one was given; a set one
goes through option_{name}.

methods.name: raw
methods.doc:
An option's stored text, as Db::option() gives it, or null when it is
unset: from the list or the group, a value written this request in
its stored form (true as "1", a list serialized).

methods.name: get
methods.doc: An option's value, decoded, or null when unset; home and siteurl answer to wp-config.php's constants.

methods.name: prime
methods.doc:
Reads several options at once (wp_prime_option_caches): the ones not
held yet in one query, each kept under its own key or noted unset, as
a read of each one alone would leave them.

methods.name: exists
methods.doc: Whether an option exists.

methods.name: knownMissing
methods.doc: Whether a read this request already found the option unset (the reference's notoptions).

methods.name: add
methods.doc:
Writes a new option. add_option has already decided it is new (its
value is still the default); a row that is there anyway is written
over, as the reference's add does, and false comes back when it
already held this value. An autoloaded one joins the list.

methods.name: upsert
methods.doc:
Writes an option row whether or not one exists, as the reference does
for every add: two requests that both find a transient missing and
both add it must not fail on the unique name, so the second write lands
over the first. True when the row was inserted or changed, false when
the same value was already there.

methods.name: update
methods.doc:
False when the value is unchanged, as the reference reports. An
autoload flag given is stored with the value, and the value moves
between the autoloaded list and a key of its own when the flag says
so.

methods.name: autoloadOf
methods.doc: The autoload flag a stored option carries, or null when there is no such row.

methods.name: markAutoload
methods.doc: Flips the autoload column; false when the option is missing or already so. The list is read again, the option's own key dropped.

methods.name: unmarkAutoload
methods.doc: Stops an option loading on every request; false when it already did not, or is unset. It leaves the list.

methods.name: claim
methods.doc:
Inserts an option row only when no row holds the name yet, past every
cache: a lock (Runtime\OptionLock). Whether this call made the row.

methods.name: take
methods.doc:
Removes an option and hands back what it held, or null when it was not
there: a single-use token. The delete itself decides, so of two
requests taking the same row at once only one gets its value.

methods.name: deleteExpired
methods.doc:
Removes the options under a prefix whose value begins with an expiry
time ("1767225600:...") that has passed: tokens nobody came back for.

methods.name: delete
methods.doc: Removes an option: out of the list or its own key, and known unset.

methods.name: expiredTransientNames
methods.doc:
The names of transients whose expiry has passed. The timeout row is the
one that knows, so the sweep reads those and hands back the bare names.

methods.name: forget
methods.doc:
Brings the group back in step with an option the engine wrote behind
the store (its own rows, the CLI): the row is read again, into the list
when it autoloads, and nothing else written this request is lost.

methods.name: toStorage
methods.doc:
What the reference stores (maybe_serialize): arrays and objects
serialized, a string that looks serialized serialized again so it
reads back as that string, other scalars as their string form.

methods.name: fromStorage
methods.doc: A stored option value decoded the way the reference reads it.

methods.name: listed
methods.doc:
The autoloaded options, kept in the group under alloptions: read in one
query when the group has no list, each as stored except one written
since. @return array<string, mixed>

methods.name: missing
shapes: @return array<string, true> the names a read found unset, kept in the group under notoptions

methods.name: lookup
methods.doc:
An option's held value, or null when it is unset: from the list given,
else not at all when it is known unset, else its own key, else its row
(kept under its own key, or noted unset).

methods.name: decode
methods.doc: A held value decoded the way the reference reads it, once while it stays the same (never one holding an object).

methods.name: remember
methods.doc:
What the group holds for a value just written: scalars as given,
arrays and objects as stored. Its decoded form is the value itself,
so a string that only looks serialized reads back as that string.

methods.name: found
methods.doc: Takes a name off the list of those known unset.

methods.name: holdsObject
methods.doc: Whether a stored value has an object record in it (a string that only mentions one decodes afresh too, which is harmless).

methods.name: switchAutoload
shapes: @param list<string> $already the stored values that already mean $wanted

params.name: already
params.doc: the stored values that already mean $wanted

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\OptionsGroup
classes.doc:
wp_cache's options group, where option reads are kept as the reference
keeps them: the autoloaded list under alloptions, the names a read found
unset under notoptions, and one key per option not autoloaded. The
engine's own object cache holds it, or an object-cache.php drop-in once
the facade hands over its functions.

A drop-in's cache outlives the request, and the engine writes some
options behind the store (its own state, the CLI), so a key left by an
earlier request is never trusted: each is read from the database the
first time a request asks for it, then kept in step for the rest of it.

methods.name: useExternal
methods.doc: Hands the group to an object-cache.php drop-in's functions.

methods.name: get
methods.doc: A key's value, found only when this request may trust it.

methods.name: set
methods.doc: Stores a key; a drop-in is written only when it holds something else.

methods.name: delete
methods.doc: Removes a key.

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\OutputFloor
classes.doc:
The output buffers the engine reads its pages from. The reference prints
as it goes, so a plugin that ends every buffer mid-page
(wp_ob_end_flush_all) only sends what it has early; the engine builds the
page in its own buffers and sends it whole, so ending those would send
part of the page out ahead of its headers and lose it from the rest.
Each capture holds its level while it is open, and such a plugin ends
only the buffers above the innermost one (suite output-flush).

methods.name: hold
methods.doc: Marks the buffer just opened as one the engine reads.

methods.name: release
methods.doc: Lets the innermost capture go.

methods.name: level
methods.doc: The level buffers may be ended down to: the innermost capture's, or none.

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\Pages
classes.doc:
get_pages() as the reference shapes it: its arguments as a post query
(WP_Query, so its filters shape it), the tree order of the result, then
the get_pages filter. wp_list_pages, wp_dropdown_pages and the
navigation's page list take their pages from here.

methods.name: get
methods.doc: The pages get_pages() answers for parsed arguments.

methods.name: queryArgs
methods.doc:
The post query the get_pages() arguments amount to, shaped as the
reference hands it to get_pages_query_args (probe filter-inputs-2): the
order by the columns as named, then (unless pages are picked by id)
the excluded ones and the meta pair, the number or -1 and the offset,
the type, the statuses as a list and the cache flags; then the picked
pages, the authors and the parent, each when given.

methods.name: arrange
methods.doc:
The pages as the reference leaves them: with a hierarchy (unless a
parent is named or pages are picked by id) or a child_of, only what
descends from that page (the root by default), each parent followed
by its subtree; then any branch left out, its places left empty.
shapes: @param list<object> $pages objects with ID and post_parent

methods.name: children
methods.doc:
What descends from a page within the list, depth first, siblings in
list order (get_page_children); a page whose parent is not reached is
left out.

methods.name: descendants
methods.doc: Every page under one ancestor, in list order. @param list<object> $pages @return list<object>

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\Patterns
classes.doc:
The block pattern, pattern category, and block style registries as data.
Entries registered after init are remembered separately, because the
editor asks for those on their own.

methods.name: registerPattern
methods.doc: Registers a block pattern, or the refusal.

methods.name: unregisterPattern
methods.doc: Forgets a pattern.

methods.name: pattern
methods.doc: One pattern, or null.

methods.name: patterns
methods.doc: Every pattern.

methods.name: patternsAfterInit
methods.doc: The patterns registered after init, which the editor lists separately.

methods.name: registerCategory
methods.doc: Registers a pattern category, or the refusal.

methods.name: unregisterCategory
methods.doc: Forgets a category.

methods.name: category
methods.doc: One category, or null.

methods.name: categories
methods.doc: Every category.

methods.name: categoriesAfterInit
methods.doc: The categories registered after init.

methods.name: registerStyle
methods.doc: Registers a block style, or the refusal.

methods.name: unregisterStyle
methods.doc: Forgets a block style.

methods.name: style
methods.doc: One block style, or null.

methods.name: styles
methods.doc: Every block style, or one block's.

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\PlaceholderTrace
classes.doc:
Records every call into a generated placeholder while a site opts in by
having wp-content/minn-placeholder-trace.log on disk: one line per call
with the symbol, the plugin file that called it, and the request. The
log says which placeholders deserve behaviour; an absent file costs one
stat per request.

methods.name: deadEnd
methods.doc:
Logs a call to a method of a real class that Minn answers with nothing by
design (an admin-screen helper): compat-status counts the method as a
dead end, where a hit() marks one still owed.

methods.name: hit
methods.doc: Logs a placeholder symbol being called, when the trace file exists.

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\Placeholders
classes.doc:
The printf placeholders plugin code hands wpdb::prepare, filled the way
the reference fills them: a bare %s is escaped and quoted; a numbered
(%1$s), padded (%5s) or precise (%.2f) one is formatted and escaped but
never quoted, so a plugin can name a table with it; %d and %f cast; %i
backticks an identifier; %% is a literal. Numbered placeholders address
the argument list directly while unnumbered ones count from the first
on their own, as vsprintf does. A placeholder with no argument behind it
empties the whole query, as the reference does.

methods.name: fill
methods.doc: Fills a query's placeholders from the arguments; null when one has no argument.
shapes: @param callable(string): string $escape the connection's string escape

methods.name: prepare
methods.doc:
fill() with what wpdb::prepare reports alongside: how many placeholders
the query has (%% not among them) and the type of each argument it
could not use (an array or an object fills as '').
shapes: @param callable(string): string $escape the connection's string escape

methods.name: quoted
methods.doc: A bare %s is the one placeholder the reference wraps in quotes.

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\Pluggables
classes.doc:
Where the pluggable functions are declared. The reference declares them in
wp-includes/pluggable.php, and code that asks where one lives (a mail
plugin reading ReflectionFunction('wp_mail')->getFileName() to decide
whether it may take over mail, as SandyWP's mail helper and FluentSMTP do)
stands aside when it finds them anywhere else. So an install lays the
engine's own wp-api/pluggable.php at that path, whole, behind a header
that hands over to the engine's copy when the laid one is not the running
engine's (an engine updated past it, a checkout edited since): a laid copy
never declares anything the engine running would not (Austin, 2026-10-24).

constants.name: LAID
constants.doc: Where the reference declares the pluggable functions, from the webroot.

constants.name: HEADER
constants.value: '<?php // Minn Engine: the pluggable functions, declared where the reference declares them, so code that asks // where one lives finds this file. Laid by the engine from minn/wp-api/pluggable.php; a copy that is not // the running engine\'s leaves the declaring to the engine\'s own. Requested on its own, it does nothing. if (!defined(\'MINN_ENGINE_DIR\')) {     return; } if (!\\Minn\\Runtime\\Pluggables::current(__FILE__, MINN_ENGINE_DIR)) {     require_once MINN_ENGINE_DIR . \'/wp-api/pluggable.php\';     return; } '

methods.name: laid
methods.doc: The file an install lays at wp-includes/pluggable.php for an engine: the header, then the engine's own file after its opening tag.

methods.name: current
methods.doc: Whether the file at $file is the copy this engine lays.

methods.name: file
methods.doc: The file that declares the pluggable functions for this webroot: the laid copy when it is the engine's, else the engine's own.

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\PluginActivation
classes.doc:
Switching a plugin on and off the way the reference's activate_plugin
and deactivate_plugins do (probe plugin-activation), for the facade and
for the engine's own REST routes and WP-CLI verbs alike. Activating
checks the plugin's requirements, then loads its main file through the
runtime's gate (so its activation hook is registered, silent or not),
fires activate_plugin and activate_<file> (which runs that hook), writes
active_plugins sorted through update_option, and fires activated_plugin;
whatever the plugin printed meanwhile makes the answer unexpected_output,
with the plugin left active, as the reference leaves it. Silent skips the
actions, not the load. A plugin the gate will not load (it needs
functions or classes the runtime lacks) is refused rather than recorded
active with code that could never run its activation hook. Deactivating
fires deactivate_plugin, deactivate_<file> and deactivated_plugin for
each plugin, then writes the list once.

methods.name: activate
methods.doc:
Activates one plugin ("dir/file.php"), announcing it to the hooks
given, or to nobody (silent); null when it is active afterwards with
nothing to report.

methods.name: deactivate
methods.doc:
Deactivates plugins ("dir/file.php" each), announcing each to the hooks
given, or to nobody (silent); those not active are passed over.

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\PluginCall
classes.doc:
Calls code a plugin, theme or drop-in registered (a hook callback, a
shortcode, a widget, a REST permission or field callback), as WordPress
calls it. PHP judges a call's argument types by the file the call is made
from: the engine's own files declare strict types, so a callback typed
`int $post_id` handed the string "3494" would throw a TypeError there,
where WordPress's untyped files let PHP convert it (Elementor's heartbeat
passes the post ID it was posted, a string, to just such a callback).
Every call into extension code is made from here, the one engine file
that leaves strict types off.

methods.name: run
methods.doc: Runs a callback extension code registered, with the arguments given.

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\PluginFiles
classes.doc:
A plugin's files as WordPress's plugin functions know them: where a
plugin folder really is (a symlinked one noted), a plugin file's name
under the plugins folder, its headers as read and as the plugin screens
show them, and whether it can be uninstalled.

constants.name: HEADERS
constants.value: array (   'Name' => 'Plugin Name',   'PluginURI' => 'Plugin URI',   'Version' => 'Version',   'Description' => 'Description',   'Author' => 'Author',   'AuthorURI' => 'Author URI',   'TextDomain' => 'Text Domain',   'DomainPath' => 'Domain Path',   'Network' => 'Network',   'RequiresWP' => 'Requires at least',   'RequiresPHP' => 'Requires PHP',   'UpdateURI' => 'Update URI',   'RequiresPlugins' => 'Requires Plugins', )
constants.doc: The headers a plugin's main file may carry, by field.

methods.name: registerRealpath
methods.doc:
Where a plugin's folder really is, noted under the folder as given
(wp_register_plugin_realpath); a file not on disk notes an empty
place. The plugins and must-use folders themselves are refused.

methods.name: basename
methods.doc: A plugin file's name under the plugins or must-use folder (plugin_basename), a symlinked folder read as noted.

methods.name: all
methods.doc:
The plugins in the plugins folder, or in a folder of it named from the
plugins folder on ("/name"), each by its file relative to the folder
read and in name order (get_plugins). The reference keeps each folder's
list for the rest of the request in the 'plugins' cache group (probe
plugin-list-cache): a later call answers the kept list, even one a
plugin set there, until wp_clean_plugins_cache, and a folder that is
not there answers nothing and keeps nothing.

methods.name: data
methods.signature: data(mixed $pluginFile, mixed $markup = true, mixed $translate = true): array
methods.doc:
A plugin's headers (get_plugin_data), marked up and translated unless
asked not to be; a plugin in its own folder that names no text domain
uses the folder's name.

methods.name: shown
methods.signature: shown(mixed $pluginFile, mixed $data, mixed $markup = true, mixed $translate = true): array
methods.doc:
The headers as the plugin screens show them
(_get_plugin_data_markup_translate). Translated: the plugin's domain
loaded from its folder unless it is already, then the name, addresses,
version, description and author through it. Always: the text cut to a,
abbr, acronym, code, em and strong, the addresses escaped. Marked up:
the title and author linked, the description texturized with its "By"
line.

methods.name: uninstallable
methods.doc: Whether a plugin can be uninstalled (is_uninstallable_plugin): it registered an uninstall callback, or ships an uninstall.php.

methods.name: roots
methods.doc:
A plugins folder as named and as it really is, resolved once a process:
plugin_basename runs for every plugin URL and hook a plugin registers,
and under open_basedir each realpath checks the whole path again.

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\PluginRemoval
classes.doc:
Deleting plugins as the reference's delete_plugins does it: each in turn
is uninstalled first when it can be (its uninstall.php, or the callback
it registered), then delete_plugin, its folder (or file) removed,
deleted_plugin, and its installed translations removed with it; the
updates offered for the deleted ones are forgotten. A plugin already
gone counts as deleted. Only what lies inside the plugins folder is
ever removed, and a symlinked folder is unlinked, never followed.

methods.name: delete
methods.doc: delete_plugins: true, false for none asked, or the error naming those left behind.
shapes: @param array<int, string> $plugins plugin files, relative to the plugins folder

params.name: plugins
params.doc: plugin files, relative to the plugins folder

methods.name: uninstall
methods.doc:
uninstall_plugin: pre_uninstall_plugin, then the plugin's uninstall.php
(WP_UNINSTALL_PLUGIN naming it) or the callback it registered (heard on
uninstall_<file>, with the plugin loaded); either is forgotten once run.

methods.name: deleteOne
methods.doc: One plugin, uninstalled, removed and announced; whether it is gone. @param array<string, mixed> $translations

methods.name: removeFiles
methods.doc: The plugin's folder, or its file when it has none; false for anything outside the plugins folder.

methods.name: removeTranslations
methods.doc: A folder plugin's installed translations (.po, .mo, .l10n.php, script .json), by locale. @param array<string, mixed> $translations

methods.name: forget
methods.doc: The registered uninstall callback, dropped from the option. @param array<string, mixed> $registered

methods.name: forgetUpdates
methods.doc: The updates offered for plugins that are gone. @param array<int, string> $deleted

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\PluginRequirements
classes.doc:
Whether a plugin can be switched on here, as the reference's
validate_plugin_requirements answers (probe plugin-activation): the
plugin header's "Requires at least" against the WordPress version the
site speaks, its "Requires PHP" against the running PHP, and every slug
in its "Requires Plugins" installed and active (a readme.txt is not
read). A refusal carries the reference's code, its HTML message word for
word, and for missing plugins the slugs found inactive (slug => name) and
not installed (slug => slug). The slugs are taken sorted (one that is not
a lower-case slug is passed over), and named in that order.

methods.name: check
methods.doc: Null when the plugin may be activated, otherwise why not.

methods.name: dependencies
methods.doc: The required plugins that are not installed and active, refused together.

methods.name: installed
methods.doc: The installed plugin a slug names: the first file in its folder with a plugin header, else a single-file plugin of that name.

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\PluginUpdates
classes.doc:
The update offers the site's own plugins publish. A plugin that hosts
itself, or sells itself, is not in the wordpress.org directory and never
appears in the directory's answer: it publishes its offer by filtering
the update transient WordPress reads, which is the only place anyone
learns of it. The engine asks the same question of the runtime, in the
shape the reference asks it, so a self-hosted plugin is offered its
update here exactly as it would be on WordPress.

The transient carries `checked` (every installed plugin and its version),
and a plugin's updater returns early when that is empty, so the installed
versions are what make the question answerable.

methods.name: supplied
methods.doc:
What the site's plugins offer for themselves, empty when no runtime
is booted or nothing filters the transient.
shapes: @param array<string, string> $installed plugin file => installed version
@return array{plugins: array<string, array<string, mixed>>, no_update: array<string, array<string, mixed>>}

methods.name: fromFiltered
methods.doc:
The filtered transient as the state's two buckets: offers under
`plugins`, plugins that answered "current" under `no_update`, both
as arrays, and only for files this site actually has.
shapes: @return array{plugins: array<string, array<string, mixed>>, no_update: array<string, array<string, mixed>>}

methods.name: bucket
methods.doc: One bucket of the transient, normalised.

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\Plugins
classes.doc:
Loads the site's plugins into the runtime the way the reference does:
mu-plugins first, then active_plugins in stored order, each file
included once. A plugin loads only when the static symbol read finds
nothing the runtime lacks; otherwise it is reported and skipped so the
site keeps rendering. The lifecycle actions fire between the phases.

constants.name: MINN_ADMIN
constants.doc:
Minn Admin loads as code for its adapters (surfaces, licenses,
connectors, custom CSS, the plugin routes the engine has no
controller for, and maintenance mode's holds), but the engine owns the
shell, the front bar and the sign-in flow: those hooks come off right
after the include so the two never print twice or disagree. The
plugin's own app route (maybe_render_app) stays: the engine answers
/minn-admin/ itself before template_redirect runs, and the plugin
answers ?minn_admin=1 (plain permalinks) as it does on WordPress.

constants.name: MINN_ADMIN_HOOKS
constants.value: array (   0 =>    array (     0 => 'login_redirect',     1 =>      array (       0 => 'Minn_Admin',       1 => 'login_redirect',     ),     2 => 20,   ),   1 =>    array (     0 => 'show_admin_bar',     1 =>      array (       0 => 'Minn_Admin',       1 => 'enforce_toolbar_policy',     ),     2 => 99,   ),   2 =>    array (     0 => 'show_admin_bar',     1 =>      array (       0 => 'Minn_Admin_Bar',       1 => 'suppress_core_bar',     ),     2 => 100,   ),   3 =>    array (     0 => 'wp_enqueue_scripts',     1 =>      array (       0 => 'Minn_Admin_Bar',       1 => 'enqueue',     ),     2 => 10,   ),   4 =>    array (     0 => 'wp_footer',     1 =>      array (       0 => 'Minn_Admin_Bar',       1 => 'render',     ),     2 => 10,   ),   5 =>    array (     0 => 'body_class',     1 =>      array (       0 => 'Minn_Admin_Bar',       1 => 'body_class',     ),     2 => 10,   ), )

methods.name: load
methods.doc:
Loads the active plugins as code and fires the boot hooks. Recovery
is armed for exactly this window: a failure here is one every
visitor would hit, so it may be recorded against its extension.
Where the mode keeps the site's plugins out (MINN_WP_API, WpApiMode)
no plugin or must-use plugin is included, Minn Admin's file aside where
the mode asks for it; the theme's functions.php still loads, and the
boot hooks still fire for the facade's own registrations.

methods.name: loadTheme
methods.doc:
The theme's setup without the plugins: setup_theme, the theme's
functions.php, after_setup_theme, then wp_loaded. The probe runtime
ends its boot with this, so a theme's supports are what a request's
would be and a late declaration is judged as one; it skips init,
whose work the probes compare on their own.

methods.name: loaded
methods.doc: The plugins that loaded.

methods.name: skipped
methods.doc: The plugins the symbol gate refused, with what they lacked.
shapes: @return array<string, array<string, mixed>> plugin file => why it did not load

methods.name: loadNow
methods.doc:
Loads one plugin's main file now, as activating it does: the reference
includes the file (once) before activate_plugin fires, so the plugin's
activation hook is in place to hear activate_<file>, and announces no
plugin_loaded for it. The same gate as the boot decides, its folder
walked again first; null once the plugin is running, otherwise why the
gate refused it.

methods.name: isLoaded
methods.doc: True when the named plugin file is running as code this request.

methods.name: loadThemeFunctions
methods.doc:
The active theme's functions.php, child first then parent, between
setup_theme and after_setup_theme as the reference loads them. Each
file goes through the same symbol gate as a plugin folder and is
reported under "theme:{slug}" when it cannot load. Templates never
run as PHP; a block theme's functions.php only registers hooks.

methods.name: rememberThemeDomain
methods.doc:
An active theme's folder, where a domain's files are named by locale
alone, and its own text domain, the one its stylesheet names (the slug
when it names none), read from its "Domain Path" (or "/languages").

methods.name: registerRealpath
methods.doc:
A symlinked plugin folder resolves __FILE__ to its real location; the
global map from the plugins directory's folder to that location keeps
plugin_basename() and plugins_url() truthful, as the reference's
$wp_plugin_paths does.

methods.name: isolatedInclude
methods.doc: The include gets a clean local scope, as wp-settings.php gives every plugin file.

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\PostCaches
classes.doc:
A post's cached rows let go as WordPress lets them go: its row, its meta
and the terms read with it, then plugins told (a page told twice); held
back while cache invalidation is suspended.

methods.name: clean
methods.doc: A post's caches let go (clean_post_cache).

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\PostData
classes.doc:
The loop's view of a post, as the reference's generate_postdata and
get_the_content give it (probes the-content, excerpt): the content split
into pages at <!--nextpage--> (the line breaks beside the marker go with
it) and handed to content_pagination, the page the query asks for, and
"more" when the main query shows a single post, a page or a feed; then
the content of that page, cut at the more tag with a more link (or run
on past it when "more" is set), the teaser dropped when asked or marked
<!--noteaser-->.

methods.name: setup
methods.doc:
A post made the one being read (setup_postdata): through the query
being answered when there is one (which tells the_post), else its
globals set here; false for no post.

methods.name: globals
methods.doc: The loop's globals for a post: its id, author, dates, pages and whether more shows.

methods.name: generate
methods.doc:
id, authordata, currentday, currentmonth, page, pages, multipage,
more, numpages. The page comes from the query given (the main query
otherwise); more is set on a single, a page or a feed, or past the
first page of a post split into pages (probe query-compat).

methods.name: content
methods.doc:
The content get_the_content gives: the asked page, cut at the more tag
unless "more" is set.
shapes: @param array<string, mixed> $elements as generate() gives them, with strip_teaser when the teaser should go

params.name: elements
params.doc: as generate() gives them, with strip_teaser when the teaser should go

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\PostEvents
classes.doc:
What the reference's REST controllers tell plugins about a post they
write, for the engine's own controllers: the same actions in the same
order with the same arguments, fired through the facade's lifecycle
functions so the facade's own writes say the same (contracts/runtime.md
"Writes tell plugins"). Without a booted runtime every method does
nothing, so a write with no plugins loaded is exactly what it was.

methods.name: deleteForGood
methods.doc:
A post deleted for good through the reference's own deletion, so its
hooks fire and its children (revisions, autosaves) go with it: the
one path every permanent delete takes. Deleting needs the facade, so
unlike the events it runs only under a booted runtime, which the
engine's write routes are. Answers what the deletion answered.

methods.name: trash
methods.doc: A post (an attachment too) sent to the trash through the reference's own trashing, as deleteForGood deletes.

methods.name: live
methods.doc: Whether plugins are loaded to be told anything.

methods.name: beforeSave
methods.doc: Before the row is written: pre_post_insert for a new post, pre_post_update for one that exists. @param array<string, mixed> $columns

methods.name: saved
methods.doc: Once the row is written: the caches, the status transition, the edit actions of an update, the save actions.

methods.name: ensureCategory
methods.doc:
A post keeps a category through every save, the default when it has
none: through wp_set_post_categories with plugins loaded (which tells
them, set_object_terms included), quietly without.

methods.name: applyTerms
methods.doc:
The terms a REST body names, set through wp_set_object_terms with
plugins loaded, quietly without: a plugin's type takes its own REST
taxonomies under their REST bases (probe rest-plugin-types).

methods.name: applyMeta
methods.doc:
The meta a REST body names: through the registered keys with plugins
loaded (probe rest-meta; a plugin's type only when it supports custom
fields), core's own written directly without.

methods.name: attachmentGenerated
methods.doc:
A new attachment's metadata made by the runtime, as the reference's
REST upload makes it: wp_generate_attachment_metadata over the stored
file (the sizes cut with the attachment's id, the metadata stored as
each one lands, so an optimiser hooked there finds it), then
wp_update_attachment_metadata. Every upload has some: an image its
sizes, a PDF its previews, any file its size (probe hook-inputs-2).

methods.name: restInserted
methods.doc: rest_insert_{type}, before the request's own terms and fields are applied; a post with no $before is a new one.

methods.name: restAfterInsert
methods.doc: rest_after_insert_{type}, once the request's terms and fields are in; a post with no $before is a new one.

methods.name: afterInsert
methods.doc: wp_after_insert_post, last; the revision of an update is saved from it.

methods.name: restDeleted
methods.doc: rest_delete_{type}, after a trash or a delete, with the post as it was answered and the response. @param array<string, mixed> $data

methods.name: rest
methods.doc: One of the two REST insert actions, with the post as it stands and the request.

methods.name: wpPost
methods.doc: A record as the runtime's post object, for a state the database no longer holds.

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\PostFields
classes.doc:
A post's fields put in a context as WordPress's sanitize_post_field puts
them: raw as stored; for the database through the pre_ filters; for
editing through the edit_ filters and made safe for a form; for display
through the field's own filter, escaped for an attribute or a script when
asked. The integer columns stay integers in every context.

methods.name: value
methods.doc: One field in a context (sanitize_post_field).

methods.name: sanitize
methods.doc: Every field of a post object or array in a context (sanitize_post), unless it is in that context already.

methods.name: formatToEdit
methods.doc: Text made ready for an edit field (format_to_edit): through format_to_edit, encoded for a textarea unless rich.

methods.name: richEdit
methods.doc: Whether the user edits in the rich editor (user_can_richedit): their preference, and a browser that can.

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\PostInsert
classes.doc:
The decisions behind wp_insert_post: which columns a postarr fills, when
the post counts as empty, the status a publish request lands in, the dates
and the slug, the categories a new post gets. The rows are written by
Content\PostWriter; the facade fires the hooks around each step.

constructor.signature: __construct(Minn\Content\PostWriter $writer, int $userId, Closure $discussion, Closure $supports, Closure $canPublish, Closure $gmtFromDate, Closure $now)
shapes: @param Closure(string, string): string $discussion a new post's comment or ping status by type, as get_default_comment_status has it
@param Closure(string, string): bool $supports whether a post type supports a feature
@param Closure(string): bool $canPublish whether the current user may publish the type
@param Closure(string): string $gmtFromDate the site-local date as GMT
@param Closure(bool): string $now the current local (or GMT) MySQL time

params.name: discussion
params.doc: a new post's comment or ping status by type, as get_default_comment_status has it

params.name: supports
params.doc: whether a post type supports a feature

params.name: canPublish
params.doc: whether the current user may publish the type

params.name: now
params.doc: the current local (or GMT) MySQL time

methods.name: columns
methods.doc: The columns the posts table takes, filled from a postarr, with a new post's defaults. @param array<string, mixed>|null $existing @return array<string, string>

methods.name: isEmpty
methods.doc: A post with nothing in title, content, and excerpt is empty when its type supports all three. @param array<string, mixed>|null $existing

methods.name: resolve
methods.doc:
The columns as they will be written: the status a request lands in
(attachments inherit, unprivileged publishes pend, a future date
schedules), the dates, the slug (sanitized; not yet free), and the
integer columns.

methods.name: persist
methods.doc: Writes the resolved columns. @return int the post id

methods.name: unwritten
methods.doc:
The error for a post the database door would not write, its text not
what the table holds (probe refused-writes): an insert's or an
update's (a post that already has an id), naming the first such column.

methods.name: fillGuid
methods.doc: Gives a new post written without a guid its permalink as one, once its slug, terms and meta are in.

methods.name: categories
methods.signature: categories(array $postarr, int $id, string $type, string $status, bool $update, array $taxonomies): ?array
methods.doc:
The categories a saved post hands wp_set_post_categories: none when
its type has no categories (null); an update that names none keeps
the ones it has; otherwise the ones given, each empty value dropped.
None left is the default category for a post that is not an
auto-draft, else an empty list (which wp_set_post_categories decides).

methods.name: categoryIds
methods.doc:
The category ids wp_set_post_categories sets, and whether they add to
the post's: none given (null or an empty list) is the default
category in place of the post's, for a post of a type that takes one
(posts and the types default_category_post_types adds) that is not an
auto-draft; a lone blank string is nothing to set (null ids); else
each value as an id, any that is none dropped.

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\PostLinks
classes.doc:
Post addresses as the reference's link functions build them (probe
permalinks): a post through pre_post_link (the structure) and post_link;
a page from get_page_uri through _get_page_link and page_link; an
attachment under its parent's address, or its own; a plugin's type by
its address pattern (the permastruct its rewrite registered) through
post_type_link, by its query var without one. Plain (?p=, ?page_id=,
?post_type=) unless its status is public, or private and readable by
whoever asks, or it is a sample: a draft, a scheduled or trashed post, a
revision, a private one a visitor asks for. "Leaving the name" keeps the slug as its placeholder
(%postname%, %pagename%, %{type}%) for an editor to fill in, and
get_sample_permalink shows a draft as it would be published.

constants.name: LEAVE_NAME
constants.doc: The slug kept as its placeholder.

constants.name: SAMPLE
constants.doc: The address an editor previews: a draft as if published.

methods.name: permalink
methods.doc:
A post's address by its kind (get_permalink): a page's, an
attachment's, a plugin type's or a post's; false for no post. A post
filtered for "sample" is shown as it would be published.

methods.name: pageLink
methods.signature: pageLink(mixed $post = 0, mixed $leavename = false, mixed $sample = false): mixed
methods.doc: A page's address (get_page_link): the home address for the front page; then page_link.

methods.name: pageAddress
methods.signature: pageAddress(mixed $post = 0, mixed $leavename = false, mixed $sample = false): mixed
methods.doc: A page's own address, front page or not (_get_page_link); no such page is the plain address with no id.

methods.name: attachmentLink
methods.doc: An attachment's address (get_attachment_link), or false.

methods.name: customLink
methods.signature: customLink(mixed $post = 0, mixed $leavename = false, mixed $sample = false): mixed
methods.doc: A plugin type's post address (get_post_permalink), or false.

methods.name: post
methods.doc: A post's address (not a page, attachment or plugin type).

methods.name: page
methods.doc: A page's own address, before page_link: ?page_id= while unpublished, its tag when the name is left, else its path.

methods.name: attachment
methods.doc: An attachment's address: under a parent it belongs to, else its own slug, else ?attachment_id=.

methods.name: custom
methods.doc: A plugin type's address by its pattern, by its query var, or by the type and id plainly.

methods.name: sampleFor
methods.signature: sampleFor(mixed $post, mixed $title = NULL, mixed $name = NULL): array
methods.doc:
The address an editor shows with the slug to edit, and the slug
(get_sample_permalink); two empty strings for no post.

methods.name: sample
methods.doc:
The address an editor shows with the slug to edit: the post as if
published, its name made unique, the address with the name left,
a page's parents written in.

methods.name: flags
methods.doc: The flags for leaving the name and showing a sample.

methods.name: tokens
methods.doc: What each structure tag of a post stands for; the name stays a tag when it is left, and the author is read only for a structure that names it.

methods.name: category
methods.doc: The %category% part: the post's first category by id (post_link_category may choose another), under its parents.

methods.name: plain
methods.doc:
Whether a post's address is the plain one: its status neither public
nor private and readable, unless it is a sample of a status that is
not internal (a trashed post and a revision stay plain as samples).

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\PostLocks
classes.doc:
A post's edit lock (_edit_lock, "time:user"): who holds it while it is
fresh, for the editor and the autosave that must not write under it.

methods.name: holder
methods.doc:
The user who holds a post's lock other than the one asking
(wp_check_post_lock): the lock's user, or the post's last editor when
