it names none, while it is newer than the window
(wp_check_post_lock_window, 150 seconds); 0 otherwise.

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\PostLookup
classes.doc: The post reads plugin code asks for by shape: a page by title, revisions, counts.

methods.name: idWhere
methods.doc:
The first post whose columns hold the values given, each as stored
(post_exists); null for none.
shapes: @param array<string, string> $columns column => value; only post_title, post_content, post_date, post_type and post_status

params.name: columns
params.doc: column => value; only post_title, post_content, post_date, post_type and post_status

methods.name: idByTitle
methods.doc: The id of a post with this title among the types, or null.

methods.name: revisionsOf
methods.doc: Revision rows newest first. @return list<array<string, mixed>>

methods.name: countByStatus
methods.doc: How many posts of a type there are per status.

methods.name: countAttachments
methods.doc: How many attachments there are per mime type.
shapes: @return array<string, int> mime type => count, plus 'trash'

methods.name: countByAuthor
methods.doc: How many posts an author has among the types and statuses.

methods.name: countsByAuthors
methods.doc:
Post counts for several authors at once, as stored (strings), for
those that have any.

methods.name: publishingAuthors
methods.doc: How many authors (up to a limit) have published posts of a type, for is_multi_author.

methods.name: countsByAuthor
methods.doc:
Post counts by author for wp_list_authors: the types' posts in the
statuses given, and the private ones of the viewer (an id, or -1 for
none) beside them.

methods.name: idsByAuthor
methods.doc: Every post id of an author.

methods.name: attachmentIdByFile
methods.doc: The attachment whose stored file path is the given one.

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\PostQuery
classes.doc:
WP_Query::get_posts as the reference runs it (probe wp-query-sql): the
variables parsed and handed to pre_get_posts, the clauses written piece by
piece, every filter a plugin may change them through in the reference's
order (suppress_filters keeps the ones it keeps), the request split into
an id query when that is cheaper, the count, a single post's status check
and preview, sticky posts on the home listing, and the results filters.
A lookup the engine can answer from what it has read (QueryAnswers) runs
every filter and no SQL, unless a plugin changes it.

constants.name: SHAPING
constants.doc: The hooks that shape the request: an engine answer stands only while none of them has a listener.

methods.name: run
methods.doc:
Runs a query object's variables and fills it in: the posts (or ids, or
id => parent), the request, the counts. Returns what get_posts returns.

params.name: wpdb
params.doc: the database object plugins see, so the request runs where their filters expect it

params.name: urlSearch
params.doc: the search string the URL carries, if any (a search from elsewhere is url-decoded)

methods.name: search
methods.doc:
A search's WHERE fragment, settling the search variables (the terms,
how many the string split into, the title matches its order ranks by).

methods.name: stopwords
methods.doc: The search stopwords, translated and filtered. @return list<string>

methods.name: prepare
methods.doc: Parses the variables, hands them to pre_get_posts, and reads the meta query from them.

methods.name: defaults
methods.doc: The defaults get_posts settles before it writes a clause. @param array<string, mixed> $q

methods.name: pageSize
methods.doc: posts_per_page from the option, showposts, an archive's own size or the feed's, and nopaging. @param array<string, mixed> $q

methods.name: clauses
methods.doc: Writes the clauses, in the reference's order. @param array<string, mixed> $q

methods.name: taxonomies
methods.doc: The tax query's clauses (not for a single post), a taxonomy archive's types, and the compatibility variables. @param array<string, mixed> $q

methods.name: searchOrder
methods.doc: A search's relevance order, ahead of the order asked for, when no other order is asked for. @param array<string, mixed> $q

methods.name: filtered
methods.doc: The clause filters, paging between the first two and the rest, and posts_selection. @param array<string, mixed> $q

methods.name: through
methods.doc: Each piece through its filter, then all seven through the clauses filter. @param array<string, string> $hooks

methods.name: paging
methods.doc: LIMIT for a listing that pages: the offset when one is given, the page's start otherwise. @param array<string, mixed> $q

methods.name: execute
methods.doc: Writes the request, runs it (or takes posts_pre_query's answer), and finishes the results. @param array<string, mixed> $q

methods.name: idsOnly
methods.doc: The ids (or id => parent) a query for them returns. @param array<string, mixed> $q

methods.name: select
methods.doc: Runs the request: ids first, then their posts, when the query can be split that way. @param array<string, mixed> $q

methods.name: answered
methods.doc:
The ids an engine answer gives, when the query is still the one the
engine wrote; null when it is not, or it has none.

methods.name: foundPosts
methods.doc: found_posts (from FOUND_ROWS() when the query paged, else the posts' count) and max_num_pages. @param array<string, mixed> $q

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\PostQueryParts
classes.doc:
The pieces of one WP_Query run as the reference builds them and hands
them to filters. The seven clause pieces stay untyped: a filter may hand
back anything, and the request is written from whatever it handed back.

constants.name: PIECES
constants.doc: The pieces posts_clauses and posts_clauses_request see, in their order.

properties.name: statusJoin
properties.doc: Whether an attachment's status follows its parent's (a taxonomy archive's attachments).

properties.name: postType
properties.doc: The post type the query settles on: a name, a list, `any`, or empty.

properties.name: statuses
properties.doc: The statuses asked for by name, which a single post's status check lets through. @var list<string>

methods.name: pieces
methods.doc: The seven pieces by name. @return array<string, mixed>

methods.name: take
methods.doc: Takes back the pieces a clauses filter returned; one it dropped becomes empty. @param array<array-key, mixed> $clauses

methods.name: request
methods.doc: The SELECT as the reference writes it, line breaks and all, for the given field list.

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\PostQueryResults
classes.doc:
What WP_Query does with its posts once it has them, as the reference does
it (probe wp-query-sql): a single post whose status is not public is
dropped unless the reader may see it (a draft its editor may preview, with
the_preview); sticky posts move to the front of the home listing's first
page, the ones it did not find fetched by a nested query; the_posts; and
the post objects, count and current post set.

methods.name: settle
methods.doc: Settles the posts a query found: status check, stickies, the_posts, then the count and the current post. @param array<string, mixed> $q

methods.name: singleStatus
methods.doc: A single post the reader may not see is dropped; a draft its editor may edit is a preview.

methods.name: visible
methods.doc: Whether the reader may see the first post in its status (a draft they may edit becomes a preview, dated now).

methods.name: stickies
methods.doc: Sticky posts to the front of the home listing's first page; those it did not find, fetched. @param array<string, mixed> $q

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\PostQueryStatus
classes.doc:
WP_Query's post type and status clause as the reference writes it (probe
wp-query-sql). Statuses asked for by name: the type clause, then the
statuses (any, less those excluded from search; private kept apart when
the query asks for readable posts; the user's own when they may not read
or edit others'; an attachment's parent's status for a taxonomy archive).
None asked for, on a listing: each queried type, sorted, with its public
statuses, the admin list's protected ones in the admin, and private ones
the signed-in user may read. A single post: the type clause alone.

methods.name: settleType
methods.doc:
Settles the post type the caps come from: a list of several types has
none (its caps are named for multiple_post_type), any other names one.

methods.name: append
methods.doc: Appends the type and status clause. @param array<string, mixed> $q

methods.name: typeWhere
methods.doc: The type clause, and whether there are no searchable types to give statuses to. @return array{0: string, 1: bool}

methods.name: cap
methods.doc: The cap a type's object names, or the one its name makes.

methods.name: named
methods.doc: Statuses asked for by name (or `any`), under the query's perm.

methods.name: listing
methods.doc: A listing with no statuses asked for: each type with the statuses its reader may see.

methods.name: privateStatuses
methods.doc: The private statuses a signed-in user sees in a type: all of them with the cap to read them, their own otherwise.

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\PostQueryTax
classes.doc:
The taxonomy side of WP_Query as the reference runs it (probe
wp-query-sql): the clauses its variables make (tax_query, taxonomy and
term, each taxonomy's query var, cat and the category__ lists, tag and the
tag__ lists), settled back into the variables; the post types a taxonomy
archive with no type searches; and the cat, category_name, tag_id,
taxonomy and term variables set from the terms queried.

methods.name: clauses
methods.doc: The tax query a set of variables makes, settling the variables it reads.

methods.name: postTypes
methods.doc:
The post types a taxonomy archive with no type searches: every
searchable type the queried taxonomies are registered for, one as a
string, several sorted, none as `any`.

methods.name: compat
methods.doc:
The compatibility variables the queried terms set: taxonomy and term
(or term_id) from the first taxonomy other than category and post_tag
when none is set, and cat, category_name and tag_id from those two.

methods.name: tag
methods.doc: The tag variable as tag_slug__in or tag_slug__and.

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\PostQueryWhere
classes.doc:
The WHERE fragments WP_Query writes from its variables, in the reference's
order and spacing (probe wp-query-sql): menu order, the legacy m date and
the date variables, a slug or a page path, ids, parents, a page id (which
replaces everything before it), authors, comment counts, mime types,
passwords, and comment and ping status. Each appends to the parts it is
handed and settles the variables it reads, as the reference leaves them.

methods.name: dates
methods.doc: Menu order, the m date, the date variables and the date_query. @param array<string, mixed> $q

methods.name: names
methods.doc:
The post a slug, a page path, an attachment slug, a name list, an id or
an id list names, and the parent; a post type's query var stands for
the name (the page path, for a hierarchical type).

methods.name: authors
methods.doc:
Authors (an author list's negatives become author__not_in, which wins
over author__in), an author slug, a comment count, and mime types. The
slug and mime clauses wait to follow the search.

methods.name: access
methods.doc: A password, or whether there is one, and comment and ping status. @param array<string, mixed> $q

methods.name: nameList
methods.doc: A name list, sanitized in place; the clause lists each name once, sorted. @param array<string, mixed> $q @param list<mixed> $names

methods.name: pagename
methods.doc: A page path: the page it finds (in a hierarchical type queried), unless it is the posts page. @param array<string, mixed> $q

methods.name: ids
methods.doc: An id or an id list, the parent or a parent list, and a page id that replaces all before it. @param array<string, mixed> $q

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\PostReads
classes.doc:
What WordPress's post functions tell about posts: a page's path and a
page by its path, a post's type, status and fields, whether it can be
viewed, when posts last changed, posts by query arguments and a post's
children and categories, the SQL that limits a query to what an author
may read, and the caches primed for a list of posts.

methods.name: pageUri
methods.doc: A page's path from its ancestors' slugs (get_page_uri), or false.

methods.name: pageByPath
methods.doc: A page by its path (get_page_by_path): one type looks among attachments too; a list looks among exactly its types.

methods.name: type
methods.doc: A post's type (get_post_type), or false.

methods.name: status
methods.doc: A post's status (get_post_status): an attachment's is its parent's (a trashed parent's from before the trash); false for none.

methods.name: field
methods.doc: One of a post's fields in a context (get_post_field), empty when there is none.

methods.name: publiclyViewable
methods.doc: Whether a post can be viewed by anyone (is_post_publicly_viewable): its type and its status both viewable.

methods.name: lastTime
methods.doc:
When a public post was last published or changed (_get_last_post_time),
in GMT, the site's time or the server's (with microseconds); false for
none or a question it cannot answer.

methods.name: lastDate
methods.doc: When a public post was last published (get_lastpostdate), as get_lastpostdate leaves it.

methods.name: lastModified
methods.doc: When a public post last changed or was published, the later (get_lastpostmodified), pre_get_lastpostmodified answering first.

methods.name: query
methods.doc:
Posts by query arguments (get_posts): five published posts by date
unless asked otherwise, numberposts read as posts_per_page, category,
include and exclude read as the query's own, stickies ignored, no rows
counted.

methods.name: children
methods.doc:
A post's children (get_children), the post being read's when none is
named, keyed by id, as objects or arrays.

methods.name: categories
methods.doc: A post's categories (wp_get_post_categories), their ids unless asked otherwise; empty on an error.

methods.name: mimeTypeWhere
methods.doc: The WHERE clause for MIME types (wp_post_mime_type_where), a wildcard or a list.

methods.name: byAuthorSql
methods.signature: byAuthorSql(mixed $type, mixed $full = true, mixed $author = NULL, mixed $publicOnly = false): string
methods.doc:
The SQL limiting posts to what may be read (get_posts_by_author_sql): an
author's own, the published, and the private ones the reader may read.

methods.name: primeAuthors
methods.doc: The posts' authors read into the caches together (update_post_author_caches), through cache_users, which a plugin may replace.

methods.name: prime
methods.signature: prime(mixed $ids, mixed $updateTermCache = true, mixed $updateMetaCache = true): void
methods.doc: Posts read into the caches together (_prime_post_caches): rows, and their meta and terms unless asked not to.

methods.name: updateCaches
methods.signature: updateCaches(mixed $posts, mixed $type = 'post', mixed $updateTermCache = true, mixed $updateMetaCache = true): void
methods.doc: A list of posts kept in the caches (update_post_caches): whole posts kept as they are, then primed.

methods.name: idFromUrl
methods.doc:
The post an address names (url_to_postid): a ?p= or ?page_id= id, else
with pretty permalinks a page by its path, a post whose own address it
is, or an attachment by its own; 0 for none.

methods.name: filledArguments
methods.doc:
The query arguments get_posts fills from its own: a status when none
is given (inherit for attachments, publish for the rest), the page
size from numberposts when no posts_per_page is, the category as cat.

methods.name: chosenPosts
methods.doc:
The posts get_posts names by id: the included ones, the page as large
as their number; else the ones left out; else none.

methods.name: termsPrimed
methods.doc:
The posts' terms as the reference primes them (update_object_term_cache):
one wp_get_object_terms for every post and taxonomy, by name, answered
from the rows just read unless a plugin shapes the terms query; the
posts' terms are kept as it leaves them.
shapes: @param list<array{0: int, 1: int, 2: string}> $rows term, post and taxonomy, by name

params.name: rows
params.doc: term, post and taxonomy, by name

methods.name: idList
shapes: @return array<int, int> ids from a list or a string, each once, as positive integers

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\PostRevisions
classes.doc:
A post's revisions as the reference's wp_save_post_revision keeps them
(probe revisions): only for a type that supports revisions and while
wp_revisions_to_keep allows any; compared with the latest revision
(wp_save_post_revision_check_for_changes, the revision fields with their
whitespace evened out, wp_save_post_revision_post_has_changed, whose
default also compares the revisioned meta); saved through wp_insert_post
and _wp_put_post_revision (whose default copies the revisioned meta);
then the oldest dropped past the limit, after
wp_save_post_revision_revisions_before_deletion.

constants.name: FIELDS
constants.doc: The revision fields' defaults: the title, the content and the excerpt.

methods.name: all
methods.doc:
A post's revisions (wp_get_post_revisions), newest first unless asked
otherwise, keyed by id (or a list of ids); none while its revisions are
switched off, unless check_enabled is false.

methods.name: toKeep
methods.doc:
How many revisions a post keeps (wp_revisions_to_keep): WP_POST_REVISIONS
(all, -1, when unset or true), none for a type without revision
support, then wp_revisions_to_keep and wp_{type}_revisions_to_keep.

methods.name: enabled
methods.doc: Whether a post keeps any revisions (wp_revisions_enabled).

methods.name: delete
methods.doc: A revision deleted (wp_delete_post_revision); anything but a revision is left alone, and nothing comes back.

methods.name: fields
methods.doc:
The fields a revision keeps (_wp_post_revision_fields), through
_wp_post_revision_fields; the filtered list is what the next call
starts from, as on the reference.

methods.name: data
methods.doc:
A revision's row (_wp_post_revision_data): the post's revision fields,
its parent, inherit, revision, its name, and the post's modified time
as its date.

methods.name: source
methods.doc:
A post as a revision's row is made from: its own fields, as an (array)
cast gives them.

methods.name: upgrade
methods.doc:
Revisions named before 3.6 brought up to date
(_wp_upgrade_revisions_of_post; probe revision-more), under the
post's lock (Runtime\OptionLock), let go when the renaming is done.
Newest first, each old revision takes its versioned name when its
name has the "{id}-revision" or "{id}-autosave" shape, and the author
of the old revision before it (the oldest keeps its own). Unless a
revision was already up to date, the post is then saved as a revision
as a save would save it. False while another upgrade holds the lock.

methods.name: save
methods.doc: The new revision's id, or null when none was called for.

methods.name: put
methods.doc:
The revision (or autosave) row _wp_post_revision_data made, written
through wp_insert_post, then _wp_put_post_revision; its id.

methods.name: version
methods.doc: The version a revision's name carries ("{id}-revision-v1" is 1); 0 for a name from before versions, or any other.

methods.name: versionedName
methods.doc: An old revision's name with its version: "{id}-revision" and "{id}-revision-2" become "{id}-revision-v1"; another shape stays as it is.

methods.name: changed
methods.doc: Whether the post differs from its latest revision in the revision fields, or a plugin says so.

methods.name: prune
methods.doc: The oldest revisions past wp_revisions_to_keep removed (autosaves stay).

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\PostSave
classes.doc:
A REST save's columns through the filters the reference's save runs
before it writes, in its order (probe post-insert-filters,
contracts/runtime.md "Saves plugins can change"): rest_pre_insert_{type}
over the prepared post; every column through its db context
(pre_post_* and *_save_pre, where kses and the custom-CSS strip sit) on
slashed text; wp_insert_post_empty_content, which refuses a post with no
content, title or excerpt; wp_insert_post_parent; for a post that is live,
the slug, made again from the filtered title when the request gave none,
through pre_wp_unique_post_slug, the bad-slug check and
wp_unique_post_slug; and wp_insert_post_data over the row. What a filter
changes is written. Without plugins loaded the columns are as given.

constants.name: DATA
constants.doc: The row wp_insert_post_data is handed, in its keys.

constants.name: FIELDS
constants.doc: A REST field and the column it fills in the prepared post.

constants.name: PREPARED
constants.doc: The prepared post's columns in the reference's order, each with the REST field that sends it (null: always there).

constants.name: NEW_POSTARR
constants.doc: The new post array wp_insert_post_parent is handed beside the whole one.

constants.name: DEFAULTS
constants.doc: wp_insert_post's defaults, in its order (the order its filters run in).

methods.name: filter
methods.signature: filter(array $columns, ?Minn\Content\PostRecord $before, array $body, Minn\Http\Request $request, string $type, Minn\Content\PostSlugs $slugs): array
methods.doc: The columns to write after the filters.
shapes: @param array<string, mixed> $columns what the engine settled: a new post's whole row, or an update's changes

params.name: columns
params.doc: what the engine settled: a new post's whole row, or an update's changes

params.name: slugs
params.doc: the rules a live post's slug is settled by

methods.name: sanitized
methods.doc:
wp_insert_post's array with its defaults filled in (ID 0 for a new
post), through sanitize_post's db context: slashed in, slashed out.

methods.name: refusesEmpty
methods.doc: wp_insert_post_empty_content over whether a type with an editor, a title and an excerpt has none of them. @param array<string, mixed> $sanitized

methods.name: parent
methods.doc: The parent through wp_insert_post_parent (whose default refuses a loop). @param array<string, mixed> $sanitized

methods.name: slugFilters
methods.signature: slugFilters(string $slug, int $id, string $status, string $type, int $parent, Minn\Content\PostSlugs $slugs): string
methods.doc:
A live post's slug through the reference's three filters:
pre_wp_unique_post_slug may settle it; otherwise it is made free in
its type's scope, the bad-slug filter judging the slug asked for when
nothing else has taken it; and wp_unique_post_slug has the last word.

methods.name: guidAndSlug
methods.doc:
The row's guid and slug as wp_insert_post settles them (probe
insert-defaults): an update keeps the guid it had, in its display
form, ignoring a new one asked for; a live post's slug goes through
the slug filters.

methods.name: keepsSlug
methods.doc: Whether a save leaves the slug as it is: a draft, a pending post, an auto-draft, a revision, a personal data request.

methods.name: data
methods.doc:
The row through wp_insert_post_data (wp_insert_attachment_data for an
attachment), handed slashed as the reference hands it and unslashed
back.

params.name: postId
params.doc: the post an update saves, 0 for a new one

methods.name: stored
methods.doc: The post as stored, its columns by name. @return array<string, mixed>

methods.name: prepared
methods.doc:
rest_pre_insert_{type} over the prepared post, built as the
reference's controller builds it: its id when it edits, the fields
the request named in the reference's order, the type always, both
dates and edit_date when either date was sent, page_template null.
rest_block_hooks_post_types sees it first. What
the filter changes or adds is kept; an error refuses the save.

methods.name: changed
methods.doc:
The columns to write: a new post's whole row as the filters left it;
an update's own changes plus whatever a filter changed from the row.

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\PostTags
classes.doc:
What the post template tags tell about a post (the one being read when
none is named): its id and title, whether a password stands before it,
whether comments and pings are open, how many comments it has, and its
featured image; each through the filter plugins hook there.

methods.name: time
methods.signature: time(mixed $format = 'U', mixed $gmt = false, mixed $post = NULL, mixed $translate = false): mixed
methods.doc:
When a post was published (get_post_time): a timestamp for "U" or
"G", else the date in the format, local or UTC (a GMT date not set
yet worked out from the local one), names translated when asked;
false for no post.

methods.name: modifiedTime
methods.signature: modifiedTime(mixed $format = 'U', mixed $gmt = false, mixed $post = NULL, mixed $translate = false): mixed
methods.doc: When a post last changed (get_post_modified_time), as get_post_time tells when it was published.

methods.name: authorMeta
methods.doc:
One of the author's fields (get_the_author_meta): the post's author
being read unless a user is named; ID as an integer, the user_ columns
by their short names, empty for none; as get_the_author_{field}
leaves it.

methods.name: authorPostsUrl
methods.doc: An author's archive address (get_author_posts_url): /author/{nicename} with pretty permalinks, its slash as user_trailingslashit leaves it, else ?author=; as author_link leaves it.

methods.name: titleAttribute
methods.doc:
A post's title made safe for an attribute (the_title_attribute), its
tags gone with those of before and after; printed unless echo is
false, null for no title.

methods.name: date
methods.doc: When a post was published, in the format given or the site's date format (get_the_date), as get_the_date leaves it; false for no post.

methods.name: passwordForm
methods.doc:
The password form (get_the_password_form), as the content shows it
before its paragraphs are made; a reader the post's own page sent back
with a password cookie set reads why above the field; as
the_password_form leaves it.

methods.name: id
methods.doc: The id of the post being read (get_the_ID), or false.

methods.name: title
passwordRequired
methods.doc: Whether a password stands before the post's content for this reader (post_password_required).

methods.name: commentsOpen
methods.doc: Whether comments are open on a post (comments_open).

methods.name: pingsOpen
methods.doc: Whether pings are open on a post (pings_open).

methods.name: thumbnailId
methods.doc: The id of a post's featured image (get_post_thumbnail_id), 0 for none, false for no post.

methods.name: hasThumbnail
methods.doc: Whether a post has a featured image (has_post_thumbnail).

methods.name: commentsNumber
methods.doc: How many comments a post has (get_comments_number), 0 for none.

methods.name: moment
methods.doc: A stored date as a timestamp for "U" or "G", else in the format (translated when asked); null for one that is not a date.

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\PostWrites
classes.doc:
Posts written as WordPress's post functions write them: a post stored
and changed (its columns through their filters, then its terms, meta and
template), published, sent to the trash and back, deleted with what
hangs off it, its terms and categories set, made sticky or not; each step
with the actions the reference fires in its order, and the cached rows
let go.

methods.name: insert
methods.signature: insert(mixed $postarr, mixed $wpError = false, mixed $fireAfterHooks = true): mixed
methods.doc:
A post stored or changed (wp_insert_post): its id, 0 or the error
when it cannot be; the revision is saved from wp_after_insert_post
when the after hooks fire.

methods.name: update
methods.signature: update(mixed $postarr = array ( ), mixed $wpError = false, mixed $fireAfterHooks = true): mixed
methods.doc:
A post changed (wp_update_post): the stored post under the given
fields, as the reference merges them; an attachment saved as one.

methods.name: delete
methods.doc:
A post deleted (wp_delete_post): a post or page to the trash first
unless forced or the trash is off; an attachment as one; otherwise
unstuck, its terms, children, revisions, comments and meta taken
away, then the row. The post, or what pre_delete_post answered.

methods.name: trash
methods.doc: A post to the trash (wp_trash_post): its status, time and slug kept for the way back; the post as it was, or false.

methods.name: untrash
methods.doc:
A post back from the trash (wp_untrash_post): to draft unless
wp_untrash_post_status says otherwise (an attachment to inherit), its
slug given back; the post as it was, or false.

methods.name: afterInsert
methods.doc: What plugins hear once a post and all it carries are saved (wp_after_insert_post).

methods.name: publish
methods.doc: A post published now (wp_publish_post), a floating date settled, with the save's actions.

methods.name: publishFuture
methods.doc: The publish_future_post event's work (check_and_publish_future_post): a scheduled post whose time has come goes out; one early is scheduled again.

methods.name: transitionStatus
methods.doc:
The status change announced (wp_transition_post_status). The named
hooks fire only for names that exist, so a stored status cannot forge
another action's name: {old}_to_{new} when the new status is
registered and the old one is too (or is "new"), {new}_{type} when the
new status and the post type are registered.

methods.name: setCategories
methods.signature: setCategories(mixed $postId = 0, mixed $categories = array ( ), mixed $append = false): mixed
methods.doc:
A post's categories set (wp_set_post_categories), as
PostInsert::categoryIds decides them; a lone blank changes nothing.

methods.name: setTerms
methods.signature: setTerms(mixed $postId = 0, mixed $terms = '', mixed $taxonomy = 'post_tag', mixed $append = false): mixed
methods.doc: A post's terms of a taxonomy set (wp_set_post_terms): a comma list split, a hierarchical taxonomy's terms by id.

methods.name: setTags
methods.doc: A post's tags set (wp_set_post_tags).

methods.name: stick
methods.doc: A post made sticky (stick_post), then post_stuck; nothing when it already is.

methods.name: unstick
methods.doc: A post no longer sticky (unstick_post), then post_unstuck; nothing when it was not.

methods.name: uniqueSlug
methods.signature: uniqueSlug(mixed $slug, mixed $postId, mixed $status, mixed $type, mixed $parent): mixed
methods.doc: A slug no other post holds (wp_unique_post_slug), through the reference's slug filters; drafts, pending posts and revisions keep theirs.

methods.name: suffixTrashed
methods.doc: Every trashed post holding a slug (but the one named) given the __trashed suffix, so a live post may take it (wp_add_trashed_suffix_to_post_name_for_trashed_posts).

methods.name: suffixTrashedPost
methods.doc: A post's slug given the __trashed suffix once, the slug it wanted kept (wp_add_trashed_suffix_to_post_name_for_post); the slug it now has.

methods.name: beforeSave
methods.doc: What plugins hear before a post's row is written: pre_post_insert for a new post, pre_post_update for one that exists. @param array<string, mixed> $data

methods.name: saved
methods.doc:
What plugins hear once a post's row and its own terms are written, in
the reference's order: the caches let go, the status transition, the
edit actions for an update, the save actions.

methods.name: deleteMeta
methods.doc: Each meta row of a post removed by its id, with the hooks of each.

methods.name: slugFromId
methods.doc: A live post left without a slug (no title to make one from) takes its id, made free. @param array<string, mixed> $columns

methods.name: freeSlug
methods.doc: A trashed post still holding the slug a save wants gives it up first, unless add_trashed_suffix_to_trashed_posts says no. @param array<string, mixed> $columns

methods.name: templateRefusal
inputs
methods.signature: inputs(int $id, array $postarr, string $type, string $status, mixed $update): void
methods.doc: The terms and meta a postarr carries beside the columns.

methods.name: template
methods.doc:
The page template a postarr asks for; false when it is not one the
theme offers.

methods.name: attachmentSaved
methods.doc:
An attachment's save ends as the reference's does: its file recorded,
then add_attachment, or edit_attachment and attachment_updated; no
save_post actions, and no wp_after_insert_post whatever the caller
asks (a REST save fires that itself).

methods.name: trashSaved
methods.doc: A trash or its undoing ends as the save it is: an attachment's, or a post's with its transition and wp_after_insert_post.

methods.name: remove
methods.doc: The row itself, between the delete actions, typed and untyped, and the caches let go after.

methods.name: inserter
methods.doc: The insert decisions, with the site's options, the user's capabilities and the date helpers handed in.

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\QueriedObject
classes.doc:
Which object a query is "about", read from its flags and variables: a term
(by id or slug), a post type, the posts page, the current post, or an
author. The caller materialises the record; this only decides where to look.

params.name: field
params.doc: 'id' or 'slug' (terms, authors); 'name' for a post type

methods.name: locate
methods.doc: The queried object the query vars and flags point at.
shapes: @param array<string, bool> $flags the query's is_* flags
@param callable(string): mixed $option a filtered option read

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\QueryAnswers
classes.doc:
Answers for queries the engine writes itself and already knows the result
of, from what it has read once this request: a template part's lookup
from the theme's saved templates, the theme's term from the same read. The
query still runs every filter the reference runs; only the database is
spared, and only while no plugin has changed the query (its variables, a
clause, the request), so a lookup a plugin steers runs as written.

methods.name: expect
methods.doc: Marks a query object as one the engine can answer, before it runs.

methods.name: take
methods.doc: The answer a query object was given, taken so it answers once; null for any other query.

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\QueryArgs
classes.doc:
Query arguments added to and taken from an address the way WordPress's
add_query_arg() and remove_query_arg() do, the current request's address
when none is given, and an action's nonce added to one.

methods.name: add
methods.doc:
An address with arguments added (add_query_arg): a key and value, or a
list of them, then the address (the request's when false or left
out). Values are URL-encoded; an empty one leaves its key bare, a
false or null one takes the key out.

methods.name: versioned
methods.doc:
A script's or style's address with its version, as the dependency
printers add it: the same address add_query_arg would give, its
query read without wp_parse_str's filter (probe: printing a
versioned script fires none on the reference).

methods.name: remove
methods.doc: An address with an argument, or each of a list, taken out (remove_query_arg); an empty list gives back what was given.

methods.name: withNonce
methods.doc: An address carrying a nonce for the action (wp_nonce_url), escaped for HTML.

methods.name: requestUri
methods.doc: The request's address as PHP was given it; a runtime built without one gives its request's path and query.

methods.name: with
methods.doc:
An address with the arguments set, its own query read through the
given step and encoded.

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\QueryFlags
classes.doc:
The conditional flags a set of query variables implies (is_single, is_archive,
is_home, ...), derived the way the reference's parse step derives them, plus
the variables after the integer casts that step applies.

shapes: @param array<string, bool> $flags only the flags that are on

params.name: flags
params.doc: only the flags that are on

methods.name: fill
methods.doc:
The variables with every one the reference fills given its empty
value: the template's keys up to search_columns (the ones after it are
get_posts' own, settled when the query runs).

methods.name: derive
methods.doc: The is_* flags the query vars amount to.
shapes: @param array<string, mixed> $vars the filled query variables
@param callable(string): mixed $option a filtered option read
@param array<string, mixed> $asked the query as it was given, before filling (a search is one that named s)

params.name: asked
params.doc: the query as it was given, before filling (a search is one that named s)

methods.name: customTaxonomyVar
methods.doc:
The first registered taxonomy (other than the two built-in ones) whose
query variable carries a value, as [taxonomy name, query var].

methods.name: sanitize
methods.doc:
The reference's clean-up of the free-form variables: m and the time
parts to digits, cat and author to id lists, names trimmed, an
over-long or non-scalar search dropped.

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\RecipientLocale
classes.doc:
An email written in its reader's language, as the reference writes each:
the send run inside switch_to_user_locale for the account it goes to (the
site's locale when the address belongs to none) and the locale restored
after. The facade binds how a switch is made (WP_Locale_Switcher).

methods.name: bind
methods.doc: How a switch is made (the facade's switch_to_user_locale and restore_previous_locale).

methods.name: forUser
methods.doc: What a send answers, run in a user's language (the site's for 0).

methods.name: forAddress
methods.doc: What a send answers, run in the language of the account an address belongs to.

methods.name: forSite
methods.doc: What a send to the site's address (admin_email) answers, run in its account's language.

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\Records
classes.doc:
Posts, terms and comments as WordPress hands them to plugins: found by
id (or the one being read), made from a row or an object, and given back
as the object, an associative array (ARRAY_A) or a list (ARRAY_N); and
whether a value is a list of errors.

methods.name: post
methods.doc:
A post (get_post): the one being read when none is named; a post
object as given; one made from a row or any other object (one without
an ID is a post of none); none for an array; else by id, a copy of the
cached one (what one plugin changes is not what the next reader sees).
Then put in the context asked for.

methods.name: term
methods.doc:
A term (get_term): an error for none or an unknown taxonomy; a term
object as given, one made from an object, else by id (null when there
is none). get_term and get_{taxonomy} filter the raw term, told its own
taxonomy; then it is put in the context asked for, on a copy of a term
the caller handed in.

methods.name: comment
methods.doc:
A comment (get_comment): the one being read for any empty id; a
comment object as given; one made from an object with a comment_ID;
else by id, its fields text as the database hands them over (null when
there is none), the row read once a request as a comment query keeps
it. Then get_comment.

methods.name: isError
methods.doc: Whether a value is a list of errors (is_wp_error); one that is is told to is_wp_error_instance.

methods.name: termNumbers
methods.doc: A term's numbers as integers, as the database's text would not give them.

methods.name: shaped
methods.doc: A record as the output asks: an associative array (ARRAY_A), a list (ARRAY_N), else the object.

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\Recovery
classes.doc:
Recovery from a fatal in someone else's code. When a plugin or theme
kills the boot of a request, the file it died in names it (or, when that
file is the engine's or core's, the first plugin or theme file the trace
passes through); the failure is noted, and the engine asks the site once
itself (check()): one request to the home page carrying nothing a visitor
chose. If that request fails at boot on the same extension, it is paused,
and the next request loads without it: the site comes back on its own
instead of staying down until a human reads the log. A visitor's request
never pauses anything by itself: a pause is a site-wide decision, and a
request's path, headers and their values are the visitor's to choose, so
an extension that fails on some input fails for that input alone.
Failures after boot (a route, a template) never pause anything; see
Failure::armRecovery().

The paused list is stored where WordPress stores it, in the same shape
(`paused_plugins` keyed by plugin file, `paused_themes` by stylesheet,
each holding type, file, line and message), so a site that ejects back
to WordPress finds the pause it left with. The strikes live in the
engine's own `minn_recovery_strikes` option.

constants.name: CHECK_OPTION
constants.doc: The engine's own check in flight: the extension it asks about, its token, when the token lapses.

constants.name: CHECK_HEADER
constants.doc: The header the engine's own check carries its token in.

constants.name: WINDOW
constants.doc: Seconds a strike is remembered: one check of the site per extension inside it.

constants.name: CHECK_TTL
constants.doc: Seconds a check's token is good for: one request to the site, no longer.

methods.name: inMode
methods.doc: Whether the site is in recovery mode (wp_is_recovery_mode): never, as the engine keeps no recovery-mode session; its own recovery pauses the failing plugin instead.

methods.name: blame
methods.doc:
The extension a file belongs to: a plugin as the active `folder/file.php`
whose folder holds the file (or the bare file of a single-file plugin),
a theme as its slug. The name is the one the loader checks against the
paused list, so a fatal deep inside a plugin's subfolders pauses the
plugin and not a folder nothing is called by. Anything outside the
plugin and theme folders belongs to nobody, and is never paused: a
fatal in the engine or in core is not a plugin's fault and pausing
something would not fix it. A symlinked plugin reports its real
location; the realpath map (real folder to the folder under plugins/)
brings it home first.
shapes: @param list<string>|null $active the active plugin files; read from the site when omitted

params.name: active
params.doc: the active plugin files; read from the site when omitted

methods.name: blameFailure
methods.doc:
The extension a failure belongs to: the file it died in, else the
first plugin or theme file its trace passes through, innermost first.
A plugin's hook that fails inside engine or core code (an engine call
it made, a core function) is still the plugin's failure.
shapes: @param list<string> $trace the files of the failure's stack frames, innermost first

params.name: trace
params.doc: the files of the failure's stack frames, innermost first

methods.name: pause
methods.doc:
Records an extension as paused. Returns false when it was already
paused, so a caller can tell a fresh failure from a repeat and only
notify once.
shapes: @param array{type: int, file: string, line: int, message: string} $error

params.name: error
params.shape: array{type: int, file: string, line: int, message: string}

methods.name: strike
methods.doc:
Notes a boot failure against an extension. True when one is already
noted inside the window, which is when the caller has asked the site
about it once already; the first is when it asks (check()). One time
is kept per extension, written only when it is new, so failing
requests never grow the option; it is not autoloaded.

methods.name: check
methods.doc:
Asks the site once about an extension a request saw fail at boot: a
token is kept for it, then one GET of the home page goes out carrying
the token and nothing a visitor chose (no body, no cookie, the headers
a browser sends; a fresh query steps past a page cache). If that
request fails at boot on the same extension, its own recovery pauses
it (confirmed()). The token is claimed, so of requests failing at
once only one asks. The address is the site's own, so its certificate
is not checked, as the reference sends its requests to itself (a
local certificate authority the server's own PHP does not know would
refuse it); the request carries nothing but a token good once, for a
minute. Null when the site answered or another request is asking,
else why not.

methods.name: confirmed
methods.doc:
Whether a request's token is the one check() kept for this extension
and still good. A matching token is spent, so it answers once; a
wrong one changes nothing and lapses with the minute.

methods.name: pausedPlugins
methods.doc: The plugins recovery mode has paused.

methods.name: pausedThemes
methods.doc: The themes recovery mode has paused.

methods.name: paused
methods.doc: The extensions of one kind ('plugin' or 'theme') recovery has paused.

methods.name: resumeKind
methods.doc: Lets every extension of one kind load again. Returns how many were released.

methods.name: resume
methods.doc: Lets an extension load again. Returns false when it was not paused.

methods.name: resumeAll
methods.doc: Lets everything load again, every strike forgotten as resume() forgets one's. Returns how many were released.

methods.name: storageFailure
methods.doc: Whether a failure's own file is the engine's database door or a storage drop-in.

methods.name: pluginFile
methods.doc:
The active plugin file a path under plugins/ belongs to: the entry in
the folder the path starts with, the bare file itself for a single-file
plugin, and the folder alone when no active entry claims it.
shapes: @param list<string> $parts the path segments under plugins/

methods.name: kept
methods.doc: The check check() keeps for the engine's own request, read past every cache.

methods.name: strikes
methods.doc:
The time each extension was first noted inside the window; a list an
older engine kept reads as its earliest time.

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\Refusal
classes.doc: A refused operation, the way plugin code expects to read it: a code, a message, optional data. The facade turns it into WP_Error.

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\Registered
classes.doc:
What is registered, looked up the way WordPress's lookups answer: post
types, post statuses and taxonomies by name, or listed by their flags (as
names or the objects); whether one exists, is hierarchical or viewable;
and the features a post type supports. A name that is not text or a
number finds nothing.

methods.name: postType
methods.doc: A post type's object (get_post_type_object), or null.

methods.name: postTypes
methods.doc:
The post types whose flags match (get_post_types): all of them (and),
any (or) or none (not), as names or as the shared objects, so a flag a
plugin changed on one is what the list reads.

methods.name: loadedPostTypes
methods.doc:
The objects of the post types whose flags all match, none before
plugins load: a caller with a fallback of its own uses it then.

methods.name: postTypeExists
methods.doc: Whether a post type is registered (post_type_exists).

methods.name: supports
methods.doc: Whether a post type supports a feature (post_type_supports).

methods.name: hierarchicalType
methods.doc: Whether a post type is hierarchical (is_post_type_hierarchical).

methods.name: viewableType
methods.doc: Whether a post type, by name or its object, can be viewed on the site (is_post_type_viewable), as the filter leaves it.

methods.name: status
methods.doc: A post status's object (get_post_status_object), or null.

methods.name: statuses
methods.doc: The post statuses whose flags match (get_post_stati), as names or objects.

methods.name: viewableStatus
taxonomy

classes.doc:
Post types, taxonomies, and statuses as plugin code registers and reads
them. The built-in set is data/registry.json, captured from the
reference; registrations derive their defaults the way the content
probe observed (contracts/fixtures/api/content.json).

methods.doc:
Makes the one object for each registered type and taxonomy and binds
$wp_post_types and $wp_taxonomies to them, as the reference shares
them: a plugin changing one (relabelling Posts) is heard by every
reader (probe type-object-sharing). Called once the facade classes
exist; later registrations make their own.

methods.doc:
The built-in types', taxonomies' and statuses' labels in the site's
language, as the reference registers them again on init: each label
asks for its own message (data/registry-labels.json, captured from the
reference), and a type's single-item template and a taxonomy's
archive template are named after the singular name. Rows and the
shared objects both take them; what a plugin set before init gives
way, as it does there.

methods.name: adoptPostType
methods.doc:
Takes a built post type as the registered one: the object
register_post_type made is the one every reader shares, and its
properties are the type's row. Registering again puts a new object in
the old one's place, as on the reference.

methods.doc: Takes the single-item template's name off a type registered again, its row with it, so the next registration names none either.

methods.name: labels
methods.doc:
A type's labels from its own (probe post-remaining): the labels of its
base type (page for a hierarchical type, post for any other) under the
type's own. A missing
name comes from the type's label, a missing singular name from the name,
the menu name from the name, all items from the menu name, archives from
all items, and the admin bar name from the singular name or else the
type's name; a type with a singular name also names its single-item
template.

methods.name: taxonomyLabels
methods.doc:
A taxonomy's labels from its own (probe taxonomy-remaining): derived as a
type's are, under the category labels for a hierarchical taxonomy or the
tag labels for any other; one that names no template takes "%s
Archives" with the singular name it ends up with.

methods.name: capabilities
methods.doc:
A type's capability names (probe post-remaining): the eight primitive
ones, the six more a mapped type uses, the type's own names merged over
them, and create_posts last, the edit capability unless named.

hierarchical one's]: post and page for types, tag and category for

Takes a built taxonomy as the registered one, the object every reader

An empty object filled with a row as registration left it, without
building it again (no filters, no defaults): the built-in types and
taxonomies. A built-in type's supports were taken in, so its object
has none of its own.

The labels a type or taxonomy gets from its own: a missing name from

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\RequestHeaders
classes.doc:
What WordPress's request functions say and send: the protocol the
request came over, a status line and the no-cache headers sent as plugin
code sends them, the origin a request names and whether it is allowed,
and whether the browser is a phone's.

methods.name: protocol
methods.doc: The protocol the request came over (wp_get_server_protocol): HTTP/1.1, 2, 2.0 or 3 as the server says, anything else HTTP/1.0.

methods.name: status
methods.doc:
A status line sent (status_header), through status_header; nothing for
a code without a reason phrase, outside a web request, or once the
head is out.

methods.name: fromServer
methods.doc:
A request's headers from server variables (WP_REST_Server::get_headers):
the HTTP_ ones without their prefix, CONTENT_TYPE, CONTENT_LENGTH and
CONTENT_MD5 as named, and REDIRECT_HTTP_AUTHORIZATION as AUTHORIZATION
when there is no HTTP_AUTHORIZATION.

methods.name: noCache
methods.doc: The no-cache headers sent now (nocache_headers); one set to false (Last-Modified) is taken off instead.

methods.name: origin
methods.doc: The origin a request names (get_http_origin) as PHP sees it, else the request's own, as http_origin leaves it.

methods.name: allowedOrigins
methods.doc:
The origins allowed to call (get_allowed_http_origins): the home and
site hosts over http and https, repeats dropped before
allowed_http_origins adds its own.

methods.name: allowedOrigin
methods.doc: The origin when it is one allowed (is_allowed_http_origin), '' otherwise, as allowed_http_origin leaves it.

methods.name: rawReferer
methods.doc: The referer as given (wp_get_raw_referer): the form's _wp_http_referer when it has one, else the Referer header, unslashed; false when neither.

methods.name: isMobile
methods.doc: Whether the browser is a phone's or a tablet's (wp_is_mobile), as wp_is_mobile leaves it.

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\RewriteRules
classes.doc:
The rewrite rules WordPress makes from its structures, as the reference
makes them (probes rewrite-generate, rewrite-rules), so plugins that
read, filter or add to them see the same list.

A structure is walked a directory at a time (one at a time only when
asked), each level that names something getting its rules: its feeds
and embed, its pages, its comment pages (for posts and pages), a static
front page's comment pages at the root, the endpoints placed there, and
the level itself; deepest level first. The level that names a post (a
name, an id, a page path, or a plugin post type's own tag) is the post's:
its embed and trackback, its feeds, pages and comment pages, its
endpoints and its attachments', then the post with its page number,
between the rules for attachments under it (by /attachment/ and, but for
a hierarchical type, directly). A tag nobody registered stays as written.

The full list is the plugins' top rules (each permastruct's rules join
them as they are made, and stay), the fixed files, then root, comments,
search, author and dates, then pages and posts (posts first unless the
structure begins ambiguously), then the plugins' bottom rules; each
section through its filter, the whole through generate_rewrite_rules and
rewrite_rules_array.

constants.name: TOP
constants.doc: The top rules the global object starts with: the REST routes, the sitemaps and Minn Admin's own address.

A date archive's query vars read as the post they name
(wp_resolve_numeric_slug_conflicts). Under a structure with %postname%
first, second or third, the year, month or day in that place is a slug;
when a post has it, was dated in the year (and month) the address gives,
and what follows the slug is one of its pages, the vars become that
post's name and page (0 for none). Anything else stays a date archive.

shapes: @param array{struct: string, ep_mask?: int, paged?: bool, feed?: bool, forcomments?: bool, walk_dirs?: bool, endpoints?: bool} $args

The rules as the engine itself would make them, in their stored form

The global object's top rules (REST, sitemaps, Minn Admin) and the

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\Runtime
classes.doc:
The WordPress runtime the engine offers plugin code: the procedural
facade under minn/wp-api/ plus the services it delegates to. One per
request; the facade reaches it through these statics.

constructor.doc:
The runtime for one request. Everything about the request itself
comes from the context; the fields below it are the same values,
kept as properties because plugin code reaches for them by name.

constants.name: CONTENT_DONE
constants.doc:
The the_content defaults the engine's own rendering has already done:
blocks, texturize, paragraphs, block hooks, and the image attributes.
Shortcodes run in their place in the chain (do_shortcode at 11), so a
shortcode a plugin's filter adds before then runs as on the reference,
and block markup a filter adds before do_blocks is rendered then. What
the engine has not done (an attachment's own link, smilies, the capital
P, insecure home addresses) runs with the plugins' own callbacks.

properties.name: db
properties.doc: The database door this request answers through.

properties.name: site
properties.doc: The site's options.

properties.name: request
properties.doc: The request being answered, absent on the command line.

properties.name: reader
properties.doc: Who reads this request; settled again (identify()) once plugins have said who the user is.

properties.name: capabilities
properties.doc: The capability engine.

properties.name: engineDir
properties.doc: The minn/ folder: the engine's own files.

properties.name: absPath
properties.doc: The site root with a trailing slash.

properties.name: version
properties.doc: The WordPress release whose contracts the runtime speaks.

properties.name: seams
properties.doc: The extension seams this request registered, once the front has loaded them.

properties.name: renderState
properties.doc: The counters and collected styles of everything rendered for this request.

properties.name: blockRenderer
properties.doc: The block renderer this request renders through.

methods.name: identify
methods.doc: The request's reader from now on: the user plugin code named through determine_current_user (Runtime\CurrentUser).

methods.name: useSeams
methods.doc: Holds the extension seams this request registered, so nothing static has to.

methods.name: seams
methods.doc: The extension seams, or null before the front has registered any (REST and the CLI never do).

methods.name: renderState
methods.doc: The render state for this request, made on first use: one set of counters for everything rendered.

methods.name: useRenderState
methods.doc: Makes a render state this request's, so a renderer that brought its own is the one the leaves read.

methods.name: blockRenderer
methods.doc: The block renderer for this request, made on first use over this request's own database door.

methods.name: boot
methods.doc:
Makes this request's runtime the one the facade sees and defines the
facade.

Deliberately does NOT start the facade's registries empty. A process
answering a second request would then have a fresh hook table that no
plugin can fill again: plugin files register their hooks as they are
included, and an include happens once per process. Until a plugin's
registrations can be replayed, a second boot inherits the first's
registries on purpose, which is why a worker runtime is not yet
something the engine claims (see contracts/runtime.md).

methods.name: current
methods.doc: The booted runtime; throws when there is none.

methods.name: booted
methods.doc: Whether the runtime is up.

methods.name: hooks
methods.doc: The hook registry.

methods.name: options
methods.doc: The options store.

methods.name: storeOptions
methods.doc:
The options store for a connection, made as soon as the request has
one (Engine::answer) and kept by the boot that follows: the reads made
while routing come from the same autoloaded list as everything after,
and Db::option() reads through it from then on.

methods.name: installing
methods.doc: Whether this request is installing (wp_installing()); false before a runtime boots.

methods.name: installingFlag
methods.doc: Whether this request is installing (wp_installing); given a value, it sets the flag and answers what it was.

methods.name: optionWritten
methods.doc: Tells the option store about a row the engine wrote behind it; nothing to do when no store was made.

methods.name: capture
methods.doc:
Runs an action and returns what it printed. Plugin callbacks may open
output buffers of their own during the action (a page post-processor
started in wp_head) or close one they think is theirs (the same plugin
in wp_footer); a sentinel buffer under the capture keeps the output
either way: extra buffers are flushed through their handlers into the
capture, and a capture closed early lands in the sentinel.

methods.name: classicContentFilter
methods.doc:
Classic content (no block markup) through the whole of the_content, as
the reference runs it: handed as written, core's defaults (embeds,
texturize, paragraphs, shortcodes, images) in their places, so a filter
before them is handed the stored text and what it adds is formatted
with the rest (runtime suite, "plain text a filter adds").

methods.name: blockContentFilter
methods.doc:
Block content through the_content as the reference runs it: handed as
written, so a filter before do_blocks is handed the stored block
markup; the engine's renderer in do_blocks's place, rendering what those
filters added with the rest and never parsing its own output again
(comment text a comments block prints stays text); then the rest of
the_content, the defaults the renderer has done left out. $rendered,
when given, takes the rendering at once (the engine's extension seams).

methods.name: contentFilter
methods.doc: Content the engine rendered itself, through the_content for everything else hooked there.

methods.name: cache
methods.doc: The object cache.

methods.name: textDomains
methods.doc: The text domains loaded for this request.

methods.name: locales
methods.doc: The locales this request switched into.

methods.name: shortcodes
methods.doc: The shortcode registry.

methods.name: scriptModules
methods.doc: The script modules registry.

methods.name: newScriptModules
methods.doc: A script modules registry of its own, as each new WP_Script_Modules keeps (probe script-modules-printing).

methods.name: interactivity
methods.doc: The interactivity API.

methods.name: blockTemplates
methods.doc: The registered block templates.

methods.name: registry
methods.doc: The post types, taxonomies, and statuses.

methods.name: postQuery
methods.doc: A fresh post query over the runtime's registry.

methods.name: get
methods.doc: A per-request state value.

methods.name: set
methods.doc: Sets a per-request state value.

methods.name: remember
methods.doc: A per-request state value, made once by the given callable the first time it is asked for (a facade class's single instance).

methods.name: isSecure
methods.doc: Whether the request is over HTTPS.

methods.name: contentDir
methods.doc: wp-content under the site root.

methods.name: facadeLoaded
methods.doc: Whether the facade's functions and classes are defined yet.

methods.name: loadFacade
methods.doc: Defines the facade functions once; safe to call again.

methods.name: loadPluggables
methods.doc:
The pluggable functions, once the plugins have had their chance to
define their own: each is defined only where no plugin did. The plugin
loader calls this before plugins_loaded; a boot that loads no plugins
calls it straight away. They are declared from the webroot's
wp-includes/pluggable.php, where the reference declares them, when the
copy there is this engine's (Pluggables).

methods.name: reset
methods.doc: Fresh per-request state, for suites.

methods.name: loadObjectCacheDropin
methods.doc:
A site's object-cache.php drop-in, before the facade defines its own
cache functions: the drop-in's functions and WP_Object_Cache win, and
the facade fills in only what it left out. Loaded once per process,
unless enable_loading_object_cache_dropin (asked of the hooks added
before boot, as the reference asks it whether or not there is a file)
says no.

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\SafeUrls
classes.doc:
Whether an address is one the site may fetch (wp_http_validate_url): an
http or https address that survives the protocol check unchanged, whose
host is not a private or reserved one unless it is the site's own or
http_request_host_is_external lets it through, on a safe port
(http_allowed_safe_ports). The address comes back as it was, or false.

methods.name: validated
methods.doc: The address when it may be fetched, else false.

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\ScriptLoading
classes.doc:
How a script may load, as the reference decides it (probe
dependencies-classes). A script keeps its own strategy (defer or async)
unless it has inline code after it, which makes it blocking, or an
enqueued dependent (however deep, through dependents that are themselves
enqueued) loads more strictly: blocking before defer before async. Its
fetch priority rises to the highest among those dependents: low, then
auto, then high. A delayed script that cannot be delayed (inline code
after it) waits for the footer when nothing enqueued depends on it. The
values a script may be given are checked here too.

methods.name: refusal
methods.doc:
Why a strategy or fetch priority value is refused, as the notice the
reference gives; null when the value is fine (empty is fine).
shapes: @return array{0: string, 1: string}|null the message and the version

methods.name: strategy
methods.doc: The strategy a script loads with: 'defer', 'async', or '' for blocking. @param array<string, true> $checked

methods.name: heldForFooter
methods.doc:
Whether the head pass holds a script for the footer: one that asked to
be delayed but has inline code after it, with nothing enqueued that
depends on it.

methods.name: priority
methods.doc: A script's own fetch priority and the one it loads with. @return array{0: string, 1: string}

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\ScriptModules
classes.doc:
The script modules registry: registrations with typed dependencies, the
queue, and the four things a page prints from it (the import map, module
preloads, the module tags split head/footer, and per-module JSON data).
Behaviour pinned by the script-modules probe fixture.

shapes: @param Closure(string, string|false|null): string $url turns a src and version into the printed URL
@param Closure(string, array<string, mixed>): array<string, mixed> $data applies the module data filter

params.name: url
params.doc: turns a src and version into the printed URL

methods.name: register
methods.signature: register(string $id, string $src, array $deps, string|false|null $version, array $args): void
methods.doc: Registers a module by id.

methods.name: enqueue
methods.signature: enqueue(string $id, string $src, array $deps, string|false|null $version, array $args): void
methods.doc: Queues a module, registering it when a source is given.

methods.name: dequeue
methods.doc: Removes a module from the queue.

methods.name: deregister
methods.doc: Forgets a module.

methods.name: setFetchpriority
methods.doc: Sets a module's fetch priority.

methods.name: moveToFooter
methods.doc: Moves a module to the footer or the head.

methods.name: moveToHead
methods.doc: Prints a module in the head; false when it is not registered.

methods.name: queue
methods.doc: The module ids queued.

methods.name: registered
methods.doc: One registered module, or null.
shapes: @return array{src: string, version: string|false|null, dependencies: list<array{id: string, import: string}>, in_footer: bool, fetchpriority: string}|null

methods.name: markedForEnqueue
methods.doc:
The queued modules that are registered, in queue order, each as
registered(): what the reference's get_marked_for_enqueue() answers,
a module whose dependency is missing included.
shapes: @return array<string, array{src: string, version: string|false|null, dependencies: list<array{id: string, import: string}>, in_footer: bool, fetchpriority: string}>

methods.name: dependencyRecords
methods.doc:
The registered dependencies of some modules, following the given
import types, each as registered() (get_dependencies()).
shapes: @return array<string, array{src: string, version: string|false|null, dependencies: list<array{id: string, import: string}>, in_footer: bool, fetchpriority: string}>

methods.name: source
methods.doc: A registered module's address as the page loads it (get_src()); '' for one not registered.

methods.name: printImportMap
methods.doc: The import map script tag.

methods.name: printPreloads
methods.doc:
The modulepreload links: the queued modules' static dependencies not
queued themselves, each after its own (depth first, in queue order),
fetched at the priority priorities() gives, its own named beside it
when that differs.

methods.name: printHead
methods.doc: The head's module tags.

methods.name: printFooter
methods.doc: The footer's module tags.

methods.name: printData
methods.doc: The script-module-data tags.

methods.name: printA11y
methods.doc: The a11y module's tag, once.

methods.name: queuedInOrder
methods.doc:
The queued modules in the order they print: each after the queued
modules it imports, statically or dynamically, through any that are
not queued (depth first, in queue order), as the reference prints them
(probe script-modules-printing).

methods.name: priorityOf
methods.doc:
The priority a module is fetched at (probe script-modules-printing):
the highest (high, then auto, then low; none named is auto) of the
queued modules among it and those that import it, statically or
dynamically, directly or through others; its own when none is queued.
Who imports a module is remembered from the first time it is asked
(dependentsOf), as the reference remembers it.

methods.name: dependentsOf
methods.doc:
The registered modules that import one, statically or dynamically:
worked out the first time it is asked and kept for the rest of the
request, so a module registered after that is not among them, as on
the reference.

methods.name: priorityAttributes
methods.doc:
A module tag's priority attributes: fetchpriority unless it is fetched
at auto, and data-wp-fetchpriority naming its own when that differs
and is not auto.

methods.name: tellMissing
methods.doc:
A queued module whose dependencies are not all registered is told
once, as the page first prints its module tags or preloads, not as it
registers (a dependency may be registered later).

methods.name: dependenciesFirst
methods.doc:
The modules' registered dependencies of the import types given (static
unless asked), each after its own: depth first, in the order the
modules and their dependencies are given.

methods.name: marked
methods.doc: Queued modules that are registered with every dependency registered, in queue order.

methods.name: dependencies
methods.doc:
Every registered dependency of the given modules, following only the
given import types: the modules' own dependencies in declaration
order, then theirs, a level at a time (probe script-modules-private).

methods.name: urlOf
methods.doc: A module's address with its version, as plugins may change it (script_module_loader_src).

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\ScriptPack
classes.doc:
The site-supplied script pack: the `wp-*` JavaScript packages the engine
does not reimplement, which a few plugins' front ends need (WooCommerce's
block cart and checkout are the reason it exists).

These packages are GPL, so the engine never ships them: the SITE installs
them into its own `wp-content`, the way it installs a language pack, and
the engine registers the handles only when they are actually there. A
site owner adding GPL files to a site that already runs GPL plugins is
not the engine distributing GPL; nothing under `minn/` changes.

The engine's own MIT packages under `minn/assets/wp` always win: the pack
fills the gaps around them, it does not replace them.

constants.name: RELATIVE_DIR
constants.doc: Under the site's wp-content, so backups and migrations carry it.

constants.name: VENDOR
constants.value: array (   'lodash' =>    array (   ),   'moment' =>    array (   ),   'react' =>    array (   ),   'react-dom' =>    array (     0 => 'react',   ),   'react-jsx-runtime' =>    array (     0 => 'react',   ),   'regenerator-runtime' =>    array (   ),   'wp-polyfill' =>    array (   ),   'wp-polyfill-dom-rect' =>    array (   ),   'wp-polyfill-element-closest' =>    array (   ),   'wp-polyfill-fetch' =>    array (   ),   'wp-polyfill-formdata' =>    array (   ),   'wp-polyfill-inert' =>    array (   ),   'wp-polyfill-node-contains' =>    array (   ),   'wp-polyfill-object-fit' =>    array (   ),   'wp-polyfill-url' =>    array (   ), )
constants.doc:
The vendor handles WordPress registers outside the packages manifest
(captured from the reference). `moment` matters as much as `react`:
one unregistered handle anywhere in a dependency tree drops every
script above it, which is how a missing moment silently cost the
whole WooCommerce cart bundle.

methods.name: dir
methods.doc: Where the script pack lives under wp-content.

methods.name: installed
methods.doc: Whether the script pack is on disk.

methods.name: handles
methods.doc:
Every handle the pack can register: the packages manifest keyed by
`name.js` becomes `wp-name`, plus the three vendor handles. A handle
whose file is missing from the pack is skipped rather than
registered against a 404.
shapes: @return array<string, array{file: string, deps: list<string>, ver: string}>

methods.name: installFromTree
methods.doc:
Copies the packages out of a WordPress tree (or an unpacked core
download) into the site's pack directory. Only the built JavaScript
and the manifest are taken, and only from the paths they live at, so
a wrong source folder copies nothing rather than something odd.

methods.name: remove
methods.doc: Removes the pack; the engine's own packages keep working without it.

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\Shortcodes
classes.doc:
The shortcode registry plugin code fills with add_shortcode, and the
expansion do_shortcode performs: [tag attrs], [tag attrs/], [tag]…[/tag]
(the first closing tag wins; content is not expanded again), [[tag]] as
the literal, unregistered tags left as written.

constants.name: ATTRIBUTES
constants.doc: The attribute pattern shortcode_parse_atts reads by (get_shortcode_atts_regex).

methods.name: atts
methods.doc:
A shortcode's attributes over its defaults (shortcode_atts): only the
names the defaults have, the given value else the default; through
shortcode_atts_{shortcode} when the shortcode is named.

methods.name: tags
methods.doc:
The registry itself, by reference, so the $shortcode_tags global plugin
code reads and copies is this array and not a snapshot of it.

methods.name: add
methods.doc:
Registers a shortcode. Its callback is kept as given, callable or not
yet: a plugin may name a class it declares further down its file, and
the reference only asks whether the callback can be called when the
shortcode runs.

methods.name: register
methods.doc:
A shortcode added as add_shortcode() adds it: an empty name, or one
with a space or a reserved character, is refused with a notice.

methods.name: remove
methods.doc: Forgets a shortcode.

methods.name: removeAll
methods.doc: Forgets every shortcode.

methods.name: has
methods.doc: Whether a shortcode is registered.

methods.name: all
methods.doc: Every shortcode with its callback.
shapes: @return array<string, mixed> every registered tag and its handler, to restore after a narrowed run

methods.name: restore
methods.doc: Replaces the registry, after a save-and-restore.

methods.name: names
methods.doc: Every shortcode name.

methods.name: unautop
methods.doc: Text with each shortcode that stands alone in a paragraph let out of it (shortcode_unautop); as given with none registered.

methods.name: pattern
methods.doc: The regex matching the registered shortcodes, or null for none.

methods.name: apply
methods.doc:
Content with its shortcodes run (do_shortcode, probe shortcode-run):
only the registered names the text holds; inside HTML tags first
(inTags: run, or with 'escape' as with ignore_html, left alone),
then in the text, each through run(); the brackets set aside as
entities come back at the end. Images rendered meanwhile see the
do_shortcode context.

methods.name: run
methods.doc:
One matched shortcode (do_shortcode_tag): [[tag]] gives the tag as
written; otherwise pre_do_shortcode_tag may answer, or the callback
runs with the attributes, the content ("" when it closes itself) and
the name, and do_shortcode_tag sees the output in its brackets.

methods.name: inTags
methods.doc:
Shortcodes inside HTML tags (do_shortcodes_in_html_tags), run before
the text: a quoted attribute value's shortcode runs and the attribute
is judged again by kses, kept when anything is left; an unquoted one
(or one standing as a name or as the tag) runs as written. Comments,
CDATA and, with 'escape', every tag are left alone. Brackets left in a
tag (and entities already written for them) are set aside so the text
pass cannot reach them.

methods.name: strip
methods.doc:
Content with its shortcodes taken out (strip_shortcodes): the names
strip_shortcodes_tagnames leaves, never inside a tag; [[tag]] gives
the tag as written.

methods.name: stripped
methods.doc: One matched shortcode taken out (strip_shortcode_tag): its outer brackets stay, [[tag]] gives the tag. @param array<int, string> $m

methods.name: parse
methods.doc:
Shortcode attribute text as an array (shortcode_parse_atts): no-break
and zero-width spaces read as spaces; name=value pairs (names lower
case) and bare values in order, each a token followed by whitespace
or the end, backslash escapes undone; a value holding "<" that is not
whole tags becomes "".

methods.name: present
methods.doc: The names among those given that the text opens a bracket with.

methods.name: attributesRun
methods.doc: A tag's attributes with their shortcodes run, from elementParts().

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\SiteInfo
classes.doc:
What WordPress tells about the site (get_bloginfo): its name and tagline,
its addresses and feeds', the theme's stylesheet and folders, the admin
address, the charset and content type, the version, the language and
its direction; and a feed's address.

methods.name: get
methods.doc:
One fact about the site (get_bloginfo), its name when none is asked;
for display through bloginfo_url (an address) or bloginfo.

methods.name: rss
methods.doc: One fact about the site for a feed (get_bloginfo_rss): escaped whole, tags included, through get_bloginfo_rss.

methods.name: feedLink
methods.doc:
A feed's address (get_feed_link): the default feed bare, through
feed_link handed '' for it; its ?feed= form without pretty permalinks.

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\SiteOptions
classes.doc:
The network's options, as a single site keeps them: options stored not
to autoload, with the network layer's own hooks around them, told the
network asked for (the current one, 1, when none is).

methods.name: get
methods.signature: get(mixed $option, mixed $default = false, mixed $networkId = NULL): mixed
methods.doc:
A network option (get_network_option, get_site_option):
pre_site_option_{name} and pre_site_option may answer first,
default_site_option_{name} sets its default, site_option_{name} has
the last word.

methods.name: add
methods.doc: A new network option (add_network_option, add_site_option), stored not to autoload.

methods.name: update
methods.doc: A network option changed (update_network_option, update_site_option); one not there yet is added.

methods.name: delete
methods.doc: A network option removed (delete_network_option, delete_site_option).

methods.name: network
methods.doc: The network asked for, else the current one: Minn is one network, 1.

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\SiteTime
classes.doc:
Time as the site keeps it: its timezone (the named one, else the UTC
offset), now in that zone or in UTC, a moment written in the site's
language, and a stored date read back in a format.

methods.name: zoneName
methods.doc: The site's timezone as text (wp_timezone_string): its name, else its offset as +HH:MM.

methods.name: zone
methods.doc: The site's timezone (wp_timezone).

methods.name: now
methods.doc:
Now (current_time): a timestamp for "timestamp" or "U" (the site's
offset added unless in UTC), a database date for "mysql", else the
format given, in the site's zone or UTC.

methods.name: toGmt
methods.doc: A date in the site's zone written in UTC (get_gmt_from_date); the epoch for one that is not a date.

methods.name: fromGmt
methods.doc: A date in UTC written in the site's zone (get_date_from_gmt); the epoch for one that is not a date.

methods.name: format
methods.signature: format(mixed $format, mixed $timestamp = NULL, mixed $timezone = NULL): mixed
methods.doc: A moment written in a format, its names in the site's language (wp_date), as the filter leaves it.

methods.name: fromStored
methods.doc:
A stored date in a format (mysql2date): false for none or one that is
not a date; "G" and "U" are timestamps (G with the site's offset); the
names translated unless asked not to be.

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\SiteUrls
classes.doc:
The site's own addresses as WordPress builds them: the home and site
addresses, the admin's, wp-includes', the sign-in and sign-out pages' (each with its
scheme settled and its filter run), whether the request came over HTTPS,
