the switch that forces the admin onto it, and the trailing slash the
permalink structure asks for.

methods.name: secure
methods.doc: Whether this request came over HTTPS (is_ssl): the engine's request when there is one, else the server variables.

methods.name: forceSslAdmin
methods.doc: Whether the admin is forced onto HTTPS (force_ssl_admin, FORCE_SSL_ADMIN); given a value, it sets the switch and answers what it was.

methods.name: withScheme
methods.doc:
An address in a scheme (set_url_scheme): http, https or relative when
asked for; https for the admin, sign-in and RPC ones over HTTPS or with
the admin forced; otherwise the request's. Then set_url_scheme.

methods.name: home
methods.signature: home(mixed $path = '', mixed $scheme = NULL, mixed $blogId = NULL): string
methods.doc: The home address with a path (get_home_url, home_url): in the request's scheme unless http, https or relative is asked for.

methods.name: site
methods.signature: site(mixed $path = '', mixed $scheme = NULL, mixed $blogId = NULL): string
methods.doc: The site (WordPress) address with a path (get_site_url, site_url).

methods.name: registration
methods.doc: Where registration starts (wp_registration_url): the sign-in page's register action, through register_url.

methods.name: admin
methods.doc: An address in the admin (get_admin_url, admin_url).

methods.name: selfAdmin
methods.doc: An address in the current admin (self_admin_url): the site's admin on a single site.

methods.name: content
methods.doc: An address in wp-content (content_url).

methods.name: customize
methods.doc: The Customizer's address, a theme to preview named (wp_customize_url), escaped.

methods.name: includes
methods.doc: An address in wp-includes (includes_url).

methods.name: login
methods.doc: The sign-in page (wp_login_url), told where to go after and whether to ask again, as login_url leaves it.

methods.name: logout
methods.doc: The sign-out address (wp_logout_url), its nonce after the action and where to go after, as logout_url leaves it.

methods.name: trailing
methods.doc:
An address ending as the permalink structure asks (user_trailingslashit):
with a slash when the rewrite object (or the structure) uses them,
without one otherwise; then user_trailingslashit.

methods.name: joined
methods.doc: A base address with a path after a slash, unless the path is empty, not text, or climbs ("..").

methods.name: tail
methods.doc: A path to append to an address that already ends in its folder's slash.

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\StoredObjects
classes.doc:
The classes a stored blob may name and come back as. The serialized
reader never instantiates by itself; the facade registers one factory per
value class it owns (WP_Post, WP_Term, WP_Comment), and any other class
comes back as itself only when it is plain data: a class that exists,
written in PHP, that runs nothing as it is revived or let go (no
__wakeup, __unserialize, __destruct or __set, not Serializable), so no stored
blob can make code run (PHP object injection). Plugins keep settings in
such objects (WooCommerce PayPal Payments does) and read them back typed,
as the reference revives them. Anything else stays a stdClass of its
properties.

constants.name: WRAPPERS
constants.doc: PHP's array wrappers a stored record may name, by lower-cased class name.

methods.name: maybeDecode
methods.doc:
A stored value read back (maybe_unserialize): serialized data decoded,
its objects revived by the registered factories; anything else, or
data that does not decode, as given.

methods.name: register
methods.doc: Registers what a record naming this class becomes.

methods.name: reviver
methods.doc: The reviver the serialized reader takes: PHP's array wrappers rebuilt, a factory's object, a plain data object, or the properties as they are.

methods.name: knows
methods.doc: Whether a factory is registered for the class.

methods.name: reset
methods.doc: Forgets every factory, for suites.

methods.name: plain
methods.doc:
A plain data object revived from its stored properties, as PHP's own reader
would, without its constructor: each property set in the scope of the
class that declares it (a parent's private one by its owner's name, a
readonly one where it may be initialized). Null for a class that is not
plain data, for the engine's own classes, or when a value does not fit
a typed property.
shapes: @param list<array{0: int|string, 1: mixed}> $pairs the stored names and values

methods.name: owner
methods.doc:
The class whose scope sets a stored property, and the property's name:
"\0Owner\0name" is Owner's private one, "\0*\0name" a protected one,
any other name the class's own (or a parent's, where it is declared).

methods.name: arrayWrapper
methods.doc:
PHP's own array wrappers, stored as their four numbered parts (flags,
storage, member properties, iterator class), rebuilt through their
constructors so nothing else runs. Plugins keep settings in them
(CleanTalk does), and the reference reads them back as the real class;
written back, they serialize to the same bytes. One wrapping an object,
or carrying member properties, stays a record of its parts.

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\SymbolGap
classes.doc:
The part of the reference's interface the runtime does not answer: names in
data/api-names.json that no facade file defines. It is the whole input the
symbol gate needs, so it can be exported to JSON and carried to a machine
that holds plugin source but no engine, which is how the catalogue-wide
compatibility scan runs.

shapes: @param array<string, true> $functions lower-cased function names the runtime lacks
@param array<string, true> $classes lower-cased class, interface, trait, and enum names it lacks
@param array<string, true> $known lower-cased function names in the reference's interface, lacking or not
@param array<string, true> $pluggable lower-cased pluggable functions the runtime defines after the plugins load

params.name: functions
params.doc: lower-cased function names the runtime lacks

params.name: classes
params.doc: lower-cased class, interface, trait, and enum names it lacks

params.name: known
params.doc: lower-cased function names in the reference's interface, lacking or not

params.name: pluggable
params.doc: lower-cased pluggable functions the runtime defines after the plugins load

methods.name: ofLoadedFacade
methods.doc:
Reads the reference's interface and subtracts everything the loaded facade
defines. A plugin may define a name as it loads, so each call asks again,
but only about the names still lacking: a name once defined stays defined,
and asking about all four thousand for every plugin was a cost of its own.

methods.name: ofShippedFacade
methods.doc:
The gap read from the engine's own files without loading them, for a
machine that has the engine but runs no site with it yet (preflight): a
name counts as defined when a facade file declares it.

methods.name: fromFile
methods.doc: The gap read from its JSON file.

methods.name: lacksFunction
methods.doc: Whether the runtime lacks a function.

methods.name: defines
methods.doc:
Whether the runtime already defines a function of the reference's
interface, so a plugin declaring it again without a guard would fail
to compile. The pluggable functions are not counted: the runtime
defines those after the plugins load, each only where no plugin did.

methods.name: lacksClass
methods.doc: Whether the runtime lacks a class.

methods.name: json
methods.doc: The gap as JSON.

methods.name: typeExists
methods.doc: Whether a class, interface, trait or enum of this name is defined.

methods.name: declaredIn
methods.doc:
The global functions and the classes (with their namespace) one file
declares, lower-cased; a method, a closure and an anonymous class are
not declarations.

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\SymbolTable
classes.doc:
What a folder's PHP names, collected while its tokens are read: the
functions it calls, the classes it references, and what it declares or
guards itself, so the gate can subtract those before judging it.

methods.name: call
methods.doc: Notes a function called.

methods.name: classRef
methods.doc: Notes a class referenced.

methods.name: declare
methods.doc: Notes a function the folder declares, a method included: a call by that name is not a need.

methods.name: declareGlobal
methods.doc: Notes a function declared in the global scope, which the runtime must not already define.

methods.name: declareClass
methods.doc: Notes a class the folder declares.

methods.name: guard
methods.doc: A name an existence check protects: function_exists, class_exists, defined, and the rest.

methods.name: toArray
methods.doc: The table as the gate reads it.
shapes: @return array{calls: list<string>, classes: list<string>, declared: array<string, true>, declaredGlobal: array<string, true>, declaredClasses: array<string, true>, guarded: array<string, true>, truncated: bool}

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\Symbols
classes.doc:
A static read of what a plugin's PHP calls: global functions and classes
it uses but does not itself declare, minus the ones it guards with
function_exists() or class_exists(). Checked against what the runtime
provides, this decides whether a plugin loads at all.

The read is cached in the minn_runtime_symbols option, keeping only the
reference's own names (all a verdict reads). An entry is trusted while
the folder's fingerprint (its own time and its top-level files' newest)
holds, for up to FULL_CHECK_EVERY seconds; then the whole folder is
walked again, as an update replaces it. Installing, updating or
activating a plugin walks its folder at once (recheck()). Walking every
folder on every request cost hundreds of milliseconds on a site with
many plugins.

constants.name: MAX_FILES
constants.doc:
The most PHP files a folder's walk reads; a folder past it is not loaded, as its needs are not all known.
WPML is 7,080 (64 MB at its peak, once, on activation); the next of the 215 most-run plugins is under 4,800.

constants.name: READER
constants.doc: Bumped whenever the token reader changes, so every cached scan is made again.

constants.name: FULL_CHECK_EVERY
constants.doc: How long a cached entry is trusted on its fingerprint alone before the folder is walked again.

constants.name: GIVE_UP_AFTER
constants.doc: A walk begun this long ago that never finished ran out of time or memory: its folder is held back instead of walked again on every request.

methods.name: missing
methods.doc: What a plugin folder needs that the runtime lacks, cached by mtime.
shapes: @return array{functions: list<string>, classes: list<string>, redeclares: list<string>, files: int, truncated: bool}

methods.name: recheck
methods.doc:
The folder is walked again at its next check instead of trusted on its
fingerprint: an install, an update or an activation never waits out
the window. The walk still keeps the cached read when nothing changed.

methods.name: redeclaresIn
methods.doc:
The functions one file declares in the global scope, unguarded, that the
loaded runtime already defines: including that file would not compile.

methods.name: missingAgainst
methods.doc:
The same read against an exported gap instead of the running engine, so a
folder can be judged with no database, no options, and no facade loaded.
shapes: @return array{functions: list<string>, classes: list<string>, redeclares: list<string>, files: int, truncated: bool}

methods.name: survey
methods.doc:
What a folder needs and what it reaches that Minn answers with nothing,
in one read, for a machine judging a site before the engine runs it
(preflight): the gate's verdict against the gap given, and the dead
ends it calls (the wp-admin screens, the editors, the Customizer,
XML-RPC, what was left out), by area. A call the folder guards or
answers itself is not counted, as the gate counts it.
shapes: @param array{functions?: array<string, string>, classes?: array<string, string>} $deadEnds name => area, as data/deadend-symbols.json holds them
@return array{functions: list<string>, classes: list<string>, redeclares: list<string>, files: int, truncated: bool, deadEnds: array<string, list<string>>}

params.name: deadEnds
params.shape: array{functions?: array<string, string>, classes?: array<string, string>}
params.doc: name => area, as data/deadend-symbols.json holds them

methods.name: key
methods.doc: A folder's place in the cache: its parent's name and its own (plugins/kubio, themes/kubio, mu-plugins/x.php), so a plugin and a theme of one name keep entries of their own.

methods.name: keep
methods.doc: The cache changed this request: written once, when the request ends; entries an older engine kept by name alone go.

methods.name: fingerprint
methods.doc: A folder's cheap fingerprint: its own time and its top-level PHP files' newest (an update replaces the folder; a version bumps the main file).

methods.name: namesStamp
methods.doc: The reference names a reduced scan was kept against: a new interface (a WordPress update) makes every scan again.

methods.name: reduced
methods.doc: A scan cut to the reference's own names, the only ones a verdict asks about.

methods.name: verdict
methods.doc:
Only the reference's own interface counts: a function or class the plugin
needs from WordPress. Its own integrations with other plugins and PHP
extensions are its business.
shapes: @param array{calls: list<string>, classes: list<string>, declared: array<string, true>, declaredClasses: array<string, true>, guarded: array<string, true>, truncated: bool} $scan
@return array{functions: list<string>, classes: list<string>, redeclares: list<string>, files: int, truncated: bool}

params.name: scan
params.shape: array{calls: list<string>, classes: list<string>, declared: array<string, true>, declaredClasses: array<string, true>, guarded: array<string, true>, truncated: bool}

methods.name: scan
methods.doc:
Every file's tokens into one table: the functions called, the classes
referenced, both minus what the folder declares itself or guards with
an existence check.
shapes: @return array{calls: list<string>, classes: list<string>, declared: array<string, true>, declaredClasses: array<string, true>, guarded: array<string, true>, truncated: bool}

methods.name: scanTokens
methods.doc:
One file's tokens. A class name is resolved as PHP resolves it: through
the file's use imports, else inside its namespace, so a plugin that
imports a WordPress class (a provider built on the AI client's abstract
provider) is judged on the class it really names.

methods.name: inGuardedNamespace
methods.doc:
Whether a class sits in the namespace of a class the folder checks for: a
plugin that asks class_exists( 'Vendor\\Lib\\Client' ) before using the
library treats the library as optional, its other classes with it (Ninja
Forms checks WordPress's AI client so, then builds its requirements).

methods.name: noteName
methods.signature: noteName(array $tokens, int $i, string $namespace, array $imports, Minn\Runtime\SymbolTable $table): void
methods.doc:
A name token: a class reference when it follows new / extends /
implements / instanceof or precedes ::, a call when it precedes "(",
and a guard when the call is an existence check on a literal.

methods.name: resolve
methods.doc:
A class name as PHP resolves it in the file: its first part an imported
alias, else inside the file's namespace.

methods.name: readImports
shapes: @param array<string, string> $imports alias (lower case) => class, added to

methods.name: significant
methods.doc: The nearest token in either direction that is not whitespace or a comment, as [id, text]. @param list<array|string> $tokens @return array{0: ?int, 1: string}|null

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\TagEditor
classes.doc:
Edits one start tag's attributes in place the way the reference's tag
processor does: a replaced value keeps its position, a new attribute goes
right after the tag name (after any earlier insertion), and a removal takes
only the attribute's own text.

shapes: @param list<array{name: string, value: ?string, start: int, end: int}> $attrs offsets relative to the tag

params.name: attrs
params.shape: list<array{name: string, value: ?string, start: int, end: int}>

methods.name: get
methods.doc: An attribute's value, or null.

methods.name: has
methods.doc: Whether the tag has an attribute.

methods.name: set
methods.doc: true sets a bare boolean attribute; a URL attribute (href, src, ...) keeps only a URL whose scheme is allowed, as the reference's set_attribute keeps it.

methods.name: remove
methods.doc: Removes an attribute.

methods.name: addClass
methods.doc: Adds or removes a class.

methods.name: removeClass
methods.doc: Removes a class, and the attribute when it was the last one.

methods.name: setStyle
methods.doc: Sets or removes one inline style property.

methods.name: html
methods.doc: The tag as edited.

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\TaxTerms
classes.doc:
The terms a taxonomy query's clause names, found as the reference finds
them (probe tax-terms). The clause's terms are made unique (their keys
kept). Under a hierarchical taxonomy that includes children they are
turned into term ids, each followed by its children (the children first,
then the term, repeats kept). Then they are turned into term_taxonomy_ids.
Each turn is one terms query in no order for every term at once: as many
as there are terms, or all of them in a hierarchical taxonomy. No turn
runs when the terms are already in the field wanted. An AND clause fails
when a turn finds fewer terms than it has. The engine answers a turn
from what it has just read, without the database: one by a name it knows
(the theme's own term), and the second turn when the first found terms
with no children; a later lookup by a slug a turn found is answered too.

methods.name: ids
methods.doc:
A clause's term_taxonomy_ids for its SQL (get_sql_for_clause), or null
when an AND clause names a term there is not.
shapes: @param array<string, mixed> $given the clause: taxonomy, field, terms, include_children

params.name: given
params.doc: the clause: taxonomy, field, terms, include_children

methods.name: transform
methods.doc:
A clause's terms turned into another field, as a plugin asks
(transform_query): an error in the clause's place when an AND clause
names a term there is not.

methods.name: turn
methods.doc:
One turn of a clause's terms into another field; false when an AND
clause finds fewer terms than it has.
shapes: @param list<int>|null $known the term ids the turn will find, when the engine has just read them

params.name: known
params.doc: the term ids the turn will find, when the engine has just read them

methods.name: missing
methods.doc: A clause naming a term there is not: the reference's message asked for, nothing found.

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\TemplateFiles
classes.doc:
The theme templates WordPress's template functions name: the index and
embed templates found through the hierarchy, the slugs a block template
stands for, the template types and part areas core knows, and a block
template made from the theme's file or from a saved post, as the
reference makes one (probe template-part-lookup): the theme's names and
folders read on the way, the area a theme declares checked against the
areas core knows, and the markup passed through the block hooks.

constants.name: PLAIN_TITLES
constants.doc: Template types named without a context.

constants.name: FORMAT_SLUG
constants.doc: The prefix of the post format archives' template slugs.

methods.name: index
methods.doc: The theme's index template (get_index_template).

methods.name: embed
methods.doc:
The template an embed is shown with (get_embed_template): embed-{type}-{format}.php,
embed-{type}.php, then embed.php.

methods.name: hierarchy
methods.doc:
The template slugs a slug stands for, most specific first
(get_template_hierarchy).

methods.name: defaultTypes
methods.doc:
The template types core knows (get_default_block_template_types), as
default_template_types leaves them: each named and described in the
site's language, then one per post format.

methods.name: partAreas
methods.doc: The template part areas core knows (get_allowed_block_template_part_areas), each named in the site's language, as default_wp_template_part_areas leaves them.

methods.name: partArea
methods.doc:
A template part's area as the areas core knows it
(_filter_block_template_part_area): one it does not know becomes
uncategorized, with a notice.

methods.name: templateIndex
methods.doc: The active theme's templates, saved and in its files; null with no block theme booted.

methods.name: file
methods.doc:
One theme template file, described (_get_block_template_file), after
the theme's names and folders are read: its slug, path, theme and type;
a part's area, the one theme.json declares checked against the areas
core knows (_filter_block_template_part_area); a custom template's
title and post types. Null for no such file, or a type that is neither.

methods.name: fromFile
methods.doc:
A template built from a file as file() describes one
(_build_block_template_result_from_file): the default template types'
title and description for a template they name (which is not custom),
a part's area, a custom template's post types, and the markup through
the block hooks, the theme named on every template part in it.

methods.name: saved
methods.doc:
The template or part a site saved for a theme (any theme, by its
wp_theme term) under a slug, built as fromPost() builds it, block
hooks applied; null when none is saved (probe taxonomy-blocks-user-doubts).

methods.name: fileTemplate
methods.doc:
A theme file's template by id, past whatever the site saved over it
(get_block_file_template): pre_get_block_file_template may answer
first; only the active theme's files are found; the template, or null,
through get_block_file_template.

methods.name: fromPost
methods.doc:
A saved template or part as a template (_build_block_template_result_from_post),
under the theme its wp_theme term names; an error when it names none.
A part's area is its wp_template_part_area term's, none without one.
Its origin and suggestion meta and whether the theme has the file are
read as the reference reads them; its markup goes through the block
hooks, a part's with the hooked blocks its post says to leave out.

methods.name: hookedPart
methods.doc:
A part's markup through the block hooks, as the reference runs them:
wrapped in a template-part block (so blocks hooked as its first or
last child are placed), that block marked with the hooked blocks to
leave out, then unwrapped.

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\TermEvents
classes.doc:
What the reference's REST terms controller tells plugins, for the
engine's own: with plugins loaded a term is saved as that controller
saves one (rest_pre_insert_{taxonomy}, then the runtime's wp_insert_term
or wp_update_term, and wp_delete_term), and the REST actions follow.
Without a booted runtime each write is the engine's own.

methods.name: live
methods.doc: Whether plugins are loaded to be told anything.

methods.name: restCreate
methods.doc:
A term created over REST with plugins loaded, as the reference's
controller creates one (probe rest-term-save): the request's fields
as the prepared term, through rest_pre_insert_{taxonomy}, into
wp_insert_term; a refusal is its REST error.

methods.name: restUpdate
methods.doc:
A term changed over REST with plugins loaded: the fields the request
sends, through rest_pre_insert_{taxonomy}, into wp_update_term (when
any are left); a refusal is its REST error.

methods.name: delete
methods.signature: delete(int $termId, string $taxonomy, array $data, Minn\Http\Request $request, Closure $quietly): void
methods.doc: Deletes a term, then tells plugins over REST with the term as it was and the response.
shapes: @param Closure(): void $quietly the engine's own delete

methods.name: restSaved
methods.doc: rest_insert_{taxonomy}, then rest_after_insert_{taxonomy}, with the term as it stands and the request.

methods.name: prepared
methods.doc:
The prepared term: the fields the request sends, in the reference's
order, the name and slug cleaned as its schema cleans them; then
rest_pre_insert_{taxonomy}.

methods.name: refusal
methods.doc: A save's refusal as REST serves it: a name in use with the term's id, anything else with its own status or 500.

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\TermFields
classes.doc:
A term's fields in a context, as the reference's sanitize_term_field
treats them (probe term-sanitize): the numeric fields are whole numbers,
never below zero, in every context, and raw stops there. edit runs
edit_term_{field} and edit_{taxonomy}_{field}; db runs pre_term_{field}
and pre_{taxonomy}_{field}, where the saving defaults live, and a slug
also pre_category_nicename; rss runs term_{field}_rss and
{taxonomy}_{field}_rss; any other context runs term_{field} and
{taxonomy}_{field} with the context named. Then a text field is escaped
for where it goes: a form (edit), an attribute, a script (js).

constants.name: FIELDS
constants.doc: The fields sanitize_term runs, in its order.

methods.name: field
methods.signature: field(string $field, mixed $value, int $termId, string|false $taxonomy, string $context): mixed
methods.doc: One field's value in a context; a lookup with no taxonomy names false, and its filters get false.

methods.name: term
methods.doc:
A term (object or array) with each of its fields in the context, and
its filter set to the context; the term's own id goes to the filters.

methods.name: filtered
methods.signature: filtered(string $field, mixed $value, int $termId, string|false $taxonomy, string $context): mixed
methods.doc: The field's own filters for the context, in the reference's order.

methods.name: saving
methods.doc: The db context's filters: the field's, the taxonomy's, and a slug's old category one.

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\TermLookup
classes.doc:
Terms looked up as WordPress's taxonomy functions find them: a list by
query arguments, one by a field, whether one exists, a taxonomy's
hierarchy, an object's terms, a term's address and one of its fields, its
children and ancestors, how many there are, and the caches cleaned after
a change; each with the filters plugins hook there.

methods.name: terms
methods.doc:
Terms by query arguments (get_terms), or the old ($taxonomy, $args)
shape; an error for an unknown taxonomy; get_terms filters the list
unless suppressed (a count never). The engine may hand an answer for
the query it writes (QueryAnswers).

methods.name: categories
methods.doc:
Categories, or another taxonomy's terms (get_categories): the terms
query through get_categories_taxonomy, the old type => link argument
noted as deprecated and read as the link categories, each term given
the old category fields; none when the query is refused.

methods.name: by
methods.signature: by(mixed $field, mixed $value, mixed $taxonomy = '', mixed $output = 'OBJECT', mixed $filter = 'raw'): mixed
methods.doc:
A term by slug, name, id or term_taxonomy_id (get_term_by), or false.
As the reference finds one (probe term-lookup): by id through get_term;
by the other three through a terms query of one result in no order
(the taxonomy left out for a term_taxonomy_id), and the term it finds
through get_term again; a slug or name needs a taxonomy that exists and
a value. The theme's own term, once its templates are read, and a slug
a taxonomy query has just found are answered without the database.

methods.name: knownByName
methods.doc:
A taxonomy's term by name as the engine has read it elsewhere (its row,
or none when there is no such term), kept so get_term_by answers its
lookup for that name without the database.

methods.name: exists
methods.doc:
Whether a term exists (term_exists): its id (and term_taxonomy_id when a
taxonomy is named), or null. Lookup arguments a plugin changes through
term_exists_default_query_args are run as a terms query, by slug then
by name.

methods.name: hierarchy
methods.doc:
A hierarchical taxonomy's parents and their children (_get_term_hierarchy),
built from the terms and kept in {taxonomy}_children when not kept yet.

methods.name: descendants
methods.signature: descendants(mixed $termId, mixed $terms, mixed $taxonomy, mixed $ancestors = array ( )): mixed
methods.doc:
Terms below a term among those given (_get_term_children), following
only the terms the stored hierarchy says have children; ids for ids.

methods.name: children
methods.doc:
Every term below a term (get_term_children), an error for an unknown
taxonomy. As the reference walks the stored hierarchy (probe
tax-terms): a term's own children, then those of each child that has
any, the hierarchy read again for each term walked.

methods.name: objectTerms
methods.signature: objectTerms(mixed $objectIds, mixed $taxonomies, mixed $args = array ( ), ?Closure $answer = NULL): mixed
methods.doc:
The terms of objects in taxonomies (wp_get_object_terms), as
wp_get_object_terms_args shapes the query and get_object_terms and
wp_get_object_terms leave the list; the engine may hand an answer for
its terms query.

methods.name: field
methods.doc: One of a term's fields in a context (get_term_field): empty when the term has no such field.

methods.name: count
methods.doc:
How many terms match (wp_count_terms), the old ($taxonomy, $args) shape
read too; empty terms counted.

methods.name: link
methods.doc:
A term's address (get_term_link): by its taxonomy's link structure
through pre_term_link, a changed one filled with its slug (its
ancestors' first when the taxonomy nests), by query without one; then
tag_link or category_link, and term_link. An error for no term.

methods.name: ancestors
methods.doc:
An object's ancestors (get_ancestors): a term's parents up the
taxonomy, or a post's up its type; as get_ancestors leaves them.

methods.name: postAncestors
methods.doc: A post's parents up to the top (get_post_ancestors), a loop broken.

methods.name: cleanCache
methods.doc:
Terms forgotten after a change (clean_term_cache): each term's cache,
its taxonomy's (unless asked not to), then clean_term_cache; with no
taxonomy named, each term's own.

methods.name: cleanTaxonomy
methods.doc: A taxonomy's caches cleaned (clean_taxonomy_cache): its hierarchy rebuilt, the terms' last change moved.

methods.name: queryLink
methods.doc: A term's address by query: ?cat= for a category, the taxonomy's query var, else taxonomy and term.

methods.name: below
methods.doc:
The terms below a term in the stored hierarchy, a term already walked
not walked again.

methods.name: lookup
methods.doc: A term by slug, then by name, under a parent when one is named. @return array<string, mixed>|null

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\TermOrder
classes.doc:
A term query's ORDER BY as the reference writes it (probe
wp-term-query-sql): term and taxonomy columns, the relationship's order,
the order include or slug lists give, none, or the name; then
get_terms_orderby, and after it a meta key or meta_value[_num] when the
query has meta clauses.

methods.name: direction
methods.doc: ASC when asked for, DESC for anything else.

methods.name: clause
methods.doc: The ORDER BY body for an orderby value, filtered as the reference filters it.

methods.name: meta
methods.doc: A meta key, meta_value[_num] or a named meta clause as SQL (parse_orderby_meta), or '' when the query has no such clause.

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\TermQuery
classes.doc:
Term reads in the shapes plugin code asks for: get_terms() arguments to
rows, the tree filters (child_of, exclude_tree), the fields shapes, and
the single-term lookups. Behaviour pinned by contracts/fixtures/api/content.json.

shapes: @param Closure(string): string $slug the slug sanitiser, so the reference's filters apply

params.name: slug
params.doc: the slug sanitiser, so the reference's filters apply

constants.name: DEFAULTS
constants.value: array (   'taxonomy' => NULL,   'object_ids' => NULL,   'orderby' => 'name',   'order' => 'ASC',   'hide_empty' => true,   'include' =>    array (   ),   'exclude' =>    array (   ),   'exclude_tree' =>    array (   ),   'number' => '',   'offset' => '',   'fields' => 'all',   'count' => false,   'name' => '',   'slug' => '',   'term_taxonomy_id' => '',   'hierarchical' => true,   'search' => '',   'name__like' => '',   'description__like' => '',   'pad_counts' => false,   'get' => '',   'child_of' => 0,   'parent' => '',   'childless' => false,   'cache_domain' => 'core',   'update_term_meta_cache' => true,   'meta_query' => '',   'meta_key' => '',   'meta_value' => '', )

constants.name: COLUMNS
constants.value: 't.term_id, t.name, t.slug, t.term_group, tt.term_taxonomy_id, tt.taxonomy, tt.description, tt.parent, tt.count'

methods.name: row
methods.doc: A term row joined with its taxonomy row, by id (and taxonomy when known). @return array<string, mixed>|null

methods.name: keep
methods.doc: A term row read elsewhere (a list of posts' terms, read together), kept so row() answers from it. @param array<string, mixed> $row

methods.name: find
methods.doc:
The term id and taxonomy a field value names; null when nothing matches
or the field is not one a term can be found by.

methods.name: exists
methods.doc:
Whether a term (by id, or by slug or name) exists, optionally under a
taxonomy and parent; the ids when it does.

methods.name: lookup
methods.doc:
The term whose slug or name (as stored) is exactly the value,
optionally in a taxonomy and under a parent (0 for the top level).

methods.name: hasChildren
methods.doc:
Whether any term in the taxonomies (any taxonomy for null) sits
under the parent: the reference answers a lookup under a childless
parent with nothing before it looks.

methods.name: slugTaken
methods.doc: Whether a term other than the one named holds the slug, in any taxonomy.

methods.name: normalise
methods.doc: get_terms() arguments normalised: the "get all" shortcut, integer lists, sanitised slugs.

methods.name: rows
methods.doc:
The term rows the arguments match, ordered and paged, with the tree
filters applied.

methods.name: hierarchy
methods.doc:
Every parent in a taxonomy that has children, mapped to its children's
ids. A taxonomy nobody nested reads as an empty map.

methods.name: children
methods.doc: Every term id under a term, however deep. @return list<int>

methods.name: objectsIn
methods.doc: The object ids attached to any of the terms in any of the taxonomies. @param list<int> $termIds @param list<string> $taxonomies @return list<int>

methods.name: idList
methods.doc: A comma list, array, or blank as positive ids. @return list<int>

methods.name: descendants
methods.doc: The rows under a term, however deep, in source order. @param list<array<string, mixed>> $rows @return list<array<string, mixed>>

methods.name: where
shapes: @return array{0: string, 1: string, 2: list<mixed>} the join, the WHERE clause, its parameters

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\TermQueryRunner
classes.doc:
WP_Term_Query::get_terms as the reference runs it (probe
wp-term-query-sql): the variables parsed and handed to pre_get_terms,
get_terms_args, the WHERE pieces (taxonomies, inclusions, exclusions with
excluded trees and childless terms through list_terms_exclusions, names,
slugs, term taxonomy ids, likes, objects, parent, counts, search, meta),
the order through get_terms_orderby, the fields through get_terms_fields,
all of it through terms_clauses, terms_pre_query, and the results shaped
by TermQueryTree (children, padded counts, the empty hidden, the page).
A request's rows are kept for the rest of the request, as the reference
keeps them in its object cache, until a term table is written; a lookup
the engine can answer from what it has read (QueryAnswers) runs no SQL.

constants.name: SHAPING
constants.doc: The filters that shape the request: an engine answer stands only while none of them has a listener.

properties.name: renamed
properties.doc: Whether saving's sanitising changed a name the query looks up (the answer then no longer fits it).

methods.name: run
methods.doc:
Runs a term query object's variables: its terms in the shape the
fields ask for, a count, or what a plugin answered first.

methods.name: answered
methods.doc:
The rows an engine answer gives (term ids as rows), when the query is
still the one the engine wrote; null when it is not, or it has none.

methods.name: kept
methods.doc:
A request's answer read once a request: rows (each a copy, so a
caller's changes stay its own) or a count.

methods.name: lists
methods.doc:
Names, slugs, term taxonomy ids and object ids as lists, as the
reference holds them once plugins have had the arguments.

methods.name: hierarchical
methods.doc: Whether the results have a tree to walk (a count never does). @param array<string, mixed> $args

methods.name: settle
inHierarchy
methods.doc: Whether a parent or child_of term has children in any of the taxonomies (when none, the query is not run). @param list<string> $taxonomies

methods.name: order
methods.doc: The ORDER BY clause and direction, term_order needing the relationships. @param array<string, mixed> $args @return array{0: string, 1: string}

methods.name: clauses
methods.doc: The WHERE pieces, by name, in the reference's order. @param array<string, mixed> $args @param list<string> $taxonomies

methods.name: exclusions
methods.doc: The excluded ids (an excluded term's whole tree, childless terms' parents), unless ids are included. @param array<string, mixed> $args @param list<string> $taxonomies

methods.name: names
methods.doc: Names (as saving stores them), slugs and term taxonomy ids. @param array<string, mixed> $args @param list<string> $taxonomies

methods.name: select
methods.doc:
The rest of the WHERE (counts, search, meta), the fields, the joins,
terms_clauses, and the request written from what it returned.

methods.name: limits
methods.doc: A LIMIT only when no tree has to be walked first (the tree's page is cut afterwards). @param array<string, mixed> $args

methods.name: meta
methods.doc: The meta query's join and WHERE piece, read again in case pre_get_terms changed its variables. @return array{0: string, 1: string}

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\TermQueryTree
classes.doc:
What a term query does with its rows, as the reference does it (probe
wp-term-query-sql): each row a term through get_term (with the object id
a relationship query carries); only child_of's descendants; counts padded
with the children's posts; an empty term kept only while one of its
children has posts (the rest dropped where they stood, keys and all); a
tree's page cut once the tree is walked; then the shape the fields ask
for.

methods.name: populate
methods.doc: The terms the rows name, keyed as the rows were.

methods.name: settle
methods.doc:
The terms after the tree has had its say: descendants only, padded
counts, empty branches dropped, the page cut.

methods.name: pad
methods.doc:
Each term's count raised to the published posts in it or under it, as
_pad_term_counts does for a hierarchical taxonomy.

methods.name: format
methods.doc: The terms in the shape the fields ask for.

methods.name: hasPosts
methods.doc: Whether a term, or one of its children, has posts.

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\TermSave
classes.doc:
wp_insert_term and wp_update_term in the reference's order (probe
term-insert-filters, contracts/runtime.md "Terms plugins can change").
An insert asks pre_insert_term, refuses an empty name or a missing
parent, runs every field through its db filters (sanitize_term), refuses
a name the parent (or, for tags, the taxonomy) already has, makes the
slug unique, hands the row to wp_insert_term_data, writes it (a slug left
empty becomes the term's id), puts it in the taxonomy, lets a plugin
name a duplicate to keep instead, and tells plugins. An update merges
the stored term (slashed, so a backslash in it survives) under the
changes, runs the same filters, asks wp_update_term_parent (where a
parent that would put the term under itself becomes 0), and refuses a
slug a sibling holds.

methods.name: insert
methods.doc: A new term's ids, or why not.

methods.name: update
methods.doc: A changed term's ids, or why not.

methods.name: write
methods.signature: write(Minn\Objects\Term $term, array $data, string $description, int $parent, array $args): array
methods.doc: The update's writes and their actions, in the reference's order.
shapes: @param array{name: string, slug: string, term_group: int} $data

params.name: data
params.shape: array{name: string, slug: string, term_group: int}

methods.name: nameTaken
methods.doc:
The refusal for a name already in use: under the same parent in a
hierarchical taxonomy (unless a different slug was asked for), or
anywhere in a flat one. The lookup sanitizes the name again, as the
reference's does.

methods.name: updatedSlug
methods.signature: updatedSlug(string $slug, string $asked, int $parent, int $termId, array $args): Minn\Objects\Errors|string
methods.doc:
An update's slug: as asked when no other term holds it; made unique
when it was made from the name (none was asked for) or the holder
sits under another parent; refused otherwise.

methods.name: slugFromId
methods.signature: slugFromId(Minn\Content\Terms $terms, int $termId, string $taxonomy, array $data, array $args): void
methods.doc:
A slug saving left empty (a name with nothing a slug can keep) becomes
the term's id, between edit_terms and edited_terms.
shapes: @param array{name: string, slug: string, term_group: int} $data

params.name: data
params.shape: array{name: string, slug: string, term_group: int}

methods.name: row
methods.doc:
The row a plugin's filter handed back, with the columns it dropped
put back.
shapes: @return array{name: string, slug: string, term_group: int}

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\TermTags
classes.doc:
What WordPress's template tags tell about a post's terms: its terms of a
taxonomy (as a list primed them, else read), its categories with their
old field names, its tags, its format, and a category's address and the
chain of its parents.

constants.name: CATEGORY_FIELDS
constants.doc: A category's old field names, each with the term field it mirrors, in the order they are added.

methods.name: cached
methods.doc:
The terms of a post that a list primed or the object cache holds
(get_object_term_cache), each through get_term; false when nothing
holds them.

methods.name: formatStrings
methods.doc:
The post formats' names (get_post_format_strings), in the site's
language, by slug.

methods.name: ofPost
methods.doc: A post's terms of a taxonomy (get_the_terms), as get_the_terms leaves them; false for none or no post.

methods.name: categories
methods.doc: A post's categories (get_the_category), each with its old field names, as get_the_categories leaves them.

methods.name: tags
methods.doc: A post's tags (get_the_tags), as get_the_tags leaves them.

methods.name: format
methods.doc: A post's format (get_post_format): its post_format term's slug without the prefix; false for none or a type without formats.

methods.name: categoryFields
methods.doc: A category's old field names beside its term fields (_make_cat_compat), on a term object or a term array alike.

methods.name: categoryLink
methods.doc: A category's address (get_category_link), empty for none.

methods.name: categoryParents
methods.signature: categoryParents(mixed $categoryId, mixed $link = false, mixed $separator = '/', mixed $nicename = false, mixed $deprecated = array ( )): mixed
methods.doc:
A category's parents and itself, outermost first (get_category_parents),
as names or slugs, linked or not, with the separator after each; the
error for an unknown category.

methods.name: cacheObjects
methods.doc:
Each taxonomy's term ids of the objects not cached yet, kept in
{taxonomy}_relationships (update_object_term_cache); an object cached
there keeps its entry, and one without terms gets an empty list.

methods.name: cleanObjects
methods.doc:
The objects' term caches let go (clean_object_term_cache): each of the
type's taxonomies' relationships, the terms' last_changed moved, then
plugins told; nothing at all while cache invalidation is suspended.

methods.name: attachmentTaxonomies
methods.doc:
The taxonomies an attachment carries (get_attachment_taxonomies): those
registered for attachments, for its file's extension, its MIME type,
and each half of it (attachment:image, attachment:image/png...).

methods.name: taxonomies
methods.doc:
A post's taxonomies as sentences of term links (get_the_taxonomies):
a taxonomy's own template and term_template win over the ones given;
the terms list through wp_sprintf's %l; an attachment's file types
count; a taxonomy without terms is left out.

methods.name: objectInTerm
methods.doc:
Whether an object has one of the terms (is_object_in_term): an integer
is an id, a digit string an id, a name or a slug, any other string a
name or a slug; no terms asked means any term of the taxonomy. An
error for no object (0) or an unknown taxonomy.

methods.name: cloudCountText
methods.doc:
The tag cloud's count in words for a tag's label: topic_count_text (a
nooped plural) first, then the text callback (default_topic_count_text
counts as none), then the old single_text and multiple_text, else
"%s item" / "%s items" (probe taxonomy-blocks-user-doubts).

methods.name: allLink
methods.doc:
The category list's "all" link for a taxonomy: the archive of its
first type when none of its types is a post, else the posts page or
the home page (probe taxonomy-blocks-user-doubts).

methods.name: bindingValue
methods.doc:
A term's field for the core/term-data binding
(_block_bindings_term_data_get_value): a navigation link or submenu by
its own id and type ("tag" is post_tag), any other block by the termId
and taxonomy in its context; id, count and parent as text, the name,
slug, description or link. Null for no term, or a term of a hidden
taxonomy to someone who may not edit it (probe taxonomy-blocks-user-doubts).

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\TermWriter
classes.doc:
The decisions behind wp_delete_term and the object-term relationships:
which relationships to add and remove (saves are Runtime\TermSave). The rows themselves come
from Content\Terms; the lifecycle actions fire from here in the
reference's order. Behaviour pinned by contracts/fixtures/api/content.json.

methods.name: delete
methods.doc:
Deletes a term; objects left without a category fall back to the
default one. Returns the object ids the term was attached to.

methods.name: relate
methods.signature: relate(int $objectId, array $keep, array $old, string $taxonomy, ?Closure $count = NULL): void
methods.doc:
Makes an object's relationships in a taxonomy exactly $keep (or $old
plus $keep when appending), in the reference's order: each new
relationship between add_term_relationship and
added_term_relationship, the counts of those terms, then the ones
that went, between delete_term_relationships and
deleted_term_relationships, and their counts. $count recounts a list
of term_taxonomy ids and tells plugins (wp_update_term_count); without
it those terms are recounted quietly.
shapes: @param list<int> $old the object's current term_taxonomy ids in the taxonomy

params.name: old
params.doc: the object's current term_taxonomy ids in the taxonomy

methods.name: unrelate
methods.doc:
Removes the given relationships between delete_term_relationships and
deleted_term_relationships, then recounts those terms; true when any
row went.

methods.name: publishedCount
methods.doc:
How many objects in the counted statuses a term holds, as the stored
count keeps it (published ones unless a plugin widens the list).

methods.name: split
methods.doc:
Gives a taxonomy row that shares its term with another taxonomy a
term of its own (the same name, slug and group), and moves its
children under it. Null when no other taxonomy holds the term.
shapes: @return array{0: int, 1: string, 2: list<int>}|null the new term id, the taxonomy, the children moved

methods.name: rowTermId
methods.doc: The term id a taxonomy row belongs to; null for no such row.

methods.name: rowCount
methods.doc: How many taxonomy rows hold a term id, whether their taxonomies are registered or not.

methods.name: anyShared
methods.doc: Whether any term id is still held by more than one taxonomy row.

methods.name: relationshipCount
methods.doc: Every object filed under a term, whatever it is: the count a taxonomy of links or other non-posts keeps.

methods.name: storeCount
methods.doc: Stores a term's count.

methods.name: termIdsOf
methods.doc: The term ids behind term_taxonomy ids, as stored (strings), in the order given. @param list<int> $ttIds @return list<string>

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\TermWrites
classes.doc:
Terms written as WordPress's taxonomy functions write them: a term made,
changed and deleted (its children moved up and its default kept), a slug
no other term holds, an object's terms set, and the terms' counts kept
through the taxonomy's own callback; each step with the actions the
reference fires in its order.

methods.name: insert
methods.doc: A new term (wp_insert_term), its fields through their filters in the reference's order (Runtime\TermSave).

methods.name: update
methods.doc: A term changed (wp_update_term), its fields through their filters in the reference's order (Runtime\TermSave).

methods.name: delete
methods.doc:
A term deleted (wp_delete_term): a taxonomy's default term stays (0);
its children move up to its parent, its meta goes row by row, objects
left without a category fall back to the default one; false for an
unknown term or taxonomy.

methods.name: uniqueSlug
methods.doc:
A slug no other term of the taxonomy holds (wp_unique_term_slug): one
taken in the taxonomy gets its parents' slugs added, nearest first,
until it is free (wp_unique_term_slug_is_bad_slug decides whether it
was taken), then "-2", "-3" past any term holding it in any taxonomy.

methods.name: splitShared
methods.doc:
A term two taxonomies share, split (_split_shared_term): the taxonomy
row named gets a term of its own, its children follow, split_shared_term
says so, the split is recorded for wp_get_split_term() when asked, and
once no shared term is left finished_splitting_shared_terms is set. A
row held by one taxonomy keeps its term, and a row of another term
gives that term's id (probe taxonomy-blocks-user-doubts).

methods.name: isShared
methods.doc: Whether a term id is held by more than one taxonomy row, registered or not (wp_term_is_shared); never once splitting has finished.

methods.name: parentWithoutLoops
methods.doc:
The default on wp_update_term_parent (wp_check_term_hierarchy_for_loops):
a parent at or under the term itself becomes 0; a loop already above
the parent is broken, each term in it moved to the top level, and the
parent kept (probe taxonomy-blocks-user-doubts).

methods.name: updateCount
methods.doc:
Terms counted (wp_update_term_count): put off while counting is
deferred; asked with $deferred, what was put off is counted now.

methods.name: updateCountNow
methods.doc:
Terms counted now by term_taxonomy id (wp_update_term_count_now)
through the taxonomy's count callback, then their caches let go. With
no callback of its own, a taxonomy of post types counts published
posts; one of other objects counts them all.

methods.name: countPublished
methods.doc: The published objects behind each term_taxonomy id counted (_update_post_term_count); which statuses count is the plugins' to widen.

methods.name: countAll
methods.doc: Every object behind each term_taxonomy id counted, posts or not (_update_generic_term_count).

methods.name: setObjectTerms
methods.signature: setObjectTerms(mixed $objectId, mixed $terms, mixed $taxonomy, mixed $append = false): mixed
methods.doc:
An object's terms set (wp_set_object_terms), a term named but not
there yet made; added to the ones it had when asked to append. The
term_taxonomy ids, or the error making one gave.

methods.name: removeObjectTerms
methods.doc: Terms taken off an object (wp_remove_object_terms), the ones left counted again; the error for an unknown taxonomy.

methods.name: deleteObjectRelationships
methods.doc: Every term of the taxonomies taken off an object (wp_delete_object_term_relationships).

methods.name: slugUnderParents
methods.doc: A taken slug with the term's parents' slugs added, nearest first, until no term holds it.

methods.name: moveChildren
methods.doc: What plugins are told as a deleted term's children move up to its parent (the move itself is the term writer's).

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\ThemeMods
classes.doc:
The active theme's settings (theme_mods_{stylesheet}) as WordPress keeps
them: read through theme_mod_{name}, a default with %s naming the
theme's folders, written through pre_set_theme_mod_{name}, and removed one
by one or all at once.

methods.name: all
methods.doc: Every setting of the active theme (get_theme_mods).

methods.name: get
methods.doc: One setting (get_theme_mod), else the default (a %s in it names the parent's and the theme's folder addresses).

methods.name: set
methods.doc: A setting written (set_theme_mod), through pre_set_theme_mod_{name}.

methods.name: remove
methods.doc: A setting removed (remove_theme_mod); the last one takes the option with it.

methods.name: removeAll
methods.doc: Every setting removed (remove_theme_mods).

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\ThemeSupports
classes.doc:
What a theme supports, as add_theme_support keeps it (probe rest-themes):
a bare feature is true, anything else its arguments. html5 lists add up
(repeats and all), post thumbnails stay on for every type once on, post
formats keep only real formats, the custom logo fills in its defaults at
once (flexible both ways when asked for bare), and the custom header and
background get theirs as WordPress finishes loading, a header with no
width or height made flexible that way. title-tag declared after loading
is refused. A block theme supports thumbnails, responsive embeds, editor
styles, HTML5 markup and feed links before its own setup runs.

The features themselves (data/theme-features.json, and any a theme
registers) say how each is shown in REST: its schema, or the default
when the theme does not support it.

constants.name: LOGO
constants.value: array (   'width' => NULL,   'height' => NULL,   'flex-width' => false,   'flex-height' => false,   'header-text' => '',   'unlink-homepage-logo' => false, )

constants.name: HEADER
constants.value: array (   'default-image' => '',   'random-default' => false,   'width' => 0,   'height' => 0,   'flex-height' => false,   'flex-width' => false,   'default-text-color' => '',   'header-text' => true,   'uploads' => true,   'wp-head-callback' => '',   'admin-head-callback' => '',   'admin-preview-callback' => '',   'video' => false,   'video-active-callback' => 'is_front_page', )

methods.name: get
methods.doc:
A feature's support (get_theme_support): false when the theme has none;
with an argument, that part of it (one of a list, or a key's value).

methods.name: current
methods.doc:
Whether the theme supports a feature (current_theme_supports): for the
features with parts, the part asked; otherwise
current_theme_supports-{feature} has the last word.

methods.name: all
methods.doc: Every feature the theme has declared, as stored. @return array<string, mixed>

methods.name: add
methods.doc: add_theme_support: false when refused. @param list<mixed> $args

methods.name: remove
methods.doc: remove_theme_support: false when the theme did not support it.

methods.name: classicEditorSettings
methods.doc:
get_classic_theme_supports_block_editor_settings: the editor settings a
classic theme's supports amount to, the custom-value switches, and its
palette, sizes and gradients when it declares them.

methods.name: blockThemeDefaults
methods.doc: _add_default_theme_supports: what every block theme supports before its own setup.

methods.name: editorDefaults
methods.doc: wp_enable_block_templates and wp_setup_widgets_block_editor: a block theme's templates, and the block widget editor for any theme.

methods.name: justInTime
methods.doc: _custom_header_background_just_in_time: the header's and background's defaults filled in once loaded.

methods.name: register
methods.doc: register_theme_feature: true, or why the feature cannot be registered.

methods.name: features
methods.doc: Core's features, then those registered since. @return array<string, array<string, mixed>>

methods.name: forRest
methods.doc: The active theme's supports as wp/v2/themes shows them: each feature shown in REST, shaped by its schema. @return array<string, mixed>

methods.name: prepared
methods.doc:
One feature's support as the REST API shows it (the runtime's
WP_REST_Themes_Controller::prepare_theme_support): a feature that is
not variadic shown by its first value, through its prepare_callback
or else cut to its schema.
shapes: @param array<string, mixed> $config the feature as it was registered

params.name: config
params.doc: the feature as it was registered

methods.name: withConstants
methods.doc:
The custom header's and background's arguments and their old constants, as the reference keeps them in
step (themes from before the arguments read the constants, Twenty Eleven's header among them): a constant a
theme defined first sets its argument, and an argument the theme passed defines its constant, empty or not
(header-text as NO_HEADER_TEXT, turned around).

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\ThemeSwitch
classes.doc:
Switching the theme as the reference does it, in two halves. The switch
(switch_theme): the leaving theme keeps its widgets and its menu
locations are remembered, the three theme options move, the switch is
recorded (theme_switched), the arriving theme's mods start with the
classic sidebars, only its mods stay autoloaded, then switch_theme. The
next load, on init (check_theme_switched): after_switch_theme with the
theme that left, whose defaults map the menu locations across
(_wp_menus_changed) and look the widgets over, then the rules flushed
and the record cleared. Deleting a theme fires delete_theme and
deleted_theme around its folder going, and forgets the update check.

constants.name: SLUG_GROUPS
constants.doc: The menu location names, by role, a theme's locations are matched across by.

methods.name: switchTo
methods.doc: switch_theme.

methods.name: checkSwitched
methods.doc: check_theme_switched: on the load after a switch, after_switch_theme with the theme that left.

methods.name: menusChanged
methods.doc: _wp_menus_changed: the leaving theme's menu locations mapped onto the arriving theme's.

methods.name: mapLocations
methods.doc:
wp_map_nav_menu_locations: with one location on each side, it is
kept; otherwise a location of the same name keeps its menu, then by
role, each name of a role in turn hands the next unused location of
that role (with a menu) to the arriving locations that name it.

methods.name: delete
methods.doc:
delete_theme: the folder removed between delete_theme and deleted_theme
(by $remove when the caller removes it its own way); false for no name.

methods.name: removeFolder
methods.doc: A theme's folder, directly inside the themes folder (a symlink unlinked, never followed); one already gone counts.

methods.name: nextOfGroup
methods.doc: The first location left in $old that a name of the group names, with a menu in it. @param array<string, mixed> $old @param list<string> $group

methods.name: names
methods.doc: Whether a location and a role's name contain one another, letter case aside.

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\Themes
classes.doc:
The site's themes as WordPress names and finds them: the active
stylesheet and template (as their filters leave them), the themes root on
disk and its address, each active theme's folder and its address, a theme
by its folder, every installed theme, and the extra roots plugins
register.

methods.name: stylesheet
methods.doc: The active theme's folder (get_stylesheet).

methods.name: template
methods.doc: The active parent theme's folder (get_template).

methods.name: root
methods.doc: Where themes live on disk (get_theme_root).

methods.name: rootUri
methods.doc: The themes root's address (get_theme_root_uri).

methods.name: stylesheetDirectory
methods.doc: The active theme's folder on disk (get_stylesheet_directory).

methods.name: templateDirectory
methods.doc: The active parent theme's folder on disk (get_template_directory).

methods.name: stylesheetDirectoryUri
methods.doc: The active theme's folder address (get_stylesheet_directory_uri).

methods.name: isBlockTheme
methods.doc: Whether the current theme is a block theme (wp_is_block_theme): the booted one's answer, or, for a stylesheet a filter swapped in, that theme's own.

methods.name: stylesheetUri
methods.doc: The active theme's stylesheet address (get_stylesheet_uri), as stylesheet_uri leaves it.

methods.name: templateDirectoryUri
methods.doc: The active parent theme's folder address (get_template_directory_uri).

methods.name: theme
methods.doc: A theme by its folder, the active one when none is named (wp_get_theme).

methods.name: all
methods.doc: Every installed theme by its folder (wp_get_themes).

methods.name: registerDirectory
methods.doc: A further themes root (register_theme_directory), under wp-content when not found as given; false when it is nowhere.

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\TimeSince
classes.doc:
How long ago something was, as human_time_diff words it: the span
between two times in its largest whole unit ("3 days"), through
human_time_diff.

methods.name: between
methods.doc: The span from one time to another (now when none is given).

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\Transients
classes.doc:
Values kept for a while, as WordPress keeps them in options: the site's
transients (_transient_{name}, with _transient_timeout_{name} when they
expire) and the network's (_site_transient_{name}), each read, set and
removed through the filters and actions plugins hook. An expired one reads
as false and is removed as it is read. While the request is installing, or
with a persistent object cache, they live in the object cache instead (the
transient and site-transient groups, an expiry handed along): the table is
neither read nor written, and removing one the cache lacks answers false
(probe transient-stores).

methods.name: get
methods.doc: A transient's value, or false (get_transient).

methods.name: set
methods.doc:
A transient set (set_transient): one that expires is stored not to
autoload, its timeout beside it; setting an expiry on one that had
none stores it again that way.

methods.name: delete
methods.doc: A transient removed (delete_transient), its timeout with it.

methods.name: getSite
methods.doc: A network transient's value, or false (get_site_transient); the update offers never expire by their timeout.

methods.name: setSite
methods.doc: A network transient set (set_site_transient), its timeout beside it when it expires.

methods.name: deleteSite
methods.doc: A network transient removed (delete_site_transient), its timeout with it.

methods.name: cached
methods.doc: Whether transients live in the object cache: while installing, or with a persistent object cache.

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\Translations
classes.doc:
The translations a request loads, as WordPress's l10n functions load
them: the locale in force, a text domain loaded from its file (or its
folder named for later) and unloaded, the default domain, a plugin's,
a user's locale, and the translations installed on disk; each step with
the filters that may answer first.

methods.name: folderFiles
methods.doc:
The translation files in a folder (WP_Textdomain_Registry::get_language_files_from_path):
the folder as pre_get_language_files_from_path hears it, trailing
slash and all, may answer; else its .mo and .l10n.php files, listed
once a request in the translation_files cache group.

methods.name: forgetFolders
methods.doc:
After an upgrade that installed translations, the listings of the
folders they went to are forgotten (WP_Textdomain_Registry::invalidate_mo_files_cache):
the plugins or themes language folder, else the language folder itself.

methods.name: locale
methods.doc: The locale in force (determine_locale): a switched one, else pre_determine_locale, else the configured one through determine_locale.

methods.name: load
methods.doc:
A text domain loaded from a translation file (load_textdomain), the
PHP file beside the .mo first unless translation_file_format says mo;
whether one loaded. Its locale becomes the one translations are looked
up in, and its folder where its script translations are looked for.

methods.name: unload
methods.doc: A text domain unloaded (unload_textdomain): whether it had files; one that did stays closed unless it may load again.

methods.name: fromFolder
methods.doc:
A domain's folder named for later (load_plugin_textdomain and the
rest): nothing is read and no locale asked until the domain's first
translation, which reads the folder's file for the locale then (probe
text-domain-timing).

methods.name: loadDefault
methods.doc: The default domain loaded again for a locale, the one in force unless named (load_default_textdomain).

methods.name: loadPlugin
methods.signature: loadPlugin(mixed $domain, mixed $deprecated = false, mixed $relativePath = false): bool
methods.doc:
A plugin's domain named to load from its folder
(load_plugin_textdomain): a path under the plugins folder when one is
given; else the deprecated folder under the site's root, told as
deprecated since 2.7.0; else the plugins folder itself.

methods.name: userLocale
methods.doc: A user's locale (get_user_locale), the signed-in user's for 0; the site's when the user has none or does not exist.

methods.name: installed
methods.doc:
The translations installed (wp_get_installed_translations) for core,
plugins or themes: by text domain and locale, each with its file's
headers; a .po without its .mo is not one.

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\TreeWalk
classes.doc:
The Walker contract's traversal: elements keyed by the walker's
db_fields parent/id pair, displayed depth-first through the walker's
four element methods, whole or a page of top-level elements at a time
(probe comment-walker). The facade Walker delegates here; subclasses
override the element methods (or display_element itself, as
Walker_Comment does to keep replies past the depth limit at their
parent's level) and the dispatch stays virtual.

methods.name: walk
methods.doc: Walks a tree with a Walker the way the reference does.

methods.name: page
methods.signature: page(object $walker, array $elements, int $maxDepth, int $page, int $perPage, array $args): string

methods.name: roots
methods.doc: How many of the elements have no parent. @param list<object> $elements

methods.name: forget
methods.doc:
An element's children, and theirs through the walker's unset_children,
taken out of the children list.

methods.name: element
methods.signature: element(object $walker, mixed $element, array $children, int $maxDepth, int $depth, array $args, string $output): void
methods.doc:
Walks one element and its children; replies past the depth limit stay
in the list for the walker (or the orphans) to place.

methods.name: buckets
methods.doc:
The top-level elements (no parent, or the parent given) and the
others by parent.

methods.name: alone
methods.doc: One element on its own at the top level: no children, one level shown.

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\TypeProps
classes.doc:
A post type's or taxonomy's properties from the arguments it was built
with, as WP_Post_Type::set_props and WP_Taxonomy::set_props fill them
(probe type-object-methods): the reference's defaults where an argument
is missing, a given value kept as given.

methods.name: postType
methods.doc:
A post type's properties from its arguments (probe type-object-methods):
the reference's defaults where an argument is missing, a given value
kept as given. The labels are the type's own; get_post_type_labels
makes them whole on the object.

methods.name: taxonomy
methods.doc:
A taxonomy's properties from the types it belongs to and its
arguments (probe type-object-methods): the reference's defaults where
an argument is missing, a given value kept as given. The meta box is
the category checklist for a hierarchical taxonomy and the tag box for
any other; its input is read as checkboxes for the checklist and as
text otherwise. A default term gets a name, slug and description.

methods.name: typeRewrite
methods.doc: A type's rewrite settles into its full form, public or not; feeds only where there is an archive (probe registry-rewrites).

methods.name: taxonomyRewrite
methods.doc:
A taxonomy's rewrite settles, whether queryable or not, the given keys
merged over the defaults; a rewrite of true leaves an empty "0" entry
behind, as the reference's merge does (probe registry-rewrites).

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\UpdateCounts
classes.doc:
The updates waiting, as wp_get_update_data counts them for the user
(probe admin-bar): plugins and themes from their update transients,
WordPress itself unless it is current, translations; each only for a
user who may update it. WordPress counts its own update only where
wp-admin's update functions are loaded; the engine always has them, so
it counts it everywhere.

methods.name: data
methods.doc: The updates waiting, counted for what the user may update, with their title (wp_get_update_data), as wp_get_update_data leaves them.

methods.name: translations
methods.doc:
The translation updates waiting (wp_get_translation_updates): none, as
the engine fetches no language packs on its own.

methods.name: core
methods.doc: The core releases offered (get_core_updates), each marked not dismissed; false when the offer holds none.

methods.name: forCurrentUser
methods.doc:
The counts and their title (before the wp_get_update_data filter),
and the titles one by one.
shapes: @return array{0: array{counts: array<string, int>, title: string}, 1: array<string, string>}

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\Upgrade
classes.doc:
What WP_Upgrader does with a package (probe upgrader), for the facade's
upgraders and so for everything that installs or updates a plugin or a
theme. run() is the whole pass: the options through
upgrader_package_options, the package downloaded and unpacked into
wp-content/upgrade/, put in place by install(), the result through
upgrader_install_package_result and told to the skin, and, for a single
item, upgrader_process_complete. The steps a subclass may replace
(fs_connect, download_package, unpack_package, install_package,
clear_destination) are called on the upgrader itself, as the reference
calls them, so a plugin's own upgrader class is honoured.

An update names the folder it replaces (hook_extra temp_backup); that
copy is moved to wp-content/upgrade-temp-backup/<dir>/<slug> before the
destination is cleared, moved back when the new one fails, and removed
once the pass is over. The reference keeps it for a weekly event to
clear and puts it back at shutdown; Minn keeps nothing and restores at
once.

constants.name: RUN
constants.value: array (   'package' => '',   'destination' => '',   'clear_destination' => false,   'clear_working' => true,   'abort_if_destination_exists' => true,   'is_multi' => false,   'hook_extra' =>    array (   ), )
constants.doc: The run options in the reference's order, which upgrader_package_options sees.

methods.name: run
methods.doc: WP_Upgrader::run; false when the filesystem cannot be reached.

methods.name: bulk
methods.doc:
The bulk pass of Plugin_Upgrader and Theme_Upgrader: the skin opened,
maintenance mode on when an active item is replaced, each item with an
offer run as one of many (one without is up to date, answered true),
the pass stopped when the filesystem refuses, then maintenance off, the
update cache cleaned, upgrader_process_complete told the whole list,
and the skin closed. False when the filesystem cannot be reached.
shapes: @param list<string> $items plugin files or theme folders
@param array<string, mixed> $offers item => the offer (its package)
@param array{directories: list<string>, maintenance: bool, prepare: \Closure(string): array{0: string, 1: array}, clean: \Closure(): void, complete: array} $how

params.name: how
params.shape: array{directories: list<string>, maintenance: bool, prepare: \Closure(string): array{0: string, 1: array}, clean: \Closure(): void, complete: array}

methods.name: install
methods.doc:
WP_Upgrader::install_package: the unpacked folder chosen (its one
folder, or the working folder when it holds several things), offered
to upgrader_pre_install and upgrader_source_selection, the destination
cleared or refused when something is there, the folder moved in (and
walked by the symbol gate at its next check), and the result offered
to upgrader_post_install.

methods.name: unzip
methods.doc: An archive unpacked into a folder through the site's filesystem (unzip_file): true, or the error why not.

methods.name: unpack
methods.doc:
WP_Upgrader::unpack_package, without the package's deletion (the
caller's): the upgrade folder emptied of what earlier passes left,
the package unzipped into a folder named for it with a random tail, and an archive that
will not open refused in the upgrader's words with the reader's reason.

methods.name: clear
methods.doc: WP_Upgrader::clear_destination: whatever is at the destination removed; true when nothing is left there.

methods.name: maintenanceOn
methods.doc: Maintenance mode on, as a bulk update of active plugins turns it on: the .maintenance file the front door reads.

methods.name: forgetUpdateEmail
methods.doc:
An update's own line taken out of the stored list of updates still to
be mailed about (auto_plugin_theme_update_emails), once it is done
(probe db-mail-rewrite-doubts).

methods.name: lastCoreUpdateFailed
methods.doc:
Whether a failed core update holds the next one back: a critical
failure does, and so does the same offer failing from the same version
when it is not to be retried.

methods.name: maintenanceOff
methods.doc: Maintenance mode off; said only when it was on.

methods.name: installUnpacked
methods.doc: install()'s steps, any of which may refuse.

methods.name: remove
methods.doc:
Removes a path in the upgrade folder through the site's filesystem, as
that is what unzipped it (FTP or SSH), and straight from disk when the
filesystem left it there.

methods.name: destinationFor
methods.doc: The folder the item lands in: a folder named for the package inside a known parent, otherwise the destination itself.

methods.name: clearOrRefuse
methods.doc: Clears the destination (an update's copy set aside first), or refuses when something is there and must not be replaced.

methods.name: move
methods.doc: The source moved (or, across filesystems, copied) to the destination; an existing destination is merged into.

methods.name: report
methods.doc: The run's outcome told to the skin; an update's set-aside copy put back on failure, removed on success.

methods.name: setAside
methods.doc: Moves an update's current copy to the backup folder (one left there by an earlier pass is replaced).

methods.name: backedUp
methods.doc: Where an update's copy lives ('from') and where it is set aside ('to'), or null when the update names none.

methods.name: randomName
methods.doc: Letters and digits drawn at random, $length of them.

methods.name: listing
methods.doc:
A folder's entries in the order the filesystem gives them, as the
reference's dirlist reads them (no sorting).

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\UserCounts
classes.doc:
The user counts WordPress's user functions give: how many users hold each
role (count_users), and how many posts several users wrote
(count_many_users_posts), as the reference was measured counting them
(probes user-remaining, taxonomy-blocks-user-doubts).

methods.name: users
methods.doc:
How many users there are and how many hold each role (count_users).
Only a user with a capabilities row counts; "none" is a user whose
row names nothing. The time strategy lists the registered roles that
have users, in their registered order, then none; any other strategy
lists none first, then every role a row names (registered or not), as
met user by user. pre_count_users may answer first.

methods.name: manyUsersPosts
methods.doc:
Post counts for several users (count_many_users_posts), as stored, 0
for none: published posts, and private ones too unless public only,
the viewer's own or every author's for a viewer who may read the
type's private posts. pre_count_many_users_posts may answer first.

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\UserEvents
classes.doc:
What the reference's REST users controller tells plugins, for the
engine's own: with plugins loaded an account is written through the
runtime's wp_insert_user, wp_update_user and wp_delete_user
(wp_set_password, each profile meta, the role, clean_user_cache,
user_register and the count, profile_update, delete_user and
deleted_user), and the REST actions follow. Without a booted runtime each
write is the engine's own, given as a closure.

methods.name: live
methods.doc: Whether plugins are loaded to be told anything.

methods.name: create
methods.doc:
Creates an account the way the REST controller does: wp_insert_user
with no role, rest_insert_user, then the role added, then
rest_after_insert_user. Returns the new id.
shapes: @param Closure(): int $quietly the engine's own write

methods.name: update
methods.doc:
Updates an account: wp_update_user with the changed fields, the role
when one is given, then the two REST actions.
shapes: @param array<string, mixed> $userdata the fields the request changes
@param Closure(): void $quietly the engine's own write

methods.name: delete
methods.doc:
Deletes an account, its posts going to $reassign (or with it when
none), then rest_delete_user with the account as it was.
shapes: @param Closure(): void $quietly the engine's own delete

methods.name: prepared
methods.doc:
rest_pre_insert_user over the prepared user (the request's fields), as
the reference runs it before the save; what the filter changes is
saved, an error refuses.

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\UserInsert
classes.doc:
The decisions behind wp_insert_user: what a new account needs, which email
and login collide, the resolved profile fields, and which columns an
update changes. The sanitisers and lookups arrive as closures so the
reference's filters apply. Behaviour pinned by contracts/fixtures/api/functions.json.

shapes: @param Closure(string): int $emailOwner 0 when nobody has it

methods.name: resolve
methods.doc: The validated, resolved fields, or the refusal the reference gives.
shapes: @param array<string, mixed>|null $existing the current row on an update
@return array{login: string, email: string, nicename: ?string, display_name: string, role: ?string}|Refusal

params.name: existing
params.doc: the current row on an update

methods.name: account
methods.doc: The fields a new account is created from. @param array{login: string, email: string, nicename: ?string, display_name: string, role: ?string} $resolved @return array<string, mixed>
shapes: @param array{login: string, email: string, nicename: ?string, display_name: string, role: ?string} $resolved @return array<string, mixed>

params.name: resolved
params.shape: array{login: string, email: string, nicename: ?string, display_name: string, role: ?string}

methods.name: changes
methods.signature: changes(array $userdata, array $existing, array $resolved, Closure $url, Closure $hash): array
methods.doc: The columns an update actually changes.
shapes: @param array{login: string, email: string, nicename: ?string, display_name: string, role: ?string} $resolved

params.name: resolved
params.shape: array{login: string, email: string, nicename: ?string, display_name: string, role: ?string}

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\UserOrder
classes.doc:
A user query's ORDER BY keys as the reference writes them (probe
wp-user-query-sql): the user columns by their short or full names, the
