display name, a post count (its subquery joined in), the id, the meta
key or meta value, the order include or a name list gives, or a named
meta clause; '' for a key it does not know.

methods.name: direction
methods.doc: ASC when asked for, DESC for anything else.

methods.name: clause
methods.doc: The column or expression one orderby key stands for.

methods.name: postCount
methods.doc: Joins each author's published post count in, and orders by it.

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\UserQueryRoles
classes.doc:
A user query's roles and capabilities as the meta clauses the reference
writes for them (probe wp-user-query-sql): a capability matches its own
name or any role granting it, capability__in and __not_in widen the role
lists, and each role is a LIKE on the site's capabilities meta (NOT LIKE
to leave it out).

methods.name: clauses
methods.doc: The meta query's clauses once the roles and capabilities join them.
shapes: @param array<array-key, mixed> $queries the meta query's own clauses
@param array<string, array{capabilities: array<string, bool>}> $roles the site's roles

methods.name: lists
methods.doc:
The roles asked for, the role__in and role__not_in lists (widened by
the roles granting capability__in and __not_in, then the capabilities
themselves), and the roles granting each capability asked for.
shapes: @return array{0: array{roles: list<string>, capabilities: list<string>}, 1: list<string>, 2: list<string>, 3: array<string, list<string>>}

methods.name: firstOf
methods.doc: The first of the wanted capabilities a role grants, in the order asked. @param list<string> $wanted @param list<string> $granted

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\UserQueryRunner
classes.doc:
WP_User_Query as the reference runs it (probe wp-user-query-sql): the
variables filled and handed to pre_get_users; the fields (a column list,
ids, the count), published authors, nicenames and logins, the meta query
with the roles and capabilities joined in, the order (post counts joined
in, include and list orders kept), the limit, a search over the columns
its shape suggests (through user_search_columns), ids in or out, the date
query, then pre_user_query; the query (users_pre_query may answer it),
found_users_query, and the results shaped as the fields ask.

constants.name: DEFAULTS
constants.value: array (   'blog_id' => 1,   'role' => '',   'role__in' =>    array (   ),   'role__not_in' =>    array (   ),   'capability' => '',   'capability__in' =>    array (   ),   'capability__not_in' =>    array (   ),   'meta_key' => '',   'meta_value' => '',   'meta_compare' => '',   'include' =>    array (   ),   'exclude' =>    array (   ),   'search' => '',   'search_columns' =>    array (   ),   'orderby' => 'login',   'order' => 'ASC',   'offset' => '',   'number' => '',   'paged' => 1,   'count_total' => true,   'fields' => 'all',   'who' => '',   'has_published_posts' => NULL,   'nicename' => '',   'nicename__in' =>    array (   ),   'nicename__not_in' =>    array (   ),   'login' => '',   'login__in' =>    array (   ),   'login__not_in' =>    array (   ),   'cache_results' => true, )
constants.doc: A user query's variables before its arguments are laid over them, in the order the user query hooks receive them.

methods.name: fillVars
methods.doc:
A users query's variables with their defaults filled in
(WP_User_Query::fill_query_vars), on this one site.

methods.name: prepare
methods.doc: Builds the query's pieces from its variables, as prepare_query does.

methods.name: searchSql
methods.doc:
A search over columns (get_search_sql): ID matched exactly, the rest
by LIKE with wildcards at the leading or trailing end, or both.

methods.name: query
methods.doc: Runs the query: users_pre_query may answer it; the count follows; the results take the fields' shape.

methods.name: fields
methods.doc: The SELECT's fields: named columns, ids, and the count's own. @param array<string, mixed> $qv

methods.name: published
methods.doc: Authors with published posts (of public types, or the ones named). @param array<string, mixed> $qv

methods.name: names
methods.doc: One nicename or login, or lists of them, in or out. @param array<string, mixed> $qv

methods.name: meta
methods.doc: The meta query with roles and capabilities, joined and written in. @param array<string, mixed> $qv

methods.name: order
methods.doc: ORDER BY from a key, a list, or a map of keys to directions; user_login when none is usable. @param array<string, mixed> $qv

methods.name: search
methods.doc:
The search: wildcards at either end, the columns given (those the
reference searches) or those its shape suggests, through
user_search_columns; ID matched exactly, the rest by LIKE.

methods.name: lastChanged
methods.doc: Reads a group's last-changed stamp from the object cache, setting it (wp_cache_set_last_changed) when the cache has none.

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\UserSave
classes.doc:
An account's fields through the filters the reference's wp_insert_user
runs, in its order (probe user-insert-filters, contracts/runtime.md
"Accounts plugins can change"): the login (pre_user_login), refused when
illegal_user_logins names it; the nicename, made from the login for a
new account (pre_user_nicename); the email and the URL; the nickname
(the login when none), first and last names; the display name, made as
the reference makes it when none is given; the description. Each
pre_user_* filter carries the reference's sanitisers. Then
wp_pre_insert_user_data over the row and insert_user_meta over the meta.

methods.name: fields
methods.doc: The fields after their filters, or the refusal for an illegal login.
shapes: @param array<string, mixed>|null $existing the stored account on an update

params.name: existing
params.doc: the stored account on an update

methods.name: data
methods.doc:
wp_pre_insert_user_data over the row an insert or update writes: the
row, whether it updates, the account's id (null for a new one), what
the caller gave.

methods.name: meta
methods.doc:
insert_user_meta over the profile meta, then insert_custom_user_meta
over the meta_input the caller gave beyond it; the two merged. An
update is one whose userdata names an ID.

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\UserStylesPost
classes.doc:
A theme's user styles post as WordPress's theme.json resolver finds and
makes it (probe global-styles-lookup): the newest wp_global_styles post
tied to the theme by its wp_theme term, through WP_Query (so plugins hear
the query and may steer it), made when asked and missing.

methods.name: data
methods.signature: data(mixed $theme, mixed $createPost = false, mixed $statuses = array (   0 => 'publish', )): array
methods.doc:
A theme's user styles post as an array
(WP_Theme_JSON_Resolver::get_user_data_from_wp_global_styles): the
newest of the statuses given, by the theme's name. When asked to make
one and there is none, the post is made for that theme, any theme,
its term given as tax_input (so set only for a user who may assign
it). [] when there is none.

methods.name: id
methods.doc: The active theme's user styles post id (WP_Theme_JSON_Resolver::get_user_global_styles_post_id), the post made when it is missing.

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\UserWrites
classes.doc:
Accounts written as WordPress's user functions write them: an account
made, changed (its row, profile meta and role, with the notices a
changed password or email sends) and deleted (its posts deleted or
handed on), a reset key issued, the lookups that guard a new account,
and the cached rows let go; each step with the actions and filters the
reference fires in its order.

constants.name: ROW_FIELDS
constants.value: array (   'user_login' => true,   'user_nicename' => true,   'user_url' => true,   'user_email' => true,   'display_name' => true, )
constants.doc: The fields an account's row takes from its filtered fields.

methods.name: validUsername
methods.doc: Whether a username survives strict sanitising unchanged and is not empty (validate_username), as validate_username leaves it.

methods.name: usernameExists
methods.doc: The id of the account with the login (username_exists), or false, as username_exists leaves it.

methods.name: emailExists
methods.doc: The id of the account with the email (email_exists), or false, as email_exists leaves it.

methods.name: isMember
methods.doc: Whether the user (the signed-in one when none is named) belongs to the site (is_user_member_of_blog).

methods.name: appPasswordsAvailable
methods.doc: Whether the site offers application passwords (wp_is_application_passwords_available): over HTTPS or on a local site, as the filter leaves it.

methods.name: appPasswordsAvailableFor
methods.doc: Whether a user may sign in by application password (wp_is_application_passwords_available_for_user): the site allows them, then the filter.

methods.name: resetKey
methods.doc:
A fresh reset key (get_password_reset_key), its hash stored under the
time it was issued through the account's save; the refusal when the
account may not reset.

methods.name: create
methods.doc: A new account (wp_create_user) from a login, password and email.

methods.name: insert
methods.doc:
An account made or changed (wp_insert_user) from slashed fields, as
the reference takes them: each field through its pre_user_ filter
first, slashed, in the reference's order; the row's fields then
unslashed, the profile meta unslashed as it is stored, and the
password the one given (hashed for a new account, stored as given on
an update). Its id, or the error saying why not.

methods.name: update
methods.doc:
An account changed (wp_update_user): the stored account and its
profile under the given fields, as the reference merges them, then
the notices a changed password or email sends.

methods.name: delete
methods.doc:
An account deleted (wp_delete_user): its posts deleted, or handed to
the account named; each meta key removed with its own actions, then
the row; false for an unknown account.

methods.name: cleanCache
methods.doc: A user's cached rows and meta let go (clean_user_cache), plugins told.

methods.name: row
methods.doc: An account's row from an id, a login, a user object, or an object with an ID.

methods.name: asArray
shapes: @return array<string, mixed> the account's fields from an array, a plain object or a user object

methods.name: insertAccount
methods.doc:
A new account as the reference writes it: the row, wp_set_password,
each profile meta added, the role, the caches let go, then
user_register. A role given as false leaves the account without one
for the caller to add.

methods.name: filteredRow
methods.doc:
A new account's row through wp_pre_insert_user_data, as the reference
hands it (the password hashed), and back.

methods.name: updateProfile
methods.signature: updateProfile(Minn\Objects\User $existing, array $userdata, array $resolved, array $given = array ( )): int
methods.doc:
The update half of wp_insert_user: the changed columns, the profile
meta, the role.

methods.name: changeNotices
methods.doc:
The notices a user whose password or email address changes is
mailed, to the address they had: whether each is sent is asked before
the save (a password that is the stored hash is no change), the mail
goes when the returned closure runs, after it.

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\VersionCheck
classes.doc:
Whether the WordPress version Minn reports and the PHP it runs on meet a
requirement (a plugin's "Requires at least" and "Requires PHP"), and where
to read about updating PHP.

methods.name: wordpress
methods.doc: Whether the reported WordPress version is at least the one required (is_wp_version_compatible); nothing required always is.

methods.name: php
methods.doc: Whether PHP is at least the version required (is_php_version_compatible); nothing required always is.

methods.name: updatePhpUrl
methods.doc: The page about updating PHP (wp_get_update_php_url): the filter's, unless it gives no address.

methods.name: defaultUpdatePhpUrl
methods.doc: The page about updating PHP before any filter (wp_get_default_update_php_url), in the site's language.

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\WidgetAreas
classes.doc:
The widgets helper functions as the reference answers them (probe
widget-helpers): a widget id split into its base and number, a sidebar
by id (the inactive widgets are a sidebar too, with a name and nothing
else), finding and moving a widget between sidebars, one widget rendered
in its sidebar as dynamic_sidebar renders each (an unregistered widget
renders nothing), and the sidebars with every registered one present;
the stored sidebars read and written, and which are registered.

constants.name: DEFAULT_WIDGETS
constants.doc: The widgets the engine provides.

constants.name: MAPPING_GROUPS
constants.doc: The id fragments a theme switch matches sidebars by, group by group (probe sidebars-mapping).

methods.name: registerDefaults
methods.doc:
The widgets the engine provides registered, then widgets_init for
plugin and theme code (wp_widgets_init); the Links widget only while
the link manager is on. The block widget is the one every modern
sidebar is made of, so it is registered before the action runs.

methods.name: show
methods.signature: show(mixed $widget, mixed $instance = array ( ), mixed $args = array ( )): void
methods.doc: A registered widget shown outside a sidebar (the_widget), in a div with its class unless the arguments say otherwise.

methods.name: stored
methods.doc:
The stored sidebars and their widgets (wp_get_sidebars_widgets), as
sidebars_widgets leaves them.

methods.name: convertSettings
methods.doc:
A widget's settings in the numbered form (wp_convert_widget_settings,
probe blocks-rest-widget-doubts): settings that are empty or not keyed
by number are a single widget's, made number 2, and the sidebars this
request holds name it by its new id; every result is marked a
multi-widget's. Nothing is stored.

methods.name: convertStoredSettings
methods.doc:
The same conversion as the admin makes it: a single widget's new id
goes into the stored sidebars (not this request's), and the settings
are stored under their option either way.

methods.name: store
methods.doc: The sidebars stored (wp_set_sidebars_widgets), at array version 3.

methods.name: current
methods.doc:
The sidebars with every registered one present and the widgets that
lost theirs inactive (retrieve_widgets), stored; before widgets_init,
the stored ones with the registered areas filled in empty.

methods.name: isRegistered
methods.doc: Whether a sidebar is registered (is_registered_sidebar).

methods.name: parse
methods.doc: wp_parse_widget_id: ['id_base' => ..., 'number' => n], or the id alone as its base. @return array{id_base: string, number?: int}

methods.name: sidebar
methods.doc: wp_get_sidebar: a registered sidebar, the inactive widgets, or null. @return array<string, mixed>|null

methods.name: find
methods.doc: wp_find_widgets_sidebar: the sidebar holding a widget, or null.

methods.name: assign
methods.doc: wp_assign_widget_to_sidebar: out of every sidebar, then onto the end of one ('' leaves it in none).

methods.name: render
methods.doc: wp_render_widget: a registered widget as its sidebar wraps it, through dynamic_sidebar_params; '' otherwise.

methods.name: control
methods.doc: wp_render_widget_control: a registered widget's settings form, or null.

methods.name: retrieve
methods.doc:
retrieve_widgets (probe widgets-remaining): the inactive list, then every
registered sidebar, holding only widgets that are registered. The
inactive list takes, in order, the registered widgets no list mentions
(the -1 placeholders aside, in the order they were registered), the
widgets already inactive, and the widgets of sidebars no longer
registered, which go.
shapes: @param array<string, mixed> $stored the stored lists, sidebar => widget ids

params.name: stored
params.doc: the stored lists, sidebar => widget ids

methods.name: map
methods.doc:
The old theme's widget lists fitted to the new theme's sidebars
(probe sidebars-mapping). One old sidebar and one new map straight
across. Otherwise a sidebar of the same id keeps its widgets; then,
group by group, the new sidebars whose ids hold one of the group's
fragments take, in order, the old ones that do (a new sidebar may take
from several groups); what is left goes after the inactive widgets.
When nothing is inactive then, the stored inactive widgets that are
registered and placed nowhere come back, keys kept.
shapes: @param array<string, mixed> $existing the old theme's lists
@param array<array-key, mixed> $stored the theme's stored inactive widgets

methods.name: numbered
shapes: @return array{0: array<int|string, mixed>, 1: bool} the settings numbered and marked, and whether they were a single widget's

methods.name: renamed
shapes: @param array<string, mixed> $sidebars @return array<string, mixed> each sidebar naming the single widget by its numbered id

params.name: sidebars
params.doc: @return array<string, mixed> each sidebar naming the single widget by its numbered id

methods.name: unmentioned
methods.doc: Registered widgets no stored list mentions, the -1 placeholders aside.

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\WpApiMode
classes.doc:
How much of the WordPress runtime a request gets, as the site declares it
in `wp-config.php`:

define('MINN_WP_API', 'on');    // the default: every request, as WordPress boots
define('MINN_WP_API', 'auto');  // the site's plugins run everywhere but public pages
define('MINN_WP_API', 'off');   // the site's plugins never run

A public page is a GET or HEAD that is not REST, the admin (`/wp-admin/`,
`/minn-admin/`) or one of WordPress's entry scripts (`wp-login.php`,
`wp-cron.php`, `wp-comments-post.php`, `xmlrpc.php` and the rest). Under
`auto` and `off` such a page loads no plugin or must-use plugin; an
extension route answers it without the runtime at all, and a themed page
still boots the facade the renderer draws through, with the theme's
functions.php (the theme is drawn as it is, its stylesheet among it). Minn
Admin's own plugin file is the admin's server half, so it loads on the
admin and REST in every mode. The drop-ins (`advanced-cache.php`,
`object-cache.php`) are the host's and load wherever the facade does.
WP-CLI is not a web request and always loads the plugins.

constants.name: SCRIPT
constants.doc: WordPress's entry scripts at the webroot: each is a surface of its own, never a public page.

methods.name: configured
methods.doc: What wp-config.php declared: on when nothing was, or something the engine does not know.

methods.name: loadsPlugins
methods.doc: Whether the site's plugins and must-use plugins load for this request.

methods.name: loadsMinnAdmin
methods.doc: Whether Minn Admin's plugin file loads for this request (when it is active).

methods.name: sparesRuntime
methods.doc: Whether an extension route may answer this request before the runtime boots.

methods.name: publicPage
methods.doc: A GET or HEAD for the site itself: not the admin, REST or an entry script.

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\WpdbFields
classes.doc:
The database object's writers and the charset work behind them (probe
db-mail-rewrite-doubts): an insert, replace, update or delete prepares one
statement holding every value (a null written as NULL in it), and an
insert or replace starts with insert_id at 0; the fields are checked
against their columns, every field that would not fit named in the error;
a table's columns are kept as the server's rows; a table that cannot be
read gives the charset failure; text in a charset other than UTF-8,
latin1 or binary is converted by the server; and check_safe_collation
passes ASCII, the statements that read no rows, latin1 tables and tables
whose text columns use only a binary or general UTF-8 collation.

methods.name: insert
methods.signature: insert(object $db, mixed $table, mixed $data, mixed $format, mixed $type): int|bool
methods.doc: Inserts or replaces a row from processed fields (wpdb::_insert_replace_helper): rows written, or false.

methods.name: update
methods.signature: update(object $db, mixed $table, mixed $data, mixed $where, mixed $format, mixed $whereFormat): int|bool
methods.doc: Updates the rows a where list matches (wpdb::update): rows written, or false.

methods.name: delete
methods.doc: Deletes the rows a where list matches (wpdb::delete): rows deleted, or false.

methods.name: process
methods.doc:
The fields with their formats, column charsets and lengths, or false:
when a column cannot be read, or when a value would not fit unchanged,
last_error naming every such field (wpdb::process_fields).

methods.name: charsets
methods.doc: Each field with its column's charset, or false when the table cannot be read (wpdb::process_field_charsets).

methods.name: lengths
methods.doc: Each field with its column's length, or false when the table cannot be read (wpdb::process_field_lengths).

methods.name: strip
methods.doc:
Each text value cut to what its column keeps (wpdb::strip_invalid_text):
malformed bytes dropped for UTF-8, four-byte characters too for utf8,
latin1 and binary kept, then cut to the column's length; text in any
other charset goes through the server's conversion, in one query.

methods.name: stripQuery
methods.doc: A query with what its table (the connection, when it names none) cannot hold dropped (wpdb::strip_invalid_text_from_query).

methods.name: safeCollation
methods.doc: Whether a query can skip the text check (wpdb::check_safe_collation).

methods.name: tableCharset
methods.doc:
The charset a table's text columns share, kept for the request
(wpdb::get_table_charset); pre_get_table_charset may answer first, and
a table the server cannot describe is the charset failure.

methods.name: columnCharset
methods.doc: A column's charset: false for one that holds no text, the table's for a column it does not have (wpdb::get_col_charset).

methods.name: columnLength
methods.doc: The most a text or binary column holds, false for any other column, the charset failure for a table that cannot be read (wpdb::get_col_length).

methods.name: queryCharset
methods.doc: The charset a query's text is held to: its table's, the connection's when it names none or its table cannot be read.

methods.name: columns
methods.doc:
A table's columns, the server's SHOW FULL COLUMNS rows by lower-cased
name, kept in col_meta; empty for a table the server cannot describe.

methods.name: sharedCharset
methods.doc:
The charset a table's columns come to (probe invalid-text): binary when
one holds bytes, false when none holds text, else their one charset;
latin1 beside others does not count, utf8 beside utf8mb4 is utf8, and
any other mixture is ascii.

methods.name: charsetOf
methods.doc: A table's charset through the object's own get_table_charset, which a subclass may answer.

methods.name: unreadable
methods.doc: The table charset failure.

methods.name: cut
methods.doc: A value cut to a column's length: bytes for latin1 (one character each) and the byte types, characters otherwise.

methods.name: convert
methods.doc:
Text in charsets PHP does not judge here, converted by the server to
the charset and back, cut to each column's length on the way.

methods.name: marks
methods.doc: The values a field list sends and the placeholder (or NULL) each takes in the statement.

methods.name: conditions
methods.doc: A where list as SQL: each field equal to its placeholder, or IS NULL.

methods.name: send
methods.doc: Sends a writer's one prepared statement, its values already checked.

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\WpdbReads
classes.doc:
What the database object plugins hold as $wpdb does when it runs and reads
(probe db-mail-rewrite-doubts): a query is heard by the query filter while
the last one's state is still there, and is not run at all while the
object is not ready; the readers ask check_safe_collation before running
one, give null for an empty value, and give nothing when asked to read
without a query (get_row, get_results) or in an output they do not know;
prepare's notices; and print_error, which keeps every error in
$EZSQL_ERROR and logs it with its caller. Members the object keeps
protected are reached in its own scope.

methods.name: query
methods.doc: Runs a query through the object, as wpdb::query: the number of rows read or written, true, or false.

methods.name: value
methods.doc: One value of the last result (or of a query run first): null for an empty one.

methods.name: row
methods.doc: One row of a query, as an object or an array; null with no query, or in an output it does not know.

methods.name: column
methods.doc:
One column of the last result (or of a query run first), each value read
through the object's own get_var.

methods.name: rows
methods.doc: The rows of a query in an output shape; null with no query, or in an output it does not know.

methods.name: prepare
methods.doc:
A query with its placeholders filled (Placeholders), every literal % as
the placeholder escape query() takes back out (wpdb::prepare). One
argument that is a list stands for the arguments. Reported through
doing_it_wrong: an argument it cannot use, a query with no % at all, a
count that does not match (too few arguments empty the query), and a
list of other than one value for a query with one placeholder (null).

methods.name: printError
methods.doc:
Reports a database error: kept in $EZSQL_ERROR, then (unless errors are
suppressed) logged with the calls that led to it. The markup to print
while errors are shown, else ''.

methods.name: ask
methods.doc: Runs a reader's query, skipping the text check when check_safe_collation finds it safe.

methods.name: run
methods.doc: Sends a query, unless it holds text its table cannot store.
shapes: @return array{0: mixed, 1: string, 2: bool} the result, the error, whether it reached the server

methods.name: keep
methods.doc: A read's rows kept on the object: the count of them.

methods.name: isObjectOutput
methods.doc: OBJECT in any case; the other outputs are matched exactly.

classes.name: Minn\Runtime\WpdbSetup
classes.doc:
How the database object plugins hold as $wpdb is set up (probe
db-mail-rewrite-doubts): it connects through its own db_connect, which
sets the connection's names with prepare; set_prefix answers with the
prefix it had, names the old tables too, and with set_table_names off
changes only the base prefix; set_blog_id names one site's tables from
the base prefix; CUSTOM_USER_TABLE and CUSTOM_USER_META_TABLE name the
user tables; set_sql_mode reads the session's modes without a query of
its own; a database that cannot be selected leaves the object not ready.
One site only: the engine is never a network.

methods.name: construct
methods.signature: construct(object $db, mixed $user, mixed $password, mixed $name, mixed $host): void
methods.doc: Sets the object up over the engine's connection (wpdb::__construct).

methods.name: connect
methods.doc: Takes the engine's connection and sets its names (wpdb::db_connect): true.

methods.name: charset
methods.doc: Sets a connection's charset and its names, with the collation when there is one (wpdb::set_charset).

methods.name: prefix
methods.doc:
Sets the table prefix (wpdb::set_prefix): the base prefix it had (the
new one the first time), or invalid_db_prefix for a prefix that is not
letters, digits and underscores.

methods.name: blog
methods.doc: Switches the site the object answers for (wpdb::set_blog_id): the id it had.

methods.name: tables
methods.doc:
The tables of a scope (wpdb::tables), by name to prefixed name unless
the prefix is not wanted; the user tables are the custom ones where
wp-config names them.

methods.name: select
methods.doc: Selects a database; one that cannot be selected leaves the object not ready (wpdb::select).

methods.name: sqlMode
methods.doc:
Sets the session's SQL modes (wpdb::set_sql_mode): the given ones, or the
session's own read from the connection, less the modes
incompatible_sql_modes names.

methods.name: name
shapes: @param array<string, string> $tables names each table property

classes.name: Minn\Support\Accents
classes.doc:
Accented and special characters to their plain spelling, from the
reference's own table (data/accents.json, captured with
tests/tools/accents-capture.php): text is put in composed form first, a
locale with spellings of its own (German, Danish, Catalan, Serbian,
Bosnian) has them, and a string that is not UTF-8 is read as Latin-1.
Anything the table does not name stays as it is.

methods.name: strip
methods.doc: The text with its accented characters spelled plainly, as the locale spells them.

methods.name: data
shapes: @return array{table: array<string, string>, locales: array<string, array<string, string>>, latin1: array<string, string>}

classes.name: Minn\Support\Backtrace
classes.doc:
A call stack named as wp_debug_backtrace_summary names it (probe
placeholders-a): Class->method, Class::method and function names; a
hook's function with the hook named; an included file by its path with
the given prefixes taken off, in order. Innermost first.

methods.name: summary
methods.doc: The frames' names, after the first $skip.
shapes: @param list<array<string, mixed>> $frames debug_backtrace()'s frames, innermost first
@param list<string> $truncate path prefixes taken off an included file

params.name: truncate
params.doc: path prefixes taken off an included file

classes.name: Minn\Support\ByteSize
classes.doc:
A count of bytes as a person reads it (size_format): in the largest unit
it reaches, from bytes to exabytes in steps of 1024, the number written
for the site's locale.

methods.name: format
methods.doc: The size with the decimals asked for; false for less than a byte.

classes.name: Minn\Support\DirectoryListing
classes.doc: Walks a directory the way the filesystem API lists it: named entries, dot entries skipped, hidden ones optional, recursion optional.

methods.name: read
methods.doc: A directory's entries described one by one, or false when unreadable.
shapes: @param callable(string): array<string, mixed> $describe the entry's own fields for an absolute path
@return array<string, array<string, mixed>>|false false when the path is not a readable directory

params.name: describe
params.doc: the entry's own fields for an absolute path

classes.name: Minn\Support\Email
classes.doc:
The address rules the reference applies: a local part from a fixed
character class, a dotted domain of hyphen-trimmed labels. `check` names
the first rule an address breaks; `sanitize` strips what it can and names
why it gave up.

methods.name: check
methods.doc: Why an address is invalid, or null when it passes the reference's checks.

methods.name: sanitize
methods.doc: An address with the characters the reference strips removed, and what was removed.
shapes: @return array{0: string, 1: string|null} the cleaned address (empty when refused) and the reason

classes.name: Minn\Support\Entities
classes.doc:
HTML special-character encoding with the reference's quote styles and its
"do not double encode" rule: an ampersand that already starts a known
named or numeric entity stays as it is.

methods.name: specialchars
methods.doc: The reference's special-characters escaping, with its quote styles and double-encoding rule.
shapes: @param callable(string): bool $knownEntity whether a named entity is in the allowed table

params.name: quoteStyle
params.doc: ENT_* flags, 'single', 'double', or false for none

params.name: knownEntity
params.doc: whether a named entity is in the allowed table

methods.name: decode
methods.doc: The reverse of specialchars: the five characters back, with the quote pairs the style asks for.

methods.name: convertInvalid
methods.doc: Windows-1252 numeric references rewritten as the Unicode references they meant.

methods.name: numericAsBytes
methods.doc: Numeric character references as the bytes they name, modulo 256 (wp_kses_decode_entities).

methods.name: windows1252
methods.doc:
Decimal references 128 to 159 name Windows-1252 characters, not the C1
controls Unicode puts there; each becomes the reference to the Unicode
character it meant, and a code Windows-1252 leaves unassigned is
removed. Only the exact unpadded decimal spelling is touched.

classes.name: Minn\Support\Escape
classes.doc:
Text made safe the way WordPress's escapers make it, each ending in the
filter plugins hook there, handed the result and the original: for HTML
(esc_html, esc_attr) invalid UTF-8 emptied, entities already present
normalised rather than encoded again, the specials and both quotes
encoded; for a textarea, everything encoded; for an inline script, a
single-quoted string's specials; and an address (esc_url) cleaned, its
protocol checked against the allowed ones.

methods.name: html
methods.doc: Text for an element's content.

methods.name: attr
methods.doc: Text for an attribute's value.

methods.name: tag
methods.doc: A tag name (tag_escape): letters, digits, hyphens, underscores and colons, lowercased, as tag_escape leaves it.

methods.name: textarea
methods.doc: Text for a textarea (esc_textarea): every special and quote encoded, references included.

methods.name: js
methods.doc: Text inside a single-quoted script string (esc_js): specials and double quotes encoded, single quotes and newlines escaped.

methods.name: url
methods.doc:
An address to print ('display') or to store ('db'): a missing scheme is
http (https when only https is allowed); for display "&" and "'"
become references; brackets are encoded; an address on a protocol not
allowed (the site's, unless a list is given) is empty. Then clean_url,
handed the address, the original and the context.

methods.name: validUtf8
methods.doc: The text when it is valid UTF-8, else nothing (wp_check_invalid_utf8 without stripping).

methods.name: specialchars
methods.doc:
The specials encoded in the given quote style (_wp_specialchars),
references already present normalised the way kses normalises them
rather than encoded again.

methods.name: forXml
methods.doc: Text for XML (esc_xml): invalid UTF-8 emptied, the specials encoded outside CDATA sections, through esc_xml.

methods.name: xml
methods.doc:
Text for an XML document (what esc_xml filters): named references XML lacks are
decoded (or their ampersand escaped), a bare ampersand and the four
specials encoded, and CDATA sections left exactly as written (probe
media-template-doubts).

methods.name: xmlCharacter
methods.doc: Whether a code point is a character XML allows.

classes.name: Minn\Support\FileHeaders
classes.doc:
Header values from a plugin or theme file. The labels (Plugin Name,
Theme Name, Version) are the published file-header contract; the
reader is a line scan of the first 8 KB, never PHP execution.

methods.name: values
methods.doc: The header values of a plugin or theme file, by label.

classes.name: Minn\Support\FileTree
classes.doc:
Whole-directory reads and copies. The engine's own installer, the update
unpacker and the plugins that reach for WordPress's copy_dir all want the
same two operations: list a tree, and duplicate one.

methods.name: files
methods.doc:
Every file under a directory, as list_files gives them: names starting
with a dot left out, the names in $skip left out at the top level only,
an empty folder named with a trailing slash. Depth 0 means no limit;
at the depth given a folder is named with its slash instead of entered.
shapes: @return list<string>|false false when the directory cannot be read

methods.name: filesWithHidden
methods.doc: As files(), dot files and folders included.

methods.name: copy
methods.doc:
Copies a directory's contents into another, creating it if it is not
there. Names in $skip are left behind at the top level only, which is
how the update unpacker keeps a directory it means to preserve.

methods.name: copyThrough
methods.signature: copyThrough(object $fs, string $from, string $to, array $skip, int $fileMode, int $dirMode): ?array
methods.doc:
A directory copied through a WordPress filesystem object, as copy_dir
copies it: the source listed, the destination made when it is missing,
each file copied (once more after a chmod when the first copy fails),
each missing folder made and copied in turn. A name in $skip is left
out at its own level, "folder/name" one level down. Null when it all
copied, else the refusal's code and data.

methods.name: listedFiles
methods.doc:
The files of a recursive filesystem listing (dirlist), each as a path
under $dir, in listing order, folders' files where the folder stands.

classes.name: Minn\Support\Files
classes.doc:
Recursive filesystem work behind WP_Filesystem_Direct: best-effort tree
delete and chmod (suppressed errors, keep-going semantics, the AND of
every step as the result), and the symbolic-to-octal permission string
conversion. The facade class keeps the reference's argument handling and
maps each operation here.

methods.name: octalFromSymbolic
methods.doc: drwxr-xr-x (or any rwx string) to its octal digits, the reference's tallying shape.

methods.name: deleteTree
methods.doc:
Delete a directory tree, files first, best effort; true only when
everything went. A symlinked directory is unlinked, never followed:
the dev sites symlink plugin folders into the tree, and a delete that
reached through one would empty the real source.

methods.name: chmodTree
methods.doc: Apply a mode to every FILE under a directory (the directories themselves keep theirs); always reports true.

classes.name: Minn\Support\Flag
classes.doc: A yes or no as WordPress reads one from loose input (wp_validate_boolean).

methods.name: of
methods.doc: The string "false" in any case is no; anything else is PHP's truth.

classes.name: Minn\Support\Hierarchy
classes.doc:
Loops in a parent chain, found with two walkers: a slow one that takes one
step at a time and a fast one that takes two (probe functions-utils, the
hierarchy-loop finders). They meet only when the chain loops; it ends
when a parent is empty. Each walker reads parents through the closure it
is given, so a caller can override any node's parent.

methods.name: meeting
methods.doc: The node where the slow walker meets the fast one, or null when the chain ends.

methods.name: walked
methods.doc:
Every node either walker stepped on before they met, in the order first
reached (the slow walker's node, then the fast one's two steps), or null
when the chain ends without a loop.

methods.name: walk
shapes: @return array{0: mixed, 1: array<int|string, true>} the meeting node (or null) and the nodes walked

classes.name: Minn\Support\Ip
classes.doc:
Addresses with their identifying tail removed, for logs and analytics that
must not keep a visitor's exact address. An IPv4 address loses its last
octet, an IPv6 address its last four groups. Anything that is not an
address at all reads as the unspecified IPv4 address rather than as itself,
so a malformed value can never leak through unchanged.

methods.name: anonymize
methods.doc: An address with its last octet, or its tail, zeroed.

classes.name: Minn\Support\Kses
classes.doc:
The HTML a user without unfiltered_html may store. Tags outside the
allowlist are removed and their text kept; attributes outside the tag's
list are dropped; URL attributes lose unsafe schemes; style attributes
keep only listed properties and no code. Comments keep their text, and
block delimiters are written back with their attribute values filtered.

constants.name: COMMENT
constants.value: array (   'a' =>    array (     0 => 'href',     1 => 'title',     2 => 'rel',   ),   'abbr' =>    array (     0 => 'title',   ),   'acronym' =>    array (     0 => 'title',   ),   'b' =>    array (   ),   'blockquote' =>    array (     0 => 'cite',   ),   'cite' =>    array (   ),   'code' =>    array (   ),   'del' =>    array (     0 => 'datetime',   ),   'em' =>    array (   ),   'i' =>    array (   ),   'q' =>    array (     0 => 'cite',   ),   's' =>    array (   ),   'strike' =>    array (   ),   'strong' =>    array (   ), )

constants.name: URI_ATTRIBUTES
constants.doc: Every attribute the reference treats as holding a URI, so its scheme is judged wherever the attribute is allowed.

constants.name: SCHEMES
constants.doc: The URI schemes allowed by default.

properties.name: commentDepth
properties.doc: How many comments the pass is inside now, and how deep one is still passed as found.

methods.name: post
methods.doc: Post content as an author without unfiltered_html may store it.

methods.name: comment
methods.doc: A comment, profile or term description as anyone without unfiltered_html may store it: listed attributes only.

methods.name: sanitize
methods.doc:
The whole pass wp_kses makes with its default hooks: control
characters out, references normalized, a "<" that opens no tag
escaped, block attribute values filtered the same way, then the tags.

methods.name: withoutControls
methods.doc: The control characters kses removes (tab, newline and carriage return stay).

methods.name: withoutNulls
methods.doc: The control characters and backslashed zeros taken out (wp_kses_no_null).

methods.name: normalizeEntities
methods.doc:
Every "&" made a reference, in one pass: a known name or a code point
kses accepts stays one (decimal padded to three digits, hex with a
lower-case x), anything else becomes "&".

methods.name: lessThan
methods.doc:
A "<" that reaches the next "<" or the end without a ">" is text: the
run is escaped the way esc_html escapes it (quotes included).

methods.name: escapeHtml
methods.doc: Text escaped for HTML with references kept: invalid UTF-8 gives nothing, quotes become " and '.

methods.name: blockAttributes
methods.doc:
Block markup with every attribute key and string value passed through
the same filter, and the delimiters written back in their canonical
form ("--->" read as "-->"). Markup without a comment is left alone.

methods.name: blockAttributesParsed
methods.doc:
As blockAttributes, the blocks read by the parser block_parser_class
names (probe kses-allowed-asks), written back as it read them; $entry
sees each cleaned entry with its block's name and key and returns its
value (a template part's tag names, probe sweep-1020b).

methods.name: allowing
methods.doc:
Content kept to an allowlist as wp_kses keeps it: control characters
dropped (a slashed zero kept), references normalized, then pre_kses
(handed the allowlist and protocols as given), then only the markup the
allowlist allows, with links on the given protocols. A named allowlist
(a context such as "post") is resolved by $tagsFor after pre_kses. The
URI attributes are asked for only when the content opens an element
the allowlist allows.

methods.name: uriAttributes
methods.doc: The attributes judged as URIs, through wp_kses_uri_attributes (its answer as given).

methods.name: filter
methods.doc:
The tag pass: each run from "<" to the next ">" (or the end) is a
comment, an inert bogus comment ("</" before a non-letter, "<!"
before a lower-case letter), or an element judged by the policy;
anything else in angle brackets goes. Text between keeps its
references, with stray ones escaped. Run alone (wp_kses_split), a
last "<" with no ">" still reads as a tag; inside sanitize() the
less-than pass has already escaped it.

methods.name: tag
methods.doc:
One run of the tag pass on its own (wp_kses_split2): a comment, a
tag, or, for anything not starting with "<", a lone ">".

methods.name: element
methods.doc:
An element rebuilt with the attributes the policy allows it
(wp_kses_attr), its name as written and an XHTML slash kept; an
element the policy does not know keeps none.

methods.name: attributeList
methods.doc:
The attributes written inside a tag, read the way kses reads them: a
name, then "=" and a quoted or bare value, or no value at all; junk
between (stray quotes, "=", "/") is skipped; the first of two
same-named attributes wins. Null when a quoted value never closes,
which costs the tag every attribute.
shapes: @return array<string, array{name: string, value: ?string, whole: string}>|null

methods.name: text
methods.doc: Plain text: tags gone, whitespace collapsed, control characters dropped.

methods.name: url
methods.doc:
A URL for a stored field: empty when its scheme is not one the
reference allows. The scheme is judged as a browser reads it, without
the tabs, line breaks and other control characters it drops (java,
a tab, then script: is javascript:).

methods.name: attributeUrl
methods.doc:
A URL inside markup: whatever stands before the first colon, once
every character reference and percent escape is decoded as deep as it
goes and the invisible characters are dropped, must be an allowed
scheme, or it is cut off and the rest is judged again. The reference
cuts "?q=a:b" to "b" and "javascript:alert(1)//http://" to "//" the
same way. A value with a good scheme is returned as given.

methods.name: validCodePoint
methods.doc:
Whether a code point is one a reference may name (valid_unicode): tab,
line feed, carriage return, and the rest of Unicode from space up,
except the surrogates and U+FFFE and U+FFFF.

methods.name: tagsAsked
methods.doc:
The HTML a context allows, asked as the reference asks it (probe
kses-allowed-asks): once for each element tag the content holds,
opening or closing; never for text, comments or a lone bracket. The
first answer stands for them all.

methods.name: run
methods.doc: One bracketed run as the tag pass keeps it, or nothing; a slashed quote in it is a quote, as on the reference (`title=\"x\"`).

methods.name: htmlComment
methods.doc:
A comment kept whole, its body run through the same pass (a ">" in it
escaped, tags judged), then no "--" left inside; an empty one dropped,
an unclosed one closed.

methods.name: deepDecode
methods.doc: A value with its references and percent escapes decoded until nothing changes, so no encoding hides a scheme.

methods.name: visible
methods.doc: The text with whitespace, control characters, no-break spaces, and replacement characters removed.

methods.name: normalizeText
methods.doc:
Text between tags as the reference stores it: valid references stay
references (decimal ones padded to three digits), invalid ones and
stray ampersands become "&", and a closing bracket is escaped.

methods.name: normalizeAttribute
methods.doc:
An attribute value as the reference stores it: valid references become
their characters, except that the five markup characters stay escaped
(an apostrophe as '); invalid references and stray ampersands
become "&"; raw quotes are escaped.

methods.name: named
methods.doc: What a named reference stands for, or null when the name is not one.

methods.name: codePoint
methods.doc: A numeric reference's code point, or null when it names no character the reference accepts.

methods.name: attributes
methods.doc:
The attributes the policy allows, in the order written: a value must
meet its rules, a URI keeps only an allowed scheme, srcset and style are
judged on their own terms. A tag that loses a required attribute keeps
none at all.

methods.name: rendered
methods.doc: One allowed attribute as stored, or null when its value is judged away entirely.

methods.name: srcset
methods.doc: Every candidate must be an absolute URL with a safe scheme, or the attribute goes.

classes.name: Minn\Support\KsesAttributes
classes.doc:
Kses one attribute at a time, for the shortcode pass that runs inside
HTML tags: an opening tag cut into its attributes, and one attribute
judged as kses judges it on its element. Probe shortcode-run.

methods.name: elementParts
methods.doc:
An opening tag cut as wp_kses_attr_parse cuts it: the start ("<a "),
each attribute with the whitespace after it (a shortcode standing as
a name counts as one), and the end (">" or "/>"). Null for a closing
tag, a comment, CDATA, or anything between the brackets that is not
attributes.

methods.name: parse
methods.doc:
An attribute string cut into its attributes, each with the whitespace
after it (wp_kses_hair_parse): a name (or a shortcode standing as one),
then "=" and a quoted or bare value, or nothing. Null when anything in
it is not an attribute: leading whitespace, a stray quote, a quoted
value that never closes.

methods.name: oneAttribute
methods.doc:
One attribute as written, judged as kses judges it on the element
(wp_kses_one_attr): the value escaped for an attribute and kept in its
own quotes (a bare one gains double quotes), a URL's bad scheme cut
away, style kept to the allowed properties; nothing when the element
may not carry it (the whitespace around it kept, as on the
reference), nothing at all when a quoted value never closes. The
whitespace around a kept one stays.

classes.name: Minn\Support\KsesCss
classes.doc:
The style attribute as kses keeps it (safecss_filter_attr): each
declaration whose property is on the list stays, a value's url() only
on the properties that may hold one and only with a safe scheme, the
gradients and CSS functions the reference allows, and nothing that could
end the declaration. Plugins widen the list and the verdict through the
hooks the facade wires in (safe_style_css, safecss_filter_attr_allow_css).

constants.name: CSS_PROPERTIES
constants.doc: The properties style attributes keep, as the reference lists them before safe_style_css (probe safety-filters); --* stands for custom properties.

constants.name: CSS_FUNCTIONS
constants.doc: The CSS functions a value may use (transforms, shapes and the math ones), whatever they hold.

constants.name: CSS_GRADIENTS
constants.doc: The gradients a background may use.

constants.name: CSS_URL_PROPERTIES
constants.doc: The properties that may use a url().

constants.name: CSS_GRADIENT_PROPERTIES
constants.doc: The properties that may use a gradient.

methods.name: style
methods.doc: A style attribute's value with only the listed properties kept.

methods.name: styleHooks
methods.doc:
The runtime's say over style attributes: the property list
(safe_style_css) and each declaration (safecss_filter_attr_allow_css).
The facade sets these as it loads.

methods.name: css
methods.doc:
The style attribute's declarations kept as written, as the reference
keeps them (probes kses, block-supports): a listed property, named
exactly (the list through safe_style_css when the runtime hooks it;
--* lets custom properties through), or a bare value; and nothing in
the value that could end the declaration or open a function (\ ( & =
} or a comment) once the functions it may use are taken out, with a
background's gradients and the url()s of allowed schemes a background,
a cursor, a filter, a mask or a clip path may use. Each is asked
through safecss_filter_attr_allow_css.

methods.name: cssTestString
methods.doc:
What of a declaration must hold no unsafe character: its value (or the
bare value) without the functions it may use; null for a property not
listed, or a url() with a scheme not allowed (on a property that cannot
use one, its parenthesis fails the test).

classes.name: Minn\Support\KsesDirectives
classes.doc:
The Interactivity API's bindings under kses (probe patch-714). A tag
whose allowlist checks some attribute's value cannot let post content
bind an attribute kses did not allow plainly: a binding would set at
render time the value kses judged, or never saw. Directives other than
data-wp-bind-- are left to the allowlist.

constants.name: NOT_VALUE_RULES
constants.doc: The rule keys that say nothing about an attribute's value.

methods.name: restrictsValues
methods.doc:
Whether a tag's attribute allowlist checks any value: some attribute's
rules are a list holding a key other than required and valueless
(_wp_kses_restricts_attribute_values).

methods.name: bindsRestricted
methods.doc:
Whether a directive, as written, binds an attribute the tag may not
take from a binding (_wp_kses_directive_binds_value_restricted_attribute):
a data-wp-bind-- directive on a tag that checks values, naming an
attribute (compared as written) that is not allowed plainly. Allowed
plainly is a rule of exactly true, or a data- name under "data-*".

classes.name: Minn\Support\KsesEntities
classes.doc:
The named references kses keeps as written: the list captured from the
reference (data/kses.json) plus the five XML ones. Any other name is
stored as "&name;".

methods.name: known
methods.doc: Whether "&name;" is a reference kses leaves alone.

methods.name: allowlist
methods.doc: An allowlist the reference ships, by context ("post" or "data").

classes.name: Minn\Support\KsesPolicy
classes.doc:
What one kses pass allows: the tags, each tag's attributes (allowed
plainly or with value rules), whether a tag takes data- attributes,
which attributes hold URIs, and the schemes those URIs may use.

shapes: @param array<string, array<string, mixed>> $tags tag => attribute => true, or a list of value rules
@param array<string, list<string>> $prefixes tag => attribute-name prefixes it accepts (only "data-")

params.name: tags
params.doc: tag => attribute => true, or a list of value rules

methods.name: post
methods.doc: Post content from an author without unfiltered_html: the reference's post allowlist as captured.

methods.name: comment
methods.doc: Comments, profiles and term descriptions: only the attributes each tag lists, nothing global.

methods.name: fromAllowlist
methods.doc:
A caller's own allowlist taken literally: a listed attribute is allowed
whatever it maps to (false included, as the reference only asks whether
the name is there), an array carries value rules, and "data-*" lets the
tag take any data- name. Nothing else is implied.

methods.name: allowsTag
methods.doc: Whether the tag may appear at all.

methods.name: rules
methods.doc:
The rules an attribute carries on a tag: an empty list when it is
allowed plainly, null when it is not allowed.

methods.name: bindsRestricted
methods.doc: Whether an attribute (its name lowercased, as kses reads it) is a binding the tag may not take (KsesDirectives).

methods.name: required
methods.doc: The attributes a tag must keep: lose one and the tag keeps none.

methods.name: holdsUri
methods.doc: Whether the attribute holds a URI whose scheme must be judged.

classes.name: Minn\Support\KsesProtocols
classes.doc:
The protocols an address may use, as kses judges them: the site's list
(kses_allowed_protocols), and an address with a protocol not on the list
taken off it, encoded colons and entity-spelled protocols seen through.

methods.name: allowed
methods.doc:
The protocols addresses may use (wp_allowed_protocols): the table's
list through kses_allowed_protocols, asked again on every call until
wp_loaded has run, then kept.

methods.name: strip
methods.doc:
An address with a protocol the list does not allow taken off
(wp_kses_bad_protocol): null bytes gone; an http or https address left
as written when that protocol is allowed; otherwise the protocol checked
again until nothing changes (up to six times), and empty if it never
settles.

methods.name: stripOnce
methods.doc:
One pass of the protocol check (wp_kses_bad_protocol_once): encoded
colons decoded; when what comes before the first colon (and holds no
"/?") is an allowed protocol it is lower-cased and kept, otherwise taken
off; either way what follows is trimmed.

classes.name: Minn\Support\KsesValues
classes.doc:
The value rules an allowlist attribute may carry, as the reference judges
them: lengths count bytes, bounds need a whole number (up to six digits,
up to six spaces either side), "valueless" compares the attribute's form,
"values" compares without case, and a callback decides for itself. A rule
the reference does not know passes. Where the reference fatals (a values
rule that is not a list, a callback that does not exist) the value fails.

methods.name: satisfies
methods.doc:
Whether a value meets every rule its attribute carries; "required" is
the tag's concern, so it is skipped here.

methods.name: check
methods.doc: One rule against one value; $valueless is "y" for a bare attribute and "n" for one with a value.

methods.name: pdfObject
methods.doc:
Whether a URL may be an object's data in post content: an http or https
URL on the uploads host and port, no credentials, query or fragment,
whose path ends in ".pdf".

classes.name: Minn\Support\Lists
classes.doc:
List shaping behind the facade's array utilities: arguments over their
defaults (wp_parse_args), plucking and filtering (WP_List_Util), the multi-field sort
wp_list_sort() promises (loose comparison per field, first difference
wins) and the row-shape conversions wpdb hands back for its OBJECT_K /
ARRAY_A / ARRAY_N output formats.

methods.name: filterParsed
methods.doc: Hands over the filter a parsed query string goes through (wp_parse_str), or takes it back with null.

methods.name: args
methods.doc:
Arguments as WordPress takes them (wp_parse_args): an object's
properties, an array, or a query string, over the defaults.

methods.name: pluck
filter
methods.doc:
The items matching all the fields given (AND), any of them (OR), or
none (NOT), compared loosely, keys kept; nothing for another operator.

methods.name: items
methods.doc:
A list as arguments give one (wp_parse_list): an array's entries
trimmed, the empty ones dropped (keys kept); a string split on commas
and whitespace.

methods.name: ids
methods.doc:
Ids as arguments give them (wp_parse_id_list): each a whole number made
positive, each once, in first-seen order.

methods.name: sort
methods.doc: Items sorted by several fields, each ascending or descending.

methods.name: shapeRows
methods.doc:
Rows of stdClass shaped for a wpdb output format: keyed by their first
column (first row wins a duplicate key), associative, or numeric.

methods.name: descendants
methods.signature: descendants(array $items, int $rootId, callable $id, callable $parent, array $visited = array ( )): array
methods.doc:
Every descendant of one root in a flat parent-linked list, preorder
(a child ahead of its own children), the shape _get_term_children and
get_page_children walk. Visited ids guard against a parent cycle.

classes.name: Minn\Support\Locale
classes.doc:
The locale's calendar and number vocabulary as data: the names a site
prints for weekdays, months and meridiems, and how it separates
thousands and decimals.

The names are English here because the engine carries no core
translations yet; the facade runs each one through the translation
filters on the way out, so a catalogue can answer for them later
without this class changing.

methods.name: weekdayInitial
methods.doc: A weekday's one-letter form.

methods.name: abbreviation
methods.doc: A weekday's or month's three-letter form; May is already three letters.

methods.name: monthKey
methods.doc: Months are keyed by their zero-padded number, both ways round.

classes.name: Minn\Support\Markers
classes.doc:
The BEGIN/END marker blocks insert_with_markers() maintains in files like
.htaccess: the captured shape keeps everything outside the markers,
replaces the block inside them, and writes the reference's four-line
do-not-edit preamble ahead of the inserted lines.

methods.name: write
methods.doc: Replaces the lines between a marker's begin and end comments in a file.

methods.name: read
methods.doc:
The lines between a marker's begin and end comments, every block of it
in order. A line opens or closes a block when it contains the comment
anywhere (case-sensitive); lines that start with "#" are left out, so
the preamble and any nested markers are, while indented comments stay.
Lines split on "\n" only, and a block left open at the end of the file
keeps the empty line after its final newline.

classes.name: Minn\Support\Paths
classes.doc: File-system path and permission spellings, and whether a path is safe to use.

methods.name: validate
methods.doc:
Whether a path is safe to use (validate_file): 0 when it is; 1 when it
climbs out (a bare "../", more than one, or one not at the end); 2 for a
drive letter; 3 when a list is given and the path is not on it.

methods.name: translationDir
methods.doc:
The trailing-slashed directory holding a text domain's {domain}-{locale}.mo:
a custom path first, then the language dir's plugins and themes folders,
then the dir itself for the default domain; false when none has the file.
$listed, when given, lists a folder's files (the textdomain registry's
own lister, which plugins may answer for) and is read instead of the disk.

methods.name: normalize
methods.doc: Forward slashes only, runs collapsed, a stream wrapper kept, a Windows drive letter upper-cased.

methods.name: symbolicMode
methods.doc: The `ls -l` spelling of a mode: type letter, then rwx for owner, group and world with the setuid, setgid and sticky bits folded in.

classes.name: Minn\Support\Sanitize
classes.doc:
Text made fit to store the way WordPress's sanitizers make it, each ending
in the filter plugins hook there, handed the result and what was given: a
title (accents gone when saving), a key, a line of plain text, a user name,
an email address and the check of one.

methods.name: title
methods.doc: A title as a slug's source (sanitize_title): accents gone when saving; the fallback when the filter leaves nothing.

methods.name: key
methods.doc: A key (sanitize_key): lower case letters, digits, underscores and dashes only.

methods.name: textField
methods.doc: One line of plain text (sanitize_text_field): tags, line breaks, extra spaces and stray octets gone; anything but text is empty.

methods.name: user
methods.doc:
A user name (sanitize_user): tags, accents, octets and references gone,
spaces collapsed; strictly, only letters, digits, spaces and _ . - @.

methods.name: htmlClass
methods.doc:
A class name for HTML (sanitize_html_class): escaped octets and
anything but letters, digits, _ and - taken out; the fallback's when
nothing is left; then the filter.

methods.name: hexColor
methods.doc: A hex colour as given when it is one (#abc or #aabbcc), empty for none, else null (sanitize_hex_color).

methods.name: textareaField
methods.doc: Lines of plain text (sanitize_textarea_field): as a text field, line breaks kept; then the filter.

methods.name: email
methods.doc: An email address with what may not be in one taken out (sanitize_email), and why when nothing is left.

methods.name: isEmail
methods.doc: The address when it reads as one, else false (is_email), as the filter leaves it.

classes.name: Minn\Support\ScriptTag
classes.doc:
Script elements as the reference builds them (probe script-tags): the
attributes sorted by name, a src or href through esc_url and every other
value escaped (true or null printed bare, false left out); inline code
between newlines, with any "<script" or "</script" that would end or
open an element written with its "s" as a \u escape. Only JavaScript and
JSON can carry that escape: a script of another type whose code holds
such a sequence is not printed at all.

constants.name: ESCAPABLE
constants.doc: The script types inline code is JavaScript or JSON in (lowercase, trimmed; no type at all counts as JavaScript).

constants.name: TAG
constants.doc: A sequence that would open or close a script element inside one.

methods.name: element
methods.doc: The empty element for a script file.

methods.name: inline
methods.doc:
The element for inline code (already between its newlines), or '' when
its type cannot hold the code safely.

methods.name: attributes
methods.doc: The attributes as markup, each with its leading space.

classes.name: Minn\Support\SearchReplace
classes.doc:
String replace that walks serialized-PHP arrays of scalars without
unserialize, so a domain change in an option blob keeps its lengths.

methods.name: in
methods.doc: A value with one string replaced, and how many times.
shapes: @return array{0: string, 1: int} replacement and how many times $old occurred

classes.name: Minn\Support\Serialized
classes.doc:
Tolerant readers for the serialized-PHP blobs WordPress stores. Nothing
here executes the blob; each reader scans for the one shape it needs.

constants.name: INVALID
constants.doc: Returned by decode() when the blob is not a serialized value the reader accepts.

constants.name: MAX_DEPTH
constants.doc: The deepest nesting a record may have, PHP's own default (unserialize_max_depth).

constants.name: SMALLEST_PAIR
constants.doc: The fewest bytes an array or object member can take: a key "i:0;" and a value "N;".

properties.name: open
properties.doc: The objects being encoded right now, outermost first, so a loop is seen.

methods.name: stringList
methods.doc: The string values of a serialized string list.

methods.name: serializeStringList
methods.doc: A flat string list in the stored form.

methods.name: field
methods.doc: The first "field";value pair inside a blob: string, int, or float value as a string.

methods.name: decode
methods.doc:
A serialized scalar or array as PHP data, parsed by this reader:
strings, integers, floats, booleans, null, and arrays of those. An
object record becomes a stdClass of its properties, or whatever the
reviver makes of the class name and those properties; nothing here
instantiates anything itself. A blob with trailing bytes or a
malformed shape is INVALID.
shapes: @param ?\Closure(string, \stdClass, list<array{0: int|string, 1: mixed}>): object $revive handed the class, the properties, and the stored names with their values

params.name: revive
params.doc: handed the class, the properties, and the stored names with their values

methods.name: storedClass
methods.doc: The class an object was stored as, when it came back as a stdClass of its properties.

methods.name: looksSerialized
methods.doc:
Whether a string has the shape of serialized data, as is_serialized()
judges it by default: its last byte closes the record (what
maybe_unserialize() decodes). Measured over sixty strings (probe
sweep-1020b).

methods.name: mayBeSerialized
methods.doc:
Whether a string may be serialized data, as is_serialized($data, false)
judges it: a close anywhere will do. What maybe_serialize() stores
serialized again so it reads back as the string it was.

methods.name: maybeEncode
methods.doc:
A value as maybe_serialize() stores it: an array or object serialized,
and a string that already looks serialized serialized again, so it
reads back as the string it was; anything else as given.

methods.name: encode
methods.doc:
PHP's serialize() for the values decode() accepts: null, bool, int,
float, string, arrays of those, and objects written as their class.

methods.name: intList
methods.doc: The integer values of a serialized list such as sticky_posts.

methods.name: readObject
methods.doc:
An object record. The properties land on a plain stdClass; only the
reviver may turn that into something else, and only for a class it
knows. A record it leaves alone keeps its class name and its stored
property names (visibility markers, numbered parts, a private name a
parent class shares) on the side, so encode() writes it back as it
was read instead of as a stdClass.

methods.name: encodeRecord
methods.doc:
A stdClass, or a record read back as one, in PHP's own form: the
stored class name and property names where there are some, property
names as strings otherwise, each value through encode() so a record
nested inside keeps its class too.
shapes: @param array{class: string, keys: array<string, int|string>, hidden: list<array{0: int|string, 1: mixed}>} $record

params.name: record
params.shape: array{class: string, keys: array<string, int|string>, hidden: list<array{0: int|string, 1: mixed}>}

methods.name: encodeWrapper
methods.doc: PHP's array wrappers in their own form (flags, storage, members, iterator class), the storage through encode().

methods.name: size
methods.doc:
A length or a count: digits only, and never more than the bytes left
could hold, $perItem bytes each. A negative length would move the
reader backwards and a huge count would keep it reading, so either
makes the record no record at all, as PHP's own reader finds it.

methods.name: opens
methods.doc: A type letter and a colon, then at least two bytes.

methods.name: opensRecord
methods.doc: An array, object or enum record's head: its letter, a count and a colon.

methods.name: encodeObject
methods.doc:
Plugin code stores objects (maybe_serialize's contract). A record read
back as a stdClass is written under the class it was stored as; a
stdClass and PHP's array wrappers are written here so a record inside
them keeps its class too; any other object goes through PHP's own
serializer, which runs nothing and matches the reference byte for
byte. Only reading is the hazard, and reads stay on decode().

classes.name: Minn\Support\Signatures
classes.doc:
A file checked against detached Ed25519 signatures of its SHA-384 hash,
as verify_file_signature checks it: a signature that does not decode to
the signature length is skipped, and for each one that does, every key
that does not decode to the key length is skipped too; the counts and the
hash are what the caller reports when nothing verifies.

methods.name: check
methods.doc:
Whether any signature verifies with any key, the file's hash in hex,
and how many keys and signatures were skipped.
shapes: @return array{verified: bool, hash: string, skipped_key: int, skipped_sig: int}

classes.name: Minn\Support\Slashes
classes.doc:
Magic-quote slashes the way WordPress keeps them (wp_slash, wp_unslash):
added to or stripped from every string inside a value, arrays and
objects walked all the way down, anything else left as it is.

methods.name: add
methods.doc: Every string in a value with its quotes and backslashes slashed.

methods.name: strip
methods.doc: Every string in a value with one level of slashes taken off.

classes.name: Minn\Support\Sprintf
classes.doc:
A pattern filled one fragment at a time, as wp_sprintf fills it: "%%" is
a percent sign, each other fragment (a directive and the text up to the
next one) takes the next argument or the one its position names, and
$filter may write a fragment itself (the wp_sprintf filter: the list
directive %l lives there); otherwise PHP's sprintf fills it, an array
as nothing, and a fragment it cannot fill stays as written.

methods.name: format
methods.doc: The pattern with its arguments filled in.
shapes: @param Closure(string, mixed): mixed $filter the fragment and its argument in, the fragment as written out

params.name: filter
params.doc: the fragment and its argument in, the fragment as written out

classes.name: Minn\Support\SqlTable
classes.doc:
The table a SQL statement is about, as wpdb::get_table_from_query reports
it, and a database host string read into its parts (probe wpdb). A name is
letters, digits, $ _ . - and backticks (dropped), plus two-byte UTF-8.

constants.name: LEADS
constants.doc: What leads to the table name in each statement the reference reads, tried in order.

methods.name: of
methods.doc: The table a statement names (backticks dropped), or null when it names none the reference recognises.

methods.name: host
methods.doc:
A DB_HOST read as host, port, socket and whether the host is IPv6: a
socket after ":/", an IPv6 address in brackets (more than one colon),
a port only when it is digits. Null when nothing parses.

classes.name: Minn\Support\Text
classes.doc:
Plain text shaped the way WordPress's formatting helpers shape it: cut to
a number of words or characters, named references written as numeric
ones, stray ampersands encoded, whitespace normalized, a path's last part,
and a callback run over every value of a nested structure.

methods.name: trimWords
methods.doc: The text's first words, tags gone, with $more after them when some were cut (wp_trim_words), as the filter leaves it.

methods.name: htmlExcerpt
methods.doc: The text's first characters, tags and line breaks gone, with $more after them when some were cut (wp_html_excerpt).

methods.name: numericReferences
methods.doc: Named character references written as numeric ones (ent2ncr), unless pre_ent2ncr answers first.

methods.name: encodeAmpersands
methods.doc: Ampersands that begin no reference written as & (convert_chars).

methods.name: normalizeWhitespace
methods.doc: Line breaks as single newlines and runs of spaces and tabs as one space, ends trimmed (normalize_whitespace).

methods.name: basename
methods.doc: A path's last part, multibyte names intact, without the suffix given (wp_basename).

methods.name: mapDeep
methods.doc: A value with the callback run over every scalar inside it, arrays and objects followed (map_deep).

classes.name: Minn\Support\Time
classes.doc: Human-scale spans: a number of seconds as the largest whole unit it fills, rounded, never below one.

methods.name: span
methods.doc: A number of seconds as its largest whole unit and count.
shapes: @return array{0: int, 1: string} count and unit name

classes.name: Minn\Support\TimezoneChoice
classes.doc:
The timezone choices a settings form offers (wp_timezone_choice, probe
placeholder-helpers): the zones of each continent, cities in natural
order (a zone with three parts reads "City - Sub-city"), then UTC, then
the offsets set by hand. "Select a city" leads when nothing is chosen, and
a real zone outside the list (an old name, Etc/) leads when it is the one
chosen. Each choice is a line of its own.

methods.name: html
methods.doc: The choices as option lines, the chosen zone marked.
shapes: @param \Closure(string, string): string $translate a text in a text domain, translated

params.name: translate
params.doc: a text in a text domain, translated

methods.name: zones
methods.doc:
The continents' zones in order: continent, city, then sub-city, each
compared naturally and without case.
shapes: @return list<array{value: string, continent: string, city: string, sub: string, label: string}>

methods.name: groups
shapes: @param list<array{value: string, continent: string, city: string, sub: string, label: string}> $zones
@return array<string, list<array{value: string, continent: string, city: string, sub: string, label: string}>>

params.name: zones
params.shape: list<array{value: string, continent: string, city: string, sub: string, label: string}>

methods.name: outsideList
methods.doc: Whether a chosen zone is a real one the list leaves out (not UTC, not an offset). @param list<string> $listed

methods.name: offset
methods.doc: An offset's value (UTC+5.75) and label (UTC+5:45). @return array{0: string, 1: string}

methods.name: offsets
methods.doc:
The offsets offered by hand, in hours, lowest first: every half hour from -12 to +12, the
three-quarter hours some zones keep, and the hours past +12 up to +14.

methods.name: option
methods.doc: One choice, marked when it is the chosen zone.

classes.name: Minn\Support\Url
classes.doc:
URL shaping the escaping and query helpers share: the character cleanup
esc_url applies, bracket encoding outside the authority, and query
argument merging. Behaviour pinned by contracts/fixtures/api/functions.json.

methods.name: withTrailingSlash
methods.doc: The value with one trailing slash, whatever slashes or backslashes it ended in (trailingslashit).

methods.name: withoutTrailingSlash
methods.doc: The value with every trailing slash and backslash taken off (untrailingslashit).

methods.name: clean
methods.doc: Spaces encoded, stray characters dropped, ";//" healed, a bare host given http; '' when nothing survives.

methods.name: encodeBrackets
methods.doc: Square brackets after the authority are percent-encoded; the authority itself is left alone. @param array<string, mixed> $parsed

methods.name: withQuery
methods.doc:
The URI with query arguments merged in (false removes one), the
fragment kept, a bare query string treated as such; a URI that is
only a query (or nothing) keeps its leading question mark.
shapes: @param Closure(array): array $encode encodes the existing arguments the way the reference does
@param Closure(array): string $build builds the query string

params.name: encode
params.doc: encodes the existing arguments the way the reference does

methods.name: validateForHttp
methods.doc:
The checks wp_http_validate_url makes on a URL whose protocol already
passed: an http(s) scheme, a host without credentials or a colon, no
private address unless it is this site or allowed, only the safe
ports (80, 443 and 8080 unless the caller's list says otherwise; the
site's own always). Returns the URL, or null when refused.
shapes: @param Closure(string, string): bool $externalAllowed whether a private host may be fetched anyway
@param (Closure(list<int>, string, string): array)|null $safePorts the port list for a URL that names a port

params.name: externalAllowed
params.doc: whether a private host may be fetched anyway

params.name: safePorts
params.doc: the port list for a URL that names a port

methods.name: buildQuery
methods.doc: A query string in the reference's spelling (probe query-args): keys and values as given, nested keys as `a%5Bb%5D`, null left out, booleans as 0/1.

methods.name: parse
methods.doc: parse_url that also accepts scheme-relative and path-only URLs; a single component by its PHP_URL_* constant.

methods.name: withScheme
methods.doc: The URL under a scheme, or scheme-and-host stripped for 'relative'; a protocol-relative URL is read as http first.

methods.name: safeRedirect
methods.doc:
A redirect target the site may send a browser to: http(s) only and a
host the caller allows. A relative one stays on the site: a path
without a leading slash is put after the request path's folder (up to
its last "/", the dots kept), anything else as given. Credentials
before the host are kept unless they hold an "@" (probe
functions-formatting-doubts).
shapes: @param Closure(string): list<string> $allowedHosts the hosts allowed for the target's host

params.name: allowedHosts
params.doc: the hosts allowed for the target's host

methods.name: absolute
methods.doc:
A reference made absolute against a base URL, as WP_Http resolves a
redirect's Location: one with a scheme stays as it is, "//host" takes
the base's scheme, a path without a leading slash joins the base's
folder with its "../" steps folded, and no path keeps the base's.

methods.name: isPrivate
methods.doc:
Whether an IPv4 address is one a request must not reach: anything
outside the global range (private, loopback, link-local, shared
CGNAT space with the clouds' metadata hosts, benchmarking,
documentation, reserved), the old 6to4 relays and multicast, as the
reference refuses them.

classes.name: Minn\Support\Utf8
classes.doc:
UTF-8 as the reference reads it. Well-formed means no overlong forms,
surrogates, code points past U+10FFFF, stray continuation bytes or
truncated sequences; noncharacters, NUL and a byte order mark pass. Split
into characters (the multibyte fallbacks in compat.php), a malformed byte
is one character and so is the longest start of a sequence that breaks
off, so "\xE2\x82" counts once.

constants.name: CHARACTER
constants.doc: One well-formed character.

constants.name: BROKEN
constants.doc: The start of a sequence that breaks off.

constants.name: CHARSETS
constants.doc: The database charsets a query's text is held to, by the multibyte name of each.

methods.name: isValid
methods.doc: True for well-formed UTF-8, including the empty string.

methods.name: characters
methods.doc:
The bytes cut into characters, a malformed byte or a broken-off
sequence counting as one.

methods.name: scan
methods.doc:
Reads well-formed characters from $at, as the reference's scanner does
(probe utf8). It stops $maxBytes past $at (a character begun before
that is read whole), after $maxCodePoints, or at a malformed byte. The
answer: the characters read, where it stopped, the length of the
malformed run there (a broken-off start of a sequence, else one byte,
cut at the byte limit; 0 when there is none), and whether a character
that could be a noncharacter was one (null when none could be: only
EF and four-byte sequences hold them).

methods.name: isNoncharacter
methods.doc: Whether a code point is a noncharacter: U+FDD0 to U+FDEF, or the last two of any plane.

methods.name: hasNoncharacters
