methods.doc: Whether any well-formed character is a noncharacter, malformed bytes stepped over.

methods.name: scrub
methods.doc: The bytes with each malformed run (as characters() cuts them) replaced by U+FFFD.

methods.name: span
methods.doc:
How many bytes from $offset the first $maxCodePoints characters take,
and how many there were.

methods.name: toLatin1
methods.doc: UTF-8 as ISO-8859-1: a character past U+00FF, or a malformed run, becomes "?".

methods.name: keptBy
methods.doc: What a column in this charset keeps: utf8mb4 drops each malformed run, utf8 (utf8mb3) every four-byte character too; any other charset keeps the bytes.

methods.name: fits
methods.doc:
Whether text can go to a table in this charset as the reference's
database door judges it (probe invalid-text): anything for a binary or
latin1 table or one without text; otherwise well-formed UTF-8, and of
that only what the charset holds (no four-byte character for utf8, no
byte past ASCII for ascii).

methods.name: fromLatin1
methods.doc: ISO-8859-1 as UTF-8: each byte the character of its value.

methods.name: fromCodePoint
methods.doc: The UTF-8 bytes for a code point, or null for a negative one, a surrogate, or one past U+10FFFF.

methods.name: firstCodePoint
methods.doc: The code point of the first character, or null when the bytes do not start with a whole, well-formed one.

classes.name: Minn\Support\Whole
classes.doc:
Whole numbers read from outside: the reference's absint() turns the
smallest integer into a float (it has no whole-number opposite), which
a typed int, a LIMIT or a page number cannot hold. Here it reads as 0,
as asking for nothing (security sweep 2026-11-12, finding 3.7).

methods.name: abs
methods.doc: A value as a non-negative int: its integer reading without its sign, 0 for the smallest integer.

classes.name: Minn\Theme\ArchiveTitle
classes.doc:
The label and name an archive titles itself with: `Category:` around the
term, `Author:` around the display name, the date formatted for its
granularity. One source of truth for the block path's query-title and
the classic path's get_the_archive_title(), which used to compute the
same labels separately. Search and post-type archives stay with their
callers: their captured shapes differ between the two paths.

methods.name: parts
methods.doc: The archive title's prefix and title for a resolution.
shapes: @return array{string, string} the prefix (its colon included, in the site's language) and the escaped bare name; both empty when the view has none

params.name: dateFormat
params.doc: the site's date_format option, for day archives

methods.name: compose
methods.doc: The reference's prefixed shape, `Category: Uncategorized`, through the language's own order.

methods.name: taxonomyLabel
methods.doc: The singular label a plugin registered for its taxonomy, for the archive title prefix.

classes.name: Minn\Theme\BodyClasses
classes.doc:
The body-class list a classic theme's body_class() starts from, in the
reference's order: the query tokens (with the singular and template
tokens spliced in front of the type token), logged-in, the embed and
theme tokens, with the numbered paging tokens re-seated after the embed
token. The body_class filter runs over this list in the facade.

methods.name: classic
methods.doc: The body classes a classic theme's page carries.

methods.name: forView
methods.doc:
The same list for a view named by the post type it shows alone (null
when it shows no single post), as get_body_class needs off the front
(probe post-template-remaining).

classes.name: Minn\Theme\BodyFacts
classes.doc:
The facts about a page that decide the body classes a classic theme's
page carries beyond the view tokens: a signed-in reader, a custom
logo, responsive embeds, and the Minn bar.

constructor.signature: __construct(bool $loggedIn = false, bool $customLogo = false, bool $embedResponsive = true, bool $bar = false)

classes.name: Minn\Theme\ClassicContent
classes.doc:
What a classic theme's the_content() prints: the content as written (the
more-tag teaser in listings, the password gate's form in its place) through
the_content, the engine's block renderer in do_blocks's place for block
content and core's own defaults for classic content, so plugin code is
handed what the reference hands it, in the same hook order.

methods.name: render
methods.doc: A post's content as the classic loop prints it, with the more link.

classes.name: Minn\Theme\ClassicRenderer
classes.doc:
A whole page from the active classic theme: the reference's PHP template
loader. The main query stands, template_redirect fires, the hierarchy
picks a PHP file, template_include filters it, and load_template() runs
it as the response body. The theme prints its own document; the engine
contributes the reference's wp_head defaults (title tag, robots, feed
links, REST and oEmbed discovery, canonical, site icon) as hooks the
theme's wp_head() call fires.

methods.name: create
methods.signature: create(Minn\Db $db, Minn\Theme\ClassicTheme $theme, ?Minn\Theme\Theme $styleTheme, Minn\Front\Permalinks $permalinks, int $perPage, ?Minn\Front\AdminBar $bar = NULL): self
methods.doc: A classic renderer over the database door.

methods.name: render
methods.doc: The page for a resolution through the theme's PHP templates.

methods.name: themeClasses
methods.doc: The body-class tokens before plugins filter them (get_body_class filters them). @return list<string>

methods.name: template
methods.doc: The reference's loader order: the first true conditional whose template exists wins, index.php last.

methods.name: registerHead
methods.doc: The piece only the renderer holds: the engine stylesheets. The head defaults registered at setup_theme.

methods.name: registerStyles
methods.doc: The engine's block stylesheet, and the theme.json presets when the theme ships one, where the reference prints its block-library and global styles.

classes.name: Minn\Theme\ClassicTheme
classes.doc:
The active classic (PHP-template) theme on disk. A theme is classic when
it ships no block template index; its templates are PHP files the engine
dispatches through the reference's hierarchy and runs via load_template().
The theme's own functions.php loads through the runtime's symbol gate.

methods.name: ofBlockTheme
methods.doc: A block theme as a PHP template's theme: a hybrid's own PHP template renders through it (Templates::forResolution).

methods.name: active
methods.doc: The active classic theme, or null under a block theme.

classes.name: Minn\Theme\CustomCss
classes.doc:
Custom CSS as theme.json and blocks write it (a styles node's "css", a
block's style.css): nested rules under "&" unfolded beneath the selector
they belong to, each wrapped in :root :where() as the reference prints
them. Pure: CSS and selectors in, rules out.

methods.name: scoped
methods.doc:
A block's own CSS under its selector (probe editor-styles; a block's
style.css too, probe block-supports), split at each ampersand: a part
with no rule applies to the block itself; a nested selector that starts
with a space is scoped, every comma part after the block's selector;
any other is appended to it; a pseudo element moves to the end, outside
:where().

methods.name: ofStyles
methods.doc:
The styles' own CSS (WP_Theme_JSON::get_custom_css): the top-level
css, then each block's under its root selector.

methods.name: scope
methods.doc: Every comma part of a selector list after every part of the scope.

methods.name: append
methods.doc: Text appended to every comma part of a selector list.

classes.name: Minn\Theme\EmbedRenderer
classes.doc:
A post's embed page (its /embed/ address, or ?embed= on it), the card
another site's iframe shows, as the reference prints it: the main query
stood with the embed asked for, then the embed template (the theme's
own embed-{type}.php or embed.php, else the engine's theme-compat one)
through template_include, with embed_head, embed_content,
embed_content_meta and embed_footer. An address that embeds nothing
gets the 404 card.

methods.name: asked
methods.doc: Whether a request for this resolution asks for its embed page.

methods.name: render

classes.name: Minn\Theme\FeatureSelectors
classes.doc:
A block's styles split between the selectors its metadata gives its
features (probe theme-json-css), in the metadata's order: a property with
a selector of its own first, then what is left of its feature under the
feature's selector. What is taken leaves the node.

methods.name: split
methods.doc: The styles each feature selector takes, and the node left over.
shapes: @param array<string, mixed> $selectors the block's metadata selectors
@return array{0: list<array{0: string, 1: array<string, mixed>}>, 1: array<string, mixed>} the styles each selector takes, in order, and what stays

classes.name: Minn\Theme\FeedHeaders
classes.doc:
The headers a feed is sent with, as the reference's send_headers sends
them (suite feed-hooks): the feed type's content type, and when the site
last changed (its posts, and its comments too for a comments feed) as
Last-Modified with an ETag over it; a reader whose copy carries that
date or tag is told the copy is current.

methods.name: for
methods.doc: The headers, and whether the reader's copy is current.
shapes: @param array<string, mixed> $vars the request's query variables

methods.name: carriesComments
shapes: @param array<string, mixed> $vars whether the feed's last change counts the comments: a comments feed, or a single post's

params.name: vars
params.doc: whether the feed's last change counts the comments: a comments feed, or a single post's

classes.name: Minn\Theme\Folder
classes.doc: A theme folder read from disk: its style.css headers, which folder its templates come from, its screenshot, whether it is a block theme.

shapes: @param array<string, string> $headers keyed by the caller's labels

methods.name: read
methods.doc: A theme folder with its style.css headers.
shapes: @param array<string, string> $labels key => the style.css header label
@param Closure(string, array<string, string>): array<string, string>|null $reader the header reader (the facade's, so header filters apply); the engine's own by default

params.name: reader
params.doc: the header reader (the facade's, so header filters apply); the engine's own by default

methods.name: problem
methods.doc:
What keeps the folder from being a whole theme, as the reference names
it (probe theme-headers): no folder; no stylesheet; itself named as
its parent; a parent that is not there; or, standing alone, no
index.php and no templates/index.html. Null for a whole theme.
shapes: @return array{0: string, 1: string}|null the error code and message

methods.name: dir
methods.doc: The folder's path.

methods.name: screenshot
methods.doc: The screenshot file name, or null when the theme has none.

methods.name: isBlockTheme
methods.doc: Whether any of the folders ships a block template index.
shapes: @param list<string> $dirs the stylesheet and template directories

methods.name: filePath
methods.doc: The first of the stylesheet and template directories that holds the file, or the template directory's path.

classes.name: Minn\Theme\FontCollectionSource
classes.doc:
A font collection read from an address, kept as the reference keeps it
(probed 2026-10-24 on its Google Fonts collection): the collection's
families, sanitized as the collection keeps them, in a site transient
named after the address for a day, read from there until it lapses. A
fetch that fails, answers anything but 200, or holds no font_families is
kept nowhere, so the next ask tries again.

constants.name: TTL
constants.doc: Seconds a fetched collection is kept.

methods.name: remember
methods.doc:
The collection at $url as ['font_families' => ...], or null when it
could not be read. $fetch makes the request (the WordPress layer's
HTTP API, so its filters hear it) and hands back its response;
$sanitize gives the families as the collection keeps them.

classes.name: Minn\Theme\FontFaces
classes.doc:
fonts a theme.json declares in the shape they are printed from.

A face needs a family and at least one source it can name a format for.
Its rule lists family (quoted unless it is one word or already carries
quotes), style (normal), weight (400), display (fallback unless it is
one the reference knows), the sources, then any other face property in
the order given. Sources go data URIs first, then woff2, woff,
truetype, embedded-opentype and opentype; anything else is dropped.

methods.name: css
methods.doc:
The rules for fonts given as families of faces, one rule a line; ''
when no face can be printed.

methods.name: fromSettings
methods.doc:
The fonts a theme.json's settings declare, one list of faces per
family that has any: each face's sources first (file:./ ones through
$fileUri), then its family (the first name of its own, or of the
family's, unquoted), then its other properties in kebab case.
shapes: @param Closure(string): string $fileUri a theme-relative path to its URL

params.name: fileUri
params.doc: a theme-relative path to its URL

methods.name: rule
methods.doc: One face's rule, or '' when it has no family or no source it can print.

methods.name: sources
methods.doc: The sources in the order the reference prints them: data URIs, then one each by format.

methods.name: family
methods.doc: A family name as printed: as given when it carries quotes or is one word, quoted otherwise.

methods.name: variations
methods.doc: font-variation-settings given as axis => value, run together as the reference prints them. @param array<string, mixed> $settings

methods.name: firstName
methods.doc: The first name in a comma-separated family list, without its quotes.

classes.name: Minn\Theme\FontNames
classes.doc:
The font library's names (probes fonts and font-writes): a font-family
list as a family stores it, the identity a face is stored under (its
title, which the duplicate check compares), and the font types an
upload may carry.

constants.name: MIME_TYPES
constants.doc: The font types an upload may carry, by extension.

constants.name: STRETCH
constants.doc:
Stretch keywords as percentages, replaced one after another in this
order, as the reference replaces them: a keyword that holds one
replaced before it keeps the rest ("semi-condensed" is "semi-75%",
"ultra-expanded" is "ultra-125%").

methods.name: family
methods.doc:
A font-family list as text, each name trimmed of spaces and quotes,
then joined by ", ": a name quoted as given stays double-quoted (a
generic family too, `"serif"`), a name of letters and hyphens alone is
as it is, any other (a space, a digit, an underscore) double-quoted.

methods.name: quoted
methods.doc: One name of a font-family list, double-quoted unless it is letters and hyphens alone.

methods.name: faceSlug
methods.doc:
A face's identity: its family list (trimmed, lower case, split at
each comma and the spaces after it, each name's quotes trimmed),
style (lower case), weight (lower case, normal and bold as numbers),
stretch (lower case, keywords as percentages) and unicode range
(upper case), joined by ";". A property left out takes its default
(normal, 400, 100%, U+0-10FFFF); one given empty stays empty.

classes.name: Minn\Theme\FontSchema
classes.doc:
The font library's tree sanitizer (WP_Font_Utils::sanitize_from_schema),
as the reference answers it (probed 2026-10-24): only the keys the schema
names are kept; a key whose rule is a callable gets the callable's answer
for whatever its value is, a list included (a text sanitizer makes a list
empty); a rule that is an array reads an object as a schema of its own,
and a list as a list of that rule's first entry; anything an object level
comes out with that is empty ('', '0', 0, false, null, []) is left out,
while a list keeps every item. A rule that is not callable leaves the value
as it is (the reference stops on a TypeError there).

methods.name: sanitize
methods.doc: The tree with only the keys the schema names, each through its rule.

classes.name: Minn\Theme\FrontLifecycle
classes.doc:
WordPress's front-end request steps around the main query, as WP::main
runs them (front lifecycle trace): parse the request (do_parse_request
may take it over; query_vars names the public variables, a plugin's own
read from the query string; request filters the result; parse_request
follows), the main query, the 404 decision (pre_handle_404 first), the
globals, and the headers (wp_headers, the status, send_headers). The
engine has already resolved the URL; these steps tell plugins about it
in the reference's order and let them change what the query asks.

methods.name: parseRequest
methods.signature: parseRequest(Minn\Objects\Environment $wp, array $vars, array $given, ?Closure $parse = NULL, mixed $extraVars = NULL): bool
methods.doc:
Parses the request: false when a plugin's do_parse_request took the
parse over (the main query then does not run). The query string is
the main query's to build, after.
shapes: @param array<string, mixed> $vars the variables the engine resolved
@param array<string, mixed> $given the query string and form, where a plugin's own variables are read
@param (\Closure(list<string>): array<string, mixed>)|null $parse the reference's parse vars for the public vars, when the request is known

params.name: given
params.doc: the query string and form, where a plugin's own variables are read

params.name: parse
params.doc: the reference's parse vars for the public vars, when the request is known

params.name: extraVars
params.doc: the extra vars parse_request was given, as given, which do_parse_request hears (the object's own when null)

methods.name: handle404
methods.doc:
The 404 decision, the one place it is made: a plugin's
pre_handle_404 may make it; otherwise a request for something the
site does not have is a 404, as is an empty page past the first of
any listing and an empty date archive that names nothing else (an
existing term, author or type with no posts, a date inside one of
those or inside a search, an empty search, the front: a 200); the
status and no-cache headers follow. A feed is a 404 only as an empty
page past its first (/feed/?paged=99, then printed as the posts' feed
of nothing); one of nothing else is an empty feed.

methods.name: sendHeaders
methods.doc:
The headers the reference sends for the request: no caching for a
signed-in reader or a 404, the content type, a pingback address for a
single post that takes pings; then wp_headers, the status an error
variable names, and send_headers.

classes.name: Minn\Theme\GlobalStyles
classes.doc:
theme.json to CSS. Presets become custom properties on :root and their
has-* utility classes; settings.layout sizes, root styles, elements, and
per-block styles become rules; the containers, galleries, and style
variations the page actually rendered get their own stylesheets. The
layout rules themselves (flow, constrained, flex, grid, alignments) are
the engine's own, written to the same class hooks.

params.name: user
params.doc: the site editor's saved global styles, layered over the theme

constants.name: ELEMENT_SELECTORS
constants.value: array (   'link' => 'a:where(:not(.wp-element-button))',   'heading' => 'h1, h2, h3, h4, h5, h6',   'h1' => 'h1',   'h2' => 'h2',   'h3' => 'h3',   'h4' => 'h4',   'h5' => 'h5',   'h6' => 'h6',   'button' => '.wp-element-button, .wp-block-button__link',   'caption' => '.wp-element-caption, .wp-block-audio figcaption, .wp-block-embed figcaption, .wp-block-gallery figcaption, .wp-block-image figcaption, .wp-block-table figcaption, .wp-block-video figcaption',   'cite' => 'cite', )
constants.doc:
Element selectors in the order the reference prints them, whatever
order theme.json or the saved styles list them in: the heading group
lands before the individual levels, so an h1 line-height beats the
group's. Themes list h1..h6 before heading and would otherwise win.

constants.name: BLOCK_SELECTORS
constants.doc: Blocks whose metadata names a root selector other than .wp-block-{slug}.

constants.name: STYLESHEET_LESS
constants.doc:
The reference prints a core block's theme.json styles only when the
page rendered the block with output (a generated excerpt counts), and
attaches them to the block's own stylesheet; these core blocks have
none, so their styles never reach a page. A block from outside core
has no such stylesheet to wait for, so its styles always print.

methods.name: styles
methods.doc: The theme.json (plus site-editor) styles node, under the engine's own defaults.

methods.name: resolvedStyles
methods.doc:
The same node with every `var:preset|…` token resolved to the custom
property it names, which is the shape a caller reading the styles as
data expects (the CSS writer resolves them on the way out instead).

methods.name: css
methods.doc: The global stylesheet from theme.json and the user's styles, as a page prints it: only the core blocks it rendered.

methods.name: stylesheet
methods.doc:
The stylesheet wp_get_global_stylesheet answers (probe editor-styles),
by type: the custom properties, the styles (every block's, rendered or
not), the preset classes; in that order.

methods.name: gapSupported
methods.doc:
Whether the theme turns block gaps on: settings.spacing.blockGap true,
as appearanceTools sets it when the theme leaves it unset. Without it
the reference prints no gap rules at all (the site's blocks, flow
layouts, each block's own) and flex and grid fall back to a 0.5em gap
(probe block-gap-support, contracts/front/theme.md).

methods.name: fontFaces
methods.doc:
The @font-face rules for every family that declares font files
(Theme\FontFaces), with file:./ resolved against the theme that
carries the file. The page prints them through wp_print_font_faces on
wp_head; the editor's styles read them here.

methods.name: rootRules
methods.doc: The body's margin, the global padding rules under root-padding-aware alignments, and the site's alignments.

methods.name: blockGapRules
methods.doc: The block gap between the site's blocks and inside every layout.

methods.name: layoutRules
methods.doc: The layouts' own rules: alignments inside flow and constrained layouts, the content and wide sizes, flex and grid.

methods.name: gapRules
methods.doc: The block-gap rules for a layout scope: "" for the root, or a block's -is-layout- prefix.

methods.name: elementStyles
methods.doc: The element rules (links, headings, buttons, captions, citations), each state after it; under a block's selector when one is given.

methods.name: blockStyles
methods.doc:
A block's rules: its root rule, its layout gap rules, then a rule for
each feature its metadata gives a selector of its own (the avatar's
border on its image), its own CSS and its elements (probe
editor-styles).

methods.name: scoped
methods.doc: Each selector in a list under the scope ("" for none).

methods.name: rootSelector
methods.doc: A block's root selector: its metadata's, the reference's own for a few core blocks, else .wp-block-{slug}.

methods.name: selectorsOf
methods.doc: A core block's selectors from its metadata. @return array<string, mixed>

methods.name: byFeature
methods.doc:
A block's styles split between its root selector and the features (or
a feature's single properties) its metadata selects elsewhere.
shapes: @return array{0: array<string, mixed>, 1: array<string, array<string, mixed>>}

methods.name: variationCss
methods.doc:
A numbered style variation's CSS (probe block-supports): its element
rules scoped by the numbered class alone, then the variation on the
block's root selector (the class riding on the block's own class:
.wp-block-button.is-style-outline--3 .wp-block-button__link), its own
CSS, and the blocks styled inside it.

methods.name: declarations
methods.doc:
theme.json style properties to declarations: color, typography, spacing,
border, shadow, dimensions, outline.

methods.name: json
methods.doc:
The theme's theme.json with the site editor's styles over it, those
as wp_theme_json_data_user leaves them (a plugin may add a layer
where the site editor saved none).

methods.name: withoutGaps
methods.doc: Block style nodes without their own block gaps, for a theme without gap support.

methods.name: parts
shapes: @return array{variables: string, base: string, presets: string, blocks: array<string, mixed>, gap: bool}

methods.name: rootStyles
methods.doc:
Root styles land on body. With root-padding-aware alignments the root
padding is NOT applied to body; it becomes the custom properties the
has-global-padding rules read.

methods.name: blockCustomProperties
methods.doc: Each block's own settings.custom as custom properties on the block's root selector. @param array<string, mixed> $blocks

methods.name: containerStyles
methods.doc: The page's block-support rules (layouts, element styles, and the rest), which the facade keeps in the style engine's block-supports store.

methods.name: ordered
methods.doc:
The reference prints declarations in its own fixed property order:
alphabetical, except that the sides of a margin or padding run
top, right, bottom, left.

classes.name: Minn\Theme\HeadLinks
classes.doc:
The engine's own pieces of a page's head: its block stylesheet link,
and for rest_output_link_wp_head the REST discovery link and the JSON
alternate for the queried object; the site's feed links as feed_links
prints them. Every theme's head prints them from the reference's
wp_head hooks.

methods.name: engineStylesheet
methods.doc: The link to the engine's own block stylesheet.

methods.name: siteFeeds
methods.doc:
The site's two feed links as feed_links prints them: the posts feed
and the comments feed (each unless its feed_links_show_* filter says
no), titled with the caller's separator and words, through
feed_links_args.

methods.name: restLink
methods.doc: No trailing newline: the reference prints the JSON alternate and the RSD link on the same physical line.

methods.name: jsonAlternate
methods.doc: The JSON alternate link for the queried resource's REST route (rest_get_queried_resource_route); none for no route.

classes.name: Minn\Theme\Hierarchy
classes.doc:
The classic template hierarchy: the candidate file names each template
type tries, most specific first, as the reference resolves them. The
facade's get_{type}_template() functions feed these to get_query_template(),
which locates the first candidate the theme (child, then parent) ships.

methods.name: frontPage
methods.doc: The front page templates.

methods.name: home
methods.doc: The home templates.

methods.name: privacyPolicy
methods.doc: The privacy policy templates.

methods.name: page
methods.doc: The page templates, custom first.

methods.name: single
methods.doc: The single templates, custom first.

methods.name: attachment
methods.doc:
The attachment templates by mime type: type-subtype, subtype, type
(probe template-getters).

methods.name: term
methods.doc: The term archive templates.

methods.name: author
methods.doc: The author archive templates.

methods.name: archive
methods.doc: The post type archive templates.

classes.name: Minn\Theme\MainQueryBridge
classes.doc:
Stands the main query for a themed page and runs the front-end steps
around it as WP::main does (FrontLifecycle): the request parsed, the main
query through WP_Query (so pre_get_posts and every posts_* filter shape
it), the 404 decision, the globals, the headers, then "wp" and
template_redirect. A listing's posts are the query's, and so is the 404
for an empty page past the first or an empty date; a single post the
query does not find (a preview, a draft its author reads) is the one the
engine resolved. When a plugin takes the parse over no query runs, as
on the reference, and the page stands empty.

methods.name: stand
methods.doc:
The page of posts a resolution shows, through the runtime's main
query, then template_redirect, as a page the theme draws stands; the
variables a request adds of its own (a feed's) win.

methods.name: run
methods.doc:
The main query alone, as the reference's wp() runs it for a script
that draws no template (signup, trackback): the request parsed, the
query run, the headers sent, then the wp action.

methods.name: verdict
methods.doc:
The resolution as the main query left it: a 404 when the query
decided one (an empty page past the first, an empty date), with the
vars it was asked under.

methods.name: perPage
methods.doc: Posts per page.

methods.name: vars
methods.doc:
The variables the request stands on before the parse runs (and in
its place, when a plugin takes the parse over): the matched rule's,
the posts page by its id.

methods.name: postVars
methods.doc:
The variables that name the post the engine resolved, for a page the
query found nothing to stand on (a preview, a draft its author reads).

methods.name: queried
methods.doc:
The main query for these variables: a listing is its posts; any other
page stands on the post the engine resolved when the query has none.

methods.name: seeded
methods.doc: The query globals seeded with no posts of their own (a single the query did not find is looked up by its vars), when no query ran or it found nothing to stand on. @param array<string, mixed> $vars

classes.name: Minn\Theme\NotModified
classes.doc:
Raised once a reader's copy of a feed has been found current and the
headers that say so are sent: the reference stops the request there, so
the engine answers with nothing more.

classes.name: Minn\Theme\PageRenderer
classes.doc:
A whole page from the active block theme: the template the resolution
maps to, rendered against the main query, inside the document shell the
reference emits (skip link, wp-site-blocks, the skip-link target on the
first main element).

constructor.signature: __construct(Minn\Content\Site $site, Minn\Theme\Theme $theme, Minn\Theme\Templates $templates, Minn\Blocks\Renderer $renderer, Minn\Theme\MainQueryBridge $bridge, Minn\Theme\HeadLinks $headLinks, ?Minn\Front\AdminBar $bar = NULL)

methods.name: create
methods.signature: create(Minn\Db $db, Minn\Theme\Theme $theme, Minn\Front\Permalinks $permalinks, int $perPage, ?Minn\Front\AdminBar $bar = NULL): self
methods.doc: A page renderer over the database door.

methods.name: bodyClasses
methods.doc:
The reference's body-class tokens: the singular and template tokens
sit in front of the type token ("page", "single"), the custom-logo
and embed tokens follow the core set, the paging tokens come after
those, and the theme (and child theme) tokens close the list; then
the body_class filter.

methods.name: themeClasses
methods.doc: The body-class tokens before plugins filter them (bodyClasses()). @return list<string>

methods.name: foundTemplate
methods.doc:
The fields of the template that renders a resolution, as the site
editor asks for them (?_wp-find-template); null without one.

methods.name: render
methods.doc: The page for a resolution, or null when the theme has no block template for it (none, or its PHP template wins: the classic renderer's then).

methods.name: document
methods.doc:
The block template's document: the blocks rendered, the head, the body
classes, the footer.

methods.name: skipLinkTarget
methods.doc:
The skip link points at the first <main>: at its own id when the
template gave it one, otherwise at the id the reference injects.
shapes: @return array{string, string} the body, the target id

methods.name: head
methods.doc:
The head: the charset, then wp_head (the viewport, robots, title and
discovery links from the reference's defaults, which a plugin may
remove; the engine's stylesheets inside it, where the reference
prints a theme's, after plugin styles), then the extension head (after
the stylesheets, as the seam contract says), the bar's own.

classes.name: Minn\Theme\PatternHeaders
classes.doc:
A theme's pattern files read by their headers, as WP_Theme::get_block_patterns
lists them (probe wp-theme). Each one gives title, slug and description
(empty when the header has none), then whatever of viewportWidth (a
number), inserter (false for "no"), and the lists categories,
keywords, blockTypes, postTypes and templateTypes it declares, split on
commas and whitespace. A file
without a title and a slug is not a pattern.

methods.name: of
methods.doc:
The records of a list of pattern files, file name => path (a list a
plugin may have changed); a file that is not a pattern is left out.

methods.name: read
methods.doc: One file's record from the start of its text, or null when it names no title or slug.

classes.name: Minn\Theme\PatternText
classes.doc:
Block-theme patterns are PHP files whose only code is a handful of
echo-and-escape calls around literal strings. The engine never executes
them: it interprets that small text grammar (string literals, "."
concatenation, the i18n and escaping wrappers, the theme URI helper, and
printf with %s) and leaves anything else out. A translated string is
looked up in its domain (the theme's own), with its context where it
gives one, as the reference's patterns ask for theirs. The header comment block
is dropped, and every byte outside the PHP tags is kept as-is.

constants.name: PASSTHROUGH
constants.doc: Wrappers whose value is their first argument, unchanged.

constants.name: URLS
constants.doc: Wrappers whose value is their first argument as a URL: empty when what stands before a colon is no allowed scheme.

constants.name: ESCAPING
constants.doc: Wrappers whose value is their first argument with HTML special characters encoded.

constants.name: TRANSLATING
constants.doc:
The translating wrappers, by how they read: "text" (text, domain) or
"context" (text, context, domain), escaped or not; those that echo are
statements, the rest values.

methods.name: render
methods.doc: A pattern file's HTML with its PHP interpreted, never executed.

methods.name: expression
methods.doc: A concatenation of terms.

methods.name: translated
methods.doc:
A message in the site's language, read as its wrapper reads it
(TRANSLATING): (text, domain) or (text, context, domain), escaped for
the escaping wrappers.

methods.name: escape
methods.doc: Special characters encoded once; entities already present are kept.

methods.name: skipSpace
methods.doc: Whitespace and comments, anywhere a token may follow.

classes.name: Minn\Theme\Printed
classes.doc:
Raised once a WordPress handler has printed a whole response (a sitemap,
a stylesheet) or sent a redirect, where the reference exits: the request
ends there and the engine answers with what was printed.

classes.name: Minn\Theme\QueryClasses
classes.doc:
The body-class tokens the main query stands for, in the reference's
order (captured from the oracles): the view tokens (home, blog,
privacy-policy, archive, date, search with its results token, paged,
attachment, error404), then the singular's or the archive's own, then
the numbered paging tokens. Flags combine as the query's do: a search
inside a category carries both sets. The bare paged token follows the
listing's page; the numbered ones follow a single's page too, and take
the view's prefix in one precedence (single, page, category, tag, date,
author, search, post type; the front and a plain taxonomy have none).
A 404 carries no paging tokens. The theme renderers seat the numbered
tokens after the embed token and add the template and theme tokens.

methods.name: of
methods.doc: The tokens for a main query.

methods.name: format
methods.doc: A post's format by its post_format term, standard without one (probe post-template-remaining).

methods.name: paging
methods.doc: The numbered paging tokens: paged-N and the view's own.

methods.name: named
methods.doc: A name as a class token, its id when nothing of it survives.

classes.name: Minn\Theme\SpacingScale
classes.doc:
The spacing sizes a theme.json spacing scale makes (probe
theme-json-css): Medium (slug 50) at the medium step; below it, half the
other steps rounded down, each divided by (or less) the increment, named
Small, X-Small, 2X-Small; above it the rest, multiplied by (or plus) it,
named Large, X-Large, 2X-Large; slugs ten apart, values rounded to two
places. An invalid scale makes none.

methods.name: sizes
methods.doc: The sizes the scale makes, smallest first.
shapes: @param array<string, mixed> $scale operator, increment, steps, mediumStep, unit
@return list<array{name: string, slug: string, size: string}>

methods.name: name
methods.doc: Small, X-Small, 2X-Small, and so on (Large likewise).

classes.name: Minn\Theme\StyleLayers
classes.doc:
What plugins change about the global stylesheet's layers and nodes, for
GlobalStyles: core's preset lists when wp_theme_json_data_default
changed core's layer, and the style nodes wp_theme_json_get_style_nodes
keeps (probe hook-inputs-2). Without those filters the stylesheet is the
engine's own, byte for byte.

methods.name: corePresets
methods.doc:
Core's preset lists: as stored, unless a plugin changed core's layer
(wp_theme_json_data_default), whose lists then stand in for them.

methods.name: keptBlocks
methods.doc:
The blocks' styles as far as the kept nodes reach: a block's own
declarations with its node, each of its elements with that element's
node (the reference lists them apart); a block with neither goes.

methods.name: keptNodes
methods.doc:
The style nodes a plugin keeps (wp_theme_json_get_style_nodes) as
their paths, the root, element and block nodes printed only when
kept; null when no plugin filters them.

classes.name: Minn\Theme\StylePresets
classes.doc:
The preset side of theme.json: the colour, gradient, font-size,
font-family, spacing, and shadow lists a theme declares over core's
own, as the custom properties on :root and the has-* utility classes
the reference prints for them. Pure: settings in, CSS fragments out.

methods.name: presets
methods.doc: Every preset list the theme declares, over core's own (as given, else data/presets.json), keyed by kind.

methods.name: presetList
methods.doc:
A preset list as theme.json writes it is a plain list; as the site
editor saves it, it is keyed by origin (default, theme, custom). The
reference prints the origins in that order, so the two shapes flatten
to one list here.

methods.name: fontFamilies
methods.doc: The font family presets in the settings.

methods.name: presetProperties
methods.doc: The presets as custom properties for :root.

methods.name: customProperties
methods.doc:
A settings.custom tree as custom properties: --wp--custom-- and the path
to each value, every key in kebab case, lists by index; empty values
are left out.

methods.name: presetClasses
methods.doc: The has-* utility classes the presets give every colour, gradient, font size, and font family; each under the prefix given (a block's :where(selector)).

methods.name: fontSizes
methods.doc:
Core's font sizes, always printed, then the theme's: a theme size
with one of core's slugs takes its place when defaultFontSizes is
false, and gives way to core's while core's are kept (probe
default-presets).
shapes: @param list<array{slug: string, value: string}> $defaults core's, as data/presets.json holds them
@param list<array> $own the theme's (and the site editor's) presets
@param array<string, mixed> $settings the theme's settings, which say whether core's are kept

params.name: own
params.doc: the theme's (and the site editor's) presets

params.name: settings
params.doc: the theme's settings, which say whether core's are kept

methods.name: spacingPresets
methods.doc:
The default spacing scale (20 to 80) is always present, whatever
defaultSpacingSizes says; a theme size with the same slug replaces the
default in place, and the theme's other sizes follow the scale.

methods.name: fluidFontSize
methods.doc: A font size preset as the global stylesheet writes it: fluid by the theme's settings (Typography::fontSize).

classes.name: Minn\Theme\StyleSettings
classes.doc:
The settings and styles nodes as wp/v2/global-styles reports them:
preset lists keyed by the origin that declared them, appearanceTools
spelled out as the flags it stands for, and var:preset tokens resolved
to the custom properties they name. Pure: a node in, a node out.

What appearanceTools switches on, group by group in the order the
reference appends the groups it has to add; a group already present
keeps its place and gains the flags at its end.

methods.name: normalize
methods.doc:
A settings node as written (theme.json, a variation, or the site
editor's post) with its presets keyed by origin and appearanceTools
expanded.

params.name: origin
params.doc: theme for a theme's file, custom for the site editor's

methods.name: presetsByOrigin
methods.doc: The preset lists, at the root and under each block, keyed by the origin given; nothing else changed.

methods.name: resolved
methods.doc: Every var:preset|kind|slug token replaced by the custom property it names.

methods.name: withAppearanceTools
methods.doc: The flag itself goes; a flag the node already sets keeps its value.

classes.name: Minn\Theme\Teaser
classes.doc:
What a post's full text does with the part before its more tag
(the_content's $strip_teaser): kept, or left out so the text starts
where the more tag stood.

classes.name: Minn\Theme\TemplateBuffer
classes.doc:
The reference includes a front-end template inside the template-enhancement
buffer: wp_before_include_template fires with the template's file, its
default callback opens the buffer when a plugin filters
wp_template_enhancement_output_buffer, and that filter is handed the whole
page. The engine builds the page as a string, so the string is passed
through the same buffer: every buffer the action opened is closed in turn,
its handler writing into the capture the page is read from.

methods.name: around
methods.doc:
The page a render gives, as the buffers opened before it leave it; null
when the render gives none. A render that fails leaves nothing behind.

classes.name: Minn\Theme\TemplateHierarchy
classes.doc:
The templates a block theme falls back through for a template slug, as
get_template_hierarchy builds them (probe rest-templates-lookup): the
slug itself, then its family's chain to index. A single entry's slug
reaches single-{type} and single only when the type is registered (and
goes straight to singular when not); a taxonomy's reaches taxonomy-{tax}
and taxonomy only when the taxonomy is; pages, categories, tags and
authors step through their bare name when the slug has more to it. A
prefix names the next step outright. A custom template is a page's.

methods.name: for
methods.signature: for(string $slug, bool $custom, string $prefix, array $types, array $taxonomies): array
methods.doc: A slug's fallback chain, most specific first, ending at index.

methods.name: chain
methods.doc: What follows a slug (or a prefix) down to index.

methods.name: registered
methods.doc: The registered name a slug's remainder starts with (the whole of it, or before a hyphen), the longest first. @param list<string> $names

classes.name: Minn\Theme\TemplateIndex
classes.doc:
Every block template and template part the site offers, in the order the
reference lists them: the rows the site editor saved first (newest post
date first, those of one date in the order they were saved), then the theme's own files in the order the directory hands
them back, then whatever a plugin registered. A saved row shadows the
theme file of the same slug and reports has_theme_file so the file can
be restored by deleting the row.

methods.name: all
methods.doc: Every template of a type: the theme's files with the saved rows over them.

methods.name: find
methods.doc:
The template an id names: the site's own row by that slug first,
published, draft, trashed or an auto-draft (the reference's lookup by
id; the list shows only published ones), then the theme's file or a
plugin's. Null when the id names another theme, or a slug nothing
provides.

methods.name: postRecord
methods.doc: A saved wp_template or wp_template_part row as a template. @param array<string, mixed> $row

methods.name: files
methods.doc:
The theme's files of a type, in the directory's order, each as
_get_block_templates_files describes it (fileInfo).

methods.name: fileInfo
methods.doc:
One theme file: its slug, path, theme (the parent's for a file the
child does not have) and type; a part's title (when theme.json gives
one) and area; a custom template's title and post types (pages when
it names none). Null when the theme has no such file.

methods.name: postTypes
methods.doc: The post types a custom template declares; none for any other template.

methods.name: savedId
methods.doc: The id of a template or part saved for any theme by slug, its wp_theme term naming the theme; null for none.

methods.name: themeSlug
methods.doc: The theme the index reads.

methods.name: hasFile
methods.doc: Whether the theme ships a file for a slug.

methods.name: authorText
methods.doc:
Who the caller is told made this: the theme's own name for anything
that has a file behind it, the plugin for a registered one, the
author's display name for a row a person saved, and the site's name
when nobody is recorded.

methods.name: originalSource
methods.doc: theme when a file backs it, plugin when one registered it, user when someone saved it, else site.

methods.name: customFor
methods.doc:
The custom templates a post of a type may name in its template field,
in the order the reference lists them when it refuses one: saved
custom templates the theme does not declare, which every type may
use, then those the theme declares for the type (pages, when one
names no types). Probe template-field in contracts/rest/write-fields.md.

methods.name: isCustom
methods.doc: A slug the reference does not name in its default template types is a custom template.

methods.name: defaults
methods.doc: The default template types.

methods.name: markup
methods.doc:
Markup as a caller of the REST route sees it: patterns spliced in
where the template only named them, then every template-part block
told which theme it belongs to. A record carries the markup as
stored, because that is what get_block_templates() hands a plugin.

methods.name: savedRows
shapes: @return list<array<string, mixed>> read once a request for each type, as the templates' own rows are (a write to a post drops them)

methods.name: fileTitle
methods.doc:
A theme file's title: the default template types name the hierarchy
slugs, theme.json names the rest, and a slug neither knows about is
its own title, verbatim rather than prettified.

classes.name: Minn\Theme\TemplatePartTheme
classes.doc:
A template-part block inside a template says which theme's part it means.
The theme's own files usually leave that out, and the reference fills the
active theme in on the way out, for saved rows as much as for files. It
appends the attribute and leaves every other byte of the markup alone.

methods.name: apply
methods.doc: Template part blocks with the theme attribute set.

classes.name: Minn\Theme\TemplatePatterns
classes.doc:
A template can name a pattern instead of carrying its blocks, and the
reference hands the caller the blocks: every "wp:pattern" delimiter is
replaced by the pattern's own markup before a template or part is
served. A slug the theme does not know stays exactly as it is, which is
what tells an editor the pattern went missing rather than the block.

methods.name: expand
methods.doc: Markup with its pattern blocks replaced by the patterns' content.

methods.name: closerAt
methods.doc: The offset past a self-closing delimiter's "/-->", or null when it is not one.

methods.name: stamped
methods.doc:
The pattern's own name rides on the block it opens, so an editor can
still see which pattern a stretch of blocks came from. Only a pattern
that IS one block gets the stamp: several blocks have no single
wrapper to carry the name, and the reference leaves those anonymous.
The stamp goes on the pattern's raw markup, before any pattern nested
inside it is spliced in, so when that one block is itself a pattern
reference the stamp goes away with it.

classes.name: Minn\Theme\TemplateRecord
classes.doc:
One block template or template part, whatever it came from: a theme
file, a row the site editor saved, or a template a plugin registered.
The id every caller uses is "<theme>//<slug>" in all three cases.

constructor.signature: __construct(string $theme, string $slug, string $type, string $content, string $title, string $description, string $source, ?string $origin, bool $hasThemeFile, int $author, ?string $modified, ?string $date, int $wpId, string $status = 'publish', ?string $area = NULL, ?string $plugin = NULL, bool $suggestion = false)

methods.name: id
methods.doc: The reference's template id: theme//slug.

methods.name: isPart
methods.doc: Whether this is a template part.

classes.name: Minn\Theme\TemplateWriter
classes.doc:
Saving and removing block templates. A template the theme ships is never
touched on disk: editing one writes a wp_template row that shadows the
file, and deleting that row is what "reset to the theme version" means.

methods.name: save
methods.doc:
Writes the site's own copy of a template, creating the row the first
time. Returns the post id.
shapes: @param array{title?: string, content?: string, description?: string, area?: string} $fields

params.name: fields
params.shape: array{title?: string, content?: string, description?: string, area?: string}

methods.name: create
methods.doc:
A new site copy from the collection's create: as a save inserts one,
but recording no origin, even over a theme file (probe
rest-template-create).

methods.name: trash
methods.doc:
Moves a site copy to the trash, which hands the theme's file back: as
any post goes there, its slug suffixed __trashed and its status, time
and slug kept for the way back, so the id no longer finds it.

methods.name: destroy
methods.doc: Deletes a saved template row.

methods.name: insert
methods.doc: The site copy's row, its theme term and its area.

classes.name: Minn\Theme\Templates
classes.doc:
Which template renders a resolution, and where its markup comes from:
a wp_template post saved from the site editor (matched by slug and the
theme term) wins over the theme's file. Parts resolve the same way
through wp_template_part.

methods.name: forResolution
methods.doc:
The template that renders a resolution, or null; with the runtime up,
its fields as the template object holds them too. A theme's PHP
template takes part as the reference's loader lets it (contracts/
runtime.md, "A child theme's PHP template"): within a template type,
only block templates for the slugs up to the first one a PHP file
answers are looked for, a child's PHP file passes over its parent's
block template of the same slug, and when no block template is left
the PHP file is the template ('php', its path; no markup).
shapes: @return array{slug: string, markup: string, fields?: array<string, mixed>, php?: string}|null

methods.name: template
methods.doc: A template's markup by slug, saved first.

methods.name: part
methods.doc: A template part's markup by slug, saved first.

methods.name: partSource
methods.doc:
Where a template part comes from: a part saved for the theme (its
post id), the theme's file (its path), or nowhere; with its markup.

methods.name: userStyles
methods.doc:
The site editor's saved global styles for the active theme, when any.
An emptied node is stored as [] and reads as nothing, the way the
reference reads it; a list where a map belongs is dropped the same way.

methods.name: load
methods.doc: Has the theme's saved templates (and its term) read, if they are not yet: the template-part lookup answers from them.

methods.name: savedPartIds
methods.doc:
The ids the template-part lookup finds for a slug: the newest saved
part of the theme by that name, or none.

methods.name: customTemplate
methods.doc: A page's chosen custom template, from _wp_page_template meta.

methods.name: found
methods.doc:
The first of these slugs a template answers, in their order. With the runtime up the answer is the
reference's: the templates get_block_templates finds for the slugs (its pre and result filters let a plugin
add one or change one, as The Events Calendar and WooCommerce do).
shapes: @return array{slug: string, markup: string, fields?: array<string, mixed>}|null

methods.name: filtered
methods.doc:
Plugins reshape a template type's hierarchy through the reference's
"{type}_template_hierarchy" filters (WooCommerce sends its taxonomies to
archive-product that way, The Events Calendar its archive to its own);
the filter sees PHP file names and hands back the same, which become
slugs again.

methods.name: groups
methods.doc:
The block-theme template hierarchy for each kind of resolution, as the
reference's template loader walks it: a template type at a time (the
front page, the kind's own, then singular or archive, then index), each
with its own slugs, until one has a template.
shapes: @return array<string, list<string>> slugs by template type

methods.name: savedOfTheme
methods.doc:
Every published template, part and global styles post saved for the
theme, newest first by type: read in one query once a request, with
the theme's own wp_theme term (by name, as the reference finds it), so
the term lookups the template queries make need no query of their own.

methods.name: savedRow
methods.doc:
The newest published template of a type (and slug) saved for the
theme. Every saved one of the type is read once a request, newest
first, so a template's candidates and its parts cost one query.

classes.name: Minn\Theme\Theme
classes.doc:
The active block theme on disk, read as data: theme.json, the templates
and parts directories, and the patterns index. A child theme's files
win and its parent fills in what the child does not define; theme.json
merges the same way, with the child's preset lists replacing the
parent's whole. The engine reads the site's installed theme the way it
reads the site's database; it never runs the theme's PHP.

methods.name: active
methods.doc: The active block theme, or null under a classic one.

methods.name: forStyles
methods.doc:
The active theme as styling data (theme.json present), whether or not
it is a block theme; the classic renderer prints its presets where the
reference prints a classic theme's global styles.

methods.name: parentSlug
methods.doc: The theme's own name, and the parent's, for body classes.

methods.name: json
methods.doc: The theme.json with the parent's merged in; with plugins loaded, through wp_theme_json_data_theme.

methods.name: styleFiles
methods.doc:
Every JSON file under styles/, the parent theme's first and each
theme's in path order: block style partials and style variations alike.

methods.name: merge
methods.doc:
Layered theme.json: maps merge key by key, lists (palettes, font
sizes, template parts) replace as a whole.

methods.name: templateFile
methods.doc: A template file's markup, or null.

methods.name: templatePath
methods.doc: The file a template is read from: this theme's, else its parent's; null when neither has one.

methods.name: phpTemplate
methods.doc:
The first of these template slugs a PHP file answers, as locate_template
looks (each name in this theme, then its parent's), with whether this
theme holds it itself while it has a parent (a child theme's own); null
when none does. A hybrid theme's PHP templates take part in the block
template hierarchy this way.
shapes: @return array{slug: string, path: string, child: bool}|null

methods.name: ownsTemplate
methods.doc: Whether this theme's own folder (not its parent's) holds a template file for the slug.

methods.name: partFile
methods.doc: A template part file's markup, or null.

methods.name: partPath
methods.doc: The file a template part is read from: this theme's, else its parent's; null when neither has one.

methods.name: name
methods.doc:
The theme's display name, as the stylesheet header states it; a child
theme answers with its own. Falls back to theme.json's title, then the
folder name.

methods.name: fileSlugs
methods.doc:
Every template (or part) slug the theme offers, the child's files
first and the parent's after, each in the order the directory hands
them back: the reference walks these directories unsorted and its
template list carries that order through.

methods.name: customTemplate
methods.doc: A template title and description the theme declares for a custom template slug.

methods.name: partTitle
methods.doc: The title theme.json gives a template part, when it names one.

methods.name: declaredPartArea
methods.doc: The area theme.json declares for a template part, or null when it declares none.

methods.name: partArea
methods.doc: The template-part area declared in theme.json (header, footer, or uncategorized).

methods.name: pattern
methods.doc: A pattern's markup, with its PHP text subset interpreted; null when unknown.

methods.name: patternMeta
methods.doc:
A pattern's declared Block Types and Categories, the header fields a
plugin reads to tell (say) a header pattern from any other.

methods.name: patternHeader
methods.doc:
The header fields a pattern declares, as the metadata attribute the
reference writes onto the pattern's first block when it splices the
pattern into a template. A field the header omits is omitted here.
shapes: @return array{patternName: string, name: string, description?: string, categories?: list<string>}|null

methods.name: styleUri
methods.doc: The theme's stylesheet URL when it ships one; a child's own, else nothing (the parent's is not enqueued for it).

methods.name: rawJson
methods.doc: The theme.json as written, the parent's merged in.

methods.name: withStylePartials
methods.doc:
A theme's styles/ folder can hold block style variations: a JSON file
with blockTypes and a slug (else the file name) whose styles become
styles.blocks.{type}.variations.{slug} for each named block type. The
parent's partials load first, the child's over them.

methods.name: safe
methods.doc: A template or part name is a file name, never a path.

classes.name: Minn\Theme\ThemeFiles
classes.doc:
The theme files a request reads, each read once: a theme's JSON documents
(theme.json and the partials under styles/), the JSON files under a
folder, and a patterns folder's files by slug. Several parts of a page
build a Theme over the same folders (the block renderer, global styles,
the template index, the facade's theme.json data), and each read every
file again; under open_basedir, which checks each path a file call names,
those reads were the larger part of a page's time. A process answers one
request, so the next request reads what is on disk then.

methods.name: json
methods.doc: A JSON file's contents, null when it is missing or not JSON.

methods.name: jsonUnder
methods.doc:
Every JSON file under a folder and its subfolders, in path order; none
when the folder is not there.

methods.name: patterns
methods.doc:
The PHP files directly in a patterns folder, by the slug each one's
header declares (a file without one is left out).

classes.name: Minn\Theme\ThemeHeaders
classes.doc:
A theme's headers as the reference's WP_Theme reads and shows them
(probe theme-headers): sanitized as read, in the theme's language, and
with markup.

constants.name: PLAIN
constants.value: array (   'abbr' =>    array (     'title' => true,   ),   'acronym' =>    array (     'title' => true,   ),   'code' =>    array (   ),   'em' =>    array (   ),   'strong' =>    array (   ), )
constants.doc: The tags a name or a status may keep.

constants.name: ALLOWED
constants.value: array (   'a' =>    array (     'title' => true,     'href' => true,   ),   'abbr' =>    array (     'title' => true,   ),   'acronym' =>    array (     'title' => true,   ),   'code' =>    array (   ),   'em' =>    array (   ),   'strong' =>    array (   ), )
constants.doc: The tags a description or an author may keep: those, and links.

methods.name: read
methods.doc:
A header as WP_Theme::get reads it, once for its theme object (probe
theme-headers): Tags as a list; a value sanitized (the name and status
through kses, the description and author too with links, the addresses
as URLs, the version and requirements, and each tag, without tags; the
rest as written); Status "publish" when an existing theme leaves it
out.

methods.name: shown
methods.signature: shown(string $header, mixed $value, mixed $markup, mixed $translate, string $domain, Closure $loadDomain, Closure $plain): mixed
methods.doc:
A header's value as shown, sanitized as read (read()): unless asked
not to, in the theme's language (any header with a value, its text
domain loaded first); then with markup a list joined, the author linked
to their address (shown the same way), the addresses escaped and the
description texturized.
shapes: @param Closure(): mixed $loadDomain loads the theme's text domain, once for its theme object
@param Closure(string): mixed $plain another header of the theme, shown without markup

params.name: loadDomain
params.doc: loads the theme's text domain, once for its theme object

params.name: plain
params.doc: another header of the theme, shown without markup

methods.name: loadFor
methods.doc: A theme object's text domain (WP_Theme::load_textdomain), loaded once for it.

methods.name: loadDomain
methods.doc:
A theme's text domain named to load from its folder, as
load_theme_textdomain names it: the folder its Domain Path names, its
languages folder when it names none. False for a theme that names no
domain.

classes.name: Minn\Theme\ThemeJsonData
classes.doc:
The theme's theme.json as plugins and the theme's own functions may
change it (wp_theme_json_data_theme, a WP_Theme_JSON_Data they update
with presets and settings of their own), as the reference's resolver
hands it to them, and the core and site editor layers likewise
(wp_theme_json_data_default, wp_theme_json_data_user). Worked out once
a request for each set of callbacks, so a filter added late still counts.

methods.name: theme
methods.doc: The theme layer through wp_theme_json_data_theme; as written when nothing filters it. @param array<string, mixed> $json

methods.name: layer
methods.doc:
The core layer (wp_theme_json_data_default, origin default) or the
site editor's (wp_theme_json_data_user, origin custom) as plugins
leave it, each a WP_Theme_JSON_Data they update; as given when
nothing filters it. Worked out once a request for each set of
callbacks and layer.

methods.name: asWritten
methods.doc:
The filtered layer back in theme.json's own shape: each preset (and
the spacing scale) the theme's list again, everything else in the
order it came, as the reference's resolver keeps the layer's object.

classes.name: Minn\Theme\ThemeStyles
classes.doc:
The active theme's global styles as wp/v2/global-styles/themes/{stylesheet}
reports them: the engine's defaults (captured from the reference under a
theme with no theme.json) with the theme's own settings and styles over
them, and the style variations the theme ships.

shapes: @param array{settings?: array, styles?: array}|null $core core's layer when not the stored one (a plugin changed it)

params.name: theme
params.doc: null under a theme without theme.json: the defaults alone

params.name: core
params.doc: core's layer when not the stored one (a plugin changed it)

methods.name: withFilteredCore
methods.doc:
The same styling data over core's layer as wp_theme_json_data_default
leaves it, for the places the reference reads core's layer through
that filter (its resolver's core and merged data).

methods.name: forSite
methods.doc: The site's active theme as styling data, whether or not it is a block theme.

methods.name: settings
methods.doc: Settings: presets by origin, appearanceTools expanded, the defaults underneath.

methods.name: themeLayer
methods.doc:
The theme's own layer, as the resolver's theme data holds it: no core
layer under it, its settings normalized as settings() normalizes
them, its styles with partials and section styles in, and the
template lists and pattern slugs it declares.

methods.name: patterns
methods.doc: The pattern directory slugs the theme.json lists (its patterns), as given; [] when it lists none. @return array<mixed>

methods.name: styles
methods.doc: Styles: the theme's over the defaults, block style partials and section styles in, every var:preset token resolved.

methods.name: variations
methods.doc:
The style variations under styles/: every JSON file there that names
no blockTypes (those are block style partials), the parent theme's
first, in path order, $schema dropped and the nodes normalized the
way the theme's own are.

methods.name: withSectionStyles
methods.doc:
A root styles.variations node names section styles by the slug of
the block style partial that declares them; each lands under every
block type that partial names, the blocks it has to add in name
order, and the root node goes.

methods.name: partials
methods.doc: The block style partials under styles/: slug => the block types each names.

methods.name: defaults
shapes: @return array{settings?: array, styles?: array} core's layer: the one given, else the stored one

methods.name: storedCore
shapes: @return array{settings: array, styles: array} core's own layer as stored

classes.name: Minn\Theme\TreeStyles
classes.doc:
The CSS one theme.json tree writes, as WP_Theme_JSON keeps the tree
(presets keyed by origin): its custom properties, its preset classes, its
styles (the root layout, the root, elements, blocks) and its own CSS, by
type, origin and option (probe theme-json-css). The rules are
GlobalStyles'; what the page's writer takes for granted is read from the
tree instead: block gaps only when the tree turns them on, the root padding
only on the sides it gives, and none of the engine's own defaults.

constants.name: KINDS
constants.value: array (   'aspect-ratio' =>    array (     0 =>      array (       0 => 'dimensions',       1 => 'aspectRatios',     ),     1 => 'ratio',   ),   'color' =>    array (     0 =>      array (       0 => 'color',       1 => 'palette',     ),     1 => 'color',   ),   'gradient' =>    array (     0 =>      array (       0 => 'color',       1 => 'gradients',     ),     1 => 'gradient',   ),   'font-size' =>    array (     0 =>      array (       0 => 'typography',       1 => 'fontSizes',     ),     1 => 'size',   ),   'font-family' =>    array (     0 =>      array (       0 => 'typography',       1 => 'fontFamilies',     ),     1 => 'fontFamily',   ),   'spacing' =>    array (     0 =>      array (       0 => 'spacing',       1 => 'spacingSizes',     ),     1 => 'size',   ),   'shadow' =>    array (     0 =>      array (       0 => 'shadow',       1 => 'presets',     ),     1 => 'shadow',   ),   'border-radius' =>    array (     0 =>      array (       0 => 'border',       1 => 'radiusSizes',     ),     1 => 'size',   ),   'dimension' =>    array (     0 =>      array (       0 => 'dimensions',       1 => 'dimensionSizes',     ),     1 => 'size',   ), )
constants.doc: Preset kinds in the order they print: where each sits under settings, and the key holding its value.

methods.name: stylesheet
methods.doc:
The stylesheet for the types asked for, in the order variables,
styles, presets, the tree's own CSS; origins narrow the presets.

methods.name: variables
methods.doc:
The presets and settings.custom as custom properties: on :root, then
on each block's settings selector that has its own.

methods.name: variablesOf
methods.doc: One settings node's custom properties under its selector; nothing when it has none.

methods.name: presetClasses
methods.doc: The has-* classes: the root's bare, each block's under :where(its settings selector).

methods.name: classesOf
methods.doc: One settings node's has-* classes, under :where(selector) unless it is the bare :root.

methods.name: styles
methods.doc:
The styles: the root layout (unless skip_root_layout_styles), the
root's own rule, its CSS when the root is not body, the elements, then
each block; under the root_selector and scope options.

methods.name: rootLayoutRules
methods.doc:
The root layout: the content and wide sizes, the body's margin, the
global padding rules, the alignments; for body, the block gap (or the
fallback gap of flex and grid) and the layouts' own rules.

methods.name: layoutStyles
methods.doc: The block gap and the layouts' own rules; flex and grid fall back to a 0.5em gap when the tree has no block gap.

methods.name: rootStyles
methods.doc: The root's own rule: body as it is, any other root under :root :where().

methods.name: blockStyles
methods.doc: One block's rules; its own block gap only when the tree turns block gaps on.

methods.name: blockOwnStyles
methods.doc: One block's own rules, its elements left out: each element is a style node of its own.

methods.name: blockElements
methods.doc: The elements a block styles, in the order they print.

methods.name: elementStyles
methods.doc: One element's rules, under a block's selector when it belongs to one.

methods.name: customCss
methods.doc: The tree's own top-level CSS, as written.

methods.name: settingsSelector
methods.doc: A block's settings selector: its experimental selector when it has one, else .wp-block-{slug}.

methods.name: blockGap
methods.doc: The block gap: the styles' value when the tree's settings turn block gaps on, else null.

methods.name: presets
methods.doc:
A settings node's presets by kind, the origins asked for in order, one
per slug; a font size is written fluid by the root's typography
settings.

classes.name: Minn\Theme\Typography
classes.doc:
Font sizes as the reference writes them (probe plugin-queue3): a size in
px, rem or em, and, with fluid typography on, a clamp() that grows
linearly from a minimum at a small viewport to the size (or the preset's
own maximum) at the wide one.

methods.name: valueAndUnit
methods.doc:
A CSS length split into its number and unit (px, rem or em, or the
units given), converted to another unit on request at a 16px root
(or the one given); a bare number is px. Null for anything else.
shapes: @param array{coerce_to?: string, root_size_value?: int|float, acceptable_units?: list<string>} $options

params.name: options
params.shape: array{coerce_to?: string, root_size_value?: int|float, acceptable_units?: list<string>}

methods.name: fontSize
methods.doc:
A font size preset as CSS (wp_get_typography_font_size_value). It
stays as written unless fluid typography is on and the size is in a
known unit and above the floor (14px, or the settings' minFontSize);
then it grows from a minimum (the preset's own, else the size scaled
by 1 - 0.075 log2 of its px, held between 0.25 and 0.75, never under
the floor) to a maximum (the preset's own, else the size).
shapes: @param array<string, mixed> $settings typography and layout, merged over the global settings

params.name: settings
params.doc: typography and layout, merged over the global settings

methods.name: clamp
methods.doc:
The clamp() between two sizes over two viewport widths
(wp_get_computed_fluid_typography_value): the slope in the minimum's
unit, the base in rem. Null when a size or a width is missing or in an
unknown unit, or the widths are equal.

methods.name: number
methods.doc: A number as PHP writes a float: no trailing ".0".

classes.name: Minn\Theme\UserStyles
classes.doc:
The site editor's saved global styles: one wp_global_styles post per
theme, tied to it by the wp_theme term, holding a versioned JSON body
of the settings and styles the editor wrote. Every changed save leaves
a revision behind, as a post's does.

methods.name: idFor
methods.doc: The newest published global-styles post carrying the theme's term, or null.

methods.name: ensure
methods.doc: The theme's post, made the way the reference makes it when there is none yet.

methods.name: find
methods.doc: The post when it is a global-styles post, else null.

methods.name: decode
methods.doc:
What a global-styles body holds; a missing, malformed, or list-shaped
node is empty, as the reference reads it.

methods.name: isBlank
methods.doc: True when the body carries nothing at all under settings or styles, malformed or not.

methods.name: changes
methods.doc:
What a save changes, as columns: the title when one is given, and,
when the caller names settings or styles, the content rebuilt from
them, the stored styles and settings it leaves out (a node the stored
config never had stays out), the marker and version 3, as the
reference rewrites it; any other stored key is dropped. A save naming
neither leaves the content as stored, broken or not. Null for no such
post. The REST controller saves it as a post update.

classes.name: Minn\Widgets\TextWidgets
classes.doc:
The text and custom HTML widgets' behaviour (WP_Widget_Text,
WP_Widget_Custom_HTML; probes widget-methods, nav-pomo-rest-doubts):
which text instances are legacy ones the visual editor would change, how
an update settles the filter and visual flags, and the two widgets'
output, their filters run with no global post and a gallery inside
belonging to no post.

constants.name: KEPT
constants.value: array (   'b' =>    array (   ),   'i' =>    array (   ),   'u' =>    array (   ),   's' =>    array (   ),   'em' =>    array (   ),   'strong' =>    array (   ),   'code' =>    array (   ),   'abbr' =>    array (   ),   'ul' =>    array (   ),   'ol' =>    array (   ),   'li' =>    array (   ),   'a' =>    array (     0 => 'href',   ),   'img' =>    array (     0 => 'src',     1 => 'alt',   ),   'hr' =>    array (   ), )
constants.doc: The elements the visual editor keeps as written, each with the attributes it keeps.

constants.name: VOID
constants.doc: The kept elements that are empty by nature.

methods.name: isLegacy
methods.doc:
Whether a text instance is a legacy one: one with a visual flag is
legacy when the flag is off, one filtered as content never is, nor
blank text. Otherwise its text is legacy when it has a line break
without the paragraph filter, a comment, an element or attribute the
visual editor does not keep, or an element left empty.

methods.name: settled
methods.doc:
An updated text instance's flags settled: filtered when the new one
asks, visual as the new one says (always for content filtering), and a
visual instance always filtered.
shapes: @param array<array-key, mixed> $instance the instance with its title and text set
@param array<array-key, mixed> $new the settings as submitted

params.name: instance
params.doc: the instance with its title and text set

methods.name: text
methods.doc:
The text widget's markup: a visual instance (visual and filtered, or
filtered as content) through widget_text and widget_text_content; any
other through widget_text, then paragraphs when it asks for them, then
its shortcodes.

methods.name: customHtml
methods.doc:
The custom HTML widget's markup: its content through widget_text (as a
text instance would carry it) and widget_custom_html_content, the text
widget's class first in the wrapper.

methods.name: galleryAttributes
methods.doc:
Gallery attributes inside a text or HTML widget: off a singular view,
a gallery naming neither an id nor included images belongs to no post (-1).

methods.name: withoutPost
methods.doc: A widget's filters run with no global post and its gallery filter on; both put back after.

classes.name: Minn\Widgets\WidgetForms
classes.doc:
The core widgets' settings forms, the markup a widget's form() prints and
wp/v2/widgets returns as rendered_form, character for character as the
reference prints it (probe rest-widgets): field ids and names from the
widget's number, values escaped, defaults filled in. The whitespace is
the reference's own and is part of the answer.

methods.name: title
methods.doc: The title field most widgets open with.

methods.name: titleOnly
methods.doc: search, meta, calendar: the title alone.

methods.name: pages
methods.doc: The pages widget: title, sort order, pages to leave out.

methods.name: archives
methods.doc: The archives widget: title, dropdown and counts boxes.

methods.name: categories
methods.doc: The categories widget: title, dropdown, counts and hierarchy boxes.

methods.name: recentPosts
methods.doc: The recent posts widget: title, how many, whether to show dates.

methods.name: recentComments
methods.doc: The recent comments widget: title and how many.

methods.name: customHtml
methods.doc: The custom HTML widget: hidden title and content fields its editor syncs.

methods.name: block
methods.doc: The block widget: its block markup in a textarea.

methods.name: text
methods.doc: The text widget in its visual mode: hidden fields the editor syncs (after the indent WP_Widget_Text::form prints first).

methods.name: tagCloud
methods.doc: The tag cloud: its title, the taxonomies that show a cloud (tags unless one is chosen), and the counts box.

methods.name: navMenu
methods.doc: The navigation menu widget: a note when there are no menus, else the title and the menu to show.

methods.name: rss
methods.doc:
wp_widget_rss_form: the feed's address, title, item count (1 to 20,
10 by default) and the three display boxes, each shown unless the
caller hides it, and ticked when the settings say so (or, saying
nothing, when it is shown).

methods.name: links
methods.doc:
The Links widget: the link category (the categories given as [id, name]),
the sort order, what each link shows, and how many (the limit as the
caller shows it).

methods.name: marked
methods.doc: The attribute selected() or checked() prints, with its leading space, when the two values match as text.

classes.name: Minn\Widgets\WidgetTemplates
classes.doc:
The Underscore templates the Text and Custom HTML widgets print for their
controls (render_control_template_scripts), as the reference prints them
(probe widget-methods): a title field and the content area, the Text
widget's two hidden pointers, and, for a user who may not post unfiltered
HTML, the note on the tags the code editor refuses. The whitespace is the
reference's own and is part of the answer.

constants.name: UNSAFE_TAGS
constants.doc: The tags the note on refused tags names, those a post may hold aside.

methods.name: text
methods.doc: The Text widget's template: title, the two pointers, the content area.

methods.name: customHtml
methods.doc: The Custom HTML widget's template for a user who may post unfiltered HTML.

methods.name: customHtmlRestricted
methods.doc:
The Custom HTML widget's template for a user who may not, with the
note (shown when the code editor is off) naming the unsafe tags a post
may not hold (wp_kses_allowed_html); no note when it may hold them all.

methods.name: open
methods.doc: The script tag, the element id prefix both templates make, and the title field.

methods.name: pointer
methods.doc: A hidden pointer: its heading, its paragraph (with the reference's indents around it), a dismiss link.
